tenderTitle: VERY LARGE AND MODULAR SOLAR ARRAYS FOR IN-ORBIT ROBOTIC ASSEMBLY - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop and manufacture a robotic testbed to demonstrate the modular solar arrays robotic assembly, and validate the functionality in a laboratory environment, validating solar array modules design, and mechanical/electrical interfaces.Description: The activity aim is to develop a very large and modular solar array that is suitable to power very large space structures and thatcan be assembled in orbit. The design of the solar array and process of manufacturing on-ground shall be developed to target the modularity but with emphasis in covering a very large area, as well as allowing in-orbit integration. These can be achieved by exploiting existing technologies or proposing novel concepts. Concentrated Photovoltaics can be also considered, particularly for large structures targeting Deep Space missions. The assembly of solar panels within in-orbit large space structures requires careful analysisof the panels mechanical and electrical interactions and interfaces, to enable the use of robots for interlinking and assembling the necessary infrastructure. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition and design of modular solar arrays and themechanical and electrical interfaces interconnecting them, suitable for building large area space structures. Targeting to obtain solar arrays 2 or 4 times bigger than current state-of-the-art. - Development and manufacturing of a robotic testbed to demonstrate the modular solar arrays robotic assembly. - Prototyping of electrical and mechanical interfaces between panels and with the robotic systems. - Initial proof of concept demonstration, verify functionality in a laboratory environment, validating solar array modules design, and mechanical/electrical interfaces.

tenderTitle: RAYLEIGH GUIDE STAR FOR ADAPTIVE OPTICS IN OPTICAL COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.075) EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to evaluate the use of a Rayleigh guide star as a reference beacon for adaptive opticspre-and post-compensation for optical communication through the atmosphere.Targeted Improvements:75% reduction in cost and complexity with respect to the use of a Sodium guide star laserDescription:The use of a Rayleigh guide star as a reference beacon for optical pre-and post-compensation over the current Sodium laser solution would allow for a considerable decrease in both the cost and complexity of the laser system required for adaptive optics in optical links through the atmosphere.The Rayleigh guide star shall be evaluated for its suitability and be compared to existing solutions, to demonstrate the potential improvements. An evaluation of the sub-system, the choice of equipment and the operational implementation shall be addressed for use on optical communication links through the atmosphere. The activity will perform a numerical study comparing the main possible beacons to be used as reference for pre- and post-compensation in Adaptive Optics (AO) in the context of optical communications, using as a reference the 3 main solutions: Sodium Guide Star, Beacon from the satellite and Rayleigh Guide Star. A selection of suitable equipment solutions will need to be chosen and the impact of the beacon method on the global architecture/cost, ease of operation/complexity/laser safety of backscattered light evaluated. Upon a positive solution being proposed, integration and tests will be conducted in a laboratory environment, and then on-sky tests will be conducted.

tenderTitle: PHASED ARRAYS EXPLOITING GRATING LOBESFOR SCATTEROMETER INSTRUMENTS EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a representative demonstrator of a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array with a reduced number of control points, by exploiting grating lobes.Description: For Earth Observation applications there are instruments, like Scatterometers, requiring a limited number of beams M pointing in fixed directions. A promising antenna architecture is based on an array antenna organized in interleaved subarrays (number of subarrays equal to the number of target beams M). Each subarray is having the periodic cell split in M sub-apertures. One of the M sub-apertures is occupied by a radiating element, the other M-1 slots are kept emptyto be used by the other M-1 interleaved subarrays. The dimension of the periodic cell is larger than one wavelength in order to create grating lobes exactly in the directions where the desired beams of the Scatterometer instrument are targeted. The array factor associated to the M phase centres of the M subarrays, when fed with identical phase value, creates a beam pointing at the boresight direction with radiative nulls positions coinciding with the grating lobes positions. Accordingly, when feeding the M inputs with thesame phase value a main beam in the boresight direction can be generated and the M-1 grating lobes can be cancelled by the radiative nulls. When feeding the M inputs with a linear phase in order to point the main beam exactly at one of the M possible targeted angles, the radiative nulls permit to cancel all the subarray pattern beams except the desired one. The M beams can be generated one atthe time, or simultaneously by adding a small beamforming MxM network. Possible values for M could be 3 or 5. To be noted also thatthecorresponding beams can be placed in the same azimuthal plane or not. This beamforming solution permits to reduce by a factor Mthe number of controls (phase shifters, direction couplers, amplifiers). As a consequence, a significant reduction in the cost and complexity of the entire instrument can be achieved. Reducing by a factor 3-5 the number of passive and active components in a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Instrument identification and requirements refinement. - Technology trade-off and down-selection. - Identification/optimization of most promising architectures. - Preliminary design of a baseline architecture and back-up architecture - Detailed design of a baseline architecture - Define preliminary manufacturing technique and prototype. - Definition of test and verification plan - Breadboard manufacturing and test - Results analysis and evaluation.

tenderTitle: STRUCTURAL ULTRA-COMPACT FLAT BATTERIES BASED ON HIGH SPECIFIC ENERGY MATERIALS EXPRO+
tenderDescription: To develop ultra-compact and structurally integrated flat batteries using materials with high specific energy.Description: Structural flat batteries that enhance spacecraft performance while reducing launch costs and system complexity show high potential in thepresent satellite market. This activity aims to develop ultra-compact, structurally integrated flat batteries using materials with high specific energy, for space applications with the intent of optimizing energy storage efficiency, while reducing weight and volume. The activity aims at exploring advanced materials, processes, and innovative designs to enhance performance and integration within spacecraft structures. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Literature review on Advanced Materials and structural batteries: Investigate and identify materials with high specific energy, that are/could be suitable for space applications. This includes studying their properties, performance, and compatibility with spacecraft structures and environment. - Innovative Design and Integration: Develop innovative designs that allow for integration of flat batteries within spacecraft structures. This involves optimizing the battery's shape, size, and placement to ensure efficient energy storage and minimal impact on the spacecraft's overall weight and volume. - Process Development: Explore advanced manufacturing processes to produce flat batteries. This includes techniques such as 3D printing, layering, and other methods that can enhance the battery's performance and integration. The capability of the supply chain shall be key to ensure industry competitiveness, by improving its affordability and industrialization and to reduce totaltime required to source materials, manufacture and deliver the battery. Furthermore, European independence in procurement and finalcosts should be taken into account. - Performance Enhancement: Conduct experiments and simulations to enhance the battery's performance. This should include testing the batteries under various conditions to ensure they meet the required standards for space applications. - Integration Testing: Perform integration tests to ensure the batteries work seamlessly within the spacecraft structures. This should include testing the batteries' compatibility with other systems and components.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. tenderTitle: SOFTWARE UPDATES SMS, MATERIAL AND LORENTZ - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: The ESA Antenna Laboratory operates several unique antenna and RF material measurement facilities, including the Sub-mmWave Scanner(SMS), LORENTZ cryogenic near-field scanner, and CATR Material Characterisation Facility. These facilities support antenna and RF characterisation activities covering a frequency range extending from microwave to sub-millimetre-wave frequencies and are routinely used in support of ESA programmes, technology developments, industrial activities and research campaigns.Operation ofthese facilities relies on dedicated custom-developed software that interfaces with motion control systems, network analysers and auxiliary equipment to perform automated measurements, collect measurement data and generate outputs suitable for post-processing andanalysis. Overthe past decade, this software has evolved through multiple development and maintenance activities, supporting successive laboratory upgrades and increasingly demanding measurement campaigns. The software currently comprises three principal application domains: SMS scanner control software. LORENTZ scanner control software. CATR Material Characterisation control software.In addition, a growing set of shared software components has been introduced to provide common functionality across facilities, including hardware abstraction, configuration management, measurement orchestration, data management and graphical user interfaces. Historically, software development activities were executed through a number of independent projects. Consequently, different facilities evolved at different rates and software versions diverged over time. Recent maintenance activities have established a common software management approach based on GitLab repositories, issue tracking mechanisms and shared software components, improving traceability and maintainability of the software assets. The LORENTZ and CATR applications now share a modern architecture built around common software libraries and hardware abstraction layers. The SMS software remains operational but is based on anearlier architecture and represents the principal remaining source of technical debt within the software suite. Long-term sustainability of the Antenna Laboratory software therefore requires continued maintenance, harmonisation and progressive migration towards acommon software framework.The software environment further depends on several third-party components, including software drivers and interfaces fromKeysight, ACS Motion Control, Trio Motion Technology and other equipment suppliers. Maintaining compatibility withcommercial operating systems, hardware drivers and measurement instruments is therefore an essential part of maintaining the operational capability of the Antenna Laboratory. As several ESA facilities depend on the availability, reliability and traceability of measurement data,particular attention must be given to configuration control, software version management, measurement file compatibility and preservation of laboratory know-how. The software shall therefore be maintained as an operational laboratory asset rather than as a standalone development project.- Objective(s) of the ActivityThe objective of the activity is to ensure the continuous operation, maintenance, evolution and long-term sustainability of the Antenna Laboratory software systems, while preserving compatibility with existing facilities, measurement workflows and historical measurement data.

tenderTitle: LISA-ITT-009 Battery
tenderDescription:
The gravitational wave observatory LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) has been selected as ESA’s third large class mission (L-3) within the Cosmic Vision programme. LISA’s mission objective is to observe gravitational waves from space in the frequency band of 0.1 mHz to 1 Hz, not accessible from ground-based observatories. 
The mission architecture consists of a constellation of three spacecraft placed at the vertexes of a near-equilateral triangle with side length of about 2.5 million km (LISA Constellation). An overview of the LISA mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/LISA
OHB, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the LISA programme, building the industrial consortium.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the LISA Battery.
The battery is part of the LISA Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS). The battery will be rechargeable Li-Ion type battery. This battery will supply the spacecraft with electrical energy when Solar Array power is not available or not sufficient, mainly during launch and transfer phases and during eclipse phases of the satellite. The satellite will be launched with a fully charged battery in order to be able to support the transfer and LEOP scenario until the solar array has been deployed.
The procurement of the Battery will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

An overview of the LISA mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/LISA
OHB, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the LISA programme, building the industrial consortium.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the LISA Battery.
The battery is part of the LISA Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS). The battery will be rechargeable Li-Ion type battery. This battery will supply the spacecraft with electrical energy when Solar Array power is not available or not sufficient, mainly during launch and transfer phases and during eclipse phases of the satellite. The satellite will be launched with a fully charged battery in order to be able to support the transfer and LEOP scenario until the solar array has been deployed.
The procurement of the Battery will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

tenderTitle: MINIATURIZATION OF NITROGEN-VACANCY CENTER-BASED MAGNETOMETERS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a space proven NV-Centred Diamond magnetometer with reduced SWaP. Description: Magnetic field measurements from low Earth orbit are important for understanding Earth's magnetosphere, monitoring of space weather, and studying geophysical processes. These measurements provide insights into solar-terrestrial interactions and help mitigate risks to both orbital infrastructure and terrestrial systems. NV -centres magnetometers are recent developments that have been successfully implemented on the ISS. Next to their scientific interest, one of their applications lays in using the magnetic field for AOCS purposes in space. Using a magnetic map, the full attitude of the spacecraft can be followed. This has been demonstrated during the first Ariane launch where one of these systems could follow the first minutes of the trajectory of the rocket. There is now the need to further develop such system to allow them to be utilized for navigation of spacecrafts or on other bodies (which have a magnetic field) with a specific focus on reduction of size and mass of the instrument to be integrated to AOCS system. The development shall be focused on miniaturisation and reduction of resources and on increasing the resolution of the magnetometers to pT. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of technical requirements given application in miniature quantum devices and preliminary design.- Detailed design of the magnetometer. - Manufacturing, integration and functional verification. - Test campaign, outcomes and development plan to qualification. Deliverables: Breadboard, Reports

tenderTitle: Automation of MultiSensor Turret (TMS) ( B11 )
tenderDescription:
CNES-CSG wants to digitalize its activities in order to :
•	Reduce reconfiguration delay in between two launches
•	Maintenance and Operation reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification

Description

CNES has optical facilities to follow the launchers after their lift off, for technical and media purposes.
They consist in visible and infrared video cameras, mounted on a turret, called TMS (Multisensor turret). CNES has several TMS.

Up to now, TMS are hand controlled by one or several operators who perform camera configuration and hand follow-up of the launchers

The aim of this activity is to modernize or replace these TMS in order to make them fully remote controlled:
-	Remote set-up
-	Auto-tracking of the launcher

These TMS will be design to endure French Guyana climatic conditions.
In option these TMS will made easily transportable.

Inputs will consist in a requirement specification or a technical specification
Deliveries will consist in one or several automatized TMS, operationally qualified.

tenderTitle: COST-COMPETITIVE SOLAR CELL DEVELOPMENT - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:To develop a cost-competitive solar cell either III-V-based or silicon-based for LEO satellite constellations.Description:The satellite industry is undergoing a major shift from traditional geostationary (GEO) platforms to large-scale lowEarth orbit (LEO) constellations. In this new landscape, solar cell requirements are increasingly driven by the needfor scalability, cost competitiveness, and radiation hardness tailored to the LEO environment. III-V multi-junctionsolar cells remain the benchmark for efficiency and space reliability, but their high cost and manufacturingcomplexity limit their suitability for mass production. In contrast, silicon-based solar cells, widely used in terrestrialsolar arrays, offer a more scalable and cost-efficient option, though they are not optimized for the spaceenvironment and typically have lower radiation resistance. Future development of III-V cells should focus onreducing complexity and cost. For silicon technologies, the priority is improving tolerance to radiation-induceddegradation, which is generally more severe than in III-V cells.Within this activity, it is foreseen to develop one solar cell technology that can support the LEO constellations inview of cost competitiveness and production capability. Technology options for this activity are either III-V-basedor silicon-based, with the following specific objectives: Option 1 - III-V-based technology development, to reduce production costs by up to 50% and doublemanufacturing throughput to meet large-scale deployment needs: there is substantial potential to reduce costsand increase manufacturing throughput by optimizing existing processes or implementing new ones. Potentialstrategies include increasing epitaxial growth rates, integrating terrestrial PV techniques (e.g., screen-printingfor contactmetallization), and replacing photolithography steps with more cost-effective alternatives.For this option, the activity encompasses the following tasks:o Develop an optimized manufacturing route for III-V solar cells, incorporating both improvements tocurrentprocesses and introduction of new techniques.o Fabricate solar cell samples using the newly developed manufacturing process.o Conduct an engineering test campaign to evaluate and validate the electrical and mechanicalperformance of the produced cells.This development stream complements developments performed in the following activity: T703-900EP - HighEfficient Cost-Effective Solar Cells. Option 2 - Silicon-based technology development, with the aim to achieve 21% efficiency at beginning-of-life(BOL) and 18% at end-of-life (EOL) and to improve reliability in the LEO space environment. The developmentactivity will focus on both design innovation and process optimization, aiming to enhance radiation toleranceand thermal cycling robustness while achieving the required beginning-of-life (BOL) and end-of-life (EOL)efficiency targets. For this option, the activity encompasses the following tasks:o Implement cell design optimizations already identified for existing silicon solar cell concepts toimprove radiation resistance to meet the 21% BOL and 18% EOL efficiency targets.o Investigate alternative metallization methods, anti-reflective coatings (ARCs), and interconnectiontechniques to improve thermal cycling robustness.o Explore compatibility of silicon structures with potential self-annealing properties to mitigate radiationinduceddegradation with industrial manufacturing framework.o Validate the final solar cell design through an engineering test campaign.This development stream complements developments performed in the following activity: Spin-indevelopment of terrestrial solar cell technology for constellation applications (ARTES AT 4F.175).

tenderTitle: QUANTUM-ENABLED PNT DEMONSTRATOR PHASES 0/A/B1
tenderDescription: This activity aims to prepare a future in-orbit demonstrator of novel Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) concepts based on quantum technologies. The study will investigate the integration of quantum inertial sensors, advanced timing techniques, including optical clocks, and hybrid navigation architectures combining quantum and classical sensors.Emphasis will be placed on system resilience, autonomy and GNSS-independent navigation including applications in Earth orbit and beyond. The activity will include system-level definition, performance assessment and critical pre-developments, including sensor fusion and onboard processing techniques.The objective is to mature concepts and associated key technologies up to TRL 5/6 and deliver a credible mission concept for a future PNT demonstrator.

tenderTitle: D-BAND TRANSCEIVER MODULE FOR 6G SATELLITE SYSTEMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5C.542) - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, build, test an integrated D-band transceiver module for high data rate satcom applications.TargetedImprovements: - Enabling D-band satellite links with higher than 10Gbit/sec- Increasing the transmission capacities by a factor of 4.- Smaller footprint and weight than Ka, V-band ISL or even optical ISL.- Less risk for interference as spectrum not completely allocated.- More resilient compared to Optical ISL (e.g. pointing misalignment or thermal effects).Description: The current state of satellite communication technologies, particularly in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations, relies on existing RF and microwave frequencies, which oftenstruggle to meet the growing demand for higher bandwidth and faster data rates. Withthe advent of 5G and the transition towards 6G, current systems face significantchallenges in scaling data throughput and maintaining efficient communication, especially beyond the atmosphere. This challenge is exacerbated by the limitations of traditionalfrequency bands and the complexity of integrating both passive and active elements within semiconductor-based antenna arrays.The introduction of sub-Terahertz frequencies, specifically in the D-Band range of 110 to 170 GHz, can offer a solution to these issues. These higher frequency bands providesignificantly larger bandwidths, allowing for faster data rates, lower power consumption, and smaller,more efficient hardware. However, fully utilizing the D-band spectrumrequires innovative concept to integrate both active components, such as amplifiers and receivers, and passive components, such as filters, with advanced semiconductor-basedantenna arrays.This project will address these challenges by developing two D-Band transceiver module engineering models, using the latest advancements in MMIC (Monolithic MicrowaveIntegrated Circuit) chipset technologies and packaging techniques, enabling future 6G NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) phased-array applications. It will focus on the integrationof both active (e.g. amplifiers, receivers) and passiveelements (e.g. filters) with semiconductor-based antenna arrays. This integration is crucial for power efficiency, reducingpower losses, and ensuring scalable solutions that can be applied across satellite constellations. In addition to addressing integration challenges, the proposed activity willexplore advanced multiplexing techniques, such as Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM), which can significantly increase communication capacity without requiring additionalfrequency bandwidth. This novel approach promises to optimize system performance and unlock greater scalability for satellite communication systems in the 6G era. Theproject will first focus onbreadboarding critical components like the high-power amplifier, receiver, filtering functions and antenna. Subsequently, two engineering modeltransceiver modules with critical functions will be manufactured and tested. A point-to-point link demonstrator will becreated for testing, ensuring that the system meets at leastone specific 6G use case such as Joint Communication and Sensing (JCAS), Multi-orbit Inter-satellite Link (ISL), or Extreme Capacity Backhaul (xHaul).

tenderTitle: ARGONAUT – S-Band Medium Gain Antenna Assembly  (S-MGAA)
tenderDescription:
OHB System AG, a subsidiary of the European space and technology group OHB SE, is acting as subcontractor to Thales Alenia Space (TAS-I) who has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) as prime Contractor for the realization of the ARGONAUT mission. Under its subcontract, OHB is responsible for the EPS, TT&C and GNC subsystems up to flight readiness.

tenderDescription: This activity is motivated by the need to advance the understanding of the global methane budget, with an Earth Observation (EO) led approach. Through the development of advanced scientific methods, aiming to exploit the recently launched Sentinel-5 mission onboard the Meteorological Operational Satellite - Second Generation satellite, as well as the complimentary instruments and missions that are currently in orbit, and preparing for those that will be launched in the coming years.This activity aims at advancing ongoing research into disentangling anthropogenic and biogenic methane emissions, through a Multi-Mission regional approach, and in particular to foster a set of novel developments that may result in ground-breaking scientific results and discoveries that will maximise the scientific impact of Sentinel 5, Sentinel-5P and other related missions in the field of methane retrievals.

tenderTitle: HIGH EFFICIENCY HPA WITH IMPROVED LINEARITY FOR HIGH FIDELITY RANGING SIGNALS EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
tenderDescription: Objective: To define and assess the feasibility of a digitally controlled, highly efficient and compact High-Power Amplifiers in L-band / C-band for PNT applications.Description: With the increased demand for navigation services, the number of signal componentstransmitted by a GNSS satellite has increased. Since constant envelope multiplexing schemes are not suitable (or inefficient) with ahigh number of signal components, modern GNSS systems generate signals with high PAPR (Peak to average Power Ratio). DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. The selected designs willbe demonstrated through the development and testing of elegant breadboards (EBB) This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of the operational scenarios and end-to-end user requirements associated. - Literature review, oriented at the latest developments in ET and polar transmitters in general, in analogue and in digital domain, as well as in broadband HPA solutions - Trade-off and down-selection of the most promising technologies based on the survey and preliminary high-level studies - Breadboards detailed design, and analysis and preparation of manufacturing plan and test plan - Breadboards manufacturing and test - Critical analysis of the results obtained and future roadmap.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). tenderTitle: M-IND - INDUSTRIALISATION OF MID-SIZE PLATFORMS  FOR  LEO CONSTELLATIONS (SAR  OPTICAL)
tenderDescription: Multiple studies on "Industrialisation of mid-size platforms for LEO constellations in Earth Observation". This activity is part of the "vertical axis" of the M-IND (Mid-size satellite INDustrialisation) initiative and it is intended for mid-size satellite integrators in order to support the scaling-up of the production of European mid-size satellite (100-500 kg) for Earth Observation applications with LEO constellations. It complements the "horizontal axis" of M-IND, where separate technology activities, mostly fundedunder GSTP, will support Equipment suppliers to modernise and industrialise Equipment for sub-systems in mid-size satellites.This activity will focus on the definition and establishment of credible industrialisation roadmaps covering production ramp-up of full mid-size satellites for Earth Observation, including supply chain strategies covering interchangeability and interoperability of sub-system from multiple suppliers, modular platform architectures including modernisation of capabilities like for example low latency communication via Intersatellite Links (ISL), suitability for several types of Earth Observation payloads, and sustainability aspectsfor zero debris mitigation at end of mission life and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The envisaged solutions and roadmaps shall enable cost-efficient, resilient and high-rate manufacturing aligned with future institutional and commercial mission needs in the EarthObservation domain.

It complements the "horizontal axis" of M-IND, where separate technology activities, mostly fundedunder GSTP, will support Equipment suppliers to modernise and industrialise Equipment for sub-systems in mid-size satellites.This activity will focus on the definition and establishment of credible industrialisation roadmaps covering production ramp-up of full mid-size satellites for Earth Observation, including supply chain strategies covering interchangeability and interoperability of sub-system from multiple suppliers, modular platform architectures including modernisation of capabilities like for example low latency communication via Intersatellite Links (ISL), suitability for several types of Earth Observation payloads, and sustainability aspectsfor zero debris mitigation at end of mission life and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The envisaged solutions and roadmaps shall enable cost-efficient, resilient and high-rate manufacturing aligned with future institutional and commercial mission needs in the EarthObservation domain.

tenderTitle: ON-BOARD 5G SPACE USER EQUIPMENT FOR LEO SATELLITES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5A.092) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop, and demonstrate an on-board 5G space User Equipment (UE) for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites.Targeted Improvements:Provide a standardised method - leveraging 5G NTN developments - for broadband connectivity via data relay to LEO satellites.Description: The future 5G New Radio Non-Terrestrial Networks (5G NR NTN) will offer continuous and ubiquitous coverage targeting terrestrial user equipment.Through the New Space paradigm, a new group of users emerges in the form of LEO satellites such as CubeSats.The future 5G NTN networks (LEO/MEO/GEO) can be leveraged to provide standardised broadband connectivity services also to these space users for LEO. tenderTitle: IMPLEMENTATION AND ENGINEERING MODEL TESTING OF IP BLOCKS FOR IMAGE SENSOR OUTPUTS FASTER THAN 1 GBIT/S
tenderDescription: Objectives:To have a fully European IP block to be used by European Image Sensor designers heavily dependent onnon-European sources. The objective of this activity is to design and validate high throughput serial outputsfor image sensors for dual use applications.Description:The future of infrared and visible sensors (larger formats, smaller pixels, fast frame rates) is tightly linkedtothe ability to read them out fast, but European detector manufacturers have not yet developed thecapability to adopt newer and faster communication protocols.In applications like Earth Observation, there is trend in image sensors towards more pixels and faster framerates, with analogue to digital conversion performed on chip. Transfer of information from the detector diecan become challenging using parallelized transfer standards, either limiting the frame rate or increasingthe complexity of the electrical interface.JESD204 interface standard is an ideal solution, offering a higherspeedserial interface with reduced pin-counts compared to the options currently used.In this activity, a JESD204-enabling circuitry for the Read-Out Integrated Circuits (ROICs) of image sensorsshall be implemented in the selected technology node and verified to be used in future detector designs.The IP blocks shall be radiation hard and compatible with a European foundry. The design shall bedemonstrated and verified, with the IP blocks becoming available for the European detector designcommunity.Parallel developments targeting most relevant technologies for infrared CMOS ROICs manufactured inEurope shall be implemented. It is anticipated that this leap-forward in interface speed and simplicity shallbe adopted by all European detector manufacturers using the relevant technology nodes and so shallbecome the dominant output interface in European space missions using digital output infrared sensors.This activity shall encompass the following tasks:- Study the latest JESD204 standard and future needs of the detector market in line with the developmentschedule of this activity- Derivation of requirements, IP Blocks architecture and identification of configurable parameters- Design of the IP blocks including test circuitry- Manufacture engineering model devices- Design and manufacture of the EGSE to assess the devices- Electrical and radiation test andcharacterization of the devices- Debugging and realization of the prototype- Support detector companies to implement and interface with the IP block.

tenderTitle: T811-900GS OPTIMIZATION OF LASER INTENSITY ON SPACE DEBRIS VIA COHERENT BEAM COMBINATION (EXPRO+)
tenderDescription: Recently, strategies have been explored to perturb space debris orbits using high-power ground-based lasersystems. This method, known as laser momentum transfer, can also be used for deep-space opticalcommunications. Multi-beam architectures have been designed and implemented to obtain the required powerlevels that would be unachievable with a single laser source or that would be limited by atmospheric turbulenceeffects. In a recent study on laser momentum transfer, 40 kW-class lasers based on multiple beams have beenproposed to alter the orbits of space debris and prevent collisions with active satellites.One challenge is delivering the generated power to the selected target while minimizing losses caused by laserpropagation and ensuring efficient momentum transfer for collision avoidance manoeuvres. Adaptive opticssystems have been considered but there are still several challenges due to the limited maturity of thistechnology. For example, retrieving tip-tilt information to compensate for atmospheric turbulence still dependson sunlight reflected from debris, which is a limiting factor in operational terms. Additionally, today's deformablemirror technology is not mature enough for the power levels needed for this application. While research is stillongoing, Coherent Beam Combining (CBC) techniques could offer a valid alternative to mitigate atmosphericeffects. This approach has the potential to correct the negative impact of atmospheric turbulence in systemsinvolving multiple beams.This activity aims at investigating CBC techniques to concentrate the highest possible intensity on the target,dynamically adjusting the phase of each beam, and achieving an optimal relationship between the phases ofthe multiple beams.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators. tenderTitle: NON-BODY SOLID WASTE COMPACTION AND INHIBITION
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a breadboard demonstrating single-step waste inhibition and compaction and characterize cross-linked biodegradable materials compatible for this process.Description: Re-supply and waste management are critical components of crewed space exploration. The current waste management approach exposes the crew to (bio)safety risks during the temporary storage period and is unpractical in longer space missions. Generic waste compaction/inhibition technologies of mixed waste materials in space have been generally studied. However, despite promising results on the volume reduction performance, the physical characteristics of the product obtained allow for limited transformation of re-usable resources. To address this, the activity aims to develop a breadboard demonstrating single-step waste inhibition and compaction and characterize cross-linked biodegradable materials compatible for this process. Lastly, there is a benefit in defining new packaging materials, which are biodegradable in the conditions of identified recycling systems and withstand the proposed compaction and inhibition process. The activity includes the following tasks: - Review single-step waste inhibition/compaction methods compatible with resource recovery (e.g. water) and developed biodegradable materials - Trade-off and selection of integrated waste inhibition and compaction processes and compliant packaging/padding materials. - Design and assembly of a breadboard system for single-step waste inhibition and compaction - Test to validate selected single-step waste inhibition and compaction technological modifications and biodegradability of treated packaging material - Developed cross-linking agents to enhance the barrier properties of biodegradable packaging materials, while maintaining biodegradability and process compatibility - Test to validate biodegradability and intended use of developed packaging. - Define a roadmap for technology maturation for integration into an operational system.Deliverables: Breadboard, Report

tenderTitle: S3-SW-14 SPACE WEATHER CENTRE FOR SPAIN INITIAL ESTABLISHMENT AND CORE CAPABILITY DEVELOPMENTS: PART 1
tenderDescription: Space Weather Centre for Spain Initial Establishment and Core Capability Developments: Part 1This activity will constitute the initial establishment and operation of a Space Weather Centre for affected stakeholders along with underpinning tools, capabilities and procedures required in order to deliver tailored high quality services to end users. Key user groups are expected to include operators of energy transmission systems, satellite operators, the aviation sector, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) and others. The Centre shall operate in close cooperation with ESA's Space weather Service Network with the aim to establish a node that facilitates collaborative actions with network participants while moving progressively towards a structure with a clear operational dimension ableto support the development and delivery of tailored space weather capabilities and services. Particularly the centre will focus on translating complex space weather information from multiple sources into streamlined, actionable information. A colocation of the development and operations teams shall be foreseen with the aim to streamline the R2O process, support team building and to encouragedirect feedback to research, optimising the use of facilities in ESAC.Part 1 shall include: Systematic mapping of end users and establishment of key contact points with users and stakeholders Establishment of a proactive engagement strategy and actions with the identified end users to ensure full understanding of end user needs and operational requirements Development of necessary IT infrastructure, tools and service operation procedures in order to operate the space weather front desk, initially on an 8/5 basis, with on-call support during periods of elevated space weather activity. OoProcedures shall be developed with a view to transitioning into full 24/7 support at the start of a future Part 2 of this activity. tenderTitle: COPERNICUS SPACE COMPONENT - COPERNICUS MISSION PLANNING SERVICE
tenderDescription: The objective of this activity is to ensure the continuation of the current Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 Mission Planning (MP) operations and maintenance for 31 months, up to mid-2029. The new Copernicus Mission Planning Service will cover the following activities: Sentinel-1 Mission Planning Function maintenance, Sentinel-2 Mission Planning Function maintenance, Station Resources Allocation (SRA) maintenance and operations, routine Mission Planning operations (including Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellites observation and downlink planning, planning of operational acquisition resources including X-Band services, planning of Sentinel-1 Collaborative Stations, operations of interfaces with Flight Operations Segment), emergency planning operations including those in support to the Copernicus Emergency Service and to the International Charter Space and Major Disasters-Set-up, and maintenance and operations of an interface point (MPIP) providing access to MP-related information to authorized entities (e.g., S-3/S-5P/CO2M MP services, FOS, acquisition services, etc.). An optional extension will be included to gradually integrate the Mission Planning operations for the Copernicus Expansion Missions (CRISTAL, ROSE-L, LSTM, CIMR, and CHIME) in line with their respective launch dates. This activity is funded under EU Copernicus Programme and will be open exclusively to economic operators and organisations (including subcontractors) established in a European Union Member State or a State participating in the Copernicus Component of the European Union Space Programme. The Invitation to Tender (ITT) package (Cover Letter, Special Conditions of Tender, Draft Contract, Letter of Invitation, and requirements documentation including the Statement of Work) will be available on ESA Star Publication website (https://esastar-publication.sso.esa.int/), the ESA tendering website. Any Tenderer which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier must complete theonline questionnaire in esa-star: https://esastar-emr.sso.esa.int/. Further information on the registration process can be found onthe Doing Business with ESA portal: https://doing-business.sso.esa.int/. Please, note that esa-star allows two levels of entity registration: "Light" and "Valid Full". This allows new users wishing to do business with ESA to carry out their registration in two steps. While "Light" registration will grant access to all esa-star services up to and including proposal submission, the award of ESAcontracts requires "Valid Full" status. The issue of the Invitation to Tender is foreseen in Q2 2026. ESA intends to place one (1) contract as a result of this procurement.

tenderTitle: ADHA MASS-MEMORY MODULES AND UNIT INTEGRATION EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: Objective:To develop a complete ADHA solid-state mass-memory with compatible modules, usable either standalone orwith other ADHA-compatible hardware in ADHA units for Earth observation, exploration, science, andnavigation missions.Description:The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) is a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primesand data handling equipment suppliers. It includes the definition of an architecture for data handling unitsbased on standard module functions. A standard module procurementflow has been defined, as well as astandardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent developmentofinteroperable modules that can be connected in ADHA units.This activity aims to develop ADHA solid-state mass-memory (MM) modules, based on ADHA-compatiblehardware modules. The development will follow the standard requirements for the development of ADHAmodules.The mass-memory module design will be fully compliant to the ADHA generic specification for mass-memorymodules. The developmentwill include the development of the mass-memory software (including support forfile-based operations, and CFDP Class-1 and Class-2). The developed ADHA mass memory module willsupport high-speed data reception and transfers, featuring a scalable architecture to meet the demands offuture ESA missions in earth observation, science, exploration, and navigation, as well as commercialmissions. Utilizing state-of-the-art processing, memory storage and interconnect technologies, this new massmemoryshall offer superior integration, data storage volume and processing performance compared toprevious generations. These advancements will also enable the implementation of sophisticated functionssuch as artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms for on-board data processing.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Detailed module requirements analysis, based on the existing ADHA specification documents, including theADHA generic mass-memory module specification.- ADHA mass memory module architectural design and trade-off of key components.- Engineering model (EM) design, including electrical, mechanical, thermal, FPGA design and software.- Engineering model (EM) manufacturing and EGSE procurement.- Engineering model (EM) validation campaign, including integration in anADHA unit rack.- Data-handling and storage demonstration, including performance benchmarks.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

tenderTitle: ACTIVE ANTENNA FOR DIRECT SATELLITE-TO-DEVICE 5G/6G COMMUNICATIONS IN FREQUENCY RANGE 1 (FR 1) (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5B.253) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
tenderDescription: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test a demonstrator of a Tx and Rx active antenna based on tiles for direct satellite-to-device 5G/6G communications in FR1.Targeted Improvements:Increase the antenna apertures up to 400% with respect tothe platform size while being highly storable and assessing simplification of the beamforming implementation.Description: The direct connectivity between satellites and standard mobile terrestrial user equipment such as smartphones, represents an essential feature of future non-terrestrial networks.Due to the RF characteristics of handheld devices, high antenna gains, and therefore large antenna apertures, are required on board the satellite. However, increasing the size of the array often leads to high complexity dueto the increasing number of phase shifters and/or digital signal processing units.This activity will develop and test a demonstratorof a Tx and Rx active antenna based on tiles for direct satellite-to-device 5G/6G communications in the FR1 L/S-band frequency band. A narrowband beamforming concept will be developed that allows to increase the size of the array while minimising its complexitybydividing the array into subarrays of groups of elements. The array is thus divided into multiple tiles that are deployed in orbit thanks to the same dedicated mechanism. This method reduces the number of weights to steer the beam at group level, thereby minimising complexity. Additionally, this has the advantage to split the beam forming network into two levels: subarray and array level, which simplifies the implementation compared to the fully analogue or digital beamforming approaches. Recent advances in the areas oflightweight material and RF/digital IC in ESA Member States would also naturally support the concept.The activity will design, manufacture, and validate in a laboratory environment a phased array active antenna full -scale engineering model (approximately 4m diameter) based on tiles with a fixed size, operating in L-/S-Band (FR 1). The activity shall seek synergies with the ARTES deliverables aswell as with ongoing direct satellite-to-device antenna projects within ESA Member States that are already being built-up. The activity will be implemented with a phased approach. In Phase 1, the bidder shall demonstrate the technology's feasibility through analysis and testing on a two-tiles scaled-down breadboard (TRL 4). In Phase 2, a reduced scale engineering model (TRL 5), based on afour-tile subarray with a deployable mechanism, shall be manufactured and tested. In Phase 3, a full-scale engineering model (TRL 6), including the full deployable mechanism and the thermal concept, shall be manufactured and tested. Procurement Policy: Open Competitive Tender Type: C

tenderTitle: STRATEGIC ADVOCACY FACILITY
tenderDescription: The Strategic Advocacy Facility is a strategic Action Readiness instrument within ESA's Earth Action framework that enables the translation of EO innovation, science and applications into sustained operational uptake and impact, particularly within the impact finance ecosystem of International Financial Institutions, climate and environmental funds, and developing-country stakeholders. The Facility combines programme-level impact measurement and evidence generation, strategic partnership engagement, institutional advisorysupport, country-level uptake assessment, strategic intelligence, advocacy and communication within a single integrated framework. Building on the legacy and assets of the Global Development Assistance (GDA) programme, it establishes a common Theory of Change, monitoring and evaluation system, stakeholder engagement architecture and learning framework for Earth Action, while creating feedbackloops between implementation, partnerships, communication, programme governance and future RD investments. Through interconnected task setup, the Facility acts as a cross-cutting enabler that strengthens EO adoption, supports partner alignment, captures and communicates evidence of impact, and ensures that Earth Action activities can be scaled, mainstreamed and translated into long-term societal, environmental and development outcomes.

tenderTitle: 54 MBAUD SOFTWARE DEFINED DEMODULATOR ON LOW-END PROCESSOR OR GRAPHICS PROCESSING UNIT (ARTES AT 7B.090)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test a 54 Mbaud DVB-S2 and 5G NR demodulator on a low-end Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) or Central Processing Unit (CPU).Targeted Improvements: Enabling a 54 Mbaud software defined radio for low end platforms not existing today in ESA Member States.Description: Previous projects have demonstrated that carriers of equivalent bandwidth can be demodulated in software on x86 server-level CPUs. Also, by using high-performance GPUs and parallel processing, bandwidths of hundreds of MHz or even many GHz could be demodulated. To date, a low-cost GPU or CPU-based demodulation solution with typical consumer terminal performance have not been developed. Such technology would allow field-upgradable terminals that can enable the deployment of new waveforms without expensive hardware swaps in the middle of the life of the system.This activity will develop and test a software-based demodulator running in a consumer GPU as found in a games console or a PC graphics card or a low-end CPU (Intel Core i3 or equivalent), with a throughput equivalent to a TV receiver or a consumer satellite broadband terminal. Superior demodulation algorithms than those in common open-source Software Defined Radio (SDR) toolkits will be studied and further developed and implemented.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 shall implement and test a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on one of the hardware platforms described above. The DVB-S2/X demodulator software will be tested against a hardware modulator or dedicated test equipment in the relevant environment to ensure the baud rate is met and fully compliant with as a minimum theDVB-S2 specification. Phase 1 deliverable will be a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on a low-end CPU or GPU platform. Budget is up to 700 kEuro.- Phase 2 shall implement and test in the relevant environment 5G-NR waveform or other proprietary waveform development on the hardware platform delivered by Phase 1.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

Description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test a 54 Mbaud DVB-S2 and 5G NR demodulator on a low-end Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) or Central Processing Unit (CPU).Targeted Improvements: Enabling a 54 Mbaud software defined radio for low end platforms not existing today in ESA Member States.Description: Previous projects have demonstrated that carriers of equivalent bandwidth can be demodulated in software on x86 server-level CPUs. Also, by using high-performance GPUs and parallel processing, bandwidths of hundreds of MHz or even many GHz could be demodulated. To date, a low-cost GPU or CPU-based demodulation solution with typical consumer terminal performance have not been developed. Such technology would allow field-upgradable terminals that can enable the deployment of new waveforms without expensive hardware swaps in the middle of the life of the system.This activity will develop and test a software-based demodulator running in a consumer GPU as found in a games console or a PC graphics card or a low-end CPU (Intel Core i3 or equivalent), with a throughput equivalent to a TV receiver or a consumer satellite broadband terminal. Phase 1 deliverable will be a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on a low-end CPU or GPU platform. tenderTitle: RETURNABLE TESTBED FOR IN-ORBIT MANUFACTURING PROCESSES FOR LARGE STRUCTURES O TELECOM SATELLITES (ARTES AT 3E.027) - RE-ISSUE
tenderDescription: The objective of the activity is to develop and characterize an additive manufacturing process to enable in-orbit manufacturing of large structural parts for satcom applications (e.g. large reflector, large solar array, large radiator structure). An in-orbit test-bed will be designed, manufactured and operated. Test-samples and complex demonstrators will be produced in order to evaluate the developed end-to-end in-orbit manufacturing process.Targeted Improvements: Enabling large in-orbit manufactured satcom hardware (e.g. large reflector, large solar array, radiator structure) not possible today.Description: Recent studies have explored the possibility of making large structures in orbit for future satcom applications, revealing new opportunities for applications, services andmarkets.The use of in-orbit additive manufacturing could eliminate the constraints of the launch vehicle fairings and the complexity of the deployment mechanisms, which are currently required for large deployables (e.g. very large reflectors, radiators and booms) relative to the platform size. However, the effects of microgravity, thermal, vacuum, and radiation on the additive manufacturing process in space are not well known, especially when assessing the structural, thermophysical and thermoelastic properties of the fabricated parts.This activity will characterize, through the production of test samples, the space environmental effects on the additive manufacturing processes required for future in-orbit manufacturing of large structural parts for satcom applications. An onboard testbed, using well established additive manufacturing processes and space qualified materials, will bedeveloped, manufactured andvalidated. The testbed shall accommodate visual and in situ measurements of the manufacturing process (e.g. temperature, molecular/particulate contamination induced by the process, etc) as well as allowing for the retrieval of the produced specimens for post-analysis on Earth. The testbed will also be used to producecomplex demonstrators (e.g. reflectors, booms and radiators or representative parts thereof). All in-orbit produced parts will be returned to Earth for post-analysis.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach. The first phase of the activity will develop, manufacture and achieve flight readiness of the testbed. The testbed performance will be validated on ground with reference test samples being produced and characterised. Phase 1 output will comprise of:Flight ready in-orbit manufacturing testbed, characterised end-to-end manufacturing process and reference test samples. The second phase will launch and operate the test bed to investigate the end-to-end additive manufacturing process in the space environment. Phase 2 will produce test samples in-orbit for process and material characterisation that are collected and returned for on ground analysis and comparison.The test results will be fed into Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) models to optimise in-orbit manufacturing parameters and processes for the production ofthe complex demonstrators.

tenderTitle: SERVER IN SPACE MODULE FOR COMMUNICATION PAYLOADS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5A.098) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture, and test a Server in Space (SiS) module for regenerative processors in satellite communication systems, enablingefficienton-board data processing and offering advanced autonomy applications andemergency management services.TargetedImprovements: Enabling application layer processing on-board for Servers in Space to offer advanced autonomy applications and emergency management services.Description: It is expected that satellites will have a larger percentage of regenerative processing, which opens the door to application layer processing on-board of satellites. The mainchallenge to be addressed is the availability of a Server in Space (SiS) with application layer processing, with technical challenges to be addressed in terms of powerconsumption, radiation hardening of ground-based data centre technology, and maturity of application layersoftware for embedded devices. Additionally, aspects of modularityand scalability for larger space datacentres shall be considered. Recent advancements of cloud providers in embedded processors, as well as technical developments inefficient FPGAs and computational memories, allow to link this concept to 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial-Networks (NTN) and Direct-to-Device (D2D) connectivity, enabling thesatellite to act as a server in space. By integrating the application layer on the satellite, cloud services, currently only provided on ground, could be made available to users innatural disaster situations or with special requirements that cannot use the regular network, e.g. very stringent latency needs like Internet-of-Things (IoT) or autonomousdriving.This activity will design and develop a cloud computing module, integrate it with the regenerative processor, and test it to ensure its efficiency and reliability inthe relevantenvironment. Focus shall be on the interfaces between the payload and components in the module, including also technologies used on ground, due to the high data ratesrequired. A fully functional Server in Space (SiS) module engineering module, capable of efficient on-board data processing and data storage, shall be designed, developedand tested. The SiS module shall demonstrateits capability to be integrated in future satcom digital processors and to be scaled to large data centres in space.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. tenderTitle: UNLOCKING FPUTS AT SCALE THROUGH INTERFACE STANDARDISATION ( ARTES FP 1A.137) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: This activity will evaluate the technical and commercial feasibility of developing a standardised and interoperable set of Flat Panel User Terminal (UT) building blocks and internal interfaces, able to be reused in end user equipment designed for deployment across a broad range of market sectors and network types.The objective is to support the creation of a scalable, industrialised and costcompetitive ecosystem for flat panel user terminals in the ESA Member States by enabling economies of scale through open architectures and harmonised specifications.The activity will also identify standardised FPA terminal profiles (classes'), defining their RFperformance characteristics and associated validation and certification methodologies, to facilitate objective performance assessment and enable fair and interoperable competition among vendors.

tenderTitle: QUANTUM COMPUTING ALGORITHMS DEVELOPMENT FOR SPACE APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:To develop and assess quantum computing algorithms, methods and related tools for solving specific spacerelated computational challenges with higher performance and reliability than the state of the art achieved with the classical technologies.Description:Quantum computing technologies are progressing rapidly, with early-stage commercial and academicplatforms offering capabilities relevant to space applications. As one of the strategic sectors expected to benefit from quantum advantage, the space domain offers complex, high-impact challenges that can guide algorithm development and platform requirements. Lessons learned from these applications will be transferable to other sectors, enabling a broader quantum technology ecosystem. This activity aims to ensure European industry is quantum-ready and positioned to lead in the global race for space-enabled quantum technologies. It supports European strategic autonomy by fostering sovereign capabilities in quantum algorithm development, hybrid integration, and secure processing architectures tailored to ESA or national mission needs. The initiative also strengthens Europe's industrial competitiveness by enabling use-case-driven innovation and demonstrating technical leadership in both terrestrial and space environments. This activity aimsto encourage the usage of quantum computing potentials to address the challenges in space missions and technologies. It is expectedto extensively use the precision and fast calculations to solve in the most innovative ways challenges related to, mission planningbooks, AI integration, cryptography, and onboard processing, optimisation algorithm for power batteries, among others. Technology focus areas can include but are not limited to quantum-enhanced simulation for propulsion, materials, thermal, power, satellite station keeping, radiation and orbital dynamics, optimization of tools for mission planning, routing, scheduling, debris avoidance and predictive maintenance, quantum Machine Learning (QML) for Earth Observation, anomaly detection, and FDIR, design of quantumnativepre-measurement processing flows, leveraging intrinsic quantum dynamics to condition mission-criticaldata within the quantum domainpriorto readout or classical interface, digital twin powered by quantumcomputing.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Development and benchmarking of quantum algorithms tailored to space-relevant challengesconsidering gate-based, annealing or hybridquantum computing methods- Ground-based demonstrators for performance validation on quantum computers and/or classical high performance computers- Development of a software tool or product enabling the exploitation of the quantum algorithm for oneor more specific space related use cases- Analysis of the expected performance scaling with future generations of quantum computersThe tasks shall include clearly defined use cases and assess how quantum approachesincluding hybridmethods and error mitigation techniquesperformunder realistic computational loads and spaceenvironments, compared to classical baselines.Deliverables: Software, Report

tenderTitle: JOINT IMPLEMENTATION OF SAT-3 AND COGNITIVE CLOUD COMPUTING IN SPACE (EOCOGNITIVELAB)
tenderDescription: EOCognitiveLab brings together the evolution of the sat mission series and ESA's work on Cognitive Cloud Computing in Space for Earth Observation (3CS4EO). The activity is intended to demonstrate the added values unlocked by AI-enabled, cooperative Earth Observation capabilities across multiple heterogeneous?satellites?(including, event-based acquisition replanning, coordinated acquisitions), onboard processing and inter-satellite-link information exchange,?for selected end-to-end Earth Observation use cases, and to establish an in-orbit laboratory for autonomous, distributed and software-defined Earth Observation missions.? The mission will be based on a cooperative two-satellite space segment, equipped with onboard computing capabilities, supported by ground processing, and an exploitation platform enabling data distribution and community access. In addition, EOCognitiveLab will leverage open inter-satellite-link interfaces and be designed to support future expansion through the federation of additional Earth Observation missions.? As an in-orbit laboratory, EOCognitiveLab will provide an open and expandable environment for additional in-orbit experimentation forESA Members, Associated and Cooperating States EO community. Target experimentation areas include cooperative sensing, distributed processing, novel mission-orchestration approaches, onboard federated learning and fine-tuning, and other AI techniques relevant to distributed Earth Observation systems.? The proposed?activity will be implemented through a Mission Consolidation Phase followed, subject to a successful Gate Review, by a Mission Implementation Phase covering detailed design, development, integration, verification, launch, LEOP, commissioning and in-orbit verification up to the In-Orbit Commissioning Review.

tenderTitle: ESEC-2 FLIGHT OPERATIONS SERVICE CONTRACT
tenderDescription: The subject of this procurement proposal is the procurement of "Operations Engineering Services in support in ESEC/Redu" covering operational services for the preparation and execution of the mission operations entrusted to the Directorate of Operations located in ESEC, including the relevant Galileo Hosting Agreements. ESA/ESEC is the ESA European Space Security and Education Centre located in Belgium and is one of the ESA sites in Europe. The main core business in Mission Operations relevant to this procurement are: Control dedicated Satellites and Ground Segment (so called "Small Satellite missions") Perform its In-Orbit activities. Host and operate some ground segment elements in support to the EU Space Programme within a secured environment - mainly Galileo and EGNOS The Operational services, within the scope specified above, will be therefore divided in two main WPs: WP-1 Small Satellites Operations: A number of Small Satellites (such as the PROBA ones) are or will be controlled from ESEC with the help of a dedicated ground segment. In the current set-up and number of missions, up to six passes per satellite daily are supported in automatic mode for TM reception and commanding, which may be extended in the future when new missions will be operated from ESEC. The mission products are made available at ESEC and ready for distribution. The Small Satellites Mission Operations Centre is therefore responsible of the monitoring and control of the satellite and the corresponding ground segment, the handling of the user requests, the extraction of the mission products and their availability for distribution. The Small Satellites operations concept relies on a highly automatic functioning of the ground segment and a high degree of autonomy in the space segment for the delayed execution of operations requested by telecommand and for satellite survival. No operator attended shift work is foreseen. Operational engineers supervise the small satellites mission operations and related performances usually only during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The satellites are safe by design and can survive for a long period without ground station contact. This WP will cover OPSPREP and OPS activities, support to Industry, execution of delegated tasks for critical operations (LEOP, others) together and in collaboration with Industry for this small satellite missions. This WP may implement further mission operations engineering activities carried out in support of other ESA programmes requested by ESA programme directorates to OPS. WP-2 Galileo Hosting activities: The Galileo Hosting support will be provided in response to the requirements and agreements reached with EUSPA for Galileo and EGNOS. The provision of support to the hosting and testing activities will be performed on-site during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The Agency will issue one single Invitation to Tender in Open Competition for the two WPs. Considering the relatively small volume covered by this procurement, the Tenderers will be invited to provide a single proposal covering the support to both areas. The new contract is planned to be kicked-off starting in 1st Quarter 2027 (phase-in) as required to permit sufficient time for a smooth transition (e.g. training, certification of new service provider's personnel). The operational phase of the contract is expected to start latest by 2nd Quarter 2027, at the expiry of the current INDUSTRIAL SERVICE PROVISION IN SUPPORT OF THE OPERATION OF ESA IN BELGIUM contract extension.

tenderTitle: MODULAR FRAMEWORK FOR ENHANCED PERCEPTION AND DECISION-MAKING - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a software module based on visual agents to integrate and combine visual inputsprocessing and decision-making capabilities.Description:The use of artificial intelligence for computer vision tasks has been extensively explored and applied over the lastdecade, resulting in a myriad of industrial applications. However, these approaches have predominantly relied on traditional CNN-based systems, which are often rigid, task-specific, and lack decision-making capabilities. Recent advancements, such as multimodal large language models, visual transformers, and agentic workflows, have demonstrated the potential for more flexible and adaptable solutions, that can also combine both visual input processing and decision making. This activity aims to develop a software module that will:- Define and implement a software layer (execution layer) to support the inference of visual agents and enable easy integration of new agents.- Design and implement an agentic workflow to execute various computer vision tasks (i.e.: object localization,image segmentation) on top of the defined execution layer.- Integrate decision-making capabilities into the agent implementation, leveraging the output of the vision tasks.For instance, planning and scheduling tasks or specific instruction to be executed, considering the output ofthe computer vison task processed by the agent.- Identify and deploy the solution on space-representative hardware.The software solution will integrate visual perception with decision-making capabilities that surpasses currentfunctionalities provided by traditional convolutional neural network (CNN). Unlike traditional CNNs, the agentic software developed in this activity will utilize multimodal inputs that may include various types of sensors outputs,(e.g. optical, radar, time series, astextual instructions), enabling agents to perform diverse tasks. The softwaredeveloped in this activity can impact multiple application domains, like Earth Observation missions. Additionally,the solution will enable onboard capabilities to be presented as functions or services that can be adapted based on evolving ground requirements. Therefore, at the system level (flight-ground), this solution will influence current interaction paradigms, allowing the ground segment to define new goals for a satellite dynamically. This is a key technology for the Space Domain Awareness (SDA) and for tracking activities on Earth, supporting disasters monitoring, civil protection, border control, and security applications.The activity shall encompass the following tasks:- Review and analyse traditional AI algorithms applied to computer vision tasks in space and identify new trendsusing multimodal transformers, visual transformers, and agentic workflows.- Identify use cases where the visual agent framework will be applied. At least two different use cases shall beproposed to demonstrate the framework's flexibility to adapt to different situations and covering both the visualtaskand reasoning task to be implemented by agents.- Design and develop the visual agent framework, including the final selection of onboard space hardware and the design specifications necessary for deploying the algorithm on it.- Integrate the framework into the different use cases and deploy it onto the selected hardware.- Verify and validate the framework, including performance assessment to evaluate the framework's efficiency, adaptability, and robustness compared with traditional algorithms.

tenderTitle: GSTP ELEMENT 1: DEVELOP: PREPARATION OF ENABLING SPACE TECHNOLOGIES AND BUILDING BLOCKS - STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSAL
tenderDescription: The European Space Agency ("the Agency" or "ESA") invites you to submit a Proposal under the General Support Technology Programme, Element 1: "Preparation of enabling space technologies and building blocks''The aim is to prepare and to develop enabling capabilities and the associated building blocks for space related systems and the associated sub-systems. An additional aim is to allow the targeted and coordinated development of the capabilities and building blocks (i.e. among academia and industry) in a given ESA Member State or across different Member States (in a collaborative manner). The intended output is to provide industry with a stronger foundation (i.e. building on this acquired know-how) in order to contribute to new space related system opportunities at national or international levels (institutional, commercial...) The objective is to enable Member States to support the further development of t capabilities and the associated building blocks in their industry. The technology development activities may be prepared in a targeted and coordinated manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed for a targeted type and class of space systems (in terms of performance, cost, size...) and with guiding specifications. The developments are to be performed in a coordinated manner to ensure that industry is able to work on complementary capabilities. The developments may be performed within one Member State or across several Member States in a collaborative manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed to a level such that the industrial entities may then be able to perform developments and eventually produce for concrete/more specific space related developments. The developments may go from a proof-of-concept (via simulation or experiment) up to an engineering qualification model (EQM). They address any technical area (structures, avionics/GNC, power control and distribution...). The spefications are to be linked to the guiding system or sub-system specifications. The maximum amount per activity is 1,000 K. The maximum duration is 24 months.
