tenderTitle: S2P S2-VS-06 VISDOMS-S PHASE A/B1
tenderDescription: The procurement covers the VISDOMS-S Mission Phase A/B1. Based on the previous Space Based Optical Monitoring (SBOM) feasibility study, a mission concept using a small satellite and existing imager shall be further elaborated in a short Phase A. Suitable small platform candidates shall be further investigated in terms of its capacity and compliance towards the observational needs, the deorbiting requirements, and its capability to host the identified optical imager. The preliminary technical, engineering and quality assurance requirements for the Delta-Class mission shall be reviewed, agreed and consolidated as part of the Preliminary Requirements Review. The development approach shall be further elaborated with the objective to enable the establishment of the implementation and procurement plan. System optimisations based on previous flight experience that may lead to an improvement of the mission performance and its robustness by enhancing the existing equipment and optical imager may be considered for further elaboration during Phase B1.The Phase B1 industrial system study shall produce a preliminary design of the space and ground segment that shall include all elements for the mission definition, the spacecraft and the optical imager and the ground segment. The satellite design shall be matured, and a detailed accommodation study of the optical imager shall be performed. The design of the optical imager and potential modifications that may be required shall be addressed including the detector selection, readout electronics and the control and data processing unit. The technical requirements specifications of all major units shall be established, and the system requirements shall be consolidated and verified as far as possible by analysis. The study shall produce the necessary documentation for the System Requirements Review and confirm that the review objectives are achieved.

tenderTitle: NAVISP EL1-134  ALL-WEATHER LASER COMMUNICATION LINKS FOR OPTICAL PNT SYSTEMS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: EL1-134 - This activity will investigate innovative techniques to enable continuous optical timing and ranging links under all weather conditions, addressing a key challenge for operational optical PNT (Positioning, Navigation, and Timing) systems. Optical satellite-to-ground links, such as those planned for ESA's OpSTAR mission, are vulnerable to atmospheric effects, particularly cloud cover, which can degrade or completely interrupt communications with an Optical Ground Station (OGS). The study will assess and experimentally demonstrate atmospheric transmission enhancement techniques designed to improve link availability under adverse weather conditions. It will evaluate whether these approaches can maintain accurate and reliable timing and ranging measurements between laser terminals representative of future operational optical PNT systems.

tenderTitle: MODULAR ROBUST WAVEFORM FOR END-TO-END COMMUNICATIONS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a proof-of-concept of a modular robust waveform for E2E communications that offers further protection for the missions, in a modular approach in accordance with the mission security needs.Description:Intentional RF interference is a threat to space missions, as it can disrupt the radio links between satellite and ground/users. There are waveform techniques that can counter or mitigate the impact of that interference but they need to be designed specifically against reference threats. This activity is aimed at developing a modular robust waveform for end-to-end (E2E) communications offering further protection for the missions, by designing the waveform aspects as well as the receiver operations. It will consider typical RF threats and tune the waveform against the most common ones, so that space missions do not have to develop new solutions for their case. The design of the modular robust waveform can include cryptographically robust spread sequences that can be used to drive a frequency hopping scheme, or a direct Sequence spread spectrum modulation, coupled with Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM). The adaptation algorithm of the ACM can cover both the typical Modulation and Coding schemes as well as the Transmission Security (TRANSEC) functions (e.g. Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum and Frequency Hopping), providing flexible level of protection based on the link conditions. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of the most common RF interference signals and attacks method - Investigation of state of theart signal techniques to counter RF interference and development of a SWAT analysis to select the optimum measures for the consolidated attacks options. - Detailed design of the waveform blocks to counter the identified common RF interference threats. Particular emphasis shall be devoted to the Add-on modularity so that each block can be added as plug-in. - Development of a Proof of Concept simulator including signal generator/receiver of the waveform and assessment of the E2E performance of the proposed Waveform. - Investigation of the regulatory constraints from the Radio Frequency Compatibility with specific focus on the impact of wideband signals on ITU frequency bands allocation. The software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Report, Software

tenderDescription: The overall goal of ARTES 4.0 Business Applications can be summarised as the development of pre-operational services - possibly in partnership - for a wide range of users through the combination of different systems. Business Applications activities aim at: i) collecting user feedback for better tuning of the applications and the operation of all elements involved, ii) developing commercial sustainable space based applications by linking user needs to corresponding solutions incorporating space assets requesting only limited technology adaptations, iii) demonstrating to users and stakeholders that the proposed solutions work in their operational environment and are compatible with their operational practices, iv) utilising at least one space asset (such as Satellite Communications, Earth Observation, Satellite Navigation, Human Spaceflight, or any other space asset, service or technology), leading to a better exploitation of existing space capacity and know-how together with a better understanding of how they should evolve to respond to user needs. ARTES 4.0 Business Applications operates via a 'Call for Proposals' which is always open. Partners respond with proposals as they find it opportune. The activities proposed in response to this 'Call for Proposals' must be relevant to above mentioned ARTES 4.0 Business Applications objectives. Although not a competitive tender action, this Call for Proposals' is published on esa-star Publication in order to achieve a higher degree of visibility. The closing date that is mentioned upon issue of the Call for Proposals is established solely for technical reasons connected with the esa-star Publication system and can be disregarded.

tenderTitle: STEPPING STONE MISSION DEFINITION STUDY
tenderDescription: Stepping Stone Missions are a new class of user driven Earth Observation missions designed to address gaps in the current EO ecosystem by delivering quality certified data and services tailored to environmental policy needs at European and global level. They build on and complement existing reference missions and infrastructures, while targeting observation domains and sampling requirements not adequately covered today. A key characteristic is their service oriented and commercially minded nature: missions are conceived from the outset to enable operational services, foster downstream applications, and evolve into scalable, privately operated constellations once their performance and utility have been demonstrated in orbit. The Stepping Stones activity focuses on conducting mission definition studies that mature candidate concepts up to a consolidated system baseline. This includes the parallel development of the space and ground segments, the definition of user oriented services, and the establishment of a robust business case demonstrating long term viability. The studies also encompass assessment of technical feasibility, verification and validation approaches, and readiness with respect to user needs, policy alignment, and commercial exploitation. Overall, the objective is to de risk and validate the end to end concepttechnical, service, and marketup to System Requirements Review level.

tenderTitle: EnVision – Radiator Panel
tenderDescription:
EnVision is a Venus orbiter mission selected by ESA’s Science Programme Committee as the fifth Medium-class mission in the Agency’s Cosmic Vision plan. It will be the first mission to investigate Venus from its inner core to its upper atmosphere, characterising the interaction between its atmosphere, surface/subsurface and interior. It aims at providing a holistic view of Venus, studying the planet’s history, activity, and climate. EnVision is an ESA-led mission in partnership with NASA who are providing the VenSAR instrument, Deep Space Network support for critical mission phases and Aerobraking support.
ESA is responsible for the mission, including procurement of the spacecraft and the launch vehicle together with the development of the ground segment (both to control the spacecraft, and for scientific purposes). As with most Science missions, the instruments are provided by Member States and International Partners contributions, with ESA providing several specific payload elements: the SRS dipole antenna; the MRO; the VenSpec-U detectors; the VenSpec-H detector and cooler assembly.
An overview of the EnVision mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/EnVision_factsheet.
Thales Alenia Space Italy, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the EnVision Satellite, building an industrial consortium in which OHB System AG, a subsidiary of the European space and technology group OHB SE, is responsible for the MTP-Bus.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the Subcontractor for the EnVision Radiator Panels.
Led by OHB System AG, the Contractor is responsible for the manufacturing of the fully equipped Radiator Panels for the EnVision Spacecraft. Within the Contractor’s responsibility is the application of the thermal hardware (heat pipes, OSRs, etc.), according to the specifications provided by OHB.
The procurement of the Radiator Panels will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).

tenderTitle: NAVISP EL1-132 DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF FLEXIBLE ELORAN/GNSS SIGNAL SIMULATOR- EXPRO+
tenderDescription: The increasing dependence on GNSS for positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services has highlighted vulnerabilities to jamming,spoofing, interference and space-weather effects. eLORAN is emerging as a resilient terrestrial complement to GNSS, but its adoptionrequires advanced tools capable of realistically testing and validating hybrid GNSS/eLORAN solutions. This activity will develop and validate a flexible, modular and future-proof eLORAN/GNSS signal simulator, synchronised with commercial GNSS simulators and supported by dedicated Receiver Analysis and Validation Tools. The simulator will provide high-fidelity signal generation, propagation modelling, multi-chain and multi-time-reference capabilities, and record-and-replay functions, enabling realistic end-to-end validation of resilient PNT solutions across timing, maritime and other application domains.

tenderTitle: IN-ORBIT RECONFIGURABLE SOLAR ARRAY - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To design a solar array concept allowing for in-orbit reconfiguration of strings length and section size and to optimisethe solar array power output for EOL best possible performance.Description: Solar cell voltage and current are a function of operating temperature and degradation level. String lengths and section sizes are optimised for EOL best performance. However, this means that for most of the time the solar array is not exploiting its full performance capability. If string lengths and section sizes were reconfigurable, the power output at each time of the mission could be maximised. This concept could provide various benefits, such as flexible adaptation in case of unforeseen events (e.g. solar flares, micrometeorite impacts, etc.), mission extension in GEO and potential use of cells with less performance in GEO radiation environment. These benefits can be of interest for Telecom applications, where very large solar arrays are typically required to compensate for the degradation over the entire mission. This activity targets innovative photovoltaic assembly concepts that allows for reconfiguring string lengths and section size to optimise performance in dependence of operating conditions during the mission (e.g. temperature, irradiation level). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of a solar array / photovoltaic assembly concept allowing for reconfiguration of string lengths and section sizes. - Prototyping of interconnection concepts. - Initial proof of concept demonstration.

tenderTitle: MATERIALS FOR SUSTAINABLE ATMOSPHERIC RE-ENTRY - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:To characterise spacecraft materials that minimise atmospheric impacts during re-entry.Description:ESA's Green Agendaand Ecodesign Policy require that the environmental impacts of all space missions andprogrammes are assessed and reduced across their full life cycle. Launch and spacecraft re-entry effects onthe atmosphere are known gaps to fulfil these requirements. This results in significant uncertainty andsystematic exclusion of such effects when developing materials on the basis of sustainable performance.Previous and ongoing Discovery activities, Insights into the Chemistry of Atmospheric Re-entry of JunkedSpacecraft (ICARUS) and Impacts of space Debris ablation on Earth's Atmospheric System (IDEAS), havehighlighted the potential importance of ablation products in the atmosphere while established initial modellingapproaches and experimental validation capabilities.The proposed activity addresses this critical knowledge gap by developing a consolidated experimental andmodelling framework to characterise emissionsfrom spacecraft re-entry and integrate these into atmosphericand design assessment tools. This will enable the incorporation of atmospheric impacts into Life CycleAssessment (LCA) and support both Ecodesign and Design-for-Demise (D4D) decision making. Such aframework would be the first worldwide.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identify representative launcher and spacecraftdemise-critical materials as well as Space Debris Particles(SPSs)- Propose material characterization factors (e.g. Ozon Depletionmetrics, radiative forcing proxies) andassociated quantification methodology- Refine methods to allow observation and characterization of particles generated during the vaporizationphase of selected materials- Demonstrate validation tests under realistic atmospheric re-entry conditions (e.g. Thermal, pressure andflow conditions) measuring and linking ablation fluxes to downstream chemical compositions- Parametrization and modelling of datasets for integration into re-entry and atmospheric chemistryclimatemodels-Define uncertainty and applicability ranges for model use- Formulate recommendations for standardised testing procedures to support the continuous developmentand population of material datasets.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SME RD organisations, preferably in cooperation. tenderTitle: LOW-IMPACT VELOCITY TOOLS FOR VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION OF CLOSE PROXIMITY OPERATIONS STRATEGIES EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a comprehensive set of rigorously tested tools that ensures monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance for close proximity operations.Description: Past activities related to Close Proximity Operations (CPO) highlighted the need ofdeveloping low impact velocity tools that can verify and validate that the servicer spacecraft (SC) maintains a collision risk probability of less than given threshold (e.g 10^-4) with the client SC during CPO. For missions involving multiple SC in close formation, the design of manoeuvres to avoid collisions with catalogue objects not belonging to the formation requires to take into account all SC of the formation, e.g. an avoidance manoeuvre performed by one SC of the formation shall not trigger an inner-formation collision risk but rather minimise disturbance to the formation while ensuring the required risk reduction. This activity aims at developing a comprehensive set of tools (e.g. DRAMA like tool, prototype software for formation flying) that ensure monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance during close proximity operations (including formation flying). This activity encompasses the followingtasks: - Develop and refine software tools that model the trajectory of both the target and servicer. - Develop algorithms that identify safe trajectories for close approaches and include collision avoidance features. - Develop tools that perform uncertainty propagation to estimate the likelihood of a collision between the servicer and client. - Identify sensor systems capable of providing design and operational level data about the relative positions, velocities, and orientations of both the servicer and the target. - Conduct virtual testing within the developed tools to simulate close approach and rendezvous operations in various scenarios. - Develop mathematical models of constraints and requirements and prototype a software solution suitable for realistic scenarios.

tenderTitle: ERS-EO PROOF OF CONCEPT TO SUPPORT ENHANCED PROTECTION OF CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE
tenderDescription: ERS-EO Proof of Concept on Critical Infrastructure ManagementThe ERS-EO Element 1 Critical Infrastructure Monitoring Prof of Concept is intended to demonstrate the step improvement for enhanced monitoring and management of critical infrastructure resulting from the effective combination of diverse EO and non-EO capabilities representative of the future Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) capacity. In particular, the customization and fusion of these capabilities will generate significant improvements in tasking response, persistent data collection, information delivery latency, expanded information content andflexibility and adaptability in response to dynamic situations. In this context, the Critical Infrastructure Monitoring PoC will:Stimulate innovative combinations of public and private EO systems to support improved and more flexible tasking, response latency, persistence and cross-operator cueing;Develop customized workflows connecting satellite operators, non-EO data providers, analytics tool developers and critical infrastructure operators to ensure enhanced capability to detect, characterize, respond to and mitigateemergent threats and anomalies;Verify the improvements achievable over current state of the art with respect to emerging threat detection and mitigation action execution for critical infrastructure operators under realistic operating conditions;With respect to gaps in current capabilities, elaborate technical approaches for their resolution, verify their impact under representative operational environments and conditionsand elaborate a road map for eventual transfer to full operations based on exclusively European technology. The contract will integrate existing EO and non-EO capabilities as well as capabilities at an advanced stage of development into a pre-operational network providing a range of analysis support information. The procurement will be structured into three periods as follows:Step[BJ1] 1:requirements consolidation and initial operating capability specification, implementation and testing.Step 2 initial capability demonstrations under realistic operating conditions covering extended routine threat mitigation, timely detection, characterization and response elaboration for emerging threats and anomaly/event response situationsStep 3: extended capability demonstration under fully representative conditions as agreed in the milestone review concluding Step 2 activities All underlying Information and Communication Technology (ICT) functions will be provided by the ERS-EO Element 1 Testbed.

tenderTitle: DEVELOPMENT OF AN ELECTRO-DYNAMIC SHIELD SYSTEM FOR PLANETARY MISSIONS EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop an Electro-Dynamic-Shield system to mitigate systems degradation for missions to the Moon, Mars and planetarybodies including a significant dusty environment.Description: Exploration systems in contact with planetary surfaces covered in regolith such as the Moon and Mars are subject to local dust displacement and accumulation on critical surfaces affecting system performance as for instance thermal balance, power generation efficiency and optical transmission and system lifetime. A number of mitigation strategies have been put forward and tested mostly on ground with a very limited demonstration in space. The Electro-Dynamic Shield (EDS) technology is a method used to mitigate the accumulation of dust on surfaces, particularly in space environments. This technology employs electric fields to repel dust particles, preventing them from settling on critical surfaces such as solar panels, sensors, and other equipment. This technology has been studied for more than twenty years outside of Europe for the mitigation of dust deposition on terrestrial and space system and it has been recently demonstrated on the Moon. In Europe, most of the studies performed so far have been on laboratory scale. Among others, an experimental EDS was successfully implemented on a number of samples including optical glass and Kapton sheets and demonstrated very high dust removal efficiency in a vacuum environment including UV, showing good potential for targeted system feasibility studies. Based on this success, the feasibility of implementing such technology on actual space hardware by breadboarding and testing critical functionalities can be addressed. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define the requirements for the implementation of an EDS system into relevant spacecraft structures and materials of interest with a priority towards solar arrays (with possible applicability to optical surface and other materials) and define the requirements from the target system towards EDS. - Assess the required modifications of standard designs to accommodate an EDS system, establish a list of technological gaps, define specific tests and a test plan to address the technological gaps. - Design and manufacture relevant breadboards to demonstrate EDS operational efficiency on targeted system. - Perform test for critical functionalities,including in representative laboratory environments (dusty vacuum and in presence of UV). - Based on the tests outcomes and future missions needs provide a technical roadmap with a cost outline.

tenderTitle: INCUBED CALL FOR PROPOSAL: STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS
tenderDescription: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims to accompany European economic operators in the rapid evolution of the Earth Observation market, both in Europe and globally. InCubed introduces a dedicated process within ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the development of near-to-market commercial initiatives in partnership with industry. Activities supported under InCubed include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (e.g. missions, instruments, prototype elements of EO constellations), innovative mission management solutions (including for future EO constellations), as well as the development of ground, data, and application platforms. InCubed targets commercial viability by the end of the activity (at least at minimum viable product level) and requires a substantial degree of innovation, i.e. the creation of new value within the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement is mandatory, with customers acting as beta testers and validators of the developed product or service. Customer engagement must be clearly demonstrated at both pitch and proposal stages, and letters of support or interest from potential customers are considered a strong asset. The scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves, in line with the objectives of InCubed. Two development cycles are available within InCubed, depending on the maturity of the concept: De-risking Cycle (typically starting from TRL 4), focusing on reducing technical and market risks;Product Development Cycle (typically starting from TRL 6), aiming at delivering a product ready for commercialisation. Under this Call for Proposals, economic operators are invited to submit their ideas via the OSIP (Open Space Innovation Platform) (ideas.esa.int), which serves as the entry point for the programme. The application process consists of the following step: Idea Pitch - Applicantssubmit and present a draft Outline proposal via OSIP to ESA (and potentially the relevant National Delegation(s)). Following a positive assessment, economic operators will be invited to submit a Proposal Part 2 (Full) in accordance with the established procedures and evaluation criteria. Activities supported under InCubed are based on a co-funding scheme, whereby economic operators contribute financially to the project, demonstrating commitment to and confidence in their business case.

tenderDescription: Both TGO and MEX spacecraft are equipped with UHF radios, used for relaying data to and from landers. tenderTitle: HYDRON RESILIENCE: SECURITY ASPECTS OF NETWORKS INTEROPERABILITY (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.240) EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:The objective of this study is to assess the feasibility of applying Common Criteria framework (or equivalent) to guarantee compatible security mechanisms with HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network).Targeted Improvements:To achieve security interoperability of HydRON with other networks with a clear protection profile definition in line with international standards.Description:Multiple constellations are expected to be developed in the coming years, addressing different applications, like navigation, Earth Observation and communications as well as defence. Each constellation will be optimized for the target application, in terms of technologies, coverage, but also security functions. The challenge, but also the opportunity is to make use of all the possible infrastructure to enhance coverage and resilience of these systems by the integration of optical communication security features like Low Probability to be detected or interfered (LPD/LPI).However, different users will have different protection profiles and thereforesecurity targets will differ between networks. The Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation (referred to as Common Criteria) is an international standard (ISO/IEC 15408) used to specify security functional and assurance requirements, to guarantee implementation and verification of the security features and it can be used as a baseline for the security analysis of different networks and interoperability of security levels.This activity shall define a set of protection profiles for different target users and identify the security targets for different networks. Taking HydRON as a baseline for communications, the activity shall consider additional, selected national or EC networks interconnected by optical links in space or with optical ground stations and ground networks.For such security interoperability, the activity will define the required security functions (confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication, non-repudiation...) and achievable levels of assurance by the different space networks. For the sected networks, an analysis of the impact shall be performed for each of these security functions, including a preliminary assessment of vulnerabilities by different potential threat actors and its impact on the system. The feasibility of applying Common Criterialframework or similar framework for these networks shall be assessed. Additionally, the achievable level of protection by the different networks shall be provided as a draft catalogue, to be presented to potential users. The activity shall define initial access scenarios for Ministries of Defence (MODs) and Civil Security Entities to utilise the upcoming HydRON installation to conduct dedicated, potentially classified testingvalidating defencegrade security, resilience behaviours, and interoperability in realistic operational scenarios and providing inputs to preliminary vulnerability assessment analysing operational impacts of potential attacks.

tenderTitle: ONBOARD AUTOMATIC IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM SPOOFING DETECTION MODULE FOR LOW-LATENCY AND RELIABLE MARITIME SURVEILLANCE (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 5A.096) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective is to design, develop and test an Automatic Identification System (AIS) spoofing detection system onboard the satellite for satellite-based maritime surveillance, offeringreliable AIS information with low-latency.TargetedImprovements: Reduce by half the latency of detection of non-reliable reporting vessels compared to current technologies. Decrease reliance on ground-based infrastructures by enabling onboarddetection of deceptive AIS signals.Description: With approximately 90% of international trade travelling by sea, maritime routes are becoming increasingly congested. A reliable maritime domain awareness is thus paramount toaddress critical security (e.g. submarine cables, piracy), safety (e.g. collision avoidance), economic (e.g. fleet monitoring) or environmental (e.g. illegal fishing) needs, and space-basedcomponents are critical due to the limited terrestrial systems coverage. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is one of the main components of the current maritime domain awarenessinfrastructure, being mandated by International Maritime Organisation and enabling the reporting of vessels worldwide. However, the current AIS setup suffers from reliability issues.Vessels can arbitrarily either switch off their AIS transponder or use (or being the target of) malicious deceiving techniques such as AIS spoofing and jamming or manipulation of GNSSinformation embedded in such messages. This results in fictitious abnormal behaviours that are becoming increasingly common and causing significant disruption across entire regions.Moreover, traditional satellite-based AIS processing systems rely heavily on ground-based validation, leading to high latency in spoofing detection and reducing the effectiveness of real timecountermeasures.An onboard detection module could overcome these challenges by detecting in near real-time any AIS anomaly and initiate the mitigation countermeasures, i.e. paired with communicationto other trailing satellites or direct-to-device communication links (out of the scope of this activity), such detection system could inform users about fraudulent activities faster thantraditional surveillance systems.This activity will develop and test an onboard Automatic Identification System (AIS) spoofing detection system for satellite-based maritime surveillance, offering reliableAIS informationwith low-latency. Low latency AI-based anomaly detection and other technologies such as signal fingerprinting and deterministic algorithms will be investigated and developed.The AIS spoofing detection module shall be designed according to selecteduse cases and implemented on a software-defined radio-based payload and tested in a representativemaritime surveillance scenario to evaluate its effectiveness in detecting, localising, and mitigating AIS spoofing in real time.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. tenderTitle: DEVELOPMENT OF EUROPEAN SOURCED CARBON FIBERS FOR SPACE APPLICATION
tenderDescription: Objective:To develop European suppliers for the manufacture of high strength (HS) and high modulus (HM) carbonfibres for use in space systems.Description:Carbon fibres are one of the main components used in the development of lightweight structures for spaceapplications, especially high-strength and high modulus carbon fibres. These types of carbon fibres providehigh strength/weight andhigh stiffness/weight ratio in composite structures, ensuring both mechanicalperformance and dimensional stability for composites.High performance composite materials are widelyused in ESA launch vehicles, as well as primary structures of spacecrafts (such as Sentinels or Galileo) or robotic exploration platforms. According to a market study, the demand for carbon fibres for polymercomposite materials for space applications in Europe between 2023 and 2032 is estimated at approximately450 t.High-performance carbon fibres qualified for space flight are currently sourced from outside Europe and/orlinked to non-EU IP and export regimes, representing a strategic dependency. There have been someprojects on the development of pilot lines for carbon fibre manufacturing, such as the EUCARBON (FP7)and Space Carbon (H2020) activities, but the developed manufacturing capabilities are still in their earlystages and without clear plans on industrialization and utilization of the products. There are some limitedmanufacturing plants in Europe, however most of them use precursors (raw materials) that are imported,which again leads to foreign dependence. There are currently no existing, readily available and qualifiedcarbon fibres with a fully sovereign supply chain in Europe.The activity will focus onthe mechanical characterization, processability and industrialization, and conformity with ESA qualification standards. Its objective is to strengthen the development of a robust and autonomous European supply chain. The scope of the work targets RD activities carried out with European companies striving to replicateor exceedthe performance of competing solutions originating from outside Europe.Therefore, the following, not exhaustive, tasks shall be executed:- Identification of a fully European supply chain (including precursors and prepregging) to be assessed for their material systems and processes compatibility with space applications. Preferably define a supply chain able to realize prepregs from HM fibers and a supply chain to realize HS fiber tow for filament winding.- A characterization of the identified material systems for space applications, both at fiber level and at laminatelevel. Laminate level characterization shall be performed on samples manufactured using processes thatare common in space industry. Preferably autoclave process of prepregs with high modulus fibers andfilament winding with high strength fiber system. Benchmark results against ESA-qualified, non-Europeanmaterial systems to identify performance gaps and qualification needs.- Manufacture breadboards of representative space structural components using the identified HM and HSmaterial systems and relative processes. In this phase of the project the involvement of already establishedEuropean space composite structures designers, manufacturers and test houses is highlyrecommended.- Develop a database based on the acquired results and provide recommendations for standardization, furtherdevelopment and potential qualification and industrialization paths including a preliminary budget and time estimate.- An overview of the steps needed towards industrialization of a product of high-quality, assessment of facilities wrt re-use/adapt vs build dedicated one, long-term commercial viability plan (including discussions with the end users, lessons learned from other industries or other countries should be incorporated in this plan, for example ways to reduce the energy needed in a production planned).

tenderTitle: CONSOLIDATION OF A FULL G-NODEB FOR SPACE BASED ON A EUROPEAN SIGNAL PROCESSING PLATFORM (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.089) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop a European g-NodeB (gNB) hardware and software protocol stack architecture for regenerative NGSO satellite with a fully European signal processing platform, i.e., both hardware and softwareTargeted Improvements: Enabling a European full gNB in Space for regenerative 5G/6G broadband satellite systems not existing today in ESA Member StatesDescription: The 3GPP standardisation group has defined the necessary features and enhancements in 5G mobile broadband systems tosupport non-terrestrial network (NTN) since Release 17 in 2022. The upcoming 6G NTN integration into the terrestrial telecom systemenables new features such as:a. Seamless interoperability between terrestrial and satellite networks;b. Direct-to-device connectivity without specialised satellite terminals in FR 1 (i.e., <7GHz);c. Ubiquitous connectivity across geography;d. Broadband servicesfor aviation, maritime, and cross-border mobility;e. AI-Native networking to optimise beam management, manage mobility, and dynamically allocate spectrum across the multi-layered satellitenetwork.However, today no European solution exists for a full gNB signal processing hardware platform and software protocol stack as needed for 5G/6Gregenerative NTN payloads.This activity will develop a European gNB hardware and software protocol stack architecture for regenerative NGSO satellite with a fully European signalprocessing platform, i.e., both hardware and software. The gNB shall be able to support high throughput 5G/6G connectivity either in S-band spectrum(e.g., up to 50Mbit/s) or in Ka-band spectrum (e.g., up to 1Gbit/s).The activity will: Develop a concept of an efficient signal processing hardware and software protocol stack architecture for a European gNB implementation for regenerative NGSO satellites. Identify a suitable European signal processing platform and characterise relevant functional blocks of the signal processing hardware. A laboratory breadboard will be developed together with electrical ground support equipment (EGSE) suitable to performradiation characterisation including Single Event Effects (SEE), Displacement Damage (DD), and Total Ionizing Dose (TID). A radiation mitigation approach shall be developed and implemented using a combination of software- and hardware-based solutions to compensate for identified critical performance impacts. The devicewith the applied radiation mitigation measures will be radiation tested,and the performance will be compared to the unmitigated hardware performance. Carry out analysis and concept trade-offs to ensurethehigh throughput connectivity and minimised power consumption per MHz in the selected band (S-band or Ka-band)Identify and assess relevant in-orbit experiment considerations.

tenderTitle: CONCEPT OF A NEXT GENERATION MCC - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: The main objective of this activity is to comprehensively gather, analyse and consolidate the requirements and specifications for afuture concept of a Measurement Command Control (MCC) system intended to support ESA propulsion test facilities[ID2.1][ID2.2][ID2.3] for systems and subsystems in a five- to ten-year timeframe. The main use case of such an MCC will be for larger test bench facilities such as the P5 at DLR Lampoldshausen and PF50 at Vernon (hundreds of simultaneous measurements within a large frequency spectrum) but shall be highly adaptable to other similar benches. The activity shall identify innovative technologies, architectural concepts, to support the following objectives:Improve Operational efficiency, maintainability, scalability and performance;SupportStandardization;Ensure energy efficiency for Sustainability purposesReduce Recurring Costs.Subsequently, the study aims to formulate a comprehensive concept for the future MCC, including preliminary system requirements, architectural definition, innovativefeatures, and an assessment of existing and emerging solutions and suppliers ideally from ESA Member States. Thus, the study shall assess the availability and maturity of the required technologies within the European ecosystem, identify potential capability gaps,and recommend developments needed to strengthen European technological autonomy, resilience, and sovereignty in this strategic domain. The resulting concept shall establish the foundations for future procurement and implementation activities across ESA propulsiontest facilities.[ID3.1][ID3.2][ID3.3] Particular attention shall be given to disruptive concepts and architectural evolutions capable of delivering a substantial leap in the bench capabilities with respect to the given objectives.

tenderTitle: ARGONAUT LDE – LDE/CPE SCOE Simulator
tenderDescription:
Argonaut LDE (previously named EL3, European Large Logistics Lander), is one of the keystones of the “Terrae Novae” exploration capabilities presented at Council Meeting 2022. Argonaut LDE aims at enabling a substantial and sustained European presence on the surface of the Moon ensuring Europe remains a key player in space exploration. Argonaut LDE aims at providing an autonomous European capability for regular large robotic surface missions for an extended duration. This provides the possibility to conduct independent missions if required as well as being a significant and visible contribution to the international sustainable exploration of the lunar surface.

The mission is designed to support both human and robotic exploration by providing a multipurpose lander known as the Lunar Descent Element (LDE):
•	Lunar Descent Element (LDE): 
o	A recurring lander, common to all ARGONAUT LDE missions. 
o	Designed to be compatible with different delivery missions without undergoing modifications; 
o	The LDE provides the functions of Payload transport to the Moon’s surface as well as the main mission functions common to all the different missions. 

The LDE is equipped to deliver various payloads through a mission-specific interface, typically referred to as the Cargo Platform Element (CPE). For the purpose of clarity the CPE and the related Payload are subject to a separate procurement under ESA’s responsibility. 

Thales Alenia Space Italy, have been Contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the Argonaut Lunar Descent Element (LDE) which will be used for the first mission in 2031. 

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the Argonaut LDE/CPE SCOE Simulator.

The procurement of the LDE/CPE SCOE Simulator will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).

Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

tenderDescription: ObjectivesTo increase the efficiency of photobioreactors by an improved design of light conduction anddiffusion inside the reactor.DescriptionThe need for regenerative life support systems for long term space missions necessitates a questfor increased efficiency of Photobioreactors. The light intensification of photobioreactors is animportant building block to increase the return on investment with respect to light energy introducedvs oxygen yield in a defined volume.Previous activities have identified as a priority the need to progress on specific technologies, suchas the type of light sources and on innovative materials for light conductionand diffusion (e.g.polymers, leaking rods, specific optical fibers, lightning fabrics). tenderTitle: GT1I-805GA SECURITY FRAMEWORK FOR AI APPLICATIONS (EXPRO+)
tenderDescription: Increasingly, advances in AI applications, models, and big data capabilities are making their way intoproductive applications. Roadmaps exist to introduce AI technologies into critical functional and operationaldomains. With new technology spin-ins like AI, cybersecurity must be accounted for, considering new attacksurfaces and vulnerabilities. Currently, no specialized approach exists forsystems with AI components,necessitating an ad-hoc approach for each system. To avoid redundant efforts, a coherent security approachfor AI applications in the space domain should be defined. Common mitigation measures for identified threatsand risks related to data and models need to be integrated into the AI lifecycle, ensuring a secure and AIenabledinfrastructure. Systems today demand increased security and even security certification. Whilesecurity approaches for non-AI systems are well understood, AI components introduce new threats. Thisactivity will guide developers in creating secure AI systems and assist project teams with certificationbasesfor AI solutions. Building on previous ESA work where security threats and mitigation measures for spacesystems were identified and considering emerging policies and regulations, this activity will develop an'MLSecOps' framework, i.e. a comprehensive set of practices and tools, processes, and datasets to addressnew vulnerabilities. These will be integrated with operational MLOps infrastructure and validated in a spacesystem context. The targeted space system applications may range from engineering aids to securitymonitoring solutions. The solution will be based on public standards and knowledge bases such as the ENISAreport "Cybersecurity of AI and Standardisation," MITRE ATLAS, and OWASP Gen AI Security Project. Theseoffer a rich list of vulnerabilities and controls without considering the required adaptations for space missionspecifics. This activity will establish a set of practices and createcommon tools for AI systems to providestandardized security features and functions, easing the certification process.

tenderTitle: GT17-883GS ALL-DIGITAL GROUND STATION
tenderDescription: The signal processing approach of satellite ground station back-ends is undergoing a major conceptual changeworldwide: instead of processing the signal in the back-end in the classical way with a dedicated up-/ downlinkchain, there is the more flexible approachof sampling the signal directly before transmission / after reception. Thisstep also includes the up- and down-conversion. Thereafter the data is transferred via the network using theDigital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability (DIFI) protocol and processed on a Software Defined Radio (SDR)platform (instead of a classical modem). Commercialisation of this concept is on-going on both sides: the classicalmodem/back-end providers and the providers of commercial satellite ground station services. For the latter one,the high flexibility, the easy scalability and the interoperability are only some of the key advantages. For all sidesadvantageous isthe high degree of modularity, that can be achieved with an all-digital ground station. This allows,to program dedicated modules for dedicated satellite missions, which can then be plugged into any ground station,without changing hardware components, just simply by a software update. The use of the open DIFI standardinstead of other proprietary protocols also helps avoid vendor lock-in by allowing systems from different vendorsto communicate with each other. The open DIFI standard can also be a door-opener for new andexisting vendorsto offer COTS components with the option to include custom developments according to customer requests.Furthermore, the signal digitisation right at the beginning allows for much more flexibility in terms of processing.For example, the processing could even be split between a COTS SDR and a custom developed SDR part (e.g.for a dedicated mission need(s)). This allows to take profit of low-cost COTS developments, while still maintainingall the dedicated custom developed functionalities in a separate SDRsystem. Moreover, the given flexibility of anall-digital ground station is much larger than only this and this activity will assess additional possibilities which anall-digital ground station could provide. Additionally, it will also show in which areas there are still limitations toovercome.This activity is complementary to the TDE activity, T712-703GS - Ground Station Backend Architecture with High-Rate Sampling and Software Defined Radio, for a very limited all digital ground station.

tenderTitle: LISA-ITT-070 CFRP Struts
tenderDescription:
The gravitational wave observatory LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) has been selected as ESA’s third large class mission (L-3) within the Cosmic Vision programme. LISA’s mission objective is to observe gravitational waves from space in the frequency band of 0.1 mHz to 1 Hz, not accessible from ground-based observatories. 
The mission architecture consists of a constellation of three spacecraft placed at the vertexes of a near-equilateral triangle with side length of about 2.5 million km (LISA Constellation). An overview of the LISA mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/LISA
OHB, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the LISA programme, building the industrial consortium.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the LISA CFRP Struts.
The CFRP Struts are part of the LISA platform tertiary structure. They connect different mechanical elements and combine metallic end-caps for attachment and a CFRP middle section. The combination of the CFRP section to the metallic end-caps is considered a critical structure technology and will require adequate design and verification or heritage.
The procurement of the CFRP Struts will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

tenderTitle: ARGONAUT LDE – Mechanical Ground Support Equipment [MGSE] and Transport Container
tenderDescription:
Argonaut LDE (previously named EL3, European Large Logistics Lander), is one of the keystones of the “Terrae Novae” exploration capabilities presented at Council Meeting 2022. Argonaut LDE aims at enabling a substantial and sustained European presence on the surface of the Moon ensuring Europe remains a key player in space exploration. Argonaut LDE aims at providing an autonomous European capability for regular large robotic surface missions for an extended duration. This provides the possibility to conduct independent missions if required as well as being a significant and visible contribution to the international sustainable exploration of the lunar surface.

The mission is designed to support both human and robotic exploration by providing a multipurpose lander known as the Lunar Descent Element (LDE):
•	Lunar Descent Element (LDE): 
o	A recurring lander, common to all ARGONAUT LDE missions. 
o	Designed to be compatible with different delivery missions without undergoing modifications; 
o	The LDE provides the functions of Payload transport to the Moon’s surface as well as the main mission functions common to all the different missions. 

The LDE is equipped to deliver various payloads through a mission-specific interface, typically referred to as the Cargo Platform Element (CPE). For the purpose of clarity the CPE and the related Payload are subject to a separate procurement under ESA’s responsibility. 

Thales Alenia Space Italy, have been Contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the Argonaut Lunar Descent Element (LDE) which will be used for the first mission in 2031. 

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the Argonaut LDE Mechanical Ground Support Equipment [MGSE] and Transport Container.

The procurement of the MGSE and Transport Container will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).

Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

tenderTitle: S3-CL-07 SYSTEM-INTEGRATED SPACE MATERIALS DATABASE FOR DARK  QUIET SKIES COMPLIANT DESIGNS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: The increasing deployment of satellites is raising concerns regarding their impact on ground- and space-based astronomical observations and the need to comply with emerging Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) requirements. Reliable assessment of spacecraft visibility requires accurate knowledge of the optical properties of external spacecraft materials and their environmental degradation over time. However, existing data are limited, fragmented and often unsuitable for consistent spacecraft-level brightness analyses. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a system-integrated European database of optical properties for spacecraft materials with potential observational impacts, including solar arrays, multilayer insulation, thermo-optical coatings, antennas and external optical elements. The activity shall establish the required material datasets, perform dedicated measurement and characterisationcampaigns, and integrate the resulting data into an open-access database supporting DQS compliance assessments and brightness prediction tools. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 7.

tenderTitle: IMPROVED TTC SUB-SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objectives: To consolidate alternative solutions for on-board loss minimization. To develop the prototypes of the most relevant solutions identified, to confirm the predicted performance. To provide road-map to flight models. The state of art TTC Sub-System architectures for Science and Exploration missions are nowadays quite complex. In order to allow communications during all mission phases, several antennas are needed in combination with redundant High Power Amplifiers (HPA) and transponders (DST). The interconnectionamong these components is accomplished by the RF Distribution Unit (RFDU), which has to guarantee the maximum degree of reconfigurability and reliability to failures. In addition, it has also to implement the necessary filtering action, to allow full duplex communications. Its design is therefore quite complex encompassing the use of several switches, Diplexers, Filters and interconnecting waveguides (WG) runs. The latter can be quite long as they have to reach antennas which are typically far from the location of the rest of the TTC subsystem. All this results in high losses with RF power reduction in transmission and increased noise figure in reception.The design solutions used so far in the frame of ESA projects are quite recurrent with no major improvements in the last decades. As shown in a TTC Sub-System architecture survey carried out in 2017, different approaches exist, as identified for example by other agencies and already flown successfully in the past years. For a complex RFDU as used in Deep Space missions, we can consider RF path losses in the order of 1 to 3 dB in X-band and 3 to 4 dB in Ka-band, withsignificant impacts in terms of data return (up to50% reduction) and in terms of spacecraft recovery possibilities in case of anomalies (increasedoperations complexity and limitation on maximum achievable distance). Therefore, there is a clear need for loss reduction in the RFDU paths, through the implementation of novel solutions. A study is on-going to consolidate the possible alternative subsystem Architectures, and define relevant requirements. This will be completed in early 2024, but its conclusions need to be consolidated by experimental results. The activity shall focus on the specification, detailed design, development and tests of prototypes of the components which will have the most significant impact on the TTC subsystem performance and whose feasibility has to be demonstrated. Three main items have been already identified, which may need to be completed by additional technologies as an outcome of the on-going study:- Receiving only antenna with integrated low-noise-amplifier (LNA) and downconverter (D/C), with a possible alternative for a receiving and transmitting solution;- High-gain-antenna dual-band feed including receiving LNA and D/C, and with direct interface to power amplifier;- Transponder front-end to manage the interfaces with new antennas designs.Tasks:1. Consolidation of requirements and design2. Design and manufacturing of bread-boards3. Testing of bread-boards4. Development plan for flight models.

tenderTitle: ERS-EO SPACE RESILIENCE NODES USER NEEDS HARMONISATION STUDY - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: As part of the European Resilience from Space - Earth Observation (ERS-EO) Element 2 Programme, and in line with the Space Resilience Node (SRN) Workplan 2026 approved on 26th February 2026, ESA intends to issue a competitive tender (ERS-SRN-02) for one (1) harmonization study (up to 300k, 5 - 12 months) which will consolidate the findings from individual SRN User Needs Studies (see Tender Action 1000046333). The objective of the study is to derive or confirm common user needs and requirements for SRNs to inform the SRN Reference Framework, and to identify gaps in space-enabled products to support SRN users' public protection and disaster response activities.

tenderDescription: The European Space Agency and the Ministry of Science, Education and Youth of Croatia hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above Call for Proposals (CfP), which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Croatian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types:Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use onfuture ESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL 3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 150,000.Type B Product or Service Development activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 6. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 400,000 (hardware development)/EUR 250,000 (all otheractivities).Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 100,000.Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRL shall be at least 5 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR200,000. tenderTitle: ERS-EO ALPSTAR PHASE A/B1 STUDY FOR A BESPOKE SAR MISSION WITH OPTIONAL ELINT (ACTIVITY 3)
tenderDescription: The ALPSTAR Phase A/B1 study for a bespoke X band SAR mission, with optional ELINT capability, aims to define a technically feasible, sovereign European space segment architecture aligned with emerging user needs and the ALPSTAR federated concept. Conducted through up to two parallel industrial contracts within participating states, the study focuses on the design of a high performance SAR payload as the primary driver, including its integration on a mature platform (TRL 8-9), while assessing the feasibility, added value,and implementation impacts of incorporating an ELINT capability either as an embedded or hosted payload. The activity includes mission and system architecture definition, interface specification with the ground and federation layers, compliance with SRD and evolving MRD use cases, and evaluation of key technologies and TRL gaps. It further delivers preliminary design solutions, end to end performance considerations (including L0/L1 processing and ELINT simulation), trade offs, and a credible roadmap toward flight readiness. Outputs also encompass a comprehensive development and procurement plan, industrial organisation, launcher options, and robust ROMcost and schedule estimates for subsequent B2/C/D/E phases, ensuring decision readiness for the ALPSTAR Governance Board.

tenderTitle: NON-ORTHOGONAL MULTIPLE ACCESS (NOMA) FOR BEYOND 5G (B5G) SATELLITE SYSTEMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.060) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective is to develop, implement and test Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) on the uplink of a Beyond 5G (B5G)satellite system. The link shall be representative of3GPP-compliant Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) scenarios .TargetedImprovements:Improving resources utilisation in dense and / or heterogenous system environments, allowing 50% spectral efficiency increase withrespect to orthogonal multiple access.Description: Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) is recognized as a key technology for beyond 5G networks, aiming to enhance the system capacity and tackle the challenges ofmassive connectivity by improving spectrum efficiency. NOMA was studied in 3GPP release 15 for New Radio (NR) in TN context but it was not pursued. Instead, it wasclassified as a technology for next generation. However, only Code-Domain NOMA was analysed in release 15. Since then, both academia and major industry players havebeen working on enhancing NOMA, including both Code-Domain (CD-NOMA) and Power-Domain (PD-NOMA) variants and they have yielded promising results including NTNscenarios up to 80% throughput gain. Among the challenges that these efforts have targeted are implementation complexity and interference management.This activity will develop and test over-the-air an efficient and low complexity NOMA techniques for satellite uplink using 3GPP NR NTN air interface. The developments concernboth the strategy for poweror code allocation and user pairing, as well as the efficient implementation of successive interference cancellation at the receiver. User pairing andpower allocation shall consider both a distributed grant-free AI-based strategy such as a distributed leaning methodology with an agent at each user, and a static strategy basedon the network architecture. The implementation of Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) at the receiver side shall consider the receiver processing chain based on 3GPPair interface. The selected NOMA solution shall be compared to a benchmark orthogonal multiple access scheme in the specified scenarios and use cases considering as aminimum the system throughput, latency and complexity. Furthermore, the outcome of the activity shall serve as a benchmark for beyond 5G standardization. The integration ofNOMA in beyond 5G shall be seen either as stand-alone access scheme (for massiveconnectivity scenarios for example), or opportunistic on top of orthogonal access when thelatter is not able to serve all users (sudden user population peaks or specific heterogenous systems).

The integration ofNOMA in beyond 5G shall be seen either as stand-alone access scheme (for massiveconnectivity scenarios for example), or opportunistic on top of orthogonal access when thelatter is not able to serve all users (sudden user population peaks or specific heterogenous systems).

tenderTitle: IHE1-2 SMALLSAT PROJECT 2026
tenderDescription: One of the main objectives of the Space strategy for Europe is to foster a globally competitive and innovative European space sector, in particular by improving support to technological maturation for sub-systems, equipment and technologies, including in-orbit demonstration and validation activities, to reduce time to market.To ensure the European Union non-dependence and competitiveness in technologies, there is a clear need for a regular, sustainable, cost-effective and responsive In Orbit Demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service in the European Union. Space flight heritage in real conditions and environment is often required to de-risk innovations such as new technologies, products, concepts, architectures, and operations techniques are they for unique or recurrent, institutional or commercial missions.On 31 March 2023, the European Commission issued a Call for Expression of Interest for In Orbit Demonstration/Validation of Experiments Needing Aggregation, open until 15 March 2027 with multiple cut-off dates. The objective is to promote European competitiveness and non-dependence by offering flight opportunities through IOD/IOV for European Experiments. The European Commission pre-selects on a regular basis a number of Experiments that may fly with the Horizon Europe In-orbit Demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) Service.The SmallSat Project 2026 will provide the Horizon Europe In-orbit demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service with a Carrier based on European SmallSat platforms, with a system total mass (including experiments) in the range of 250 kg.The SmallSat Project 2026 Contractor will be responsible for specifying and delivering all elements required to accommodate a set of experiments selected by the European Commission, in order to bring them into space and to allow for demonstration and/or validation purposes.These activities include:-system studies, at ground and space segments levels, including accommodation analysis of theIOD/IOV Experiments on the IOD/IOV Carrier and the compatibility analysis with the available launch solutions, -input to the launch mission analysis for the launch services provider, -manufacturing, assembly, integration and test of the whole IOD/IOV spacecraft based on EU manufactured solutions including the selected experiments, -ground segment capabilities (facilities and operators) to operate the IOD/IOV mission, -management of interfaces between the different IOD/IOV Experiments and the IOD/IOV Carrier, -inputs to launcher interfaces, -transport and delivery of the IOD/IOV spacecraft to the Launch Site, -launch campaign, -launch and Early Orbit Phase (LEOP), -operations of the IOD/IOV spacecraft for maximum one year taking into account the specific needs of the experiments, -delivery of the experiments in-flight data to the experiment providers, with a right to use for ESA and EU, -decommissioning of the IOD/IOV spacecraft at the end of the operations. This project is funded by the European Union. ESA is the Contracting Authority and runs the procurement under the ESA/REG/001 rev.5 adapted as per the signed FFPA Agreement.

tenderTitle: TGO-MEX RADIO OCCULTATION - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: RO occurs when the transmitter of a radio signal appears to set behind a planet, as viewed from a receiving station. The radio signal is refracted by the atmosphere and ionosphere causing a frequency shift; analysing this frequency shift allows reconstruction of a high-resolution vertical profile of density (and thus pressure and temperature) in the neutral atmosphere and ionospheric electronabundances in the ionosphere. Spacecraft-to-Earth RO has been carried out for many decades by planetary missions, but the opportunities for this are limited by the orbital geometry and ground station availability.

tenderTitle: NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORK DIRECT SAMPLING RADIO UNIT (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5C.544) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design and test an engineering model of a Direct Sampling Radio Unit (DSRU) covering the 5G frequency bands FR1 and FR2.TargetedImprovements:Enabling direct sampling of all 5G frequency bands, providing an RF front end and Digital Signal Processing chip to achieve flexible 5G NTN communication with 20%reduction in power consumption compared to the current state of the art.Description: Current RF Systems-on-Chip (SoC) enables direct sampling in Frequency Range 1 (FR1), but higher frequency ranges still require down-conversion stages to sample atbaseband. There is a significant market need for a solution that enables direct sampling across all 5G frequency bands, simplifying the system architecture and improving theefficiency of5G Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN). As payload capacity and re-configuration requirements increase, the conventional functions - such as separate analoguereceiver / transmitter, filtering and DSP - become more complex, power hungry and with a time to market which is not suitable for a fast-moving NTN scenario. To address thesechallenges, direct RF sampling with wide bandwidth and software-defined architecture offer a simple, scalable, and efficient solution. It supports flexible frequency planning,reduces filtering requirements and enables higher modulation schemes for higher throughput. In addition, integrated DSP enables agile frequency tuning, on-chip digital signalprocessing, and clock for multichip synchronization. Integrated digital signal processing will support the transition to software-defined radio payloads, creating a highlyconfigurable, common hardware / software device that can be used in next generation of communication satellites.This activity will identify discrete Commercial-of-The-Shelf (COTS) ADC / DAC or mixed-signal chips capable of direct sampling of Frequency Range 2 (FR 2), covering both KuandKa-Band. An engineering model of a Direct Sampling Radio Unit (DSRU) covering the 5G frequency bands FR1 and FR will be designed and manufactured. Testing shallevaluate the full Radio Unit (RU) functionality - including RF and lower / upper parts of the physical layer (Low-PHY / High-PHY) .Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. tenderTitle: LEO CONSTELLATIONS REAL-TIME RADIO RESOURCE MANAGEMENT DEMONSTRATOR - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To develop an active antenna combined software and hardware demonstrator representative of a LEO satellite payload by exploiting advanced strategies for real time dynamically managing radio resources.Description: On-board satellite resource allocationstrategiesare essential for managing the distribution of limited resources from the antennas to multiple user terminals. These strategies involve dynamic allocation techniques that can adjust in real-time based on traffic demand. However, in dense traffic scenarios like onboard LEO satellites, these strategies face significant challenges. The high volume of demand can lead to congestion, resulting in increased latency and reduced QoS. Additionally, the limited on-board processing capability challenges the satellite's ability to efficiently manage traffic which leads to degraded antenna performance. Considering these challenges, the objective of this activity isto develop an active antenna combined software and hardware demonstrator representative of a LEO satellite payload by exploiting advanced strategies for dynamically managing radio resources, i.e. beamforming for real time tracking and coverage change combined with power and bandwidth allocation. Resource allocation should be defined as an optimization problem, considering factors like channelconditions, user demands, interference levels, and power constraints. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Derive real-time complex coefficients, using optimization strategies for the beamforming network. - Emulate users' movement and channel changes for proactive beam steering. - Develop models to detect and classify interference sources and use optimization techniquesfor mitigation. - Manufacture and test a proof-of-concept hardware demonstrator with a limited size active phased array and associated adaptivebeamforming, mounted on a mechanically movable platform with additional antennas located in fixed positions.

tenderTitle: DIGITAL PROCESSING UNIT FOR RF PAYLOADS AND MICROWAVE INSTRUMENTS- EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objectives: The objective of this activity is to design and develop a digital processing unit for RF payloads and microwave instruments using novel European technologies and components and to evaluate their performance.Description: Novel high-speed data acquisition and conversion devices together with reconfigurabledigital processing devices and high-speed digital data transmission are enabling a new generation of flexible, scalable and compact digital processing units for RF payloads.These units can perform direct conversion and reconfigurable digital processing for data reduction, allowing a simpler RF chain and reusing the same hardware to address different needs, from single channel reception and/or transmission to multiple channel reception and transmission, and in different domains, such as Earth Observation, Navigation, etc.Novel technologies exist, ranging from direct conversion to/from Ka-band, microprocessors, reconfigurable FPGAs with high-speed serial links, etc. in either fullyEuropean EEE components or EEEs with a significant European contribution such as building blocks and/or IP cores. These have promising performances and key parameters compatible with advanced digital processing units, but a comprehensive evaluation of these technologies working together as part of a system is still missing.Therefore, the proposed activity aims to take a systemic approach to the evaluation of such building blocks and technologies through breadboarding of a digital processing unit for RF payloads and microwave instruments. Reference operative scenarios relevant toRF payloads and microwave instruments shall be specified as use-cases and implemented, getting insight into technology gaps and limitations. The use cases focus on generic applications (i.e. EO, NAV).The following tasks are foreseen in the frame ofthis activity: Define at least two RF payload and/or microwave instrument use-cases, derive requirements for breadboarding and processing and assess EEE components with a significant European contribution to be used as building blocks of digital processing unitfor RF payloads (data acquisition and conversion, digital data processing, clock generation and distribution, high-speed links), including supporting SW toolchains. Breadboard representative digital processing unit using the identified technologies, such as analogue-to-digital (ADC), digital-to-analogue (DACs)converters, digital processing, and evaluate the selected technologies. DevelopSoftware and/or VHDL (Very High-Speed Integrated Circuit HardwareDescription Language) for implementing at least one of the defined use-cases.

tenderTitle: ESA BUSINESS INCUBATION CENTRE CYPRUS
tenderDescription: The network of ESA Business Incubation Centers (ESA BICs) is the largest network of space incubators in Europe. The two main objectives of an ESA BICs are to:Support entrepreneurs with a space-based business idea;Create and grow clusters of space related start-ups across Europe. All the ESA BICs are managed by local incubators with experience in supporting start-ups. They have good connections with local industry, universities, research organisations, as well as relevant government agencies and investor communities. ESA BICs follow the ESA BIC Common Approach to business incubation. So far, the network of ESA BICs has supported more than 2000 start-ups. Cyprus recently completed the ESA-Cyprus Plan for European Cooperating State (PECS) programme and recognized that Spaceis not only an important domain of research and development, but one of the key pillars of modern economy. On the 17th of March 2026, Cyprus became an Associate Member of the European Space Agency (ESA). The seven-year agreement opens the way for Cyprus's participation in ESA's optional programmes. As such, the Cypriot delegation asked ESA to start the implementation of an ESA BIC in Cyprus, under the ACCESS optional programme, in order to promote and foster the creation of startups active in the Space sector. The objective is to find and support 15 space-related incubatees over an active period of four years, with additional two years added to thecontract duration to support any incubatees until the end of the incubation program. Each selected incubatee shall be entitled to an incentive funding of at least 60kEUR.

tenderTitle: HIGH-PRECISION MECHANISM FOR ON-SKY OPTICAL BEAM DIVERGENCE ADJUSTMENT (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.080) - EXPRO+ (ON REQUEST)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a mechanism for an optical ground station that can adjust the beam's divergence during the link sessionwithout link interruption and whilst maintaining the optical pointing accuracy.TargetedImprovements:To enable dynamic adjustment of the beam divergence without needing optical realignment. This will enable real-time optimisation of the link based onthe elevation angle and the turbulence conditions. Eventually, integrating the beacon capabilities with the communications beam.Description: Alignment of the optical system at an optical ground station is usually needed before a link session, especially if the optical configuration (beam divergence)has changed. Links to Low-Earth Orbit are highly dynamic, ranging for very small elevation angles up to zenith, and atmospheric turbulence conditionsevolving during a link session. It is essential that for links targeting optical feeder applications the ground-space connectivity must be maintained.Furthermore, ground-to-space links usually make use of a beacon during the acquisition phase. For these reasons, developing a mechanism that allowsfor real-time beam-divergence adjustment without the need to re-align the optical components is considered very useful.Some of the off-the-shelf components used in optical ground stations are limited in accuracy and optical power, and therefore not suitable for an on-skyreal-time adjustment of the beam divergence. This activity shall evaluate the state-of-the-art of mechanisms, with their limitations on accuracy, precisionand maximum supported power. The design and development of an engineering model shall demonstrate the capabilities of the mechanism. This goalcan be achieved either in the laboratory with realistic interfaces or at an optical ground station.
