tenderTitle: HYDRON MARITIME: SATELLITE OPTICAL NETWORK EXTENSION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.239) EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept evolving HydRON services to maritime communications and identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap.Targeted Improvements:To enable maritime communications with satellite HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) systemDescription:Maritime routes are strategic in a connected world, where economies are interdependent. 80% of the global trade depends on shipping. Current strategical routes include South China, South India, Suez Canal, Mediterranean see, trans-Atlantic and Panama Canal. Together with the current routes, the transit along the arctic seais currently becoming more attention for cargo ships but also for defence purposes. Climate change may enable the use of this route,which could mean a drastic reduction in transport costs and service time (reduction of 25-40% in distance). From a logistics perspective, cargo companies aim to monitor their goods and containers, while ports seek to receive advance information about incoming cargo to optimize and plan the unloading process.Additional to the commercial and logistic interests, the defence aspects connected to maritime communications are of special interest, especially in an arctic route, where any developed infrastructure, could enhanceresilience.Currently, maritime communications relay on low-data rate satellite communications, or the use of low-band frequencies, when the ships are located close to shore. HydRON provides space-space and space-ground connectivity, extending terrestrial networksin space and providing global coverage.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements and system concepts for maritimecommunications (space-sea, sea-sea, sea-shore/ports), to extend the use of HydRON in maritime scenarios. Technology gaps and related technology roadmaps shall be developed, considering optical terminals and any critical technologies. The system shall consider themanagement of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a maritime ship-to-ship free-space network or hybrid communications with RF. The space segment shall consider the coverage along the most used routes. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be demonstrated. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

Climate change may enable the use of this route,which could mean a drastic reduction in transport costs and service time (reduction of 25-40% in distance). From a logistics perspective, cargo companies aim to monitor their goods and containers, while ports seek to receive advance information about incoming cargo to optimize and plan the unloading process.Additional to the commercial and logistic interests, the defence aspects connected to maritime communications are of special interest, especially in an arctic route, where any developed infrastructure, could enhanceresilience.Currently, maritime communications relay on low-data rate satellite communications, or the use of low-band frequencies, when the ships are located close to shore. HydRON provides space-space and space-ground connectivity, extending terrestrial networksin space and providing global coverage.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements and system concepts for maritimecommunications (space-sea, sea-sea, sea-shore/ports), to extend the use of HydRON in maritime scenarios. Technology gaps and related technology roadmaps shall be developed, considering optical terminals and any critical technologies. The system shall consider themanagement of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a maritime ship-to-ship free-space network or hybrid communications with RF. The space segment shall consider the coverage along the most used routes. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be demonstrated. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

tenderTitle: SENTINEL-2 NEXT GENERATION SATELLITE PHASES B2CDE1
tenderDescription: The Copernicus Sentinel-2 Next Generation space component, which is the subject of this procurement, will ensure a seamless continuation of the current Sentinel-2 first generation capabilities, whilst increasing both the quantity and quality of the products. The development of the Sentinel-2 Next Generation (Sentinel-2 NG) Space Component aims to build upon and enhance the initial observations provided by the first generation. In particular, Sentinel-2 NG (S2NG) will respond to the needs of Copernicus Services, with particular emphasis to the Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) and the Emergency Management Service (CEMS), together with, as secondary objective, the Marine Environment Monitoring Service (CMEMS). This will be characterised by enhanced spatial sampling and spectral sampling compared to Sentinel-2 first generation. S2 NG will provide observations for the next generation of operational products such as landcover maps, land-change detection maps, and geophysical properties, together with, as secondary objective, for the next generation of operational products over a larger portion of coastal and marine waters compared to Sentinel-2. S2NG will provide quantitative evidence in support to European and global policies, including the Green Deal, the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), the EU Forest Strategy, the EU Biodiversity Strategy, the EU Soil Strategy, the EU Water Framework and the UN SDGs. The S2NG space segment is expected to comprise of a constellation of two identical satellites (A- and B-units) flying at an altitude of approximately 650 km, in a sun-synchronous orbit. Each satellite will embark a payload comprised of the Advanced Multi-Spectral Imager (AMSI) instrument with two detection chains, one for Visible and Near-Infrared (VNIR) detection and one for the Short Wavelength Infrared (SWIR) detection, with a total of 21 bands (16 in VNIR, 5 in SWIR).The ITT for the Sentinel-2 NG Phases B2/C/D/E1 is in open competition. The ITTwill cover all spacecraft development phases (B2/C/D/E1) of the complete Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft (i.e. including Payload and Spacecraft subsystems), and the Model B Spacecraft the latter through a contractual mandatory option. This ITT will be arranged in two Contractual Phases as follows: Phase 1 will include: - all Payload Instruments activities up to the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Instrument Preliminary Design Review, and subsequent payload advanced phase C activities up to the end of the satellite Phase B2 (PDR);- all Sentinel-2 NG spacecraft activities, including the System Requirements Review (SRR), up to and including the Satellite Preliminary Design Review (PDR); and - the procurement of relevant long lead Items (LLI) for both Sentinel-2 NG Model A and Model B Spacecraft. Phase 2 will include: - All remaining Spacecraft activities up to and including the Sentinel-2 NG Model A Spacecraft Qualification and Flight Acceptance Review (QAR).Additional information: The Invitation to Tender (ITT) will be published on ESA Star. In order to access the ITT Package, Tenderers must be registered in esa-star as potential ESA suppliers. Any Tenderer, which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier, must complete the online questionnaire in esa-star, https://esastar-emr.sso. esa.int/. Further information on the registration process can be found in ESA's INDUSTRY PORTAL available at: - http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/esa-star_open_for_business - http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/How_to_do/esa-star_Registration_Process Please note that esa-star allows two levels of entity registration: "Light" and "Full". This allows new users wishing to do business with ESA to carry out their registration in two steps. While "Light" registration will grant access to all esa-star services up to and including proposal submission, the award of ESA contracts requires "Full" registration.

tenderTitle: MAKERSPACE FOR HUNGARIAN OPTICAL COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY PROJECTS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.045) EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:The identification of Hungarian industry / academia capabilities and interests in optical communication technologies, and a survey / test campaign of Hungarian infrastructures in view of finding potential locations for optical ground stationsTargeted Improvements:Selection of optimum optical ground infrastructure sites for participation in optical and quantum communication programsDescription:This activity will identify the capabilities and interests of Hungarian industry and academia in optical communication technologies and survey existing Hungarian infrastructures in view of finding potential locations for optical ground stations. The survey needs to identify Hungarian companies and academia suited to perform small prototyping projects with minimal administrative burden. In addition, the Makerspace will conduct a study on Hungarian potential to develop and operate a network of optical ground stations: aspects to be investigated include, but are not limited to, e.g. the optimum location of potential optical ground stations, the daily and seasonal cloudiness level of the sites, the atmospheric seeing conditions, the sky brightness mainly during thenight, but also during the day. Other topics related to optical and quantum communication development will also be made possible with this activity.The activity will specifically involve small industrial players throughout Hungary, which are at present focused on terrestrial consumer-oriented telecommunication projects.A prime contractor will be responsible for managing the separate individual development contracts. This prime will coordinate and manage all Makerspace activities, and oversee the prototyping projects/surveys. Initially, one activity will be defined by ESA and requested as part of the Statement of Work.The subsequent projects/activities will be jointly defined by ESA and the prime contractor, during the course of the activity. This will allow aligning the activities with the national developments and interests. The activities will target SMEs and industries that do not usually engage with ESA.

tenderTitle: S3-CL-15 ECOSTAR-S  CONSOLIDATION PHASE - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: This activity addresses the evolution of small satellite platforms toward sustainable space operations, in line with ESA's Zero Debris objectives and Ecodesign policy. It aims to consolidate system-level requirements for the next generation small satellite platform, integrating space debris mitigation constraints and environmental sustainability considerations across the full life cycle. Building on previous ESA and industry studies, the activity will identify key design drivers, perform trade-offs, and define a baseline platform concept up to System Requirements Review (SRR) level. It will also assess enabling technologies, engage with European suppliers, and establish a roadmap toward platform maturation and future demonstration. In parallel, the activity will analyse mission scenarios, hosted payload opportunities, and commercialisation aspects to support the preparation of a potential In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD). Overall, the objective is to support the development of reusable satellite product lines that embed Zero Debris compliance and Ecodesign principles while maintaining technical and economic viability.

tenderTitle: GSTP ELEMENT 1: DEVELOP: PREPARATION OF ENABLING SPACE TECHNOLOGIES AND BUILDING BLOCKS - STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSAL
tenderDescription: The European Space Agency ("the Agency" or "ESA") invites you to submit a Proposal under the General Support Technology Programme, Element 1: "Preparation of enabling space technologies and building blocks''The aim is to prepare and to develop enabling capabilities and the associated building blocks for space related systems and the associated sub-systems. An additional aim is to allow the targeted and coordinated development of the capabilities and building blocks (i.e. among academia and industry) in a given ESA Member State or across different Member States (in a collaborative manner). The intended output is to provide industry with a stronger foundation (i.e. building on this acquired know-how) in order to contribute to new space related system opportunities at national or international levels (institutional, commercial...) The objective is to enable Member States to support the further development of t capabilities and the associated building blocks in their industry. The technology development activities may be prepared in a targeted and coordinated manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed for a targeted type and class of space systems (in terms of performance, cost, size...) and with guiding specifications. The developments are to be performed in a coordinated manner to ensure that industry is able to work on complementary capabilities. The developments may be performed within one Member State or across several Member States in a collaborative manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed to a level such that the industrial entities may then be able to perform developments and eventually produce for concrete/more specific space related developments. The developments may go from a proof-of-concept (via simulation or experiment) up to an engineering qualification model (EQM). They address any technical area (structures, avionics/GNC, power control and distribution...). The spefications are to be linked to the guiding system or sub-system specifications. The maximum amount per activity is 1,000 K. The maximum duration is24 months.

tenderTitle: DYNAMIC HIGH-VOLUME DATA DISTRIBUTION FOR INTEGRATED OPTICAL AND RF NETWORKS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.082) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop bundle protocol and network stack, enabling automatic high-volume end-to-enddata distribution within integratedRF and optical networks. The testbed shall be developed to test networks feature heterogenous links, e.g. in terms of data rates or latencies, and includeend users, mission and payload control centres, optical and RF ground stations and space data relay systems.TargetedImprovements:Standardised data distribution irrespective of RF or optical communication.Reduced ground segment complexity (single system for RF and optical).Automatic network-based distribution.Increased E2E data delivery accountability leveraging unified reporting.Description: The need for hybrid (optical and RF) networks is due to the volumeof data transferred by satellites 00that is ever increasing. Optical communicationpotentially combined or augmented with RF communication at higher frequencies is supporting high or very high data rates. The distribution of this datais non-trivial and faces several challenges like non-permanent connectivity and asymmetric data rates in space and on ground just to name a few. It ishighly desirable to take a reliable and interoperable end-to-end approach with a common addressing scheme to cross organisational boundaries whilebeing able to monitor and manage the overall process of data distribution.The activity will develop an integrated optical andRF scalable high-volume data distribution testbed (demonstrating beyond 1 TB per downlink) based onDisruption Tolerant Networking (DTN). The activity will develop combined software and hardware. The testbed will be tested for high speed DTN nodesconnected over Wide Area Networks, emulating end users, control centres, and ground stations connecting with simulated spacecraft. It will includemonitoring and control aspects of individual nodes and DTN Network Management. The activity will allow the gathering of valuable experience in arepresentative environment and will address the problem of reliable and efficient data distribution in heterogenous ground networks and prepares theexpected deployment of DTN in space nodes in the future.

tenderTitle: HIGHLY ACCURATE RELIABLE AND PRECISE GNSS POSITIONING WITH QUANTUM OPTIMIZATION - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: ObjectivesDeriving algorithms and their optimal settings for enabling real-time highly accurate and reliable navigation based on GNSS carrier phase measurements exploiting quantum optimization algorithms.DescriptionHigh Accuracy with GNSS requires usage of phase measurements, which are ambiguous. Carrier phase Ambiguity Resolution (AR) is a stochastic process which requires a minimizationsearch for the correct ambiguities which can require a very large search to find the correct solution.In recent years, a series ofquantum algorithms for mathematical optimisation has been formulated which could be exploited to replace the classical approaches, such as those currently in use for GNSS AR. Quantum least squares can be used to perform Integer Least Square minimization, which would speed up the processing time for searching the right solution even in a larger search space. A fast and accurate solution of theGNSS carrier phase AR problem by means of quantum optimisation, in particular, would enable real-time Highly Accurate Reliable and Precise (HARP) positioning based on GNSS carrier phase positioning with integrity capabilities for users, achieving stringent positioning bounding with a very high level of confidence.This activity will define algorithms and their optimal settings for quantum optimization algorithms enabling real-time highly accurate and reliable navigation based on GNSS carrier phase measurements. The activity will rely on the quantum computers or simulators nowadays available to users as free prototypes from various companies, anticipating the advent of Quantum Processing Units which could become operational in the mid to long term.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Definition of the quantum optimisation algorithms for GNSS AR;- Prototyping of quantum navigation estimator for PPP-AR users;- Prototyping of quantum carrier phase AR and identifying its implication on integrity related to achieving HARP positioning;- Trading off of the number of qubits and the achievable performance.DeliverablesReport, Software

tenderTitle: LISA-ITT-067 LCA Integration MGSE
tenderDescription:
The gravitational wave observatory LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) has been selected as ESA’s third large class mission (L-3) within the Cosmic Vision programme. LISA’s mission objective is to observe gravitational waves from space in the frequency band of 0.1 mHz to 1 Hz, not accessible from ground-based observatories. 
The mission architecture consists of a constellation of three spacecraft placed at the vertexes of a near-equilateral triangle with side length of about 2.5 million km (LISA Constellation). An overview of the LISA mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/LISA
OHB, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the LISA programme, building the industrial consortium.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the LISA LCA Integration MGSE.
The LISA LCA Integration MGSEs shall provide several mechanical elements, such as trolleys and frames, to support the integration of the MOSA into the LCA. It shall enable flexible and safe height adjustment and rotation of the LCA to allow access for AIT operations, as well as provide a stable MGSE structure to support the LCA during test activities.
The MGSEs will be used under ISO 5 cleanliness conditions and in direct contact with high performance optical instruments. Therefore, the GSEs shall ensure full instrument safety, and special care shall be taken in the selection of materials to comply with the magnetic cleanliness requirements of the LISA project.
The procurement of the LCA Integration MGSE will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

tenderTitle: DIGITAL TWIN OF ATTITUDE AND ORBIT SENSORS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:To develop and test a model for a digital twin of attitude and orbit control system (AOCS) sensors as well as toassess compatibility of this multi-physics model-based digital twin with on-board self-calibration employing datadriven techniques and withthe simplification of ground verification processes of new satellite platforms.Description:Advances in model based engineering and digital twin (DT) development has led to growth in the interest of multiphysic modelling of space systems, including, for example, AOCS sensors. The AOCS sensor DTs includefunctional and performance behaviour, complemented by physical behaviour (thermal, power, electronic, etc.), as well as failure and degradation modes. This detailed modelling is based on analytic and background suppliermodels. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) / machine learning (ML) combined techniques, potentiallyaugmented with analytical a priori knowledge, offer the potential to improve the overall accuracy and validity ofthis modelling, together with a specific interest for statistical interpretation in the case of mass production (sensors for constellations, for example, gyros, star trackers, sun sensors). These new engineering techniques aimed at better fidelity in the AOCS sensor modelling offer the prospect of extending the benefits to on-board performance, for example, by adapting these techniques to the ultimate AOCS sensor calibration: self-calibration on board the spacecraft (e.g. constellation or low-cost platform). The following techniques and use cases will be studied:- Digital Twin for AOCS sensors, preferably from sensors used on platform series: architecture; interoperabilityneeds, multi-physic modelling trade-off and key components; use of data-driven techniques (AI/ML) to populate the DT models; statistical interpretation and validation of AOCS sensor performance (mass manufacturing, groundself-calibration based on sample measurements and statisticextrapolation).- Use of ground models and knowledge for on-board self-calibration; data fusion techniques for on-board use to consolidate ground self-calibration with flight measurements, autonomously; autonomous verification of on-board self-calibration (fault detection).This activity will bring tools, methods, and processes for increasing the end-to-end autonomous handling of AOCS sensorsin the platform development and verification chain. It includes predictive maintenance monitoring to inform on the overall health status and to prevent anomalies/failures. This activity aims at providing digital data and models to improve knowledge of the units in flight, allowing correction and improvement by the supplier and better integration in model-based system engineering (MBSE) or digital production.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Define the system into which the deliverable items will be integrated, establish the end user requirements andquantify the advantages of utilising the new items with respect to state-of-the-art alternatives.- Define a complete, self-standing and traceable set of technical requirements for the deliverable items.- Select the technical baseline that offers the best potential to achieve the activity objectives.- Detailed design and demonstrate, by appropriate analyses, simulations, tests or other means, that it cansatisfy the technical requirements.- Establish all detailed plans necessary to successfully implement and test the deliverable items and verify theircompliance to the technical specifications.- Implement the deliverable items, quantify their performances by means of a suitable test campaign anddemonstrate compliance to the technical requirements.

tenderTitle: ADVANCED SUSTAINABLE MANUFACTURING OF SPACE-QUALIFIED COMPONENTS FROM RECYCLED HIGH-VALUE FEEDSTOCK - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:To identify, demonstrate, and implement recycling of high-value scrap into quality feedstock for additivemanufacturing of components for space applications.Description:As the demand for spacecraft, satellites and launch systems grows, so too does the consumption of criticalraw materials - many of which are finite, expensive and environmentally burdensome to extract. Recycling andreusing materials offer a strategic solution, reducing dependency on virgin resources, lowering carbonemissions and enhancing supply chain resilience. By integrating recycled materials into components, thespace sector can not only reduce its environmental footprint but also pioneer circular economy practices that will be essential for long-term sustainability - both on Earth and in future off-world manufacturing ecosystems.Furthermore, materials like titanium, aluminium and nickel alloys are in high demand in the space sector, yetthese materials are primarily imported from non-European sources. Developing local recycling solutions for high-value, critical materials is a vital step towards achieving European material self-sufficiency, especially in the current geopolitical and economic context. Potentially significant sources of scrap include machining waste (e.g. swarf, off cuts) and unused powder from additive manufacturing. Scrapped parts due to manufacturing defects are expected to be a secondary, less frequent, source but may become more relevant in the context of out-of-earth manufacturing. The space sector should also consider sourcing waste/scrap materials from other industries (e.g. aviation, automotive).The activity will start by identifying hot spots of high-value material scrap across European manufacturing(space and non-space). A hot spot in this context would be defined as materials with high volume of scrap,high material value/cost, raw material being sourced outside Europe, and high demand by the space industry.Selected scrap will then be processed into quality raw materials, tested, and used to produce and evaluate ademonstrator part to be defined based on a business case (e.g. bracket, fuel tank).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identify sources of scrap material, material types relevant for space, and their possible use; down-selection of the most interesting cases (including economic, ecological and technical factors).- Develop processing route(s) for high-value material waste identified in the first task to transform into highquality raw materials for use as space hardware. This will most likely require dedicated alloy development to factor in what properties and quality can be realistically extracted from recycled materials.- Develop the advanced manufacturing process(es) for the use of "up-cycled" materials, considering theinfluence of impurities, potential development of detrimental phases, etc.- Test the produced material on a sample level (material characteristics, mechanical properties, etc.).- Design and manufacture a relevant spacedemonstrator part for subsequent testing to check compliance with relevant functional requirements.- Provide guidance on how to design components produced from recycled materials, seeking to identifypotential trade-offs between quality requirements, safety factors, cost and lead time.Deliverables: Breadboard, Report

tenderTitle: IMPACT-10: SCIENTIFIC AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT ASSESSMENT OF EARLY EARTH OBSERVATION SCIENCE ACTIVITIES- EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: IMPACT 10 is an ESA Earth Observation activity aimed at assessing and demonstrating the scientific and socio economic value generated by selected activities of the Earth and Mission Science Division (EOP SM). It focuses on scientific studies, mission science contributions, and programme enabling work supporting future EO missions. It also covers a new branch of "Future Science" activities. Within EOP SM, "Future Science" refers to forward looking science studies aligned with the ESA EO Science Strategy. These studies are designed to address fundamental Earth system science gaps that are not covered by current or planned missions. They therefore go beyond the scope of existing Science Plans activities. The activity will develop a robust and traceable methodology to assess both science impact and socio economic impact. Science impact will include, for example, scientific outputs, modelling advances, retrieval improvements, uncertainty characterisation, mission requirement support, community building, and uptake in international assessments. Socio economic impact will include, for example, industrial competitiveness, innovation spillovers, policy support, and broader societal and economic value.

tenderTitle: LISA-ITT-069 Payload Hoisting MGSE
tenderDescription:
The gravitational wave observatory LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) has been selected as ESA’s third large class mission (L-3) within the Cosmic Vision programme. LISA’s mission objective is to observe gravitational waves from space in the frequency band of 0.1 mHz to 1 Hz, not accessible from ground-based observatories. 
The mission architecture consists of a constellation of three spacecraft placed at the vertexes of a near-equilateral triangle with side length of about 2.5 million km (LISA Constellation). An overview of the LISA mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/LISA
OHB, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the LISA programme, building the industrial consortium.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the LISA Payload Hoisting MGSE.
The LISA Payload Hoisting MGSE shall provide multiple hoisting GSEs for flexible and safe handling of different LISA Payload sub-assemblies during AIT activities. The MGSEs will be used under ISO 5 cleanliness conditions and in direct contact with high performance optical instruments. Therefore, the GSEs shall ensure full instrument safety, and special care shall be taken in the selection of materials to comply with the magnetic cleanliness requirements of the LISA project.
The procurement of the LISA Payload Hoisting MGSE will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

tenderTitle: EARTH UPPER ATMOSPHERE FORECAST TOOL FOR MISSION DESIGN AND OPERATIONS EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a software for VLEO atmospheric environment models that could reduce mission design margins and risks of satellite loss by non-compensated atmospheric drag effects at low altitudes.Description: Atmospheric density increase during geomagnetically active periods is a well know phenomenon. However, the increase of atmospheric density is not well-constrained and predictableand becomes particularly troublesome for the early phases of spacecraft commissioning that rely on a very low altitude (e.g. 200 to300 km) initial orbit. To date, for general spacecraft design purposes, the ESA Space Environment Information System (SPENVIS) includes various Earth atmosphere and wind models, some of which also consider geomagnetic activity. Several upper-atmosphere co-exist butthere are no comprehensive model or database of atmospheric and thermospheric parameters allowing to capture intra- (local time, seasonal, solar and magnetospheric inputs-driven) and inter-model variabilities, in order to derive better informed engineering margins. In such context, the proposed activity aims to fill that gap by developing a software allowing to interrogate models and definevariability envelopes based on major variability drivers (e.g. solar events, seasonal effects etc.) useful for design and exploitationphases. Software outputs shall feed the existing Space Weather modelling network with relevant products. In addition, the activity will establish a method to build model-based, time-dependent, 3D atmospheric parameter snapshots in order to produce a database of relevant parameters (at least species densities, temperatures as a function of altitude), including variabilities over different timescales relevant to mission design and planning (e.g. daily to seasonal) as a function of local time and latitude. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review the existing state of the art models of the upper atmosphere, including preferably couplingeffects between the thermosphere / ionosphere system and solar inputs, as well as state of the art (e.g. ML based) methods allowingto capture atmospheric variability and temporal evolution as a function of external forcing (e.g. solar activity). - Define LEO/VLEO user and software requirements definition, including interfacing with relevant Space Weather tools and databases, and the capability toevolve as updated models and data become available. - Concept design, and a preliminary architecture design. - Develop and test critical functions to validate the approach. - Consolidate the design, full implementation and testing of the software. - Validatethe software by using independent data where possible and inter-models comparisons.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). tenderTitle: ECODESIGN HARNESS FOR SPACE APPLICATIONS -EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To design and assess the life cycle of an optimised harness including cables, connectors, and back-shell components, allmanufactured using eco-friendly processes and alternative materials.Description: Spacecraft harnesses are essential for power distribution, data transmission, and signal integrity within satellites and other spacecraft systems. However, conventional harness designs rely on materials and manufacturing techniques that have a significant environmental impact, such as PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene)-based insulation, gold and nickel plating, and energy-intensive production processes. The ecodesign harness initiative focuses on the development of a sustainable harness architecture, incorporating alternative materials and environmentally optimised production methods. This includes innovative approaches to conductors, insulation, jacket, connectors, accessories, tie bases, assembly processes and integration, all tailored for space qualification. This activity aims to minimise environmental impact while maintaining space-grade reliability and performance, contributing to the broader vision of sustainable space through responsible material selection, reduced emissions, and improved end-of-life strategies. A comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA) will be performed to comparethe environmental impacts of the optimised harness against conventional designs, from raw material extraction through to end-of-life,including phases such as manufacturing, integration, launch, and decommissioning. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Trade-off analysis and environmental impact assessment. - Key environmental contributors identification. - Optimisation actions and technical feasibility. - Characterisation and LCA validation.Deliverables: Breadboard, ReportProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). tenderTitle: GNC SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE FOR PARAFOIL FLIGHT  WIND KNOWLEDGE FUSION EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a robust, adaptive guidance framework for parafoil-based recovery systems based on the fusion of wind data from both ground-based measurements and onboard sensors.Description: Parafoil-based recovery systems offer a lightweight, low-cost, and reusable solution for space re-entry and payload delivery. They require advanced GNC strategies to achieve precise and reliable landings in highly dynamic atmospheric conditions. Their aerodynamic controllability and passive deployment make them suitable for various missions. However, achieving precise landings in real-world conditions remains challenging due to atmospheric variability, especially wind, which introduces uncertainty in trajectory prediction and landing dispersion. Accurate and timely wind knowledge is therefore not just a helpful input, but a critical enabler of parafoil performance and reliability. Current GNC systems often treat wind as a disturbance, relying on conservative margins or reactive filtering. This limits system performance, increases landing footprints, and misses opportunities for optimization. Crucially, there is a gap in the systematic use of wind dataforecasted, sensed, or inferredin guidance and navigation design. This activity addresses that gap with a GNC architecture that treats wind knowledge asa core element, integrated by design into both preflight planning and onboard adaptation. By continuously adjusting to atmospheric variations, this approach aims to enhance landing accuracy and improve system robustness to weather conditions. This activity explores wind-aware GNC through two synergistic layers: (1) ground-based wind profiling and forecasting for mission planning, and (2) onboard sensing and virtual estimation to refine wind knowledge in-flight. By fusing this data into navigation filters and adaptive guidance laws, the system dynamically adjusts trajectories, reduces dispersion, and exploits beneficial wind structures. This leads to more accurate and resilient landings. The output will be a modular GNC software prototype, validated in Monte Carlo simulations, and designed for future TRL scaling. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define GNC architecture, wind data levels, simulation environment, and test interfaces. - Develop wind estimation (onboard sensors, virtual sensing), integrate with navigation filters. - Design adaptive guidance using wind input, implement real-time trajectory updates. - Integrate full GNC stack, simulate full missions, and evaluate robustness to wind variability in a representative simulation environment.

tenderTitle: N2O SATELLITE OBSERVATION REQUIREMENTS - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is an important greenhouse gas that also contributes to stratospheric ozone depletion. This study aims at characterising the needs for space-based observations of atmospheric N2O, starting from a user and science perspective. Knowledge gaps are identified related to the N2O production and life cycle, its impact on stratospheric ozone, and its role in the Earth's radiation balance that can be addressed with the help of satellite observations, with a focus on information that can be provided from satellite observations. The study explores the space of requirements that satellite observations of atmospheric N2O (Level-2) and measurements of radiances at the top of the atmosphere (Level-1) would have to meet in order to contribute to addressing these knowledge gaps.

tenderTitle: SECONDARY HEAT EXCHANGER FOR COMBUSTION CHAMBER COOLING OF ROCKET ENGINES - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: The objective of this activity is to develop a cooling approach for steady state rocket engines to enable the use of more cost-effective materials. This should be achieved with the use of secondary heat exchange.Currently only two cooling approaches are used forrocket motor chamber design. Direct regenerative cooling with the propellants or much simpler radiative cooling. Regenerative cooling recovers energy lost in the radiative approach and offers both higher performance and, wider material options which is possible due to the lower operating temperature.Regenerative cooling is almost never limited by the sensible enthalpy, the temperature rise of the cooling propellants. It is typically limited by local effects in the cooling channel design. These effects come down to two factors the local geometry and the local vapor pressure of the coolant. The geometry is naturally constrained by the need for a rocketchamber shape.In the absence of local geometric options then the local vapor pressure can only be improved for a given propellant by driving up the local static pressure. This rules out many in-space applications where gas pressurized feed systems are the norm, the static pressure is too low. The power for high pressure pumps to regeneratively cool current spacecraft engines would require pumps more than 1.5 kWs. An alternative approach is to design a heat exchanger to transfer the heat from the wall of the combustion chamber to propellant indirectly. This has the advantage of allowing the design of specified cooling rates independent of the geometryor propellant feed conditions. Either end of the exchanger can be designed to operate at specified temperatures. This simplifies the material selection of the chamber and the transfer of energy to the propellant.A fixed temperature exchanger would have none of the limiting factors of a classical regeneratively cooled chamber. It could also simplify start up transient for many larger engine cycles. The more benign operating conditions would also allow for greater reusability; thermal gradients could be more tightly managed and more robust materials could be used, eliminating issues such as plasticity and deformations of the cooling channels. As statedearlier local conditions drive the failure in regenerative engines these are compounded when the engine flow conditions are dynamicwhen throttling. Lander engines tend to require deep throttle rates. Secondary heat exchangers operate outside these constraints and would maintain thermal integrity of deeper throttling designs. Similarly higher performance engine architectures such as aerospikes are inhibited from adoption due to the thermal complexity ofimplementing them compared to classical designs. Various ideas have been considered; however liquid metals are only one potential solution. Active pumping of a secondary coolant would also be feasible.This activity shall focus on the concept of secondary heat exchange design for high performance engine design and demonstrate a secondary heat exchanger unit by firing a representative breadboard. This would allow a greater exploitation of the propellant sensibleenthalpy than current regenerative approaches. In addition, secondary heat exchange would allow low pressure drop designs and enable actively cooled design applications where currently radiative cooling is mandated. Finally secondary heat exchange would allow theenergy to be exploited in other systems if required: repressurization, power recovery, etc. The activity encompasses the following tasks: Analysis of the state of the art of secondary heat exchanger options for combustion chamber applications. Develop and manufacture a breadboard of a secondary heat exchanger for combustion chamber. Demonstrate a secondary heat exchanger for combustion chamber design by firing a representative breadboard with heat exchanger or an appropriatesimulator. Validate the design tools toimplement such a chamber.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation offinancial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

tenderTitle: DISTRIBUTED ARRAY END-TO-END PAYLOAD SYSTEM ARCHITECTURES FOR PNT - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop innovative end-to-end payload system architectures, techniques and algorithms enabling large distributed arrays for PNT based on high-gain beamforming.Description: Large arrays of antennas and distributed arrays of antennas are being considered for the generation of very high-gain beamforming. In this case, the main objective is to achieve a high received power by the ground user receivers, such that high data rates can be supported per user. Large and distributed arrays can be considered for PNT, both for Earth and Spaced Service Volume users and applications. One clear expected advantage would be to achieve much larger received power on the user receivers than with current GNSS systems. This can be of interest in particular in harsh propagation conditions, including the presence of interference and jamming, or to reach very far-away space users/assets. The objective of this activity is to design techniques and algorithms to enable large distributed array satellite and payload (PL) system architectures/configurations for PNT. The focus will be on the generation of very high-gain beamforming, while ensuring the transmission of high-accuracy signals-in-space, even when wide-band signals are used. Both the transmission in L-band (reference) and alternative bands (e.g., S and Cbands) will be addressed. Additionally, the activity will investigate innovative ideas for the exploitation of the large distributedarray architecture for PNT purposes, leveraging concepts and operational modes exploited in other space applications like SyntheticAperture Radar (SAR) systems. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition and design of innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Implementation of the required tools/software enabling the assessment of the proposed techniques and algorithms; - Assessment/test of the different techniques and algorithms in simulated conditions; - Identification of themost promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained; - Definition of the proposed the way-forward to further matureeach of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Deliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. tenderTitle: PROPAGATION MODELS FOR THE CLUTTER LOSS IN FREQUENCY SHARING ANALYSIS EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop propagation models and improve their applicability for clutter loss on terrestrial and Earth-space paths to frequency sharing methods used by ESA and European frequency managers.Description: The development of terrestrial 5G systems has ledto the developments and updates of propagation models for what regards the effect of clutter on interference with space services andwith other Earth stations. The initial development done in ITU-R SG3 and in past TDE activities (ref. no. T507-601EF) focused in frequency bands used by passive EO missions, and by Earth stations for Space exploration and EO data downlink. These models are used for radio regulation frequency sharing analyses to determine the compatibility of services using radio spectrum. The frequency sharing analyses have specific needs, stemming from the considered system configuration (e.g. use of active antennas, coverage area etc.)On the other hand, clutter models can be relatively complex, as they depend on several system and stochastic parameters (e.g. frequency, elevation angle, height of the ground transmitter, characteristics of the clutter environment etc.). Therefore there is the needto improve clutter propagation models and to define their usage in to frequency sharing methods. To address this, this activity improves clutter loss models and defines the methods and the requirements for their use by frequency management engineers in system simulations to assess the compatibility of different radio services of the radio regulations and to perform the respective studies. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - State-of-the-art review and development plan, - Clutter model improvement and implementation, - Design and Implementation of system simulation for test-cases for sharing analyses, - Execution and analysis of test cases- Inputs for radio regulations and Conclusions Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. tenderTitle: ENHANCEMENT OF THE PHASE SPACE DENSITY OF LASER COOLED NEUTRAL STRONTIUM ATOMIC SYSTEMS - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To develop a system enhancement in the cold atom production rate, and reduction of the thermodynamic temperature, of atomic Strontium (Sr), using novel Magneto Optical Trap (MOT) laser cooling techniques and technologies. DescriptionThe availability of an efficient and simplified system to generate a laser cooled Sr sample, in large atom numbers at low temperature, is a key driver and project enabler for both laboratory systems and field deployable systems and those for space deployment. Laser cooled atoms are an essential resource for ultra-high stability Optical Atomic Frequency Standard (OAFS) and specifically for Sr, using the quantum forbiddenelectronic transition at 698nm. These optical systems have demonstrated performance metrics (fractional frequency stability) which are orders of magnitude superior to their laser cooled RF counterparts. This opens up experimental possibilities that cannot be realised with RF systems. An Atom Interferometer, using clouds of laser cooled Sr atoms has also been proposed, and demonstrated, in a laboratory environment. Such an instrument can measure gravitational waves, in a frequency band not possible by LISA or the ground-based systems (LIGO, VIRGO etc).This activity shall serve as a development approach for both of above mentioned applications for future space implementations. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Analysis of system performance requirements and parameters leading to an OAFS and mater wave interferometry (MWI) implemented with neutral Sr - Theoretical analysis of neutral Sr atomic system and implementation of system modelling tools to explore the implementation possibilities- Develop several viable design options leading to a PDR- Trade off the design options based primarily on flux enhancement and thermodynamic temperature reduction anddesign simplification; leading to CDR - Develop manufacturing, integration and test plan to verify the performance of a breadboardunit - Roadmap the development of the Sr MOT system for specific mission scenariosProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restrictedto non-prime contractors (incl. tenderTitle: IMPLEMENTATION OF AN ESERO (EUROPEAN SPACE EDUCATION RESOURCE OFFICE) IN LITHUANIA
tenderDescription: The European Space Education Resource Office (ESERO) is ESA's main project in the field of formal and non-formal early childhood, primary and secondary education. Under the coordination and steering of ESA and the national space agencies and offices, and with the support of national institutions and organizations active in the field of formal and non-formal education, the project aims at enabling capacity building in the school level teacher and educator communities and at designing and promoting the use of didactic resources and activities that make use of space as a context for the teaching and learning of STEM-related disciplines.National ESERO offices are established to implement activities across their hosting country. They are staffed by national education experts able to work in strong synergy and partnership with the national education authorities, stakeholders and networks, as well as the national space sector - an approach that has already proven to be effective and successful across 22 ESA Member States. In July 2026 a new ESERO will be established in an ESA Associate Member State - Latvia. Other countries have also now expressed interest in hosting an ESERO.

tenderTitle: DYNAMICALLY ADAPTIVE SYSTEM ARCHITECTURAL MODEL FOR CONNECTIVITY GAP AREAS IN 4G AND 5G TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.048) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
tenderDescription: The objective of this activity is to design, implement and evaluate different types of satellite system architectural models aimed at dynamically focusing available resources on coverage gaps in terrestrial 4G and 5G networks.Targeted Improvements:Achieving national regulator coverage and service objectives for direct-to-device services and enabling twice as efficient satellite resourcespooling over the service area.Description: Today there are coverage gaps of the terrestrial telecommunication system despite initiatives from non-European industries to provide supplementary coverage from space. Concentrating satellite connectivity exclusively on coverage gap areas (including low service areas) rather than aiming for satellite connectivity over a broad coverage has the potential to maximize the efficiency of the satellite system. It could offer an increased throughput which translates in reduced deployment costs per bit and higher quality of service for end users. Moreover, this approach could enable flexible resources allocation based on the population density as well as step up and step down of terrestrial connectivity services.This activity will design,implement and evaluate satellite system architectural models addressing non-uniform spatiotemporal traffic patterns in particular of handheld services. First, the activity will develop a high-resolution spatiotemporal traffic model, which shall consider available datasets and trend analyses of service requirements of Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) and their representative organisations, along with actual and target service coverage obligation set by National Regulation Administrations (NRAs) for terrestrial network gaps. The outputs of this model will be used to define coverage gaps from existing and planned terrestrial networks and space networks. The activity will then study and implement in a software prototype Distributed Satellite System (DSS) concepts for Frequency Range 1 (FR1) considering different orbits, multi-connectivity techniques (e.g. beam overlapping, coordinated multi-point etc) and infrastructure configurations (e.g. fractionated, swarm and federated concepts). System sizing optimizing the satellite resources will be carried out of at least 3 selected DSS concepts and the performance will be evaluated by simulation. The activity shall identify the most promising DSS concept and development roadmap considering complexity and system performance and the ability to accommodateopportunities beyond direct to device services. tenderTitle: DEPLOYABLE REFLECTOR FOR CUBE- AND SMALLSATS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:To design, manufacture and test a 1m deployable offset fed reflector antenna for small/cube satellites suitable formissions up to Ka-band.Description:A strong need for deployable Ka-band high gain antennas for cubesat and small satellites for various applications (TTC, payload data downlink, black hole observation VLBI (very long baseline interferometry), rain/precipitation observation and more) has been identified, hence, the importance to develop this technology to further maturity, which is currently notavailable in Europe.The antenna to be developed is 1m (scalable up to 3m) diameter deployable reflector antenna in an offsetconfiguration (reduction of aperture blockage) suitable for missions up to Ka-band. An engineering model including the reflector, the boom and the feed will be manufactured and tested demonstrating the critical functions of the element in a relevant environment. The testing will include, as a minimum, surface accuracy measurement after deployment, deployment test in representative environment (TVAC), vibration tests, thermal cycling, RF performance tests, passive intermodulation (PIM) tests at sample level.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Preliminary design (including de-risking activities of new, modified or unmodified (re-used) modules with lower TRL and/or higher risk)- Detailed design (including de-risking activities of unmodified (re-used) modules with lower TRL and/or higher risk).- Antenna manufacture and integration.- Test campaign and development roadmap.

tenderTitle: T709-903GA SELF-HEALING ARCHITECTURES FOR CYBER RESILIENT GROUND SEGMENT SYSTEMS (EXPRO+)
tenderDescription: Today, mission ground segment systems face increasingly sophisticated and fast-movingcyber threats that can evade static or rule-based detection tools and overwhelm traditionalrecovery procedures. As attacks grow more pervasive, dynamic and subtle, currentapproaches, such as rule-based or ticket driven responses struggle to react at the requiredspeed, resulting in prolonged attacker dwelltime and potential disruption of critical missionoperations, if an attack is detected at all.Real-time automated responses or self-healing' mechanisms, such as fall-back tosecure/minimum configurations, runtime policy/rule change, trusted state reconstitution, orrapid tear-down and re-deploy of compromised systems, can reduce the time required tocontain threats. The aim is to reduce attacker dwell time and maintain service continuityduring otherwise high impact incidents. This activity addresses that gap by developing anddemonstrating a proof-of-concept autonomous self-healing architecture tailored to thecritical mission operations ground segment. It will provide an adaptive resilience mechanismaddressing detection, isolation and recovery with an emphasis on service continuity. Moderntechnologies and techniques are to be explored including:- declarative infrastructure as code for cloud-agnostic redundancy and recovery automation- decoupled micro-service isolation and zero-trust architectures- secure root of trust and immutable system configuration restoration- failure prediction- adaptive response mechanisms leveraging machine learning.The proof-of-concept demonstrator will be integrated into a multi-mission, cloud nativeground segment scenario, leveraging existing (Cyber) Security Operations Centres((C)SOC) monitoring and diagnostic capabilities to ensure operational relevance. It willdemonstrate end to enddetection, isolation, and recovery in the context of missionmonitoring and control systems operating in the loop.

tenderTitle: AURION  ADVANCING UNDERSTANDING THROUGH RESEARCH AND INDUSTRY-ORIENTED CO-DESIGN OF NEW MISSIONS - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: AURION aims to establish a structured pre-Phase-0 co-design environment in which scientific ambition and industrial feasibility aredeveloped concurrently to define credible, innovative Earth Observation mission concepts.The activity targets mission concepts at SRL =3 that have not previously been assessed within ESA, and enables their maturation through joint science-industry system-level design, including early assessment of technical feasibility, cost drivers, and programmatic viability.AURION studies are characterised by:Joint science-industry leadership (mandatory co-design) Concurrent SRL and TRL maturationFocus on novel mission concepts, not incremental extensions Early integration of industrial feasibilityExplicit treatment of technical, cost, and programmatic riskSelected consortia shall perform integrated science-engineering co-design studies covering:Definition of measurement concept and observing principleExploration of mission architectures (orbit, geometry, constellation vs monolithic)Elaboration ofpreliminary Level-1 and Level-2 mission requirementsIdentification and maturation pathway of critical enabling technologies (TRL13+) Development of end-to-end data chain, including calibration and processing Preliminary cost and risk assessmentActivities shall remain strictly within pre-Phase-0, shall not converge prematurely to a single industrial solution, and shall maintain architectural optionality through structured trade-space exploration.

tenderTitle: T709-801GD DLT-BASED ACCESS MANAGEMENT FOR THE (CO-)OPERATION OF SHARED SPACE ASSETS (EXPRO+)
tenderDescription: There is an increasing trend towards collaboration among space agencies and a rapidly growingnumber of commercial space actors. This raises the scenario and challenge of how different partiescan cooperatively operate shared space assets through distributed access control mechanisms.The standard approach to manage access to a shared asset, e.g., hosted payloads, where one ofthe collaborating parties assumes full authority over the asset, while the other parties strictly rely onthis authority, may be too rigid for manyemerging use cases. Modern concepts such as launch rideshares, ground segments and platforms as a service models, or even token-based economiccommercialisation of space missions require a more fully collaborative approach.Thus, in the pursuit towards true collaboration and along trends such as web3 and Blockchain, thisactivity shall aim to demonstrate fully distributed identity and accessmanagement. DecentralisedLedger Technologies (DLT) shall be leveraged to support associated operations concepts andmanage credentials and policies for individual actors interacting with the space assets. DLTsolutions differ in key aspects regarding cybersecurity, performance and scalability thus a specificemphasis shall be placed on measuring overheads in terms of data, network traffic and computingpower in the constrained environment of space systems. DLT applications shall be identified andtested in support of:- managing credentials and access to collaborating space assets in a distributed manner- public key certificates including revocationand enforcement (e.g., revoke access of a specificoperator)- distributed identity establishment (e.g., how parties trust each othersendorsement of actors)- cryptographic key management and root of trust aspects (e.g., securely managing keys via trustedhardware and use of merkle-tree hashs and proof of inclusion concepts)

tenderTitle: HIGH PERFORMANCE INSULATING MATERIALS FOR L4 ENCELADUS LANDER - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: To assess the potential use of alternative insulating materials (e.g. aerogel) to improve the thermal performance of classical MLI,and sustaining the extreme environments applicable to L4 Enceladus Lander.Current thermal insulation solutions for Solar System missions are mainly based onconductive and radiative insulation (e.g. JUICE Nomex reinforced MLI), or includeconvective insulation function, not assessed for L4 Enceladus Lander environments (e.g.ExoMars Upilex foam). Due to the L4 Lander extreme environment on Enceladus (lowtemperatures, potential interaction with plumes, snow and/or ice and challenging landingconditions), the use of classical MLI technology, even with an efficient, reinforced designsuch as the one used in JUICE, is probably insufficient to achieve the required thermalinsulation and reduce the use of electrical heating. Heaters use is to be minimized (with atarget of 0 W), as the electrical power consumption is directly linked to the mass andlifetime span of the Lander on Enceladus surface. In addition, the selected thermal controltechnologies shall ensure nominal performance while keeping physical integrity (stringentmechanical loads during landing) and fulfilling mass, EMC, planetary protection and otherrequirements of the mission.Potential technologies such as Aerogel have been identified in similar missions such asMars Pathfinder ("(...). The WEB is a thermal isolating composite structure with cocuredthermal control surfaces and an ultralightweight hydrophobic solid silica aerogel whichminimizes conduction and radiation. This design provides excellent thermal insulation atlow gas pressures and meets the structural requirements for spacecraftlaunch loads andfor a 60 g impact landing at Mars without damage to the insulation or structure. (...)",https://www.jstor.org/stable/44725574). The use of these technologies or alternative onesneeds being assessed for L4 Enceladus Lander. The activity encompasses the followingtasks:Requirements consolidation and assessment of state of the art- Design of breadboard and associated test bench- Manufacture of breadboard, test bench- Execution of tests and exploitation of results- Conclusions elaboration and roadmap for further development towards a flight applicationThe outcomes of this activity are extendable to other planetary missions.

tenderTitle: DETERMINISTIC ETHERNET SPACE TIME-SENSITIVE NETWORKING SOFT IP CORE  - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:To develop a technology independent soft IP (Intellectual Property) core that complies with the aerospace profile of TSN(Time Sensitive Networking).Description:TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) and TTE (Time Triggered Ethernet) are the two technologies that allow to deliver determinism and quality of service on top of standard Ethernet networks. Since TTE can be considered relatively closed technology (i.e. proprietary solution, patents pending on the technology), since a few years TSN is emerging as a potential successor of that technology. TSN is IEEE supported set of standards that implements wide range of quality of services (i.e. reliability, determinism, mixed criticality traffic, redundancy, time synchronization) on top of the standard Ethernet protocols. TSN benefits from Ethernet Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) tools/ecosystem, it is free of patents and is being introduced step-by step in industrial applications (automotive/industrial) and aerospace domain (IEEE P802.1DP - TSN for Aerospace Onboard Ethernet Communications). Although TSN is very successful in the automotive/industrial sector, in space applications TSNis still being considered as low TRL technology. Many current and future Exploration and Space Transportationmissions are considering Ethernet-based networks for the data-handling communication bus. Having thistechnology available for future ESA missions is seen as a key driver for future missions. The aim of this activity Is to develop an IP core that contains the core functionalities of Time-Sensitive Networking needed for space applications. Although the set of TSN standards is very wide, there are several on-going activities aiming attailoring of TSN for space applications. Having an TSN IP tailored to space applications could be considered asa key enabler of this technology in future ESA and national missions.The following technical aspects shall be considered:- Development of End-system IP Core. Switch IP core is out of scope of this activity- One or two Ethernet ports shall be supported.- Host integration: AXI4 lite for registers and IP configuration, and AXI4 stream for packet data- The IP shall support 10/100/1000Mbps speeds. 10Gbps is considered optional.- Compatible and configurable with various PHY interfaces (i.e. MII/GMII/RGMIII).- To be developed as technology independent VHDL.- To be implemented and validated in 2 FPGA/ASIC technologies (preferable NG-Ultra/Ultra300 andMicrochip Polarfire).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- TSN IP core requirements identification and development of the high-level architecture of the TSN soft IP core.- Prototype development and integration into a representative Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) based network platform.- Verification and validation targeting high speed use cases- TSN soft IP core release and related documentation.Deliverables: Prototype, Report, SoftwareApplication/Need Date: Exploration and Space Transportation missions. Mission Classification: alpha, beta,gamma, delta

tenderTitle: MEASUREMENT AND MODELLING OF THE ATTITUDE OF METOP AND SENTINEL 1 TO PREPARE FOR ERASE PHASE A - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Summary Description The proposed activity is will support the preparation for the ERASE Phase A. ERASE aims to prepare the removalof large, non-cooperative and unprepared objects in low Earth orbit, initially considering Metop and Sentinel-1 targets (starting with METOP-A and S1B, both being decommissioned), thereby supporting ESA's Space Safety Programme and the transition towards a circular economy in space. This activity will establish and demonstrate ground-based laser-ranging measurement, modelling and analysis capabilities to characterise the attitude state and tumbling behaviour of non-cooperative, unprepared targets, with initial focus on Metop and Sentinel-1 targets. The output is essential and urgent for the ERASE Phase A study. Without this information available at the start of Phase A, there is a risk that the technical feasibility of the mission is incorrectly assessed. The target spin rate is adesign driver for the servicer delta-V and operations timeline, the relative navigation subsystem, and the robotic capture sizing and loads. The spin-axis orientation drives the safe approach direction and the capture strategy. In addition, the probability of very low spin-rate cases must be understood, as such cases may lead to long durations in unfavourable attitude conditions for target power generation, thermal control and ground contact. The challenge is that the targets are not prepared with cooperative markers or laser retro-reflectors that would facilitate attitude reconstruction. The attitude state must therefore be reconstructed from non-cooperative laser-ranging observables, making use of time-of-flight/range measurements, return-signal characteristics, pass geometry, target geometry, known or estimated surface properties, and attitude-dynamics modelling. Where beneficial, the laser-ranging data maybe complemented by passive optical or radar observations.The activity will assess the feasibility, achievable accuracy and uncertainty of attitude determination and dynamics-based propagation from ground. It will characterise and propagate target dynamics, in particular spin rate and spin-axis orientation, and will provide statistically meaningful uncertainty envelopes for ERASE Phase A design trade-offs. The activity will also prepare the capability to perform repeated attitude characterisation campaigns in support of ERASE. The attitude state of non-cooperative targets may evolve over time due to environmental torques and target-specific dynamics; therefore, measurements may be required not only during the present feasibility phase, but also before launch, to confirm that the target conditions remain within the design assumptions, and potentially at intermediate points during mission preparation. A dedicated task will assess the applicability of the developed measurement and modelling methods to a broader range of large, unprepared, non-cooperative low Earth orbit targets beyond Metop and Sentinel-1, identifying the key target properties, observation conditions and limitations that determine feasibility.

tenderTitle: TALLINN HELSINKI OPTICAL RELAY (THOR) TESTBED (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.092) -  REQUESTED
tenderDescription: The objective of the activity is to define and develop a free space optical communication testbed suitable for testing a cross-atmospheric optical connectivity in the horizontal link between Tallinn and Helsinki. Targeted Improvements: To create a terrestrial testbed capability allowing for demonstration and long-term communication testing. The testbed will provide information on the long-distance atmospheric channel and the stability of the optical links in fixed and mobile configuration. The testbed facility will support new technology developments for optical and quantum satellite communication. Description: Most of satellite constellations developed these days include intersatellite links. However, the adaptation of cross-atmospheric links remains to be progressing slowly. One of the challenges is the limited availability of outdoor, free-space testbeds. The proposed testbed facility will enable testing over the long-distance, cross-atmospheric channel created between two stations located in Tallinn and Helsinki. The testbed will allow for fixed-points free-space optical connection, demonstrating and validating a continuous datalink between interoperable terminals and transceivers aligned with satellite optical communication standards. The testbed should allow to collect and analyse information on the atmospheric channel over multiple seasons. It should monitor weather conditions and investigate beam dissipation dynamics and various mitigation strategies. The spatially dynamic optical links will also be demonstrated to test and validate a free-space optical datalink between moving terminals. The testbed should foresee and facilitate testing of quantum-encrypted free-space optical communication capabilities. The preparation to demonstrate data-relay with a satellite link is planned to be included in the activity.

tenderTitle: AEROTHERMODYNAMIC CHARACTERIZATION OF GAS-SURFACE INTERACTIONS FOR HYPERSONIC UPPER STAGE RECOVERY VEHICLES - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To model the hypersonic flow around critical points of the re-entry of a upper stage vehicle, accounting for the catalytic properties of a Si-O-C ceramics, and for the chemical modifications of the surface exposed to the air.Description: There is a renewed interest in the implementation of reusable vehicles for in-orbit operation. A critical aspect in the lifetime of a space vehicle is to improve the durability of the thermal protection structures, to limit the replacement of the thermal shield. Ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTC) materials, based on the Si-O-C compounds with dedicated coatings (boride, molybdenum etc.) demonstrated to be a good choice, due to their capability to resist and survive above 1500 K. To fully evaluate the response of any material in suchextreme operating conditions, it is also imperative to determine the catalysis in high temperature gas, strongly affecting the surface heat flux. Moreover, the interaction of the material coatings with dissociated gases such as oxygen and nitrogen, induces variations on the material properties. The technology to be developed is to model accurately the complex physical processes at the gas surface interface during ascent and descent, in which different coatings are experimental tested validating the predictive capabilitiesof the numerical models. The model will include advanced kinetics, using a hybrid state-to-state -Multi-Temperature (StS-MT) derived from the StS, where the vibrational degrees of freedom are described by the vibrational temperature, while electronic excited states are treated as independent species, in order to estimate the radiative properties. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Development of a chemical model of air interacting with the Si-O-C ceramic material, in dissociation regime; - Development of a hybrid StS-MT kinetic model - Develop a database for thermodynamic properties and of transport cross sections for air including Si-O-C species - Implementation of kinetics and transport in a numerical tool for hypersonic flows for the reliable simulation, flat plate/coupons - Model chemical gas surface interaction, chemical stability, roughness, thickness, stability of coatings, catalyst by experimental plasma testing of different samples, thermal optical properties, emission spectroscopy - Numerical modelling and testing thermal bounding of the silica based substrate bounding with the coating, testing of the attachment devices - Evaluation of differentceramics suitable for the orbital entry conditions.

tenderTitle: STANDARDISED FUNCTIONAL POWER CONTROL MODULES FOR CONSTELLATIONS SATELLITES (ARTES AT 4F.182) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, build and test standardised functional power modules resulting in a Commercial-off-the-Shelf-based Power Conditioning and Distribution Unit (PCDU) consisting of the solar array regulator, the controller module, the battery management module, the power distribution module and the deployment module, for telecomsconstellations applications.Techniques and technologies to improve the power efficiency will be studied and implemented as well as health monitoring capabilities as needed to comply with Zero Debris requirements.Targeted Improvements: - Power module manufacturing time reduction by 80% andreduction of risk of production delay- PCDU efficiency improvement of up to 15% thanks to solar regulator efficiency improvement by10 percentage points and 50% improvement of the power distribution module.Description: Typical space power units are designed andbuilt to comply with project-specific specifications. As a consequence, manufacturers implement different solutions, which are notcompatible nor interoperable. Therefore, a specific power unit can only be built by a specific manufacturer. When large number of units have to be built this often poses a supply chain challenge. APA is an advanced power architecture standard developed with EuropeanPrimes with the potential to overcome supply chain bottlenecks. It aims at standardising the electrical and mechanical interfaceofmodular power distribution units and hence unit production can easily be spread among multiple suppliers.This activity will identify opportunities for standardisation of power control modules for constellations satellites taking the APA and other available standards as a starting point. The activity will then design, manufacture and test key functional power modules for a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) based Power Conditioning and Distribution Unit (PCDU),consisting of the solar array regulator, the controller module,the battery management module, the distribution module and the deployment module, for telecoms constellations applications. Techniquesand technologies to improve the power efficiency will be studied. This shall include wide band-gap semiconductor technology and theuse of switchedlatching current limiters. tenderTitle: NAVISP-EL1-131-CHIP SCALE OPTICAL ATOMIC CLOCK FOR PNT APPLICATIONS EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Development of a compact optical atomic clock module (physics package) for PNT applications. The activity will design, manufacture,and test an Engineering Model (EM) of a chip-scale optical clock exploiting an atomic optical transition to achieve 10 improved stability (target timing drift 10-30 ns/day) versus existing microwave clocks. The clock will provide a stabilized optical frequencyoutput in a low-power (< 5 W), compact device. Tasks include detailed thermo-mechanical design for robust operation in harsh environments, definition of low-power control electronics requirements and autonomous operation algorithms, assembly of the optical clock physics package, and development of Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) to control and test the EM. The EM will undergo performance verification in ambient and thermal conditions to demonstrate its stability, targeting TRL 4-5 and paving the way for future space-qualified ultra-stable timing solutions for navigation and timing systems.
