tenderTitle: ERS-EO ALPSTAR FEDERATED LAYER DEFINITION AND PRELIMINARY IMPLEMENTATION (ACTIVITY 2B)
tenderDescription: Activity 2B addresses Phase B of the Alpstar Federation Layer, aiming to consolidate requirements, architecture, and prototype validation for a federated, multi stakeholder space system. Building on the MRD 2.0, this phase will define and specify all functional, technical, and security requirements of the Federation Layer, including secure interfaces with commercial service providers and Alpstar Nodes via unidirectional "diode" connections.The activity encompasses the full design of the Alpstar system architecture and the development and demonstration of a User Ground Segment prototype. Comprehensive specifications will be produced for all major Federation Layer components, ensuring interoperability, security, and scalability across federated participants.The procurement also includes the acquisition of a minimum of three months of satellite data, necessary to support validation and testing of the Ground Segment prototype under operationally representative conditions.A key deliverable of this phase is a User Ground Segment prototype featuring:A role based user interface, enabling differentiated access and operational views.An initial implementation of the Digital Governance Agent (DGA), enforcing a first set of provisional federation rules and acting as the central mission management and planning capability.The Alpstar Federated Layer shall integrate the following core functionalities:Digital Governance Agent (DGA)for federation rule enforcement and central mission managementSecure Data Pooling Service for controlled dissemination of observation resultsFederated Ledger to record and audit transactionsStandardised APIs interfacing with Nodes (FOS and PDGS)Federated Data Lake hosted in a cloud environmentVirtual Constellation Management for coordinated asset utilisationFederated CatalogueCross federation taskingNATO FMN / Joint ISR tasking interfaces routed to AlpstarRole based user interfaceFederation dashboard for operational and governance oversightWith a target duration of 12 months, the expected outcomes of Activity 2B include:Complete specifications of the Federation LayerDefinition of the Federation Layer architectureRough Order of Magnitude (ROM)cost estimate for implementationIdentification of the industrial consortiumDevelopment plan and integrated scheduleDemonstration of the User Ground Segment prototypeThis phase will provide the technical, architectural, and organisational foundations required to progress Alpstar toward a fully operational, secure, and governed federated space capability.

tenderTitle: LISA-ITT-041 Thermal & Contamination Protection System
tenderDescription:
The gravitational wave observatory LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) has been selected as ESA’s third large class mission (L-3) within the Cosmic Vision programme. LISA’s mission objective is to observe gravitational waves from space in the frequency band of 0.1 mHz to 1 Hz, not accessible from ground-based observatories. 
The mission architecture consists of a constellation of three spacecraft placed at the vertexes of a near-equilateral triangle with side length of about 2.5 million km (LISA Constellation). An overview of the LISA mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/LISA
OHB, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the LISA programme, building the industrial consortium.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the LISA Core Assembly Thermal and Contamination Protection (LCA TCP) System.
The LCA TCP System’s primary function is to thermally decouple critical components within LCA from LISA platform. Secondary function is the protection of these same components from both particle and light contamination. TCP System is considered critical for achieving and maintaining the required performance of the LISA payload throughout the mission, by creating and maintaining specified operational environment within the LCA both on ground and in orbit.
The procurement of the LCA Thermal and Contamination Protection System will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

tenderTitle: EUROPEAN TERABIT PER SECOND ETHERNET PACKET SWITCH/ROUTER IP CORE FOR MULTI-ORBIT CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 5C.540)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop, manufacture and test an Ethernet switch/router Intellectual Property (IP)core and test chip supporting layers 1 to 3 packet processing for constellations. The IP core shall be developed, implemented on a test chip using the optimal UDSM ASIC technology node(s) selected as part of this activity to achieve the desired performance, and tested using a validation breadboard.Targeted Improvements: Enabling a European or Canadian source of terabit class ethernet switch/routers for multi-orbit constellation applications.Description: Cost sensitive, high volume multi-orbit constellation solutions require a tailored ethernet packet switch/router adapted to high data rates (at and above 100 Gbps), number of ports (16 and more) and supported protocols. An ethernet switch/router, scalable in data rate and number of ports and supporting layer 1 to 3 protocols, is not available from a European or Canadian supplier. Existing commercial solutions cannot be readily adapted to the needs of satcom applications in low earth orbit and multi-orbit constellations.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach. In Phase 1, an ethernet switch/router IP core shall be developed utilising ultra-deep sub-micron (UDSM) ASIC technology (targeting 7nm or below) to achieve 1 terabit per second data throughput for low earth orbit and multi-orbit constellation applications. The data rateper port and number of ports forming a channel shall be configurable to suit multiple applications (configurable number of ports from 4 to at least 16 ports, with configurable port data rate from 1Gbps to at least100Gbps per port). Multi-protocol label switchingand the internet protocol shall be supported. Phase 1 will conclude with the completed IP core design, verified and synthesised in the design environment, to generate the ASIC test chip tape-out files ready for fabrication. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 2,000 kEuro.In the second phase, the IP core will be implemented in the selected UDSM ASIC technology as an ASIC test-chip (via a Multi Project Wafer Run or shared Full Mask Run). A validation breadboard shall be designed and built to undertake performance testing of thetest chip. The test chip shall be representative of a scaled version of a final product and shall be tested in relevant environment.IP cores developed in this activity shall be available for further development by ESA Member State and Canadian industries at fair and reasonable market conditions.

tenderTitle: 5G DISTRIBUTED UNIT PROCESSOR AND ASSOCIATED NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORK G-NODEB SOFTWARE (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5A.099) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture, and test a processor breadboard and associated software implementing a distributed unit (DU) onboard a satellite. TheDU will implement Radio Link Control (RLC) and Medium Access Control (MAC) functions, optimized for Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN), to address processing, memory andpower constraints, as well as service needs in terms of cells and user numbers The feasibility and implementation of control unit (CU) functions on the 5G g-NodeB (gNB)should be addressed by the activity depending on the selected 5G system split and targeted system capacityTargetedImprovements: - Increase the DU throughput by a factor of 10 with respect to currently existing terrestrial network solutions (TN) implemented on space representative hardware.- Increase by a factor of 10 the number of cells handled by the DU, with respect to existing TN solutions.Description: Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs) require optimized handling of link-layer functions to mitigate the effects of long propagation delays, fluctuating signal conditions, and limitedbandwidth. Conventional NTNs rely on extensive ground infrastructure to manage link-layer functions such as scheduling, retransmission control, and resource allocation.Implementing full CU/DU on-board with high throughput is currently unfeasible due to the high system bandwidth to route and the limited processing power available.This activity shall develop a high-throughput (target 100 Gbps) satellite router breadboard, integrating an onboard CU/DU implemented on a radiation-tolerant multi-coreprocessor.This activity will design, manufacture, and test a processor breadboard and associated software implementing a distributed unit (DU) onboard a satellite.The Radio Link Control (RLC) layer will provide:1. Segmentation and reassembly optimized for dynamic satellite link conditions.2. Retransmission control managed onboard to reduce latency and dependency on ground stations.The Medium Access Control (MAC) layer will handle:1. Onboard scheduling and resource allocation to optimize time-frequency resource use.2. Adaptive HARQ (Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request) to balance error correction and latency.3. Inter-beam coordination to optimize multi-beam traffic distribution. The CU shall perform real-time processing, ensuring efficient and reliable network operation withoutexcessive feeder link traffic. Engineering tasks include system architecture definition, hardware / software integration, and performance validation through breadboardtesting in a representative NTN environment.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

tenderTitle: T309-801GD MULTI-ASSET DISTRIBUTED SIMULATIONS (EXPRO+)
tenderDescription: Currently multi-asset simulations of exploration missions comprised of i.e. robotic assets,orbiters/relays and ground data systemsare performed individually and mostly in isolation byindividual sites with respective simulators for each asset. The goal of this activity is to investigatemulti-asset, distributed simulations capabilities for full end-to-end mission simulations of futureexploration missions spanning lander, orbiters, relays and surface assets in different locations.This activity investigates the various scenarios (i.e. current ExoMars simulation architectures, futureneeds of the Sample Fetch Rover (SFR) and European Large Logistic Lander (EL3) missions) andhow, within their respective mission scenarios, simulation systems can be distributed, synchronizedand orchestrated either in local (i.e. data center) environments, or across different agencies orindustrial partners.The challenge to beaddressed is to achieve the capability to execute full mission segments (suchas full egress campaigns) with all distributed teams and experts - usually distributed over differentagencies and industrial partners in a as realistic as possible set-up, meaning interactions,coordination and real-time data during the simulation shall be available to all actors within thesimulation. Various technological frameworks exist to interconnect simulators on the technical level.However, this activity shall specifically focus on thecoordination aspects, synchronousmanagement or orchestration that is required and suitable above the pure interfaces level to realizesuch distributed simulations. To validate defined architectures, using agile developmentmethodologies this activity aims at developing a proof of concept to demonstrate keyrecommendations of this activity. The final architecture and technology recommendations that couldsupport future SFR and EL3 mission simulation needs is captured in a roadmap for theirintroduction.

tenderTitle: ADHA INSTRUMENT CONTROLLER UNIT (ICU) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:To develop an ADHA-compliant Instrument Controller Unit (ICU) usable standalone or with standard ADHAhardware for Earth, exploration, science, and navigation missions.Description:The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) is a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primesand data handling equipment suppliers. It includes the definition of an architecture for data handling unit basedon standard module functions. A standard module procurement flow has been defined -- as well as astandardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent development ofinteroperable modules that can be connected in ADHA units. This activity aims to develop an ADHA-compatibleICU (Instrument Control Unit), with integrated Data Processing Unit(s) (DPUs). The modules target the overall control functions of an instrument with several secondary units (FEE units, mechanism control units, cryocooler unit, etc). The modules will at least include an ICU processor module, and instrument I/O module(s). The ICU processor module shall be capable to act as the system controller of an ADHA unit, running high-levelinstrument application software and providing standard high-level interfaces for connection to the spacecraftplatform units, or other instruments and implementing all the necessary functions to control peripheral ADHAmodules in the unit, including network routing capabilities. The I/O modules willcover lower-level interface functions such as additional low-speed digital interfaces (CAN, RS422/RS485, etc), and discrete interfaces(HPCs, thermistor readout, heater control, secondary power, etc) and others typically found in an ICU unit.The ICU will be basedon state-of-the-art technologies, offering a higher level of integration and performancecompared to previous generation products, and be able to perform e.g. advanced (AI-based) FDIR methodsfor the monitoring and control of a payload.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Use case analysis of instrument control units for instruments on institutional missions.- Modules requirements analysis (use case analysis, ADHA documents, ADHA ICU draft specification),including functional split between ICU processor module and I/O modules.- ICU architecture design and key components trade-off and selection.- Modules engineering model design, including electrical, firmware, and base software.- Modules engineering model manufacturing.- Modules engineering model functional and performance verification and validation.- Validation testing of modules using an ADHA backplane, in an ADHA unit rack.- Performancebenchmarks and end-to-end data handling demonstration.Deliverables: Engineering Model, Report

tenderTitle: EFFECTS OF THE SPATIO-TEMPORALLY VARYING ATMOSPHERE ON SAR IMAGING: THE IONOSPHERE CASE - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To derive more accurate expression of atmosphere irregularities effects with a focus on the ionosphere, and devise mitigation techniques for both geo- and sun-synchronous SAR imaging systemsDescription: For Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) systems the atmospheric turbulence is generally assumed to be time-invariant during the synthetic aperture time due to itsshort duration. Such assumption is not always correct, as horizontal atmospheric drifts and vortices exist. Especially for SAR systems at low frequency (P-Band, L-Band), SAR operating on repeat-track basis, geo-synchronous SAR systems characterised by long integration time and extensive imaging scene, the ionosphere can have an important role on the performance. Furthermore, both temporal andspatial variations of the ionosphere have to be jointly taken into account, which further complicates their characterisation. Therefore, the effects of the flowing ionospheric irregularities need to be investigated, aiming in particular to image shifts, defocusing and repeat-track interferometry. The aim of this activity is to provide a comprehensive analysis to evaluate effects of both spatial variation and flowing ionospheric irregularities on SAR systems operating both at P-, L- and C-band. In particular, the ionospheric scintillations, which act remarkably in the polar cap and equatorial zone at night need to be considered. The Ionosphere characterisation shall originate from previous developments, analyses performed in the framework of previous missions developments and from knowledge built up in the navigation community. This activity encompasses the following tasks: -Analytical models of the physical effects of spatial-temporally ionospheric background variations on the SAR signal. - Assessment of the impacts on the SAR performancesdemonstrating, both theoretically and numerically, the geometric fidelity, focusing aspect and interferometry quality (i.e., relative image shifts and the decorrelation of interferometric pairs, interferometric phase screen errors). - Validation of the models andof the performance analysis using ionospheric monitoring measurements (i.e., Global Positioning System). - Develop mitigation techniques. - The implementation of the aforementioned components in a software framework. The methods developed in this activity are expected to be developed in such a way that they can be later broadened to other atmospheric effects such as tropospheric scintillations. Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member Statescan access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SMEs RD Entities. tenderTitle: S3-PD-01 NEOMIR PHASE B1
tenderDescription: The purpose of this activity is to study in detail the system and subsystem requirements for a planetary defence mission that aims at building a space-based infrared telescope dedicated to detection and characterisation of Near-Earth Objects (NEOs) that approach from the direction of the Sun. The mission builds on extensive work done by the Agency and European industry between 2022 and 2026. The target is to reach a consolidated mission and satellite architecture, finalize the major trade-offs and generate system and subsystem level requirements. In particular, the study will provide a consolidated spacecraft design and payload interface supported by detailed analyses and prepare the implementation phase including the establishment of the spacecraft development plan, preparation activities for Phase B2/C/D/E1 procurement, and cost estimates. The study will be carried out in two phases: one phase of 18months with a goal of reaching the objectives of an SRR-level review, and an additional optional 6-months phase that will aim at ingesting additional data fed by the Agency on the payloads into the system level design.

tenderTitle: EGV-PILOT: GEODETIC FOUNDATIONS FOR FUTURE EARTH OBSERVATION - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: EGV Pilot is an ESA pilot study aimed at structuring, mapping and assessing the geodetic foundations required to support future Earth Observation missions and Earth system science. The activity focuses on the role of geodetic observations and products as foundational enablers for Earth system monitoring, mission preparation, and the generation of long term geodetic data records. It builds on internationally coordinated developments on Essential Geodetic Variables (EGVs), in particular within GGOS and IAG, and translates these advances into an ESA-relevant framework aligned with the Earth Observation Science Strategy (EOSS), FutureEO missions, and other ESA programmatic elements. The study will establish clear traceability between geodetic requirements, products, observing systems and future EO missions. It will assess the readiness and maturity of geodetic observations and products, identify missing or degraded capabilities, and analyse how future ESA space and ground segment infrastructures could strengthen the geodetic foundations. Explicit consideration will be given to synergies with ESA missions such as GENESIS and NGGM/MAGIC, as well as to preparedness for integration into Digital Twin Earth.

tenderTitle: SUB-MM WAVE NOISE SOURCES FOR INTERNAL CALIBRATION SUB-SYSTEMS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To evaluate the capability of heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) technology (such SiGe as and/or InP) as an internal calibrator noise source at sub-mm wave frequencies and manufacture a heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT) based noise sources at two selected frequencies such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz.Description: Microwave radiometer calibration routine onboard a satellite is currently based on the measurement of external well known reference targets such as cold sky and onboard blackbody target. However, external calibration implies complex moving mechanics and long calibration cycles which are non-optimum from system performance perspective and therefore set certain limitations to instrument performance. Considerable improvements in smaller fluctuation of noise power density are foreseen by complementing or replacing the mechanically switched quasi-optical external calibration systems by internal calibration sub-systems (ICSS) based on electrically switched active semiconductor devices. Semiconductor based noise sources (cold or hot) are key blocks in these ICSS units which will benefit developments of future EO sounders and imagers on small platforms and cube-sats as well as multipixel imagers on bigger platforms. ICSS concept based active cold-loads have already been adopted in Copernicus Imaging Radiometer (CIMR). At higher mm-wave frequencies, hot load -based ICSS's are currently being developed for applications at 89 GHz and 183 GHz based on noise diodes and between 200-250 GHz based on HBTs. Development of a HEMT-based noise source is ongoing at 325 GHz. This activity aims to manufacture a breadboard of a noise source waveguide modules based on HBT technology (e.g. SiGe/InP/GaAs) at two selected sub-mm frequencies of interest for future EO instruments, such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz. The stability of the HBT-based noise sources will be compared with counterparts built on different technologies by means of theoretical assessment and experimental results where available. The HEMT technology provides advantage having the highest frequency capability as anoise source due to its high transition frequency which is already in 1 THz region. However, the anticipated advantage of HBT in comparison to HEMT is its inherently smaller fluctuation of noise power density - a key parameter for a calibrator. The recent developments in HBT technologies (both SiGe and InP) and their frequency capability open possibilities to implementation of a HBT noise source up to sub-mm region which would be a very desirable component for a stable ICSS's. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Noise source requirements definition from system level - Preliminary to critical design of a noise source waveguide modules basedon HBT technology at two selected sub-mm frequencies such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz - Manufacturing and characterization of the breadboardDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

Considerable improvements in smaller fluctuation of noise power density are foreseen by complementing or replacing the mechanically switched quasi-optical external calibration systems by internal calibration sub-systems (ICSS) based on electrically switched active semiconductor devices. Semiconductor based noise sources (cold or hot) are key blocks in these ICSS units which will benefit developments of future EO sounders and imagers on small platforms and cube-sats as well as multipixel imagers on bigger platforms. ICSS concept based active cold-loads have already been adopted in Copernicus Imaging Radiometer (CIMR). At higher mm-wave frequencies, hot load -based ICSS's are currently being developed for applications at 89 GHz and 183 GHz based on noise diodes and between 200-250 GHz based on HBTs. Development of a HEMT-based noise source is ongoing at 325 GHz. This activity aims to manufacture a breadboard of a noise source waveguide modules based on HBT technology (e.g. SiGe/InP/GaAs) at two selected sub-mm frequencies of interest for future EO instruments, such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz. The stability of the HBT-based noise sources will be compared with counterparts built on different technologies by means of theoretical assessment and experimental results where available. The HEMT technology provides advantage having the highest frequency capability as anoise source due to its high transition frequency which is already in 1 THz region. However, the anticipated advantage of HBT in comparison to HEMT is its inherently smaller fluctuation of noise power density - a key parameter for a calibrator. The recent developments in HBT technologies (both SiGe and InP) and their frequency capability open possibilities to implementation of a HBT noise source up to sub-mm region which would be a very desirable component for a stable ICSS's. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Noise source requirements definition from system level - Preliminary to critical design of a noise source waveguide modules basedon HBT technology at two selected sub-mm frequencies such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz - Manufacturing and characterization of the breadboardDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

tenderTitle: T512-900GS CO-PHASING OF SEGMENTED MIRROR TELESCOPES FOR FREE-SPACE TO FIBERBASED QUANTUM COMMUNICATION (EXPRO+)
tenderDescription: Large optical antennas provide higher gain and sensitivity, ensure high data transmission rates,improve weak-light signal detection and are therefore necessary in photon starving regimesapplications as interplanetary, deep space and quantum communication. Segmenting the mainmirror is a very cost-effective solution when building large telescopes. However, large collectingareas of superior optical quality per se are not sufficient to achieve the alignment performancerequired to transmit entangled photons over long distances without decoherence. Co-phasingdifferent mirror segments with the accuracy required for quantum communication protocolsconstitutes an acknowledged challenge.This activity aims to develop, test, and validate a breadboard co-phasing system for segmentedmirror telescopes for single mode fiber coupling, supporting next-generation quantumcommunication networks, long-distance optical links, and turbulence-free telescope operations. Thesystem shall be suitable for the alignment of large (6 m and above) segmented mirror antenna andshall grant the wavefront distortions, focus, and tip-tilt continuous correction. The system shallactively adjust themirror positions to compensate for thermal, mechanical, gravitational flexure, andother environmental disturbance to enhance beam quality, coupling efficiency, reduce optical losses,maintain interferometric stability and improve single-photon detection efficiency to support satellitebased Quantum Key Distribution (QKD).Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors(incl. SMEs). tenderTitle: NAVISP-EL1-130-ROBUST GNSS TRACKER FOR SENSITIVE APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards system is designed to verify States' legal undertakings to use nuclear material for exclusively peaceful purposes. States declare their nuclear material and activities to the IAEA, and the IAEA verifies thecorrectness and completeness of these declarations.This requires robust and resilient GNSS trackers which can withstand sophisticated attacks (jamming, spoofing, and especially treacherous meaconing) and tampering attempts by State-level actors, providing Assured PNT (Trusted positioning data).The GNSS tracker shall be battery powered and capable of unsupervised operations. In previous projects (in particular, EL1-077) building blocks for this technology have been developed. The IAEA has expressed interest in a joint project to increase the protection against additional attacks identified and to raise the TRL level and to make the tracker ready forcommercialization. The objective of the activity is to study, design, implement and demonstrate a resilient and robust GNSS tracker to support IAEA safeguards activities, and other similar activities requiring Assured PNTThe tasks to be performed shall include:Based on EL1-077, the activity will study, design, implement and demonstrate the technologies required for the GNSS tracker, capable of detecting and mitigating jamming, meaconing and spoofing attacks, with focus on concrete uses cases and attack scenarios identified by IAEA.Additional technologies (for example tightly coupled INS and CRPAs) will be integrated into a functional prototype. As part of the demonstration, the prototype will be subject to thorough tests representative of challenging jamming, meaconing and spoofing scenarios mounted by capable attackers.The activity is part of a roadmap to make available to customers GNSS trackers with Assured PNT and will bring the technology to a TRL which will allow industry to make confident proposals for an Element 2. The activity will not include any Galileo PRS technology, as per NAVISP Declaration.

tenderTitle: DEVELOPMENT OF PVA AND BLANKET TECHNOLOGIES FOR SATURN MISSIONS SOLAR ARRAYS - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
tenderDescription: ObjectivesTo develop fully European PhotoVoltaic (PVA) and Blanket technologies that can be used on a Solar Array for deep space missions to Saturn.DescriptionLarge solar arrays are currently being developed for telecommunication and scientific missions. Recent examples include the semi-rigid ENEO array, the fully flexible SolarFlex array of the Novacom 2 telecommunications satellite and the rigid array of the JUICE mission to Jupiter. With a high specific power, such arrays lend themselves for use in exploration missions. Feasibility studies have demonstrated that missions to Saturn, fully powered by solar arrays, are indeed feasible. In a recent development activity, the feasibility of a solar array architecture scalable up to 100 m2 per wing and with the capability to retract and re-deploy, to protect the array from damage, has been successfully demonstrated. In the frame of this study, the development of PVA and Blanket frame technologies suitable for the Saturn environment has been indicated as the main focus point for further development of suchsolar array architecture. Saturn environment places demanding requirements on PVA and Blanket technologies: the PVA shall be capable to supply power at very low temperatures and Sun intensities,and the blanket shall be lightweight yet strong enough to support the PVA and to sustain the large temperature range of a Saturn mission. Also, the blanket structure interface shall allow smooth deployment/retraction operations. The activity therefore encompasses the following tasks: Investigation into actual PVA LILT technologies and potential adaptations for its use on a Saturn mission (e.g. reduced thickness) Definition of blanket and blanket frame design, to act as PVA support and able to cope with the required temperature range Demonstration via mechanical and electrical analyses of the suitability of the selected design for the Saturn mission Demonstration of the suitability of the selectedtechnologies for the Saturn mission by means of thermal cycling and vibration tests of a representative Blanket segment (PVA and blanket) mock-up Identification of development needs Preparation of a roadmap

tenderTitle: PORTABLE SELF-CALIBRATED RYDBERG ELECTRIC FIELD PROBE FOR ANTENNA MEASUREMENTS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:To design and realize a first European portable self-calibrated SI-traceable Rydberg atom-based Electric field probe.Description:Accurate measurement of electric fields is crucial for the development and operation of RF communicationsystems, particularly in space missions. Conventional antennas need fine calibration for high-integrity reception. The calibration is performed by placing uncalibrated antennas in a known EM (electromagnetic) environment that is measured via a well-calibrated antenna which creates a dependency. Whereas Rydberg based receivers allow precise measurements of RF signals which is directly related to Planck's constant and hence can self-calibrate by relying on SI (international system of units)-traceable atomic standards The activity aims to develop a portable, self-calibrated Rydberg atom based electric field probe.The probe is based on the interaction of RF-fields with Rydberg atoms, where alkali atoms are excited opticallyto Rydberg states and the applied RF-field alters the resonant state of the atoms. For this probe, the Rydbergatoms are placed in a glass vapor cell. The vapor cell acts like an RF-to-optical transducer, converting an RF Efield to an optical frequency response. The probe utilizes the concept of Electromagnetic Induced Transition (EIT), where the RF transition in the four-level atomic system causes a split of the transition spectrum for the pump laser. This splitting is measured and is directly proportional to the applied RF field amplitude. Therefore, by measuring this splitting, we get a direct measurement of the RF E-field strength. This technique could allow traceable measurements over a large frequency band including 1-500GHz. The new approach has the following benefits: 1) it will allow direct SI units linked RF E-field measurements, 2) It is self-calibrating due to atomic resonances, 3) it will provide RF field measurements independent of current techniques, 4) the probe will not perturb the field during the measurement, since no metal is present in the probe.This activity encompasses the following tasks:-Assessment of different Rydberg atom-based methods of detection of RF fields.- Requirement consolidation and performance assessment.- Detailed concept design with analysis of critical functions.- Development of the breadboard and verification in relevant environment.- Development of a technology roadmap for an EQM.

tenderTitle: GUIDANCE  CONTROL ENTRY TECHNOLOGY FOR MARS PRECISION LANDING - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop and assess Mars guided entry and control algorithms for the entry and descent phases, including smart parachute or retro-propulsion triggering, and implement them as on-board software.Description: Entry, descent, and landing (EDL) of Mars missions are critical for ensuring the successful deployment of precision landers for human and robotic exploration. In particular, the entry and descent phases involve complex aero/thermodynamics which require precise guidance and control to achieve the proper conditions for deploying parachutes or for activating supersonic retro-propulsion. In fact, most of the dispersions occur in these phases, and while various approaches for guided-entry algorithms (reference path tracking, predictor-corrector methods, and model-basedtechniques) offer different advantages, all of these come at the expense of many challenges and trade-offs. This activity aims to trade-off different approaches for the design of Mars guided entry and control algorithms, in combination with smart parachute and/orsupersonic retro-propulsion triggering (when applicable), to reduce the dispersions that shall be removed by the landing phase. By assessing their performance through high fidelity Model-in-the-loop (MIL) simulations, the most effective algorithms can be identifiedand considered for numerically efficient and robust implementation as on-board guidance software. The added value includes improvedlanding precision, enhanced safety, and optimized entry and descent performance, which are all essential for the success of future Mars missions. The performance of the developed algorithms will be evaluated via high-fidelity dynamical simulations, while portability to flight processors will be assessed through profiling of the developed guidance control algorithms. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation/review of the proofs-of-concept and state-of-the-art of guided entry. - Definition of requirements, operational scenarios, use-cases, and preliminary validation and verification (VV) plan. - Detailed development of guidance and control algorithms with focus on performance, and optimization for embeddability. - Implementation and performance assessment ofalgorithms in an End-to-End Mars landing EDL simulator. - VV campaign of the proposed solutions and algorithms. - Assessment of computational performance on a space-graded processor through profiling. - Study synthesis, and recommendations for a technology roadmap to increase TRL.

tenderTitle: HE-SWE-03B - GLOBAL MULTI-MOMENT MULTI-FLUID MODEL OF THE MAGNETOSPHERE
tenderDescription: The Agency seeks to assess the applicability and operational potential of a multi-moment, multi-fluid modelling approach for forecasting and nowcasting the Earth's magnetospheric space weather environment. While current operational systems predominantly rely on global MHD models and fully kinetic approaches remain computationally challenging for routine use, this activity aims to demonstrate whether a multi-fluid framework can provide an effective balance between physical realism and operational performance. Bidders are expected to employ real observational data for model verification, validation, calibration, and performance enhancement, investigating techniques such as data assimilation, data-driven boundary conditions, and other observation-informed methods to improve forecasting capability and scientific fidelity. The activity should include comprehensive testing against measurements and reference models, the assessment of computational performance and operational suitability, and the quantification of forecasting skill for key space weather phenomena. The work shall identify the strengths, limitations, and maturity of the approach, while establishing a clear roadmap towards a future three-dimensional global magnetospheric forecasting capability that can operate faster than real time and support advanced operational space weather services.

tenderDescription: The European Space Agency and Xjenza Malta of the Republic of Malta hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above Call for Proposals (CfP), which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to legal entities of Malta that are registered in ESA-STAR. This CfP foresees the following standard activity types:Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participationin ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on future ESA missions or commercial missions. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 175,000.Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 400 000 (hardware development)/EUR 250 000 (all other activities).Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 80,000.Type F Space (downstream) Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 250,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity.Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in space and answer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000.To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: Type G2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industry and would lead to a new product or service being able to be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. tenderTitle: DATA RELAY RF SIMULATOR SYSTEM - EXPRO PLUS (RE-ISSUE)
tenderDescription: Objectives: The objective of this activity is to develop a system simulator for testing the RF links of multi satellite missions. The focus of the simulator should be the modelling of a full set of satellite and laned assets transmitters and receivers with their precise orbit determination around different bodies of the solar system (e.g. Earth, Moon, Mars).Description: There is a high interest in the development of cluster of data relay satellites for planetary exploration and navigation. There are different studies and developments ongoing related to this concept both for Moon and Mars. Such a simulator system for Moon and Mars is considered an asset to support the development of this cluster missions and to support the development and test of the user terminals in an operating environment.The objective of the activity is hence to develop a RF simulator of a data relay system. The simulator shall be able to interface via RF either with a user terminal unit or with a data relay unit and to: Model full satellite's cluster transmitters and receivers. Model user terminals' transmitters and receivers. Emulate the user terminal spacecraft dynamic motion on planet surface, orbit, or during descent and ascent from the surface: Doppler, Doppler rate and delay. Emulate the relay satellite dynamic motion in orbit: Doppler, Doppler rate and delay. Emulate transmitter and receiver antenna gain and phase patterns of the relay satellite and of the user spacecraft host. Emulate the interference generated by the multiple transmitters of the cluster. Emulate multipath effects. Emulate any atmospheric attenuation or delay effects (for Mars case). Emulate the (two way) range measurement function of the relay link to characterize the performance and functionality.The RF relay simulator shall emulate the signals of each satellite of the cluster in both Sband and K-band in a modular fashion (i.e. S-band module independent from K-band module). The data relay RF simulator system shall employ software in the loop and hardware in the loop techniques to allow the user to design the test scenarios and to control external hardware blocks. The main goal is to have full control of all aspects of the useroperating environment, to enable exact repeatability of the test and to allow the application of systematic errors or incidents that are normally impossible to verify or not tested during the RF compatibility tests. The Emulation of the relay satellites shall be configurable to emulate different relay systems such as different (type of) Moon or Mars scenario.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Revision and consolidation of requirements. Architectural and detailed design, including the design of the simulator system at system level and building block level. The detailed requirements for each buildingblock of the system should be derived. It shall be determined if each building block need to be developed or if there are COTS blocks that can be embedded. Implementation of the hardware and software needed to constitute the system simulator prototype. Test and demonstration of the simulator.Deliverables: Hardware prototype, Software, Report.

tenderTitle: EVALUATION OF FAULT MITIGATION TECHNIQUESFOR NEUROMORPHIC HARDWARE ACCELERATOR - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: Objective: To analyse the impacts of fault propagation in spiking neural networks (SNN), propose design mitigation techniques, identify relevant neuromorphic IPs and select a baseline concept for implementation.Description: Future missions, including planetary landing, planetary exploration, docking, debris removal, space situational awareness, in-orbit servicing, etc. will need increased autonomy to address latency issues. This autonomy will rely on AI-driven computer vision and advanced computing capabilities. However,traditional neural network inferences typically require hardware platforms such as FPGAs or GPUs, which may consume anywhere from afew tens of watts to 100 watts. This high-power consumption may necessitate active cooling systems, impacting weight, volume, complexity, and ultimately resulting in additional costs and risks for missions. Safety-critical class 1 missions, including autonomous docking, autonomous landing, and autonomous rover/drone navigation, will require lower power, low footprint (pin count), scalable, and fault-tolerant hardware accelerators. Event-based processing with Neuromorphic technologies, show potential for the future of intelligent sensing, whether it involves event-based cameras, LiDAR, or radar sensors. Neuromorphic technology can address in an effectivemanner the challenge posed by edge AI, sustaining a high processing load, while keeping power consumption low (from few Watts to sub-Watt). Concrete use cases such as, autonomous landing, autonomous docking have been studied, validating Neuromorphic technology through the deployment on commercial device (COTS). Neuromorphic technology is suited for computer vision applications, planned activities should also confirm the suitability for radar as well. Few commercial IPs have shown potential in studies as explained above.However, additional work is needed to adapt a solution for space missions, ensuring low power, scalability, low pin count, and fault tolerance. Leveraging state-of-the-art neuromorphic commercially available IPs, this activity aims to propose a solution that addresses these needs effectively by designing a neuromorphic hardware accelerator using advanced rad hard ASIC technology. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Hardware accelerator specifications consolidation - selection and product roadmap definition - IP fault mitigation techniques analysis - Hardware accelerator architecture definition - Hardware accelerator design - Hardware accelerator validation / simulation.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators.For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

tenderTitle: HYBRID MANUFACTURING FOR SPACE APPLICATION - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To advance hybrid manufacturing strategies that integrate conventional and advanced techniques to enhance the performance, functionality and competitiveness of space hardware.Description:Hybrid manufacturing combines subtractive methods (e.g. milling, turning,grinding) with additive processes(e.g. powder bed processes, direct energy deposition). It may also include fabrication/joining steps like welding,bonding or brazing. This approach aims to overcome limitations of individual processes, enabling theproduction ofhigh-performance, competitive components. Such methodologies are of growing relevance particularly in propulsion, thermal management and structural systems. The key drivers include:- Geometric complexity: enabling the manufacture of intricate, topology-optimisedstructures difficult to realiseby conventional means alone.- Material efficiency: by adding material only where needed, hybrid manufacturing reduces waste and optimizes material usage.- Functional performance: enabling graded material properties, local reinforcements or tailored functionality.- Cost and lead time: consolidating steps, minimising waste and enabling complex geometries, though it mayrequire specialised planning, equipment and qualification.- Design flexibility: greater customization and flexibility in design, making it ideal for producing bespoke or low volume parts.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Survey of relevant techniques, materials and equipment capabilities relevant to a hybrid manufacturing approach.- Selection of two representative case studies with associated requirements (e.g. one propulsion component, one thermal management part).- Design and definition of the hybrid manufacturing route for each case study.- Manufacturing and functional testing of demonstrators. The utilisation of new digital methods for supportinghybrid manufacturing decisions is welcomed. This may include artificial intelligence techniques, such asdeep/federated learning techniques, as well as a focus on use-cases of generatively designed parts (whichinherently benefit from the hybrid manufacturing techniques), alongside the artificial intelligence and machine learning data-driven learning.- Economic analysis, including cost comparison with conventional approaches and life-cycle considerations.Deliverables: Breadboard, ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

tenderTitle: S3-CL-05 SIMPLIFIED LCA AND ECODESIGN TOOL FOR SPACE MISSIONS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Following the endorsement of the ESA Ecodesign Policy in October 2025, the systematic integration of ecodesign principles into ESA programmes and projects has become a key enabler for achieving ESA Green Agenda objectives. However, current Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approaches remain too complex and resource-intensive for routine use during mission conception and preliminary design. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a simplified LCA and ecodesign tool for space missions, enabling rapid environmental assessments and the comparison of alternative design solutions during phases A/B1. The tool developed in this activity will provide a practical and harmonised means to support ecodesign implementation across the European space sector while ensuring consistency with ESA environmental datasets and European assessment methodologies. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 6.

While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Bulgarian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types: Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on future ESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 6. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 500,000 (hardware development)/EUR 250,000 (all other activities). Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000.Type E: Phase 0/A/B1 small sat mission definition studies with potential to lead to either a national or a commercial mission, in the area of Earth Observation for Climate, Agriculture, Disaster Management and Environmental Monitoring, enabling the development and demonstration of Bulgarian technologies and products in space. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity. tenderTitle: LOCAL TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND ON-SITE SUPPORT FOR THE DEEP SPACE ANTENNA (DSA-5)- EXPRO+

tenderTitle: HYDRON HAPS: HAPS-BASED OPTICAL NETWORK EXTENSION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.242) EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept extending High-throughput Optical Network (HydRON) services to High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) and their networks. To identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap including estimations of schedule and costs.Targeted Improvements:To enable the connectivity of HAPS to an evolution of the satellite optical network system.Description:High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) will play the role of an intermediate, airborne layer in a multi-domain/orbit communications architecture in line with the optical-6G concept. HAPS operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 15 to 50 km, where they can maintain a near-stationary position for weeks or even months at a time. A single HAPS cancreate a wide-area communication cell that provides reliable connectivity to remote or rural areas where building traditional terrestrial infrastructure is uneconomical. A satellite-to-HAPS optical link can serve as a high-bandwidth feeder link, backhauling data from the HAPS to the satellite network and then to the terrestrial network, avoiding the need for a ground gateway in an inaccessiblelocation. HAPS can conduct long-term surveillance or monitoring missions over a specific area of interest, providing a significantadvantage over LEO satellites which only pass over a given point for a few minutes at a time. With an optical link, a HAPS can uplinkreal-time, high-resolution imagery and sensor data to a satellite (or another HAPS), enabling rapid analysis for applications like border security, environmental monitoring, or situational awareness. In the event of a natural disaster that destroys ground-basedcommunication networks, HAPS can be rapidly deployed to provide a temporary but persistent communications hub. The optical link to an optical backbone network like HydRON ensures that the HAPS remains connected to the global network, providing critical communicationcapabilities for first responders and civilians.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements, and system concepts for HAPS-space bidirectional optical communications, to upgrade the HydRON System with an airborne layer. Technology gaps and relatedtechnology roadmaps shall be identified and addressed for any critical technology, including optical terminals. The system shall consider the management of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a HAPS-to-HAPS free-space network or hybrid communications in RF. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be verified. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

tenderTitle: COMMERCIAL APPLICATIONS ENABLED BY SPACE ENVIRONMENTS (CASE) CALL FOR PROPOSALS
tenderDescription: Space can be the ideal environment to exploit a wide range of phenomena and physical processes that are not possible under the effects of gravity experienced on Earth, such as different fluid dynamics, material behaviour or cell biology. Besides microgravity, space offers extreme conditions, such as huge temperature differences and radiation, as well as an unobstructed vantage point for remote sensing or communication. All these characteristics can unlock benefits for commercial businesses on Earth in a wide range of sectors from energy to food and pharmaceuticals production. Now, access to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) has become easier thanks to established space service providers operating onboard the International Space Station (ISS): ESA ISS Commercial Partners and other service providers offer unique services along with clear pricing policies, which cover the complete service chain from preparation, launch, operations onboard the ISS, to sample return. The 'Commercial Applications enabled by Space Environments (CASE)' Open Call for Proposals aims to support the development of commercial services that benefit from microgravity and space environments.

tenderTitle: IMPROVED TTC SUB-SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To consolidate alternative solutions for on-board loss minimization. To develop the prototypes of the most relevant solutions identified, to confirm the predicted performance. To provide road-map to flight models. The state of art TTC Sub-System architectures for Science and Exploration missions are nowadays quite complex. In order to allow communications during all mission phases, several antennas are needed in combination with redundant High Power Amplifiers (HPA) and transponders (DST). The interconnection among these components is accomplished by the RF Distribution Unit (RFDU), which has to guarantee the maximum degree of reconfigurability and reliability to failures. In addition, it has also to implement the necessary filtering action, to allow full duplex communications. Its design is therefore quite complex encompassing the use of several switches, Diplexers, Filters and interconnecting waveguides (WG) runs. The latter can be quite long as they have to reach antennas which are typically far from the location of the rest of the TTC subsystem. All this results in high losses with RF power reduction in transmission and increased noise figure in reception.The design solutions used so far in the frame of ESA projects are quite recurrent with no major improvements in the last decades. As shown in a TTC Sub-System architecture survey carried out in 2017, different approaches exist, as identified for example by other agencies and already flown successfully in the past years. For a complex RFDU as used in Deep Space missions, we can consider RF path losses in the order of 1 to 3 dB in X-band and 3 to 4 dB in Ka-band, with significant impacts in terms of data return (up to50% reduction) and in terms of spacecraft recovery possibilities in case of anomalies (increasedoperations complexity and limitation on maximum achievable distance). Therefore, there is a clear need for loss reduction in the RFDU paths, through the implementation of novel solutions. A study is on-going to consolidate the possible alternative subsystem Architectures, and define relevant requirements. This will be completed in early 2024, but its conclusions need to be consolidated by experimental results. The activity shall focus on the specification, detailed design, development and tests of prototypes of the components which will have the most significant impact on the TTC subsystem performance and whose feasibility has to be demonstrated. Three main items have been already identified, which may need to be completed by additional technologies as an outcome of the on-going study:- Receiving only antenna with integrated low-noise-amplifier (LNA) and downconverter (D/C), with a possible alternative for a receiving and transmitting solution;- High-gain-antenna dual-band feed including receiving LNA and D/C, and with direct interface to power amplifier;- Transponder front-end to manage the interfaces with new antennas designs.Tasks:1. Consolidation of requirements and design2. Design and manufacturing of bread-boards3. Testing of bread-boards4. Development plan for flight models.

tenderTitle: MARITIME LASER COMMUNICATION TERMINAL ENABLING OPTICAL LINKS WITH SPACE (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.012) - ON REQUEST
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a maritime laser communication terminal prototype to enable optical communication links between aship-based and a space-based laser terminals.TargetedImprovements:Enhance the reliability and stability of a laser communication terminal (LCT) in maritime environments for optical satellite communication. This will resultin a reliable and resilient system for bidirectional ship-space links.Description: While Laser Communication Terminals (LCTs) are being explored for aeronautical and land-mobile sectors, their use in maritime-satellite link applicationsremains untapped. Maritime LaserCommunication Terminal (MLCT) systems offer significant advantages, including secure communications (resilienceto jamming and low probability of interception), high data rates, direct line-of-sight links, which can enhance connectivity for ships but are not available yetin ESA Member States or Canada.This activity will develop and test MLCT prototype for maritime communication applications. It will assess the state-of-the-art for maritime LCTs andevaluate the constraints imposed by dynamic maritime environments, such as sea waves. Following this analysis, existing Pointing, Acquisition, andTracking (PAT) mechanisms, optical head mechanical designand optical communication systems will be benchmarked, and one will be selected andoptimised for effective performance in maritimeconditions. A prototype MLCT will be developed with Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) specifications closeto a final product, ensuring compatibility with current and future planned space LCTs. The MLCT shall be designed for manufacturability at a competitivecommercial cost. The possibility of a test to be conducted with a satellite LCT should be explored

tenderTitle: ADVANCED SUB-THZ PACKAGING TECHNOLOGIES - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a 664 GHz direct detection receiver using innovative packaging techniques for future ultra-compact array instruments.Description: Future array instruments and ultra-compact payload instruments require ultra-compact receiver integrating all RF (Radio Frequency) functions with very small SWaP (Size, Weight and Power), removing complex mechanical and electrical interfaces such as standard waveguide flanges and DC/IF (Direct Current/Intermediate Frequency) coaxial connectors. Novel silicon micromachining techniques are key-enablers to develop ultra-compact RF front-end by integrating in a High-Aspect-Ratio silicon-wafer stack all the key components required to achieve state-of-the-art performance, including high-gain antenna, RF LNA MMIC (Microwave Monolithically Integrated Circuit), RF filters, diode detector, video amplifier and associated DC electronics.This activity aims to develop an integrated 664 GHz Direct Detection Receiver, including a novel high-gain flat-antenna, RF LNA MMIC, a narrow-bandpass filter, and a zero-bias detector with integrated video-amplifier. The developed receiver will be tested radiometrically, including beam pattern measurement, Noise Figure, Short-Term-Gain-Stability, and Gain response over temperature. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Design of an integrated direct detection receiver operating at 664 GHz. - Investigation ofsilicon-micromachined fabrication and packaging techniques for all critical RF elements: flat-antenna, waveguide active (LNA) and passive (filter) devices, RF/IF/DC interconnections. - Manufacturing and testing of a breadboard model. - Development plan and future roadmap.

tenderTitle: T311-900SD DEBRIS ENVIRONMENT MODELLING IN CIS-LUNAR SPACE (EXPRO+)
tenderDescription: Description: Currently, debris environment models for cislunar space are very limited as such have been primarily developed for Earth-bound orbits. Such models are a necessary asset for collision/impact risk assessment and traffic coordination. With the expansion of human activities beyond Earth, notably in cislunar space, there is an increasing need for models and tools to support missions. This need is reflected on the latest Space Debris Mitigation requirements for lunar orbits, including disposal and availability of space traffic coordination methods. With various studies having explored disposed objects and debris clouds in cislunar space, the development of such models becomes increasingly feasible. Methods and software tools to perform assessments in Earth orbits exist and are well-used. To ensure safe operations and sustainability in cislunar space, an extended density-based model can be used for risk event statistics, delta-v planning for collision avoidance manoeuvres and reliability assessment due to impacts. The model shall leverage the results of recent studies on debris and clouds around the Moon and build upon the well-established tools andmethodologies for Earth orbits. For the dynamically complex lunar orbits, a long-term propagator is needed to support the characterisation and evolution of the population. Under this activity, cislunar long-term propagators are aimed to be coupled with break-up, lunar impact, and traffic models to create a consistent debris and dust density map for the cislunar environment. To demonstrate the usability and mission application, the model shall be coupled with collision and impact risk assessment tool and tested on a Lunar mission design.

tenderTitle: LUNAR EUROPEAN POWER PACKS: SYSTEM-LEVEL CONCEPT STUDY (E3CX-033) - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: This Lunar European Power Pack aims to accelerate the maturation of European thermal control and power systems as well as related electronics equipment enabling lunar night survival and lunar night operations in the frame of the ESA lunar roadmap. The output of the Lunar European Power Pack will be a European lunar end-to-end integrated advanced power pack validated design providing thermal control and power as a service to surface Payloads if integrated in the relevant mission's baseline. To enable sustained surface operations on the Moon, robust and autonomous power and thermal services are essential. These systems must be able to support a range of external clients including systems and payloads hosted on landers, rovers, surface shelters, or deployed payloads under harsh lunar conditions, from mid-latitudes to polar regions, ranging from daytime to night survival. The goal is therefore to deliver reliable energy and thermal regulation as a modular service, adaptable to multiple mission profiles and operational needs. Ensuring an efficient service/mass ratio is vital for the affordability and is therefore central to any activity.

tenderTitle: HYDRON UPGRADE KIT: ESTOL-COMPLIANT PORTABLE MODEM UPGRADE KIT FOR OPTICAL GROUND STATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.091) EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:To develop a portable modem that can be easily integrated in an existing optical ground station to make it compatible with ESTOL specificationsTargeted Improvements:Increased interoperability between existing optical ground stations and future satellite systems (e.g., HydRON).Description:There are a number of existing or planned optical ground stations (OGSs) that are currently used for scientific missions or to demonstrate quantum technologies. Those OGSs are not compliant to the ESA Specifications for Terabit/s Optical Links (ESTOL). To maximise the benefit of early Member State investments, the activity shall develop an upgrade kit" for multiple existing OGS infrastructures. An easy-to-integrate modem will facilitate the upgrade of such existing or planned OGSsand increase their interoperability with future commercial and institutional systems that will adopt ESTOL and its evolutions.Thisactivity shall develop a portable breadboard for an ESTOL-compliant modem. In the scope of the activity, it shall be assumed that thetarget existing OGSs have already been developed in terms of optical elements (e.g., aperture, adaptive optics, etc.) in order tobecompatible with ESTOL. The portable modem shall be connected to the optical part of the OGS by optical fibre, and it shall implement both transmit and receive functionalities. The modem breadboard shall come with a GUI and an interface control document to facilitate its fast and easy integration and use. The functionalities of the portable modem shall be validated in the Contractor's laboratory and in an existing selected OGS.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

tenderTitle: LOW POWER KA-BAND DIRECT CONVERSION RECEIVER MODULE (ARTES AT 5C.525) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
tenderDescription: The objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a 12bit direct conversion receiver module covering the full Ka-band with significant reduced power consumption in comparison to current state of the art.Targeted Improvements:- Enabling a European source of low power direct conversion Ka-band receivers.- Factor 5 reduction of power consumption compared to the State of the Art.Description: Today's flexible telecommunication satellites require receivers operating at higher frequencies and over a wider bandwidth than in the past, with a complex RF chain and lossyharnesses. A trend towards highly integrated solutions using direct sampling receivers compatible with Software Defined Radios (SDRs) is one solution, but the power consumption of these direct sampling architectures can be prohibitive for some applications. The available direct conversion receivers in Ku-band and Ka-band have power consumption figuresin excess of several Watts and limited conversion accuracy, constraining the application areas where these could be used for space telecommunication applications. A direct conversion receiver system in a single package integrating the Analog to Digital Converter (ADC) in the advanced semiconductor technology and using a time-interleaved ADCarchitecture can achieve the desired lower power consumption and higher conversion accuracy.This activity will develop a prototype wideband ADC with high-speed track-and-hold circuit, implemented as a System-in-Package (SiP) RF to digital front-end module including digital processing features, operating in upper Ka-band. Available State-of-the-Art low-power wideband ADC will be assessed, and a trade-off analysisperformed to determine the optimum RF chain architecture (including the track-and-hold with digital processing engine and high-speed interfaces) suitable for wideband SDRs operating in full Ka-bandapplications. The breadboard will be designed to meet key performance requirements in terms of power consumption (<500mW per channel), bandwidth, and input frequency. The noise and linearity performance shall be measured to determine suitability for a range of SDR scenarios also considering synchronisation and clock jitter requirements. The breadboard shall be tested in a representative RF chain architecture in a laboratory environment, to demonstrate direct sampling at upper Ka-band frequencies and assess viability for V/W band applications. Additionally, radiation tolerance shall be demonstrated by analysis to assess suitability of the low-power ADC for future applications in space.

tenderTitle: LARGE INPUT VOLTAGE RANGE GAN BDR FOR PRIMARY BATTERIES EXPRO+
tenderDescription: ObjectivesExplore topologies based on GaN switches and digital control to discharge primarybatteries down the minimum possible voltage.The objective is to maximise the use of the energy in primary batteries.Build a breadboard with the most promising option and test its performance.DescriptionPrimary batteries have very high energy density but they cannot be recharged. Thus, itsmain use is for one-time use cases, for instance, landers or launchers.Typically a lander will not have any solar array so its only energysource is a battery. Sincethey will not be recharged, primary batteries make total sense.To extract the maximum amount of energy,the battery voltage will go down as the currentis taken out. The lower you go in voltage, the more energy you extract.However, decreasing the voltage has serious implications for the power system. In general,DC/DC converters operate at high efficiency levels in a narrow input voltage range.Moreover, the topologies will limit the maximum and minimum input voltage, which meansthat, in mostcases, the DC/DC converter used to discharge the battery will limit theoperation and the performance.This activity aims at exploring DC/DC converter topologies that can operate through largeinput voltage ranges with high performance. Efficiency is also very important in landerapplications since it is paramount to waste as little energy as possible.There are topologies that can operate through larger ranges that have not been used inspace applications so far and can be adopted easily. Moreover, new GaN switchesimprove the efficiency of the system and, if controlled by means of digital devices, complexenergy management systems can be built. Thus, multiple stages could be connected insuch a way that the optimum operation point is always at reach.The activity aims at building a breadboard of a high efficiency, high input voltage rangeDC/DC converter with GaN switches and digital control. The breadboard will be tested toverify the performance.

tenderTitle: QUALIFICATION  PERFORMANCE ENHANCEMENT OF EUROPEAN SPACE ADHESIVES FOR STRUCTURAL AND OPTICAL BONDING - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: Objectives:To qualify a European space adhesive, focused on structural and/or optical bonding applications, andcapable to withstand ground, launch and space environment effects.Description:Europe lacks a fully qualified space-ready adhesive for structural and optical bonding, despite the criticalrole these materials play in ensuring mission integrity across thermal, mechanical, and vacuumenvironments. Current ESA missions depend on long-established non-European systems whoseformulations and supply conditions are outside European control, creating operational and industrial risks for long-term use. Furthermore, ESA's industrial partners rely onthe extensive past heritage andvalidation of these non-European solutions, and adapting a European solution would require having dataavailable so that it can be done with confidence. This activity focuses also on validating and qualifyingexisting European adhesive candidates to demonstrate their suitability for space-relevant bonding processes. Rather than developing new formulations, the goal is to rigorously benchmark available European products, perform the necessary environmental and mechanical testing, and generatea complete qualification dataset. This will enable large system integrators and subcontractors to adopt EU-sourced adhesives with confidence, strengthening European autonomy and ensuring dependable access to mission-critical bonding materials.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of available European adhesive formulators manufacturers and products with structural andglass-to-metal applications (focused on epoxies and potentially UV-curing adhesives, but otheralternatives are possible),- Review the TRL status, the performances already available and the manufacturing capabilities andidentify the gaps with respect to non-Europeanadhesives commonly used in space- Down select three with the largest potential with a focus on applicability. Characterize, if notavailable, asminimum E/G modulus in wide range of temperatures, CTE, thermal vacuum stability and outgassingperformance- Performadequate testing to verify the suitability of the adhesive/substrate solutions to the requiredenvironments. This includes space-application thermal response (at least thermal vacuum, mechanicalloads, adhesion strength) and dimensional stability tests (permanentpolymerisation shrinkage). It shouldalso include the main common substrates for these applications.- Apply and verify the use of the adhesive in the most common space-relevant adhesive bondingprocesses.The expected outcome is an increased TRL for European adhesives, supported by a comprehensive gap analysis of their properties, and the generation of robust performance data to make them available to theEuropean industry. The ultimate objective is to have qualified-European produced adhesives available toall space system integrators categories and subcontractors, facilitating a transition from non-European to fully European space adhesives.Deliverables: Technical report, Samples of developed adhesivesApplication/Need Date: All Missions Mission Classification: alpha, beta, gamma,delta.

tenderTitle: SOLAR SYSTEM INTERNET REFERENCE FRAMES AND TIME SYSTEMS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To study the state-of-the-art concerning time and reference systems applicable to Solar System navigation and propose a definition of Solar System time and reference systems.Description: Currently ESA is developing interoperable communication and navigation services for the Moon (through Moonlight) and Mars (through MARCONI). To increase the autonomy of space missions across the full Solar System, and thus offloading the overloaded ground stations, ESA is developing a concept for Solar System Internet. Currently, spacecraft navigating in the Solar System rely on explicit, pre-planned setup of point-to-point communication links for their navigation. Such approach, does not scale well with the large number of missions planned in the future. Such a system would combine existing (i.e., GNSS) or planned (i.e., Moonlight, MARCONI) systems and would complement this with dedicated SSI nodes. These nodes would provide ranging capabilities through point-to-point links (as broadcast links are not scalable over long distances). As all spacecraft and SSI nodes are connected (through the Solar System Internet), raw data could be shared, through the decentralized network,enabling more advanced positioning techniques such as collaborative positioning. To achieve this goal, the definition of accurate timescale and reference systems, similar to GNSS or Moonlight, is crucial. The objective of this activity is to study the state-of-the-art concerning time and reference systems applicable to Solar System navigation, assess the gaps and suitability. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Analyse the state-of-the-art of existing Barycentric/planetary reference frames and timescales and the accuracy/availability of transformations between them (e.g., Mars planetocentric to Barycentric) - Investigate how the realizationof existing Barycentric/planetary reference frames can be improved using SSI PNT nodes, pre-selecting the most promising approaches. - Investigate the impact of relativity on Solar System PNT and assess the need for the definition of one (or more) Solar System timescale(s) and the relationship between them, pre-selecting the most promising approaches. - Implement the pre-selected reference frames and timescales, for usage in a Solar System PNT system, in a software simulator, such that end-to-end PNT performance assessment que be performed for the different models and PNT system configurations. - Based on the implemented models in the software simulator, assess the performance and suitability of the pre-selected Barycentric/planetary reference frames and timescales for a Solar System PNT system. - Based on the results obtained via simulation, propose one (or more) Solar System time and reference systems. Thisanalysis will need to beProcurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested.
