tenderTitle: CAN BACKPLANE INTERFACE MEZZANINE BOARD - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To build a mezzanine board to interface with a CAN bus on the units' backplane.Description:As part of the APA (Advanced Power Architecture) initiative, a standardised approach is being developed for internal communication between APA modules within an APA unit. This activity supports that effort by designing a compact, reusable TM/TC interface based on the CAN bus, known for itsreliabilityand simplicity.The mezzanine will serve as a common building block / solution for all APA modules, reducing integration effortandpromoting consistency across designs. By consolidating all required components into a small footprint, it simplifies system architecture, supports modularity and eases procurement, manufacturing and recurrence.This activity focuses on developing a compact mezzanine PCB that integrates five essential components required for CAN-based backplane communication (FPGA or microcontroller, ADC, voltage reference, CAN transceiver and XTAL/oscillator). The goal is to consolidate these elements into a small 30x30 mm footprint, supporting a range of external interfaces and operating on a 3.3V supply.This modular solution aims to simplify internal communication across systems where CAN is the preferred protocol, offering a reusable and scalable interface.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidate the CAN protocol implementation.- Architecture definition (evaluating if FPGA-based or microcontroller-based).- Identify two suitable options for each one of the 5 required components, prioritising compact packaging and cost.- Design a 30mm x 30 mm PCB accommodating the 5 components and ensuring signal integrity andmanufacturability, ready to be assembled into an APA module and to interface with CAN bus and the APA module.- Implement the software or the VHDL code with the CAN protocol.- Prototyping and testing, assemble and validate the board to confirm functionality and performance.Deliverables: Breadboard,ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

tenderTitle: S3-CL-03 ERASE PHASE A  ACTIVE DEBRIS REMOVAL MISSION FOR LARGE UNPREPARED LEO PLATFORMS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: ESA intends to implement a Zero Debris policy by 2030 and has a long-term vision for a sustainable and safe space environment leveraging on the development of a space circular economy.Large Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites in particular present significant risks, both in terms of potential collisions and ground casualty hazards resulting from uncontrolled re-entry. The ESA's Clean Space Office has been pioneering the study of ADR since 2012, starting with the e.Deorbit study, followed by the ClearSpace-1 and the CAT mission in more recent years, under the ADRIOS initiative part of the ESA Space Safety Program. In the past years there has been growing interest in ADR services targeting large LEO debris objects. This topic has recently been the focus of discussions and studies between ESA and external stakeholders, including EUMETSAT in the frame of a feasibility study (e.g. CDF) and the European Commission(EC) via its ISOS framework. This led to the implementation of industrial activities for a 6 month ERASE phase 0 mission and systemstudy which was kicked-off Q1 of 2026.The activity proposed here is to further mature the concept of the ERASE mission up to the Preliminary Requirement Review (PRR) milestone. The result of the activity and the maturation of the ERASE concept should be in linewith the outcomes of an ESA Preliminary Requirements Review as described by the ECSS. If successful, ESA intends to follow this study by the Phase B1 and a eventual full mission implementation acceptance after CMin 2028

This topic has recently been the focus of discussions and studies between ESA and external stakeholders, including EUMETSAT in the frame of a feasibility study (e.g. CDF) and the European Commission(EC) via its ISOS framework. This led to the implementation of industrial activities for a 6 month ERASE phase 0 mission and systemstudy which was kicked-off Q1 of 2026.The activity proposed here is to further mature the concept of the ERASE mission up to the Preliminary Requirement Review (PRR) milestone. The result of the activity and the maturation of the ERASE concept should be in linewith the outcomes of an ESA Preliminary Requirements Review as described by the ECSS. If successful, ESA intends to follow this study by the Phase B1 and a eventual full mission implementation acceptance after CMin 2028

tenderTitle: RADIATION EFFECTS INSIDE THE SPACECRAFT COMPATIBLE WITH ADHA DEVELOPMENT- EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a breadboard of a radiation detection unit based on Advanced Data Handling Architectures (ADHA) in order to minimise on-board resources, while improving the integration and deployment.Description: The Agency has had success developing and flying radiation monitors, starting with the REM in the 90's, the SREM in the 2000s, and the EMU and NGRMs since 2017. These monitors have all been self contained and externally mounted, with masses and power requirements exceeding 1 kg and 2 W - low resource, butnot insignificant. Some of these instruments have housed dosimeters, but none have provided measurements within the other spacecraft units. At the moment, there are no low resource radiation monitors available capable of integration within the spacecraft and its units where the sensitive systems are located and capable to provide useful, unparalleled feedback to satellite operations. The benefits include enabled monitoring of the spacecraft health, and providing useful operational diagnostics, and accurate information on the environment. Radiation monitors are the first modules to be discarded during phase A of design due to additional mass and power budget constraints. This disrupts the huge potential of in-orbit data collection, which affects radiation model accuracy and uncertainty a measure, Radiation monitor will allow to manage approach to radiation effects, potentially extending mission lifetimes and opening the door to widespread use of COTS. It is envisaged that this should become standard on all platforms as part of S/C 'health' data - as is already done with thermal measurements. In order to enhance the European competitiveness for LEO applications for mid-size satellites, it is aimed to design and test a portfolio of standardized dosimeters and memories. By including the radiation monitors in the Advanced Data Handling architecture (ADHA), standardized, interchangeable, and inter-operable electronics modules equipped with the latest generation of microelectronics components can be integrated within the spacecraft units. Components and commercialprocesses from European foundries and manufacturers shall be baselined for dose measurements. Several configuration can be considered: detection unit embedded into each ADHA board, detection unit placed at different point of ADHA or to be considered as a standalone board. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - A trade-off shall be made between of the different solutions considered -Breadboarding and functional testing - Total ionising Dose and SEE testing - Roadmap to fully characterise and fly European memories once they become availableDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

tenderTitle: GSTP ELEMENT 1: DEVELOP:ASSESSMENTS TO PREPARE AND DE-RISK TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENTS - STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS
tenderDescription: The objective of this framework is to allow for assessments that will help prepare and de-risk potential development activities. The assessment will help evaluate the potential added value and to address critical issues. The results are intended to be used to help orient and adapt the follow-on development activity with respect to various aspects (i.e. technical, implementation, cost, etc.).Description:When examining new applications of existing technologies (i.e. already used in space or coming from other sectors) or new technologies, there are often questions to resolve about the most promising application and the actual potential added value or performance of the technology (as compared to the state-of-the art). There are also sometimes questions about the potential adaptation effort required or the feasibility of dealing with the environment conditions of Space.Although it is not possible to address all potential questions, it is relevant to address the most critical issues to make an assessment and provide orientation before embarking on a full technology development. In addition, by addressing these issues, it also possible to shape the full development activity with respect to a targeted application, to refine the associated specifications and work programme and to help dimension the cost and the schedule. The assessments for potential development activities are intended to provide a better understanding of the potential advantages of a given technology for a given application and to address critical issues (i.e. to help mitigate risks with respect to a future development activity).Activities will typically include at least one of the following tasks: Identification and analysis of specifications for one or more space applications and the technical assessment of the development actions and associated schedule and cost. Assessment of the potential benefits (performance, cost, lead time, risks...) and disadvantages of the potentiallution with respect to the state-of-the-art. Assessment of potential critical issues related to using a given technology for a specific application, using analysis/simulation and/or breadboarding and testing. Define the full development activity with respect to a targeted application, refining the associated specifications and work programme and estimating the cost and establishing the schedule.The de-risk framework is targeted to develop generic technology but will also cover dedicated initiatives to boost specific technologies (e.g. AI, Energy systems, propulsion systems, Quantum technology, Advance manufacturing, etc.) and to support established companies to improve their products portfolio with a longer term development. In particular, this framework covers the first stepof the product portfolio initiative. This initiative aims to strength medium entities, with already established experience in termsof developing products, to maintaining a product family and intend to expand the sales of their products beyond present opportunities.The maximum amount per activity is 250 k.

tenderTitle: LIGHT CONDUCTION AND DIFFUSION MATERIALS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF LIGHT INTENSIFIED PHOTOBIOREACTORS
tenderDescription: ObjectivesTo increase the efficiency of photobioreactors by an improved design of light conduction anddiffusion inside the reactor.DescriptionThe need for regenerative life support systems for long term space missions necessitates a questfor increased efficiency of Photobioreactors. The light intensification of photobioreactors is animportant building block to increase the return on investment with respect to light energy introducedvs oxygen yield in a defined volume.Previous activities have identified as a priority the need to progress on specific technologies, suchas the type of light sources and on innovative materials for light conductionand diffusion (e.g.polymers, leaking rods, specific optical fibers, lightning fabrics). This activity attempts to push theboundaries of photobioractor efficiency even further (compared to BIORAT-1) by investigating amore efficient light diffusion and as well characterization of the impact on the process and thebiomass.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review the state of the art for light intensified photobioreactiors and energy efficient lightguidance systems- Design a test bench with realistic operational parameters (light, flow, active species etc.)and test the most optimal configuration to achieve best possible efficiency w.r.t. volumetricoxygen and biomass production- Assess the potential biological effects of immersed light sources and possiblecountermeasures against fouling and clogging- Provide a development plan for operational hardware on ground and in space includingMAIT aspects for an operational scenario and define the scaling laws.

tenderTitle: IP CORES FOR HIGH-SPEED ADC  DAC INTERFACE - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To develop and verify reusable digital IP cores fully implementing the JESD204B/C high-speed interface standards, addressing current and future high-speed data acquisition and conversion EEE devices. DescriptionNext generation Earth Observation, Telecom and broadly Software-Defined Radio payloads exploit high-speed Analog-to-Digital (ADC) and Digital-to-Analog (DAC) devices, which requirehigh-speed digital interfaces to cope with the throughput demand in the order of gigabit-per-second (Gbps). Furthermore, these devices are thoroughly used in Multiple-Input/Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, and therefore require synchronisation for simultaneous operation. Two major protocols are JESD204 and ESISTREAM; while the former is an industry standard adopted by many EEE suppliers, thelatter is supported by one supplier.Commercial JESD204 IP cores exist, but they are either open, but prohibitively expensive; locked to a development tool/device vendor; locked to a given ADC/DAC vendor. Furthermore, these IP cores have not been developed with the Space environment in mind, therefore require hardening against single-event effects (SEEs), which may not be possible due to their closed nature. Meanwhile, ESISTREAM IP, is open source and provided free by the supplier, however its' verification status requires improvement and its' adoption is unclear. With many ESA missions and industry products relying on devices having JESD204 interfaces, it is imperative to have verified, SEE-hardened, configurable and device technology independent IP cores.The provision of aJESD204 IP core covers two different needs simultaneously: interface of ASIC/FPGA with existing EEE components, and a building-block for future EEE ADC/DAC devices. The IP cores will be part of the ESA IP Core's portfolio, making it accessible for future ESA projects and missions, devices and also for smaller companies.Activity encompasses the following tasks: - Study the latest JESD204 standard, derivation of requirements and identification of configurable parameters - Develop verification environment based on Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) - Development of JESD204 IP cores for Transmit and Receive in VHDL, and verification using UVMframework - Development of user-friendly IP core configuration tool for tailoring based on specific device/mode requirements - Synthesis on representative FPGA devices: space-qualified BRAVE, RTG4/PolarFire and COTS (Xilinx) - Trial synthesis for selected ASIC targets - Laboratory demonstrator with representative FPGA and data conversion devices - Produce User Manuals, with integration guidelines

tenderTitle: DUAL-ACTIVE 5G NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORK MODEM WITH SMART RESOURCE MANAGEMENT (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7A.089) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a 5G NTN dual active modem prototype with active resource management for improving link reliability and performance, whileoptimizing the space segment resources utilization.TargetedImprovements:-doubling the peak data rate compared to state of art modems.- reduction by half link outage time.Description: The need for a dual-active modem in 5G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) arises from the growing demand for reliable, high-performance communication links particularly inscenarios where terrestrial networks are unavailable or unreliable. A dual-active NTN modem can maintain two simultaneous satellite links, significantly reducing the risk ofoutages caused by shadowing, fading or interference. At the same time, it provides an additional communication channel that enables load balancing across space segmentnodes, helping to distribute traffic efficiently and improve peak user data rates. Active resource management is essential in this context. Strategies must be designed todynamically allocate resources based on real-time link conditions and performance metrics. These strategies should ensure that the satellite system can optimize keyperformance indicators, such as peak data rate and service availability, while minimizing the resources allocated to each link and network node (e.g. payloads). Developingcontrol plane methodologies is also a critical aspect of this solution. The control plane manages the signalling and control information required for the operation of thecommunication links. It enables the system to gather real-time measurements of links conditions, which are essential for making informed decisions about resource allocationand link management. These methodologies also provide mechanisms for communicating decisions to the network including satellites and user terminals ensuring that thesystem can adapt to changing conditions and maintain optimal performance.This activity will develop a prototype dual-active 5G modem, potentially based on open radio stacks, and implement a testbed to evaluate the prototype under realisticconditions. This testbed will include a channel emulator with multiple RF interfaces to emulate themultiple links. Channel performance as well as satellite system resourcesallocation will be tested for various operational scenarios, and both resource management methodologies and control plane techniques will be assessed.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

tenderTitle: EO Network of Resources 2023-2028 - Best Practices ITT to procure services from resource and platform tier providers
tenderDescription: Exploitation Platforms are a central element of ESA's Earth Observation (EO) Innovation Europe concept, which aims at the integration of EO data and information for a much broader use, for scientific, social and economic purposes, as well as for the generation of new commercial applications and services. The EO Network of Resources (NoR) initiative promotes the use of European resource and platform services to facilitate a simplified and efficient exploitation of EO data in cloud environments. The initiative incentivizes providers to contribute to a common framework harmonising the access to their services and helping the user to work with the data. RHEA has been awarded the EO Digital Platform – EO Network Of Resources 2023-2028 contract (AO/1-11738/23/I-EF), the follow-up of the project Procurement of Earth Observation Exploitation Platform Network Resource Services (ITT AO/1-9217/18/I-LG) finished in November 2023. RHEA has therefore the mandate to select under the supervision of ESA, and via ESA’s Best Practices Processes, the services of eligible Resource and Platform Tier Providers for the next phase of the Network of Resources. The NoR portal (https://nor-discover.org) lists in an online directory all the onboarded providers together with their NoR service portfolio. ESA can sponsor or co-fund scientists and value adding users for eligible research, development and pre-commercial projects. The portal also provides users with links to each providers helpdesk and website. This intended tender is for the selection of Resource Tier and Platform Tier providers using cloud services with collocated Sentinel and non-Sentinel data. Resource Tier and Platform Tier providers wishing to contribute to the NoR service directory are invited to provide a proposal. Following the previous NoR Open Call, the tender process is made as simple as possible for interested service providers to respond to.

RHEA has been awarded the EO Digital Platform – EO Network Of Resources 2023-2028 contract (AO/1-11738/23/I-EF), the follow-up of the project Procurement of Earth Observation Exploitation Platform Network Resource Services (ITT AO/1-9217/18/I-LG) finished in November 2023. RHEA has therefore the mandate to select under the supervision of ESA, and via ESA’s Best Practices Processes, the services of eligible Resource and Platform Tier Providers for the next phase of the Network of Resources. The NoR portal (https://nor-discover.org) lists in an online directory all the onboarded providers together with their NoR service portfolio. ESA can sponsor or co-fund scientists and value adding users for eligible research, development and pre-commercial projects. The portal also provides users with links to each providers helpdesk and website. This intended tender is for the selection of Resource Tier and Platform Tier providers using cloud services with collocated Sentinel and non-Sentinel data. Resource Tier and Platform Tier providers wishing to contribute to the NoR service directory are invited to provide a proposal. Following the previous NoR Open Call, the tender process is made as simple as possible for interested service providers to respond to.

tenderTitle: BI-DIRECTIONAL GENERIC CHARGE/DISCHARGE MODULE FOR GENERIC STORAGE SYSTEM - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a bi-directional DC/DC converter able to charge and discharge a generic storage system with a targeted reduction of 50% area and mass in the charge/discharge system.Description: Most of the current state of the art considers a dedicated converter for charging and a dedicated converter for discharging power into and from the energy storage system. This has impacts on the overall area and mass, as just half of the circuitry is in use at a given time. For those missions where mass and volume is a concern, a bi-directional converter allows to increase the power density and therefore to minimize mass and volume. In addition, currently the solution to charge and discharge an energy storage system is specific to the energy storage system in use. This activity aims to develop a bi-directional charge and discharge module, allowing the same circuitry to be used for charging and for discharging. The benefit of the bi-directionality reduces the area and the mass of the HW by 50%. On top, it is intended to analyze a generic solution to cover different energy storage systems (e.g. Li-Ion batteries and RFCS -Regenerative Fuel Cell Systems-). This provides a lot of flexibility, since the HW of the power management subsystem does not depend on the energy storage system, and therefore could be produced in advance. This also could lead to a reduction in time to delivery by 30%, by allowing recurrent use of the same design. The objective is challenging because the behavior of these storage systems is quite different and the converter must adapt to them. A charger/discharge module with bi-directional capability based on a non-isolated DC/DC topology with new switching devices (e.g.GaN based switches) and a versatile control system to adapt to the different storage systems. Possibly digital control may be considered to perform an adequate management of the battery or RFCS. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Confirmation of the scope of the charger/discharge (energy storage systems to be compatible with, power levels...) with a final consolidation of the preliminary requirements - Identify potential solutions (best topologies, control logic, switching devices...) and perform dedicated trade-offs to select a baseline - Design of the baseline, with the appropriate design analysis - Prototype manufacturing of a bi-directional charge and discharge module - Testing of a prototype - Analyse test results, identify and check deviations, implement corrections on the prototype if any to cover deviations to a final designDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

This renovation takes into account the environmental and architectural constraints of this protected site.

tenderTitle: PHOTONICS-BASED OPTICAL APERTURE FOR LASER COMMUNICATION TERMINALS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.056) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a thin optical aperture leveraging advances in integrated photonic technology to reduce the size andweight of space-based optical communication terminals.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of both size and weight of satellite laser communication terminals by 50%.Description: Optical communication terminal solutions with lower size and weight are required to serve the increasing role of small spacecraft for satellitecommercialisation by maximising the amountof payload space for mission-enabling processing or sensors. State-of-the-art optical communicationterminals are often too bulky and heavy for such small platforms and a leap in technology is required. This activity will seek innovative integrated photonicsolutions to replace the telescope subsystem of an optical communication terminal and eliminate as much as possible the need for free-space propagationinside the laser terminal. By doing so, it is expected to greatly reduce the size and inertial mass of the telescope subsystem, enabling for instance furtherreductions in steering assembly size, weight and power.This activity will design and prototype a photonic aperture (or flat telescope) that shall provide good beam quality (for coupling/emitting into/from singlemode waveguides such as single-mode fibres), shall be relatively large (at least several cm in diameter) or provide enough optical gain to enable convincingreplacement of conventional beam expansion and free-space propagation optics (traditional telescope assemblies) in space optical communicationterminals. A foundry-compatible fabrication process of the photonic aperture shall also provide a low-cost telescope alternative by eliminating the need forexpensive optics and assembly and alignment touch labour.The following tasks are envisioned:- Identify the potential solutions and latest innovations in integrated photonic able to replace conventional optical aperture assemblies in space-basedoptical communications for small platforms and/or use cases where accommodation of optical communication terminals is drastically constrained bytheir size and weight.- Develop a preliminary design and expected performance of the chosen solution.- Manufacture and test a prototype and evaluate the performance in a representative laboratory environment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). tenderTitle: MULTI-APERTURE DIGITAL COHERENT AND INCOHERENT GROUND MODEM FOR OPTICAL COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.081) - EXPRO+ (ON REQUEST)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a digital coherent and incoherent signal combining receiver that utilises multiple smalltelescopes, achieving a large effective collection area.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of system cost and complexity by using multiple small apertures to avoid the use of a larger aperture with an adaptive optics system whilemaintaining the total corresponding coupled power-in-fibre.Enabling modular system design, allowing incremental future upgrades to enhance link power budget.Description: The logical progression in optical receiver development is to use a modular receiver design with multiple apertures combined coherently and incoherently.Firstly, small aperture telescopes are significantly less affected by atmospheric disturbances and can operate with cost-effective hardware, such as tilt tracking.Secondly, advancements in large Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and digital signal processing (DSP) blocks can significantly simplifythe optical part of the receiver and enhanced reliability, while shifting the complexity to the digital domain. Functional verification of proposed idea hasbeendemonstrated in laboratory environment by research groups.The present activity shall analyse and demonstrate via a free-space-optical experiment at minimum 10 Gbps for coherent and up to 10 Gbps for incoherentmodulation (e.g. DP-QPSK, OOK) receiver system over atmospheric turbulence conditions that are representative (or worse) of those encountered inGEO/MEO/LEO. A receiver should perform optical front-end conditioning, followed by digital coherent and incoherent multi-channel combination, and thenprovide an output toa modem.This demonstrator will feature, but not be limited to, the following critical functions: cost-efficient tilt-tracking stage, optical multi-channel front end unit withdigital coherent and incoherent combiner, electrical output to a modem.

tenderTitle: HYDRON EVO: MULTI TBPS SPACE BACKBONE NETWORK (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.241) EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective:The objective of this study is to investigate the High-throughput Optical Network evolution (HydRON EVO) as the backbonenetwork enabling a total capacity of tens to hundreds TbpsTargeted Improvements:To assess the feasibility of optical space backbone network with total capacity in the range of tens to hundreds TbpsDescription:Following the terrestrial network analogy, backbone (long-haul) networks provide capacity beyond Terabit-per-second (Tbps) per single line (with links beyond 800 Gbps per wavelength). The current HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) demonstration system will demonstrate single-link communications from 2.5G to 100Gbps, addressing both user access and the lower datarate backbone links. To enable growth of optical space networks, as an extension of the terrestrial fibre network, a space backbone is required to support multi-Tbps capacity in space. The backbone should be interoperable and interface with multiple networks like the one developed in HydRON demonstration system. However, using DWDM technologies and commercial coherent transceivers, the single link capacity can be increased beyond Tbps, and by aggregating multiple channels the network capacity can be increased to tens or even hundreds Tbps.This activity shall address the design and technology trade-offs of a space network backbone exceeding several Tbps and serving other space networks. It shall provide a set of requirements and a system concept. It shall be verified by analysis that the system concept is scalable at higher rates. Interoperability aspects shall be analysed, to guarantee the connectivity among networks (including terrestrial fibre networks). Technology gaps shall be identified and technology roadmap provided. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technologyas well as the operational concept can be demonstrated, to further push the technology borders in terms of data rates/capacity aiming to maintain the strategic leadership position of the Europen/Canadian Industry The activity will also contribute to the evolutionof ESTOL.

tenderTitle: 3U VERSION OF THE ADVANCED POWER ARCHITECTURE (APA) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a small three-rack-unit version of the Advanced Power Architecture (APA) with aim of having a highly compact architecture fit for small missions.Description: The Advanced Power Architecture (APA) is being designed for general ESA mission /medium scale platform but is not addressing smaller mission needs. This activity aims at developing the APA concept in a three-rack-unit (3U) version; this footprint would be suitable for smaller satellites up to 500 kg. The activity targets to investigate the miniaturisation of the already identified functions by integrating novel technologies such as digital control and Gallium Nitride High-Electron Mobility transistor (GaN HEM FET). The Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) has already a 3U version which, if coupled with a 3U version of the APA, it would enable a single frame for a very compact avionics system. In fact, the APA will provide the input power interface, the TM/TC interface, the internal power rails and the internal communication bus. Thus, any platform function not needing internal high speed data communication buses could fit perfectly in the 3U APA. For instance, the solar array drive function or any motor drive function, propulsion valves drive functions, thermal control, etc. The activity targets to enhance industrialisation of power units for mid-size satellites by having the full power system functionality integrated in one unit. If deemed adequate for the application, a cost-effective solution could be available by having the components as COTS. A strong focus on manufacturability and industrialisation will be done, focusing on automatic manufacturing, planar transformers, SMD components, etc. This activity focuses on the development of the Solar Array Regulator (SAR) module with miniaturised DC/DC converter and on the Solar Array Drive Electronics (SADE) demonstrating the applicability of the concept to the entire avionics functions. These will be the firstbuilding blocks for the development of the complete functionality. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Converter andfilter size reduction thanks to the use of HEM FET (GaN) - Inclusion of the Solar Array Drive Electronics to embed all potential EPS need - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard - Test of the breadboard - Validation and verification - Way forward for industrialization

A strong focus on manufacturability and industrialisation will be done, focusing on automatic manufacturing, planar transformers, SMD components, etc. This activity focuses on the development of the Solar Array Regulator (SAR) module with miniaturised DC/DC converter and on the Solar Array Drive Electronics (SADE) demonstrating the applicability of the concept to the entire avionics functions. These will be the firstbuilding blocks for the development of the complete functionality. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Converter andfilter size reduction thanks to the use of HEM FET (GaN) - Inclusion of the Solar Array Drive Electronics to embed all potential EPS need - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard - Test of the breadboard - Validation and verification - Way forward for industrialization

tenderTitle: SUSTAINABLE MINERAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Sustainable mineral resource management involves the responsible extraction, use, and conservation of mineral resources to meet present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. It emphasizes efficient mining practices, minimizing environmental impacts, and restoring ecosystems after extraction. An important component of this approach is the use of Earth observation technologies, which allow the detection of (critical earth) minerals, continuous monitoring of mining activities, land degradation and water quality. The development of novel EO solutions and tools improve transparency, support better decision-making, andhelp detect unsustainable practices in near real time. Combined with recycling, resource efficiency, and strong environmental policies, Earth observation enhances the ability to balance economic development with environmental protection and social responsibility,ensuring long-term sustainability of mineral resources.

tenderTitle: KA-BAND HIGH POWER ACTIVE TRANSMIT INTEGRATED ANTENNA FOR LEO SATCOM APPLICATIONS (ARTES AT 5B.257) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
tenderDescription: Objective:The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test a scaled engineering model of a Ka-Band 45dBW EIRP class active transmit highly integrated antenna for LEO constellations (orbits up to about 1000km) for governmental and commercial application. This includes a thermal management system compatible with high power requirements, use of SiPs to reduce the volume and higher number of elements and beams.Targeted Improvements:-Enabling 45dBW EIRP class active phased array antenna for governmental and commercial connectivity applications.-2 to 3 times increased number of beams compared to state of the art today in Europe.-40 to 50%improvement in mass compared to analogue beamforming-based architecture.Description:Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations require high-capacity integrated active phased array antennas. Today the active antennas available can guarantee only limited flexibility in terms of number of beams, bandwidth and power dissipation. For both commercial and government applications, there is a demand for active antennas composed of more than 1000 radiating elements and enabling a minimum of 40 to 64 simultaneous beams. However, the high integration requirements for accommodating in LEO satellites operating in orbits up to about 1000km creates thermal management challenges. In order to achieve these challenging requirements, current active antenna technology must be significantly improved. On the thermal management, novel heat dissipation concepts must be investigated, developed and demonstrated. Exploring new promising solutions including Pulsed Heat Pipes should be considered. On the beamforming network, trade-off between fully digital and hybrid should be performed, considering the latest technology available on digital processors (using ultra-deep sub-micron technologies) and System-in-Package (SiP) commercial solutions. On radiating elements, recent promising results have been achieved on antenna based on waveguide and PCB technology.This activity will study, develop, and implement a beamforming architecture and thermal management solution for LEO high-capacity integrated active phased array antennas. The selected concept will be implemented as a scaled engineering model and tested in critical environment.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach where:-Phase 1 will study design concepts of beamforming architectures and thermal management solutions for active antenna technology. The solution will be designed and optimised, considering aspects such as the beam forming network architecture, the digital signal processing architecture, the amplification sizing and the thermal management. This phase will include de-risking module implementation at breadboard level with testing. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 900 kEuro.-In the second Phase, a scaled engineering model shall be produced, capable of operating over the full bandwidth to produce flexible number of beams between 4 to 10. The design must be scalable and must include active elements and optimised thermal management system. This scaled engineering model will be developed and validated in a critical environment. The scaled engineering model shall comprise one or more representative payload building blocks, including frequency conversion, signal processing beam forming, high power amplification, filtering and radiating element functions.

tenderTitle: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT OF QUANTUM COMMUNICATION SOURCES (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3H.006) - ON REQUEST
tenderDescription: Objective: Demonstrate the capability and feasibility of high-performance entangled photon sources and their monitoring testbed in space.TargetedImprovements:Creating a capability in Europe and Canada currently not present, to experiment with the operation andperformance of quantum communication sourcesin orbit, enabling future quantum communication systems.Description: Entangled photonsources are at the heart of many technological applications, including novel space-based quantum information networks (QIN).Demonstrating the capability and feasibility of high-performance entangled photon sources in space is an essential step to unlock these maturingtechnologies for emerging quantum communication applications.Disruptive technologies which could benefit from the support ofin-orbit experiment include entanglement based quantum communications, quantuminformation network building blocks (e.g. interfacing entangled photons from space with a quantum memory on ground, quantum teleportation to space,entanglement swapping between space andground), distributed quantum computing, entanglement based quantum gyroscope in space, clocksynchronisation from space, basic science experiments and test of fundamental laws of physics.This activity will carry out an in-orbit experiment of an entangled photon source. Ranging from a mere on-board performance demonstration over a singleoptical downlink scenario to a dual downlink case, different scenarios for in-orbit performance tests shall be carried out. The source performance degradationin orbit shall be measured together with in-orbit assessment of critical/sensitive items. To this end an appropriate in-situ monitoring and measurementtestbed is to be developed and operated in-orbit.

tenderTitle: MULTI WAVELENGTH LASER SOURCE FOR CO-PACKAGED HIGH SPEED SERIAL LINKS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.054) - EXRPO+ (ON REQUEST)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a multi-wavelength, multi-port light source for space applications. The source will need to be energyefficient, compact and able to generate continuous-wave multiple wavelengths output.TargetedImprovements:The multi-wavelength laser is needed to enable high-speed and high-density co-packaged optics data interconnects for space applications.Description: Modern telecommunication satellites use onboard digital processors to meet growing traffic demands. These high throughput processors can handle Tbpsof intra-processor traffic thanks to the adaptation of optical interconnects in placeof traditional electrical harness. When co-packaged photonics becomeavailable for use in space regenerative processors, they will enable even higher data rate on-board interconnects with optical I/Os. This, in turn, will requirean external continuous-wave wavelength division multiplexing laser source for operation. The present activity aims at developing such a laser source forspace use.This activity will develop and test the multi-wavelength source. The source packaging and physical configuration shall consider two variants of opticaloutput; a configuration where each wavelength can be coupled to an individual fibre, and a configuration where multiple wavelengths can be multiplexedto a single fibre output. The environmental effects on the multi-wavelength source output stability should be assessed. The laser source engineeringmodel, together with its electrical and thermal control, should be developed for satellite on-board operation. A definition and demonstration of the opticalparameters together with the measurement methods forthe source used onboard a satellite shall be produced. The parameters should include the numberof wavelengths, wavelength grid spacing, output power, relative intensity noise, side mode suppression ratio and linewidth.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). tenderTitle: RECONFIGURABLE PHOTONIC RF FILTER FOR FLEXIBLE PAYLOADS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.055) - EXPRO+ (ON REQUEST)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a reconfigurable photonic RF filter with adjustable passband and tuneable central frequencybased on photonic integrated circuits.TargetedImprovements:Efficient spectrum management andinterference mitigation for multi-band flexible payloads. Adjustable passband in the range of 36MHz to 1500MHz(target 25MHz to 3000MHz) and tuneable central frequency across Ka/Q/V bands that is not currently existing.Description: In order to address changing market demands during the satellite mission lifetime and for interference mitigation, satellite operators are interested in fullyflexible payload architectures that offer in-orbit RF bandwidth and frequency reconfigurability. To realise fully reconfigurable RF frontends, tuneable RFbandpass filters are envisaged. Photonic RF filter concepts have been developed, demonstrating the capacity to tune both central frequency and bandwidthover a wide frequency range, characteristics not offered by standard microwave equipment.This activity will develop and test an engineering model of a reconfigurable filter based on a Photonic Integrated Circuit assembly. The engineering modelshall implement all the critical functions, adjustment of the passband BW of a filter from 36MHz to 1500MHz (target 25MHz to 3000MHz) and the ability totune the central frequency across the whole of the Ka/Q/V frequency bands. The reconfiguration will be demonstrated by an electronic control of the tensof control points within the photonic circuit, driven by appropriatesoftware that will be developed in the activity. The deliverable will be an engineeringmodel closely resembling a flight unit. Thedevice will be tested under changing thermal condition to manifest that it can counterbalance such changes.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). tenderTitle: FUTURE RAILWAY MOBILE COMMUNICATION SYSTEM (FRMCS) SATELLITE SYSTEM SIMULATOR FOR LOW FREQUENCY SPECTRUM (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.018) EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design a satellite system for FRMCS which is operating in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial counterpart (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), with the purpose to exclusively service the coverage gaps of the terrestrial network while avoiding interference. The performance of such system will be evaluated with the development of a system simulator.Targeted Improvements: - Reduce by 80% the cost of the satellite system for FRMCS.- Reduce by 50% the cost of on-board railway terminals, by allowing a single terminal solution for terrestrial and satellite FRMCS connectivity.Description: The Future RailwayMobile Communication System (FRMCS), being a successor of the GSM-R system, is planned to be operational before GSM-R's predicted saturation in 2030. Through standardisation work, satcom is established as a component of the future system, while it is found that the satellite integration into FRMCS is simplified when satcom is employing the 5G NR, which is the selected air interface for the terrestrial FRMCS access. However, the frequency bands for such a service via satellite and the design of the satellite system are yetto be concluded. The advantages of an innovative approach, where the satellite offers connectivity exclusively to the coverage gapsofsuch terrestrial network, have been recently reported. In fact, such a satellite system targeting only the terrestrial coverage gaps while ignoring the areas serviced by theterrestrial network, will have a lower complexity and overall cost, as fewer satellites of less capacity will be required. In addition, such a satellite system will be able to operate in the same frequency bands as theterrestrial network (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), as each network (terrestrial or satellite) will not be available in the same area where the other network operates and therefore they will not interfere with each other. This usage of the same frequency from the satellite and the terrestrial network not only facilitates the integration of the two networks into FRMCS, but also potentially allow the usage of the same terminal for both networks, a solution that is very favourable for railway operators. This activity will thereforeinvestigate the design of a 5G NR based satellite system for FRMCS which exclusively targets the terrestrial network gaps of communication and operates in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial FRMCS network. The activity will include a traffic characterisation and capacity analysis for the terrestrial network gaps which will then feed the system design and the element sizing of the ground and space components. The impact of the railway-satellite channel for the 900 MHz and the 1900 GHz will also be thoroughly investigated. The best numerologies and 5G NR configurations will also be identified for such a satellite system. The work will be supported by the development of a system simulator which will investigate the FRMCS 5G NR satellite link performance and achieved C/I ratios under a variety of different orbits, system architectures, frequency bands, channel conditions and air interface configurations. The activity will also investigate and conclude on the feasibility of having a single modem and a single antenna equipped on board the trains, which offer connectivity both to the satellite and the terrestrial network at different time instances.

tenderTitle: Retrofit of CT & ELA service stations
tenderDescription:
The Guiana Space Centre has two service stations on its site. These two stations are strategically located at two points: at the entrance to the CSG site, at the Technical Centre site, and the other at the Ensemble de Lancement 3 area. These two stations currently distribute both Diesel and SP95 fuel for passenger vehicles (VL), as well as for trucks and operational machinery.

In order to consolidate and maintain operational service, we need to fully renovate both infrastructures.

The combined fuel volumes per station amount to 350m3/year.

tenderTitle: OPTICAL KEY DISTRIBUTION CONCEPT ASSESSMENT FOR SECURE COMMUNICATION IN SPACE (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL  3A.231) EXPRO+ (ON REQUEST)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a free-space communication link with optical key distribution (OKD) functionality.TargetedImprovements:Improvement of the key distribution rate by at least a factor of 100 with respect to QKD, alternatively, the reduction of the aperture sizes of both terminals(for the same key rate as QKD). Provision of the security assessment for OKD.Description: In the vast majority of cases, the security of communication systems is only ensured at their digital layers, leaving the lowest physical layer open toeavesdropping and interference. The primary concern in space scenarios is passive attacks, where the adversary is often able to capture an even largerportion of the signal than the legitimate receiver(s). At the same time, feasible physical layer security (PLS) solutions must meet the stringent SWaP (size,weight, and power) requirements of space missions and should be easily integrated with data transmission, even in the case of the simplest intensitymodulation/direct detection (IM/DD) links.Optical Key Distribution (OKD) is a promising solution for secure communication. It allows authenticated parties to establish a secure cryptographic key,by exploiting the high directionality of optical beams. By using optical noise, OKD is cost-effective and suitable for free-space communications, such asinter-satellite and satellite-to-ground links. The technique distributes a secure key that can be used for encryption protocols like AES, SSL/TLS, or as aone-time pad. It avoids the complexities and high costs of quantum key distribution (QKD) systems while providing adequate security for free-spacescenarios. OKD keys are quantum-safe, assuming the adversary's detection capability is limited by shot noise.The activity aims to investigate and develop a cost-effective solution for the physical layer security of optical satellite communication links, namely OpticalKey Distribution (OKD), which allows authenticated parties to establish a secure key, by monitoring the presence of an eavesdropper along the satellite to-ground line-of-sight, while avoiding the complexity and resulting significant costs of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) systems. The activity will establishsecurity assumption for OKD and provide the security assessment of the proposed OKD system. The outcome of this work shall be evaluated by a security expert with competencies in the protection of communication links.

tenderTitle: COMPATIBILITY VALIDATION TESTBED OF THE OPTICAL HEAD AND ITS CONTROL OF OPTICAL COMMUNICATION TERMINALS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.015)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a testbed that will test the interoperability between different suppliers of optical communication terminals. Thisshall include free-space optics testing to evaluate the pointing, acquisition, and tracking performance.TargetedImprovements:To enable independent on-ground validation of optical communication terminal interoperability ina facility located in ESA member states.Description: With an increasing number of constellations considering the use of optical inter satellite links and cross-atmospheric links, it is important to test, validateand ultimately certify the interoperability between different laser terminals manufactured by multiple suppliers.This activity will develop the capability of enabling independent interoperability validation between various laser communication terminals. tenderTitle: END TO END DIGITALISATION OF GNC/AOCS DEVELOPMENT EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: ObjectivesTo define the end-to-end digital development of AOCS/GNC subsystem, including definition of artefacts, tools, method andtechniques, as well as needed development, based on a pilot use case application.DescriptionDigitalisation is creating new processes and radically altering existing workflows. The goal of this activity is to analyse the digital transformations to come for the AOCS/GNC subsystem. This includes, analysis of influences of digitalisation on subsystem development process; impact on standard AOCS/GNC artefacts produced in ESA projects; impact of digitalisation and Model Based engineering on the AOCS/GNC verification process.This activity aims at defining the tools, methods and techniques to be used (and developed) for digital engineering in AOCS/GNC domain engineering, as well as the definition of needed future developments. It is intended to demonstrate the gain of the digitalisationof the process on a pilot case.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Assess the impact of digitalisation of AOCS/GNCprocess on the production of artefacts used in the project cycles reviews as review inputs (in replacement of current standard documentation), e.g. based on current ESA reviews definition and objectives, define possible qualitative and quantitative artefacts to support these reviews, its' relation with requirements engineering, modelling validation, engineering management plan and VV cycle-Revisit a typical AOCS development case in terms of tasks, inputs/outputs flow, products, process, skills, tools, facilities to define who/what, at which steps, on which facilities, and how could the AOCS subsystem be embedded in a Model Based System Engineering process.Specifically including:- Model-based flow-down of pointing requirements and associated VV cycle ,- Data sharing: structure and phases (importance of data range for AOCS robustness, ie. nominal values and their range of variation/uncertainty ; AOCS tuning data evolution and configuration ; AOCS data tuning dependency to the use -e.g. variable with specific tuning for some testing, somepart of the mission lifetime, etc...) .- Continuity of the models used for AOCS VV and avionics/system VV, together with continuity of the test reference scenarios/success criteria and relation with system requirements,- Model-based analysis of AOCS simulations and test results.Deliverables:Report

tenderTitle: POWER MANAGEMENT IC WITH LOW VOLTAGE DYNAMIC POINT OF LOAD REGULATION - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To develop a Power Management IC with low voltage dynamic point of load regulation able to supply independently multiplesupply rails.Description: Exploration in harsh environments with long lunar nights and limited amount of energy poses difficult challenges for the success of these missions. Traditional standby modes, which consume a substantial amount of power when inactive, have proven detrimental for applications of this nature. By utilizing advanced power management techniques such as dynamic voltage scaling, selective rail supply, and sequenced control of FPGAs and microcontrollers, significant energy savings can be achieved. This Power Management ICs could be utilized in all the processing boards reducing not only the consumption during the long eclipses by entering into deep hibernation modes but also during the sun phase by adapting the consumption of the processors to their workload. Under this activity an Power Management Integrated Circuit (PMIC) is developed that is able to supply multiple rail voltages required by FPGAs andmicrocontrollers. The supply voltages are able to adapt dynamically to the workload of the FPGA or microcontroller, even switching-off non used logic, improving significantly their energy efficiency. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirement consolidation - Analysis of suitable Architectures for Power Management ICs - Design and development of a Power- Test and test results assessmen

tenderTitle: POWER EFFICIENT FAST FOURIER TRANSFORM IP CORE - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop and refine a power efficient Fast Fourier Transform IP Core for FPGA/ASIC implementationDescription: This activity focuses on the design, development and testing of a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) block to be used in space applications, which is to be developed as a configurable, reusable IP Core. A reusable IP Core is a hardware model, normally described in VHDL, which is fully verified and can be used as a building block in designs for several targets, such as FPGAs from different vendors or as an ASIC, providing savings in mission costs and development times. The developed IP shall be able to solve complex FFT / inverse FFT; convolve and correlate vectors in frequency domain, with a length up to 32768 points, gain and phase correction, filtering, etc. Several applications will benefit from such an IP Core: - Active Microwave Remote Sensing: Radar Onboard Processing, such as SAR Image Formation, RFI Detection, Compression - Passive Microwave Remote Sensing: Hyperspectral Radiometers (channelisation, RFI detection), Compression Although FFT IPs are available commercially, fine spectral resolution together with high sampling rate (e.g. direct conversion) leads to long FFT lengths, which may not be available in commercial IPs. Furthermore, many of these applications require high-throughput, e.g. channelisation, together with real-time constraints. These requirements give raise to needs regarding adequate standardized Input/Output interfaces (such as AXI-Stream buses) as well as efficient FFT architectures, to cope with the throughput. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Specifications of the FFT IP Core, taking into account the different application needs. - Description of the IP core in VHDL. The IP shall be configurable. - Development of a tool that helps the user configure and generate the IP core based on specific mission requirements. - Verification and Synthesis on relevant space FPGA devices. - Laboratory demonstrator The developed IP core will be offered to future missions and projects as part of the ESA IP Core's portfolio, which already includes a catalogue of more than 20 cores which comprise typical digital functions used in space applications (TMTC, EDAC, SpaceWire, CAN, LEON2-FT, OBDH, etc).Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). tenderTitle: EXPLORING MISSION CONCEPTS FOR QUANTUM SPACE NETWORK (QUASAR) DEMONSTRATOR (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3H.012) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to investigate mission concepts for entanglement distribution QUAntum SpAce netwoRk (QUASAR) in the context ofQuantum Information Networks. The aim is to define preliminary requirements of the in-orbit-experiment, involving a space segment and at least twodistant ground stations, required to verify entanglement distribution from space.TargetedImprovements:The targeted improvement is to mature the quantum payload concept definition and mission requirement, to improve the viability of the in-orbitexperiment of satellite entanglement distribution with the current and near-future technology.Description: The development of Quantum Information Networks (QIN) is rapidly increasing, driven largely by the expansion of terrestrial fibre networks. However,long distance quantum communication remains fundamentally constrained by fibre losses. To overcome this limitation, the integration of a space segmentis essential. A critical step towards this integration is the execution of an in-orbit experimentto validate space-to-ground entanglement distribution. Thismission would represent a major milestone in demonstrating the satellites' role in the expansion of Quantum Information Networks.The proposed activity aims to prove the technical feasibility of space-based QIN. Consequently, this would strengthen the market potential by confirmingsatellite-to-ground entanglement distribution capabilities. The main tasks of this activity will: identifying the critical elements involved in the space and ground segments (for technical and economic suitability); exploring the various possible system concepts by modelling to determine possibilities, characteristics or the criticality of certain elements; comparing these concepts against the needs, to determine levels of uncertainty andrisk; estimating the technical and industrial feasibility; identifying, for each possible system concept, the constraints relating to costs, schedules, organisation, utilisation (operations, implementation,maintenance), production and disposal, as well as the estimated margins in relation to the targets.

tenderTitle: FLEXIBLE DIGITAL COHERENT OPTICAL MODULE FOR OPTICAL COMMUNICATION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.016)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop the required digital processing hardware needed for an optical transceiver supporting multiple optical waveformsat different data rates on a single wavelength.TargetedImprovements:Provide a European solution for a flexible space optical communication coherent modem capable of reaching 100 Gbps.Description: Multiple optical transceivers are being proposed and developed by emerging suppliers in Europe. These transceivers are either already available for theterrestrial market or are currently under development for satellite applications. Some suppliers aim for less complex products, targeting 2.5 Gbps links,while some others utilise advanced optical modulation formats capable of achieving data rates beyond 100 Gbps. Consequently, the creation of an in-orbitreconfigurable transceiver is crucial to addressing different needs from back-bone network satellites and customer satellites connecting to such satellitenetworks. Flexibility in wavefront and optical interfaces will enable grater interoperability and allow flexible services to be provided by the existing andfuture European and international satellites. This activity will develop the real-time digital processing hardware of a flexible digital coherent opticaltransceiver. The digital processing module is typically composed of several chiplets including a flexible chiplet (DSP, FEC, turbulence mitigation,mod/demod), a SERDES chiplet and analogue/digital converter chiplets (TIA/Drivers, ADC/DAC). The key aspects to be considered are limited size, weightand power consumption while enabling throughput as high as 100 Gbps. Flexibility in waveform as well as client-side interfaces is required.The main engineering tasks include:- Identification of the individual components and connection interfaces (hardware and software).- Design of the transceiver architecture and development of a virtual prototype (e.g. formal verification).- Implementation of a transceiver scaled EM.

tenderTitle: ASSESSMENT OF 400 TO 800 GBPS DIGITAL COHERENT OPTICAL MODULES FOR SATELLITE OPTICAL COMMUNICATION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.017) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: The objective of the activity is to assess the suitability of the latest generation of COTS Digital Coherent Optical (DCO) modules for optical intersatelliteand cross-atmospheric links.TargetedImprovements:Enabling optical inter satellite links (OISLs) with adata rate four times higher than previously demonstrated. Improving the efficiency of transceivers(energy/bit).Description: The current generation of coherent transceivers Digital Coherent Optical (DCO) modules tested and implemented in current laser communication terminalsallow data rates from 100 to 200 Gbps. However, the latest generation of COTS DCO (fibre networks) extends this range to 800 Gbps, leveraging severaltechnological advancements, in a new (smaller) form factor.This activity will analyse and assess the performance and the environmental suitability of the COTS transceivers for their potential use, as well as theadvantages coming from using those devices in space. Relevant performance metrics are, for example, the bit error rate vs. received power, the receiversensitivity, and the synchronisation and re-synchronisation capability (during acquisition, tracking and operation). For the performance assessment, a linkemulator shall be used for both OISL and the cross-atmospheric links.t.

tenderTitle: HIGH-THROUGHPUT OPTICAL CHANNEL FOR SYNCHRONISATION OF QUANTUM COMMUNICATION LINKS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3H.007) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to assess the feasibility of the extending the use of the terrestrial time synchronisation protocols to space-based optical linksfor sub-ns synchronisation required by quantum communication links.TargetedImprovements:Improve the communication rate of a quantum channel by improving the time synchronisation of space-to-ground terminals with a target in the range of10 picosecond, by exploiting classical optical communication links with minimal communication overhead.Description: In the last decades, several protocols for precise synchronisation have been developed exploiting high throughput communication network based onoptical fibres. One example of these protocols is White Rabbit, an advanced synchronisation technology initially developed at CERN for synchronisationof devices with sub-ns accuracy through an ethernet network. Another example is ELSTAB, a protocol which works by electronically stabilising thepropagation delay in an optical fibre link using a feedback loop that compares forward and backward signals to dynamically compensate for phasevariations.This activity will study terrestrial protocols that can reach sub-ns synchronisation accuracy and evaluate their feasibility over a satellite-to-ground opticalchannel. For the suitable protocol, the activity shall produce a prototype of the transceiver demonstrating the capability of coping with typical satellite linkimpairment. The activity shall identify and investigate the most promising protocol to be used in space based optical links, evaluate the feasibility of suchtechnology, identify the technological gap, perform early development activity for the critical technologiesand estimate the expected performances of suchan implementation. The activity shall investigate the main differentiators between satellite and ground-based communication channel, including, but notlimited to:- Asymmetry of the forward and return link delays, due to satellite motion- Frequency shift of the modulated signal, due to Doppler effect- Intensity fluctuation of the optical signaldue to turbulence effects- Overall value of link delays (exceeding 100 ms roundtrip for MEO)- Effects of atmospheric refraction on light propagation- Mechanical instabilities of terminals (e.g. ground telescope).For each of the differentiators, the study shall analyse the impact on the protocol feasibility, the potential mitigation strategies that can be implemented,and the expected feasibility performance figure of the final system.The activity shall start with a feasibility study, on the impact of the differentiators on the protocol extension for use in space. Upon positive assessment ofthe feasibility study, the activity shall target the necessary technological development, toward a demonstration of an end-to-end synchronisation system,over an emulated communication channel between two optical terminal breadboards. The channel emulation shall reproduce the most relevant features,such as the changein delay time, the signal fluctuations and frequency shift.

tenderTitle: FAST AND LOW DARK CURRENT DETECTOR FOR EO LIDARS EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop a prototype focal plane detector for lidar receivers in the 935 nm/1064 nm wavelength bands.Description: Earth Observation (EO) lidar instruments on-orbit can provide atmospheric vertical profile information and resolve surface structures.For EO lidar operating in the near-infrared, detector technologies must move away from Accumulating-CCD detectors towards materialsand technologies that give sufficient sensitivity in these wavebands. Promising technologies include InGaAs Avalanche Photodiodes (APDs) operating in linear mode or Geiger-mode like Single-Photon Avalanche Diodes (SPADs). This activity assess focal plane requirements from concept EO lidar instruments to derive the detector requirements and formulate concept designs. Based on this, prototype devices are manufactured and key characteristics, measured. The architecture for synchronisation between multiple APD/SPAD arrays is also assessed for swath Lidars, where an array of APDs or SPAD detectors synchronized to emitted beams could allow to increase currenttens of meters ground sampling distance to a wide width Lidar instrument, thus allowing for better world coverage and re-visit frequency. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements assessment for detectors of future EO lidar instrumentation -Design and manufacture of prototype detectors - Electro-optic characterisation of prototype detectors - Assessment of detector characteristics against EO lidar instrumentation requirements and identification of potential design improvementsDeliverables: Prototype, Report.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. tenderTitle: AI-AUGMENTED HAZARD DETECTION AND AVOIDANCE FOR THE L4 ENCELADUS LANDER - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: ObjectivesAssess the feasibility of using physics-based granular dynamics simulation to model the formation of cryovolcanic terrains on Enceladus and derive insights into surface compactness. Develop a proof-of-concept ML model for inferring snow/ice geophysicalproperties (e.g., density, snow water equivalent) by correlating terrestrial in-situ scientific data with satellite remote sensing observations. Initiate the adaptation of classical, optimization-based HDA frameworks to integrate AIderived geophysical safety maps, establishing a baseline for a future hybrid HDA architecture. Conduct an extensive performance and resource consumption benchmark of key AI and HDA software components on representative space-grade hardware, establishing the trade-space between algorithmic capability and on-board computational budgetDescriptionThe ESA Voyage 2050 L4 mission to Enceladus requires an autonomous landing in the South Polar Terrain to achieve its core astrobiological objectives. This environment presents unique challenges that transcend classical HDA capabilities. Landing hazardsare not only geometric (e.g., slopes, rocks), but also geophysical. Due to the unknown load-bearing capacity of cryovolcanic surface deposits, landing sites can appear perfectly flat and clear of hazards and yet be catastrophically unsafe. Classical existing Hazard Detection and Avoidance (HDA) frameworks targeting Moon and Mars, are highly mature for geometric hazard assessment but are not designed to infer subsurface geophysical properties from remote sensing data. This activity shall address this critical technology gap by investigating the integration of AI/ML-based geophysicalinference into a proven HDA decision-making architecture. Additionally, the severe power and computational constraints of a solar-powered missionto Saturn imposea hard limit on the complexity of on-board AI. It is currently unknown what level of "intelligence" is achievable within a realistic resource budget. This activity shall perform the foundational trade-off analysis required to inform mission designers of the necessary hardware and power provisions for a reliable and capable AI-augmented HDA system

tenderTitle: NAVIGATION INNOVATION SUPPORT PROGRAMME ELEMENT 3  STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS
tenderDescription: Under NAVISP Element 3, the Agency issues this Call for Proposals for the development of initiatives in the Position, Navigation and Timing domain. Element 3 is focused on participating States' priorities and aims at supporting their national navigation activities along the whole value chain. Element 3 configures as an ad-hoc support element, which is envisaged per country and possibly per domain, for the development and promotion of products, applications and services based on GNSS and more widely on PNT systems. Following participating states request, ESA may provide technical assistance in various areas. Element 3 configures as an opportunity for the participating States delegations to animate and coordinate discussions with national entities and to set up the processes to identify and federate institutional demands. This will foster cooperation as well as possible national partnerships with a wide diversity of actors, enlarging the national space community (agency, industries, universities, and research centres) and strengthening its relationships with authorities, organisations, institutions, industries, and research actors from non-space sectors. Industry and research institutes of Participant States are encouraged to contact the NAVISP Element 3 team to discuss the development of activities of national relevance and matching institutional interests. Details on the tendering process and preparing the Full Proposal are provided in the Standard Call for Proposals.

tenderTitle: Recommissioning of the S3A Facility
tenderDescription:
The project's objective is to recommission the currently disused S3A building to accommodate empty or fueled payloads before their resume campaigns at the S3B/S1 or S5 EPCUs and/or the EFA.

The objective is to meet the increased production rate at the Launch Base and guarantee the availability of the EPCUs.

 

CNES has defined a payload storage strategy that takes into account the SVG constraints and those related to the overall building rehabilitation.

 

S3A is a former filling and encapsulation building with existing installations and systems:

Propellant retention systems in the highbays
Three cranes in the filling and encapsulation halls
An air conditioning system including a toxic vapor extraction function
An obsolete fluid and air network for operational activities and maintaining the building's airtightness
An obsolete toxic gas treatment system in the filling halls
Technical rooms
 

All of these systems will be upgraded to meet the project's objectives.

tenderTitle: A-PRIORI HAZARD MAPPING AND LANDMARK GENERATION FOR ENCELADUS LANDING EXPRO+
tenderDescription: ObjectivesTo evaluate the capabilities of hazard mapping and landmark generation during an Enceladus orbiting phase.DescriptionAkey challenge for landing on Enceladus lies in identifying a safe touchdown zone that aligns with the capabilities of the onboard Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) system. This challenge can be addressed either prior to descent by relying on sufficientGNC accuracy to target a pre-identified safe zone or during descent through a real-timeHazard Detection and Avoidance (HDA) system thatscans and adapts the trajectory toward detected safe areas. However, real-time HDA introduces significant complexity and uncertainty,especially during a phase with limited recovery options.In contrast, a-priori hazard mapping leverages a longer, less vulnerableorbital phase during which potential landing sites are periodically observed. Although limited by orbital altitude and visibility constraints, this method benefits from early hazard detection and allows for more complex processing with ground support and less real-time pressure. The key question is whether this method can achieve sufficient hazard detection capability andwhether the lander'sGNCsystem can accurately navigate to the identified safe zones.The primary objective of this activity is to assess the hazard mappingcapabilities of an orbiter passing periodically above potential landing sites on Enceladus. A secondary objective is to evaluate the accuracy of landmark generation from these mappings, which could assist the lander during descent to guide it toward the selected landing zone.The scope of work includes the following tasks:1. Creation of Virtual Enceladus Terrain Models: Develop detailed virtual models ofEnceladus around candidate landing sites in coordination with the Agency.2. Orbital Camera View Simulation: Simulate camera observations from the orbiter'strajectory, accounting for a variety of possible hardware configurations, including fieldofview and detector characteristics.3. Surface Mapping Pipeline Development: Conduct trade-offs and implement surfacereconstruction pipelines from multiple monocular images simulated in the previous task.4. Hazard Detection Procedure Implementation and Testing: Develop and evaluate ahazard detection algorithm against the reference terrain models to determine detectioneffectiveness and statistical significance.5. Landmark Accuracy Testing: Assess the accuracy and robustness of landmarksgenerated from reconstructed terrain models and evaluate their detectability from differentcamera views during descent.
