tenderTitle: EUROPEAN ULTRA-DEEP SUB-MICRON BEAMFORMING CHIP IP CORE FOR SATCOM CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 5C.539)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop a European beamforming chip IP core based on ultra-deep sub-micron technology for satcom constellations. Power consumption shall be minimised. Selectable waveform specific features shall be implemented to support a wide range of use cases including pre-coding and beam hopping. A test chip with compatible interfaces to high speed SerDes (Serialiser/Deserialiser) providing reliable connectivity for high throughput satellites of LEO and MEO constellations shall be designed and manufactured.Targeted Improvements: - Enabling a European or Canadian source of digital beamforming IP core for active phased array antennas.- Enabling features such as signal structure, beam hopping and precoding.- Minimised power consumption of less than 300mW per channel.Description: Due to the demand for large capacity and high spectral efficiencies, active array antennas are being increasingly employed for telecom satellites. These antennas are already playing an important role in next-generation high throughput satellite (HTS) communications together with the large low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO) constellations being implemented worldwide. Digital Beamforming (DBF) is considered the most flexible beamforming architecture and has advantages over analogue beamforming for receiving and transmitting wideband signals, and for multi-beam reconfigurable applications. However, it requires data converters and RF front-ends for each antenna element, increasing the complexity and power consumption.In this activity, a digital beamforming IP core will be developed, fabricated as a scaled Engineering Model test chip and tested based on ultra sub-micron technology (targeting 7nm or lower). Power consumption shall be minimised, targeting 300mW per channel. Selectable waveform specific features shall be implemented to support a wide range of use casesincluding pre-coding and beam hopping. The IP core shall enable Beamforming Networks with a total bandwidth scalable from GHz to hundreds of GHz for dynamic beam configuration, to achieve a BFIC of 32 GHz capacity with scalable frequency from L-Band to Ka-Band and frequency agnostic topology.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach where:- Phase 1 includes a comparative architectural study of at least four digital beam forming IC integration models. An evaluation of technology node implications shall be performed (e.g. leading-edge vs. trailing-edge). Phase 1 shall explore if a common architecture could support different use-cases (broadband, D2D) e.g. lowering DAC/ADC sampling rates and smart switching (bypassing digital mixing, decimation/interpolation) to maintain beam count while adjusting per-beam bandwidth. A system topology shall be evaluated and defined from the digital processor to the antenna for the placement of the beamforming network (daisy chain, star etc.). The output of Phase 1 is an evaluation of the critical IP blocks via design simulation concluding with tape-out of the design. Phase 1 budget is up to 1,200kEur.- In Phase 2 the architecture and technology for the beamforming chip IP shall be fully designed, implemented and tested to scaled engineering model level. This test chip will be representative of a scaled version of the final potential product. Scaled EM testing will include radiation exposure, thermal cycling, and performance benchmarking against existing space-grade beamforming chips.IP cores developed in this activity shall be available for further development by ESA Member State and Canadian industries at fair and reasonable market conditions.

tenderTitle: FAST NETWORK ENTRY PROCEDURE FOR USER TERMINALS IN MULTI-ORBIT BROADBAND SYSTEMS (ARTES AT 3A.233) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
tenderDescription: Objective: The aim of the activity is to design, develop and test a network entry procedure mechanism for user terminal modems of multi-orbit constellation systems.Targeted Improvements:Reduction by 50% the time to enter the network compared to single orbitalshell procedure used today.Description: Modem procedures for initial entry into the network are relatively complex in Non-Geostationary Orbit (NGSO) systems, in comparison to Geostationary Orbit (GSO), due to the needed management of mobility aspects. Modem procedures for initial entry into the network can take up to tens of minutes, depending on the starting conditions at modem switch on and constellation characteristics (e.g. orbit altitude and number of satellites). Most major satcom operators now feature multi-orbitcapabilities combining LEO/MEO and GEO assets, however nowadays these procedures are still mostly implemented considering a singleorbital shell and the user terminal must connect to each shell independently. In the frame of multi-orbit topology this is sub-optimal as only a subset of satellites are used. Besides there is a benefit to using the more "static" shells (e.g. GEO or MEO orbit) of a multi-orbit constellation to facilitate beam scanning and coarse synchronisation. The challenge is to design the specific mechanisms on the control plane that would enable to use all satellites of a multi-orbit constellation for network entry procedure, even if a different satellite from a different shell will eventually be used for the user traffic.The activity shall design, develop andtest a signalling mechanism enabling to perform network entry on any satellite of a multi-orbit constellation, independently of thesatellite targeted for passing the traffic. All aspects of the network entry procedure shall be covered until a steady state connected mode is reached, i.e. initial satellite search (e.g. via beam scanning), coarse synchronisation and modem acquisition, log-on procedure, etc. The procedure shall be assessed over different starting conditions around modem switch-on (e.g. "cold" start without location information, coarse location information, etc.). The ground segment architecture shall also be taken into consideration. A testbed shall be developed, implementing the multi-orbit constellation as well the waveform and signalling mechanisms, to perform theperformance verification

tenderTitle: AUTONOMOUS AND ADAPTABLE ATTITUDE AND ORBIT CONTROL FOR SATCOM CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 4C.075) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test an Attitude and Orbit Control System (AOCS) with increased level of on-board autonomy, robustness to failures, mission adaptability for satcom constellations.Targeted Improvements: - Increased AOCS autonomy, reduction of ground Telecommands, flight procedures and operational constraints by 30%- Faster response to on-board failures/improved system availability by 20%- AOCS adaptable to different missions, facilitating industrial re-useDescription: Telecom missions make use of frequent communication ground control and current state-of-the art AOCS for such missions have a limited degree of on-board autonomy. While this may simplify the overall design of AOCS on-board functions, it results in a significantground operational effort such as mode-switching and specific configuration changes.Moreover, today's AOCS architectures require significant effort and time to be adapted for different missions. Recent studies have shown that increased level of autonomy can be potentially achieved for specific operations such as orbit raising to nominal orbit (e.g. to GEO), orbit management (e.g. station keeping) or collision avoidance. Furthermore, otherstudies showed that implementing a single-mode AOCS with virtual sensors/actuators abstraction modules employing advanced estimation/control techniques could potentially reduce the operational effort in managing theAOCS during the mission.The activity will design, develop and test (in a high-fidelity simulator with Processor in-the-loop) a novelAOCS on-board software based on state-of-the art single AOCS mode and virtual sensors/actuator modules consisting of all the mainAOCS functions (sensors/actuator processing, estimation, guidance, control, embedded FDIR). The AOCS software willimplement advanced estimation, control, optimisation algorithms alongside decision-making capabilities, enabling the system to adapt to various spacecraft configurations/mission phases without mode transitions and ground assistance. In addition, the AOCS software will run with any number or types of sensors/actuators requiring minimal adaptation and will be agnostic to the type of on-board processor used. Theusecase shall cover all the mission phases from separation orbit acquisition to nominal pointing modes, orbitalmanoeuvres, safe mode and controlled re-entry.This activity shall demonstrate and evaluate:- reduction of operational effort and ground interfaces thus increasing on-board autonomy- increased availability thanks to embedded FDIR- adaptability of the architecture to any mission phase- re-usability for different missions.This activity complements the definition work performed on the architectures for autonomy identified in the frame of the Intelligent System Initiative.

tenderTitle: GROUND STATION FOCAL PLANE ASSEMBLY AND ACQUISITION SYSTEM FOR LOW-ELEVATION OPTICAL COMMUNICATION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.087) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop the ground equipment required to enable optical communication with spacecrafts at low elevation angles,including Optical Ground Station (OGS) downlink fibre coupling and Pointing, Acquisition Tracking (PAT) sequence elements.TargetedImprovements:The target improvement for LEO-Ground optical communication links is to increase of theoperation time by a factor of two. The target improvement forGEO-Ground optical communication links is to increase the usable spatial coverage of the GEO satellite by a factor of two.Description: To date, numerous optical satellite communication links have beensuccessfully demonstrated. Most of these experiments have operated at elevationangles exceeding 25 degrees to overcome significantatmospheric propagation challenges, such as intense turbulence. However, for LEO satellites,about half of their visibility in a circular orbit occurs between 5 and 25 elevation. Therefore, overcoming challenges with low elevation optical links coulddouble operation time. For GEO satellites, the elevation angle remains constant; however, enabling low-elevation links can potentially double thesatellite's spatial coverage on Earth. Moreover, improvements in low-elevation optical links have significant impact on both classical and quantumcommunications.This activity will examine the necessary techniques and develop the required hardware to facilitatelow elevation optical communication links through theatmosphere. This will involve namely: Study the required techniques to enable low elevation links and provide trade-off analysis Design and develop the PAT fibre-coupled receiver systems of an OGS that enables optical communication links at low elevations Integrate the optical PAT/receiver systems to an identified OGS Perform an experimental link campaign at low elevations Analysis of the obtained results and conclude on a way forward towards higher TRL of the technology developed under this contract.

tenderTitle: Scapesuit replacement for loading opération
Drone fleet for CSG Protection and Security (Pre-launch sweep drone – E8) (Doubt removal drone – E6) (Multi-missions drone – C13) (Tethered drone)
tenderDescription:
Context:
Today's UAVs have increasingly powerful, sophisticated and versatile technological capabilities, which can provide considerable support for surveillance and protection of people, operations and installations.
Given its operational scope, the CSG wishes to use drones for the following activities:
- Sweep the CSG and surrounding area prior rocket launch.
- Clearing up suspicious incidents.
- Tracking transfers and convoys of hazardous materials.
- Atmospheric measurements (toxic and non-toxic gases).
- Supervision during accident response.
Description:
To facilitate systems integration and ensure optimized management of resources during operations, a single ecosystem or architect is envisaged to cover the various missions.
The fleet could include several models (aerial, wired, unmanned ground vehicle, maritime) and different on-board sensors.
The drones can be deployed automatically, but can also be controlled remotely by an authorized pilot at any time.
To facilitate the transmission of instructions to remote areas, and the escalation of alerts, the data flow will be encrypted and retransmitted securely to various points on the CSG:
- Sweep operation: replace the sweep of the CSG and surrounding area currently carried out by helicopter with a plane/drone before each rocket launch. The drone will follow a pre-programmed path, while taking video footage.
- Doubt removal: the drone will travel to the site where the incident has been detected to verify the nature of the situation (in the event of a perimeter alarm being triggered, rapid observation in the event of a particular situation, inspection, etc.).
- Follow-up of transfers and convoys.
- Atmospheric measurements (toxic or non-toxic gases) during launches or for pollution research in the event of an accident.
- Accident response supervision: photo/video recognition, determination of impacted areas, delimitation of perimeters. Reconnaissance around buildings in the event of a crisis, to ensure that people reach a rallying point. Search for victims, debris, demining, post-launch mapping.

The drones can be deployed automatically, but can also be controlled remotely by an authorized pilot at any time.
To facilitate the transmission of instructions to remote areas, and the escalation of alerts, the data flow will be encrypted and retransmitted securely to various points on the CSG:
- Sweep operation: replace the sweep of the CSG and surrounding area currently carried out by helicopter with a plane/drone before each rocket launch. The drone will follow a pre-programmed path, while taking video footage.
- Doubt removal: the drone will travel to the site where the incident has been detected to verify the nature of the situation (in the event of a perimeter alarm being triggered, rapid observation in the event of a particular situation, inspection, etc.).
- Follow-up of transfers and convoys.
- Atmospheric measurements (toxic or non-toxic gases) during launches or for pollution research in the event of an accident.
- Accident response supervision: photo/video recognition, determination of impacted areas, delimitation of perimeters. Reconnaissance around buildings in the event of a crisis, to ensure that people reach a rallying point. Search for victims, debris, demining, post-launch mapping.

tenderTitle: HIGH TEMPERATURE HEAT TRANSPORT SYSTEM FOR OXYGEN PRODUCTION ISRU PILOT PLANT - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To develop a high temperature heat transport system for oxygen production ISRU Pilot Plant, providing temperature control for the pilot plant vacuum distillation cavity.DescriptionThe ISRU Pilot Plant mission concept comprises the down-scaled production of oxygen in support of sustainable human lunar exploration. The oxygen production process is based on molten-saltelectrolysis of lunar regolith. One of the challenges in the ISRU Plant operation is the thermalmanagement of the processes, such as regolith sintering, electrolysis, salt recovery, fluidmanagement and processing, and LOX storage. These, take place at different temperatures, goingfrom high temperatures (up to 1100degC) to cryogenics.The plant requires a solution to provide temperature control with a variable conductance to adedicated radiator for the pilot plant vacuum distillation cavity, operating alternatively at 600degC(distillation) and 900degC (salt re-melting). Furthermore, the developed system will cover other functions such as temperature homogenization of thermal cavities for regolith processing at high temperatures and temperature control of large thermal zone operating at 750degC.This activity aims at developing a breadboard (BB) of a high temperature heat transport system for oxygen production ISRU pilot plant based which is freeze tolerant and has heat transport capabilityup to 700 W with heat transport distance of 1 m. The system shall be able to operate in temperaturerange of 400-1100degC.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of existing technologiesand trade-offs of various housing materials and workingfluids.- Development of the technical specification- Detailed design of the high temperature heat transport system- Manufacture of breadboards (BB)- Testing of the Breadboards in the specified temperature range under vacuum conditions.- Correlate test results and provide a detail assessment on the future work.

tenderTitle: IN-FLIGHT ELECTRO-STATIC DISCHARGE MONITOR FOR SPACECRAFT - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: To develop non-intrusive sensors for the characterization of Electro-Static Discharge on Spacecraft (e.g. for LEO constellations) together with an on-board events detection algorithm based on advanced approaches (e.g. AI based).Description: Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) phenomena on spacecraft have been estimated to contribute to around 20% to 25% of satellites anomalies overall.Yet, in-flight characterization of spacecraft ESDs in-flight has never been undertaken in a systematic way. In addition, while mitigation strategies are known for classical s/c configurations, new technologies (e.g. flexible solar arrays) require specific characterization in terms of risk (including in-flight) in order to demonstrate their maturity. The need for ensuring European space assetsresilience in LEO combined with the trend to mass product, fly and operate low power low mass constellation satellites calls for efficient and standardized environmental effects diagnostics, among which the one proposed here. The occurrence of ESDson Spacecraft in-flight depends on specific spacecraft electrical configurations and coupling with environments. LEO constellations growing market are subject to such risk as reported in the case of present constellations with thousands of events observed in flight (GEO (telecom, earth observation), MEO (navigation, orbit raising), as well as SSO polar environments also present a risk in that respect) due toboth surface and internal charging. From there, identifying relevant probing location on spacecraft systems where to systematicallyaccommodate non-intrusive /low resources sensors (e.g. current probes and well located RF receivers) would be of high interest to primes, spacecraft designers and agencies to improve our understanding of ESD phenomena in space and its relation to anomalies. In particular, the systematic integration of such sensors on low resource low mass constellation elements should enable large scale environmental effects diagnostics and improve the constellations resilience. This activity shall carry two phases in parallel or sequentially: Phase 1 - Review the state of the art in ESD detection and monitoring on spacecraft - Propose a concept design for a non-intrusive and system embedded method to detect, locate and measure arcing waveform signals onboard satellites - Perform breadboard testing to demonstrate critical functionalities - Define a consolidated design for an ESD monitor - Define a way forward to reach a TRL of 6 Phase 2 - Assess available methodologies (including AI/ML based) and propose a concept design for an on-board events detection algorithm - Develop a breadboard model to simulate events detection and test the detection method - Consolidate the design and propose a detailed design - Establish a development roadmap.http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

tenderTitle: COPERNICUS SPACE COMPONENTS - COMPETITIVE FRAME CONTRACTS - ESA GROUND SEGMENT OPERATIONS FRAMEWORK PRODUCTION SERVICE
tenderDescription: COPERNICUS SPACE COMPONENT - COMPETITIVE FRAME CONTRACTS -ESA Ground Segment Operations Framework Production Service This procurement targets the delivery of the Copernicus Sentinels Production Operations Service (Copernicus Production Service). The CopernicusProduction Service is a key element of the Copernicus Space Component (CSC) operations in charge of generating the Copernicus user level data for each Sentinel satellite, starting from the acquired satellite data stream. The Copernicus Production Service includesthe following functionalities:-Systematic production for processing all the satellite data acquired into a set of pre-defined user level data that are made systematically and fully available to users;-On-demand production, allowing the generation of any user level data from archived lower level user data -Reprocessing, for the bulk re-generation of user level data Copernicus Production Service will be based on service providers' technical solution in line with the ESA defined interfaces, and the use of the Instrument Data Processors (IPF) provided by ESA for the generation of the user level data.The performance of the Copernicus Production Service will be managed through a Service Level Agreement and the measurement of the service performance itself through a set of Key Performance Indicators.The Copernicus Production Service will be procured through the ESA Framework Agreements procedure, as established at Article 15 of ESA Procurement Regulations (ESA/REG/001, rev. 3 which can be downloaded at the following URL: http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). This procedure follows a two-steps procurement approach:-Step 1 - Qualification Phase: Qualification process established through an Open Competition (Frame Invitation To Tender - Frame ITT) resulting in the award of Frame Contracts between the Agency and several service providers. Step 1 bidding period will be open until December 2021 at the earliest. -Step 2 - Implementation Phase: Restricted Competitions (Request for Proposal - RFP) between the Frame Contractors qualified under Step1resulting into the award of Work Order(s) between the Agency and one or more Frame Contractors for the implementation of the Copernicus Production Service.The Copernicus Production Service procurement is funded by the Copernicus Programme and will be open exclusively to economic operators which have their registered office in an EU Member State or a State participating in the Copernicus Programme.The Frame ITT package (Cover Letter, Frame Statement of Work, Special Conditions of Tender, Draft Frame Contract) will be available on ESA tendering website (EMITS http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). In order to access the ITT Package from EMITS, Tenderers must be registered in esa-star as a potential ESA supplier. Any Tenderer which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier must complete the online questionnaire on esa-star, under the tab "Entity registration". Further information onthe registration process can be found in ESA's INDUSTRY PORTAL available at:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/esa-star_open_for_businessPlease note that esa-star allows two levels of entity registration: "Light" and "Valid Full". This allows new users wishing to do business with ESA to carry out their registration in two steps. A "Light" registration will grant access to all esa-star services up to and including proposal submission. The award of ESA contracts requires registration.to have status "Valid Full"

tenderDescription: The objective of this activity is to develop a simulation model of a RISC-V (reduced instruction set computer) instruction set architecture (ISA) processor and peripherals, in a suitable hardware-software co-design environment, and perform design space exploration of a system-on-chip.Description:RISC-V is an open-source and royalty-free hardware instruction set architecture based on RISC principles. An open ISA is remarkably interesting for space due to several reasons: It reduces potential difficulties in license negotiation or export restrictions. It allows to perform modifications for radiation mitigation. It adds or modifies instructions to execute functions that are frequently required by space applications, such as bit manipulation, sub-word arithmetic, vector or SIMD (single instruction, multiple data) computations.RISC-V has been gaining popularity in the past years, and its use in space is now close to a reality thanks to several on-going system-on-chip (SoC) developments that will embed RISC-V multi core processor, along with several other interfaces to enable their use in satellite payloads and platforms, such as SpaceFibre, TM/TC (telemetry/telecommand) or cryptographic functions. The successful adoption of this architecture and embarking of the future SoC depends in a great extent on the features of the hardware, and on the availability of software development tool chains that enable the programming of the cores with suitable on-board software.Hardware and software developments around RISC-V can benefit greatly from the hardware-software co-design development flow, which simultaneously considers hardware and software within the design process. This enables the co-development and co-verification of hardware and software using simulation and/or emulation with the help of tools such as virtual platforms where simulation models of the processor ISA, and models of other components of the SoC can be executed at different levelsof abstraction, and with the required simulation speed. A fast ISA simulator of RISC-V facilitates early software development and the development software tool chains. All this before the first hardware prototypes are available.ESA has promoted the development of the SoCRocket virtual platform, which has been made available to missions and projects. This platform is comprised by several functional blocks, and can be used to simulate a SoC, but now, only LEON based systems are currently supported.This activity aims at developing a simulation model of RISC-V that can be executed in a suitable virtual platform at an appropriate abstraction level, easing the development of software, and enabling hardware-software co-design and design space exploration of a system-on-chip.The main tasks to be accomplished are: Assess the suitability of a virtual platform to simulate a RISC-V based SoC considering trade-offs related to accuracy of the models and simulation speed, SoCRocket and possible alternatives. Create a simulation model of the RISC-Vinstruction set, that can be integrated in a virtual platform, directly or through an emulator, and aid the development of software. Develop and integrate new functional blocks in a virtual platform, such as: SpaceFibre, TM/TC functions, cryptography, Ethernet. Design space exploration in a RISC-V based multicore model of a SoC.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

tenderTitle: Thruster Orientation Mechanism (TOM)
tenderDescription:
Each LISA TPS will consist of two TOMs, one primary and one redundant. Each TOM will support one HET. The purpose of the TOM is to adjust the orientation of the thruster to precisely align the direction of the force to the centre of mass of the Spacecraft in order to avoid generating disturbance torques when the Hall Effect Thruster is thrusting. This will allow for uncertainties in the position of the spacecraft centre of mass as the Xenon propellant is depleted during orbit raising.
The TOM satisfies three main functions, which are to support the HET, to deploy and drive the thruster position, and to provide the necessary functional links between the HET, xenon flow controller and the spacecraft.
The TOM enables a controlled angular movement of the HET about two orthogonal and independent axes. This commanded position is then held for thruster firing with the TOM actuators in an unpowered mode without back driving. Position control can be by step counting (if stepper motors are used), and absolute position sensors as well as physical end stops are needed
The procurement of the TOM will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements”. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

tenderTitle: Maintaining the CC3 in operational conditions
tenderDescription:
In order to maintain the CCU3 in operational conditions, it is necessary to improve interfaces and deal with the obsolescence of the fluid, electric, air conditioning and monitoring systems. The mechanical strength of the various elements on the CCU3 platforms will also have to be maintained. The main objective is to upgrade all systems by improving the air cushions movements of the CCU3 in order to increase the flight time necessary to perform docking and undocking operations.
This upgrade will have to increase the reliability of the CCU3.

tenderTitle: HIGH FREQUENCY AIRBORNE RADIOMETER INSTRUMENT FOR THE SUPPORT OF FUTURE ALTIMETRY MISSIONS
tenderDescription: Satellite altimetry plays an essential role in producing sea level and waves products such as sea surface height (SSH), significantwave height (SWH), mean sea level and near surface wind/wave products.Today, a low frequency channel microwave radiometer is in general used to correct the altimeter range for water vapor path delay over ocean. The wet tropospheric correction (WTC) is consideredas one of the largest source of uncertainty in sea level estimate. As any artificial temporal drift in the wet tropospheric correction translate immediately to a similar drift in the mean sea level, there is a need for extremely well calibrated radiometer instrument to retrieve this wet tropospheric correction in support of the accurate altimeter measurement. Depending on the targeted temporal and spatial scales, some recent studies and projects ("Radiometer Instrument for Swath Altimeter missions", Sentinel-6 HRMR instrument, Sentinel-3 NG-T) have shown that the two existing classes of satellite altimeters such as the conventional nadir looking altimeters and the wide swath altimeters would both benefit from the addition of one or several high frequency channels (89/165/172 GHz)to the low frequency channels (18.7/23.8/36.5(or 31.4) GHz) already used for the WTC retrieval. The advantages brought by the addition of the high frequency channels in the microwave radiometer are several fold. For a given RF radiating aperture, the high frequency radiometer would exhibit a high spatial resolution and therefore shall be less prone to land contamination in coastal areas that would directly impact the uncertainty of the WTC based on brightness temperature measurement near the coastline. For wide swath altimeters, a multibeam microwave radiometer combining the low and high frequency channels would help to retrieve the WTC across-track with an increased accuracy and with better spatial resolution commensurate with the high spatial resolution radar retrievals from a swath altimeter. Moreover, the high frequency channels (typically 89 GHz or 165/172 GHz) can provide additional information for precipitation screening.This new proposed activity aims at developing an airborne demonstrator instrument to validate the benefits of thehigh frequency radiometer measurement, to support the continued improvement of the altimeter measurement and observation capabilities. The activity shall start with the detailed analysis of user requirements and the design of the instrument, then continue with themanufacturing, integration and test of the airborne system and finally concludes with the airworthiness certification on an airborne carrier and a functional test flight to validate the airborne radiometer function and performance and collect first experimental data.

tenderTitle: STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS FOR LUXIMPULSE PROGRAMME ACTIVITIES
tenderDescription: The Luxembourg's National Programme - LuxIMPULSE Programme, aims to strengthen worldwide competitiveness of Luxembourg industry in the near term in existing markets and to establish strategic capabilities which will result in stronger competitiveness in the medium term on existing or new markets, and to support the implementation of Luxembourg national priorities.The Call for Proposals is addressed only to economic operators - be it as Prime or Subcontractor level - registered in Luxembourg, unless otherwise instructed and approved by the Luxembourg Space Agency. The proposed work shall not overlap with any currently running ESA Contract awarded to any entity in the proposal consortium.Activities submitted in the frame of LuxIMPULSE Programme may be related to the study, improvement or development of space systems, subsystems, technology, ground systems for space applications, or downstream service products based on space data.It must be noted that according to the Procurement Regulations ESA/REG/001 rev. 5, Art. 18, Tenderers areeligible to participate in a tendering procedure of the Agency provided they possess the necessary professional and technical qualifications, professional and technical competences, financial resources, equipment and other physical facilities, managerial capability, reliability, experience and the personnel, to perform a Contract.The support to the activity by the Luxembourg Space Agency ismandatory. The activities selected will be funded by the Agency at a level depending on the nature of the economic operator and the maturity and proximity to market of the activity. The remainder will be funded by the economic operator's internal own resources and shall not include any additional source of public funding. The economic operator's contribution can be either monetary or in-kind.

tenderTitle: Rehabilitation of S5 maintenance workshop
tenderDescription:
The S5C maintenance workshop no longer meets the functional needs and ergonomic, technical, or safety requirements of the activities carried out there.

It is composed of two enclosed, air-conditioned spaces used for storing small electrical and mechanical equipment, maintenance operations and training new staff.

It also consists of a semi-open space that is the heart of mechanical maintenance activities, particularly for work on equipment related to payloads. It contains fixed machine tools, workbenches, and several storage cabinets.

Finally, above these two areas, there is an open space for storing furniture and bulky equipment.

It is therefore necessary to redesign these three areas of the workshop in order to respond more effectively and efficiently to electrical and mechanical maintenance needs, the training of new operators, and the storage of equipment on the upper floor, which we wish to close in an air-conditioned environment.

tenderTitle: S2-SW-10: CANADIAN PARTICIPATION IN THE ESA SPACE WEATHER SERVICE NETWORK FEASIBILITY STUDY
tenderDescription: This feasibility study shall analyse Canadian space weather assets including measurement, modelling and service provision capabilities and carry out initial pre-developments demonstrating these assets potential incorporation into the ESA Space Weather Service Network. Assets providing data access to be reviewed shall include both space and ground-based sensors along with data archives and repositories.Available assets shall be reviewed in terms of the Space Safety Programme's space weather customer and service requirements baseline along with the current level of service provided by the existing Space Weather Service Network in order to highlight priority areas where Canadian assets are expected to bring substantial capability enhancements. Consideration shall be given to the development planning prepared by the five Expert Service Centres participating in the network to ensure complementarity.Recommendations shall include identification of a set of high priority product development activities in key areas highlighting the potential contribution of Canadian space weather assets and capabilities both alone and in combination with other existing or potential SWE Service Network participants. Predevelopment shall take place in order to produce a set of representative product mock-ups. The first products shall be foreseen for integration into the SWE Service Network within the 2026 timeframe.

tenderTitle: DEVELOPMENT OF SERIALIZER AND DESERIALIZER IP CORE FOR ULTRA DEEP SUB MICRON TECHNOLOGIES - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To develop a Serializer and Deserializer IP Core, without any access restriction for European Industry, to provide a low power HighSpeed Serial Link up to 56GbpsDescription: Most of the required functionalities for the future space components such as processors, accelerators, routers, analog/digital converters will be developed within the GSTP activity GTE3-101ED "Ultra Deep Sub-Micron - Foundation and Platform Technology".The High Speed Serial Link (HSSL) is one of the key functionalities required for the next generation of space components that could not be included in the GTE3-101ED. Due to the importance to provide this functionality in a timely manner, this dedicated activityhas been defined with the aim to develop a Serializer and Deserializer (SERDES) IP Core to enableHSSL to at least 32Gbps and up to 56Gbps.This IP Core will support the different HSSL protocols used in space like SpaceFibre, Ethernet, PCIe, JESD204. Specifically the HSSL IP Core will be compliant to the newer PCIe 5.0 and Ethernet802.3cd link operation. TheHSSL IP Core will support power efficient operation both for short range as well as long range applications (two optimized implementations might be considered). The outcome of this activity shall be made available whenever required with concomitant activities, and in particular the GTE3- 101ED and shall be made accessible for future developments ofEuropean space products.The activity encompasses the following tasks :- Identify the space component requiring SERDES IP Core and targeted UDSM technology and foundry- Determine the HSSL requirement specifications and suitable commercial SERDES IP Core design- Perform Radiation test of selected HSSL in the targeted UDSM technology- Design radiation harden HSSL IP Core with improvedperformances- Validate the HSSL IP Core functionalities and performances on test vehicles, including radiation hardened operation- Demonstrate compliant operation on optimised and corrected design- Perform functional ESCC testing, characterization, andevaluation- Make the HSSL IP Core available and support the integration into the activity GTE3-101ED- Package the HSSL IP Core for use into future developments Deliverables include SERDES IP Core, Simulation model files, samples of the test chips and documentation as per applicable Standard for IC development, tailoredas required for the development of reusable IP.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

tenderTitle: FEASIBILITY AND PRE-DEVELOPMENT OF INFLATABLE TANKS PROPELLANT STORAGE - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: To provide a feasibility analysis about the construction, storage, deployment, and operation of propellant tanks that are inflatable.Description:This activity aims at providing a detailed feasibility analysis on the construction, storage, deployment, and operation of propellant tanks that are inflatable. It is envisaged that these propellant tanks can be used to store cryogenic propellant(LOX, LCH4, LH2) or to store conventional propellant (O2, H2, CH4, CO). Most important, inflatable propellant tanks can be used to store the gases produced by using in situ resources in a Regenerative Fuel Cell Systems (RFCS) in electrolysis mode. Applications tothe Moon and Mars will be addressed.Major critical points (material compatibility with propellant, zero boil off for cryogenic propellant,...) are aimed at being investigated and solutions proposed.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Trade-off analyses of inflatable tank design- Prototype and test a proof of concept (for different applications and propellants for Moon and Mars scenarios)- Roadmap development plan

tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design a Laser Communication Terminal (LCT) to enable communication links with various satellites at the Lagrange point 2 (L2) with hemispheric pointing rangeand a minimized vibration and angular disturbance profile.Targeted Improvements:To increase the return data rate from beyond-Earth communication by a factor of 10 compared to typical RF payload missions (75 Mbps - class links).Description:Multiple space telescopes have been placed at Lagrange point 2 (L2) and this trend will continue in the future because it is an ultra-low disturbance environment. Laser communication terminals(LCT) can provide very high data return rates from L2. However, the (angular) vibrations induced by the LCT shall not disturb the spacecraft operations.The activity shall perform the conceptual design of an optical communication terminal for L2 with hemispheric pointing range and minimized vibration and angular disturbance export. Critical functions of the LCT (SWaP, minimization of angular momentum during coarse pointing, etc.) shall be breadboarded.

tenderTitle: ESPRIT WIT ECLSS Air Check Valve (ACV)
tenderDescription:
The Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The Gateway – European System Providing Refueling Infrastructure and Telecommunication (ESPRIT) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with refueling, logistic and telecommunication functions (this latter function will be provided with a different element that will reach Gateway at a different time). The ESPRIT includes contributions from USA, and Canada. 
The ESPRIT WIT is the Windowed Infrastructure Tunnel devoted to the logistic and circular viewport functions, in addition to the Primary Structural function of the complete system.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the development and qualification of the ECLSS Air Check Valve (ACV) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).
The Air Check Valve (ACV) is part of the Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS). 
ACV is a mechanical valve installed downstream of the Cabin Fan and it provides a reverse pressure protection in the environmental system supply. 
Being the CFAs cold redundant units, the Air Check Valve avoids unwanted backflow through the still fan and, of course, in case that the fan is not operating due to a failure. 
The ACV consists of a simple butterfly valve that opens when the air flows through the fan and remains closed when the fan is not operating. 
Its definition, development, qualification and the procurement of the equipment represent the object of the present tender.
Further information concerning the ESPRIT campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon. 
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

tenderTitle: TRUTHS PHASE AdvC/C/D - Invitation to tender: Payload Monitoring & Control System (PMCS)
tenderDescription:
TRUTHS (Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial- and Helio- Studies) is an element of the European Earth Watch Programme.

TRUTHS will help deliver improved confidence in Earth Observation (EO) data gathered from space and the forecasts driven by this data.
This mission will enable the upgrade of the performance of the EO system, both in space and on the ground. The mission will facilitate the development of a global, climate observatory, delivering data of unprecedented accuracy with SI traceability - establishing a 'standards laboratory in space'.

TRUTHS was authorised at ESA CMin22 for a Phase B2/Advance C, whereas the continuation of the mission through Phase C/D-E1 is subject to further approval at ESA CMin25.
In this framework, Airbus Defence and Space Ltd will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the PMCS HW and SW for the TRUTHS Phase Advance C (1 year), with a mandatory option for Phase C/D. 

Procurement of PMCS will be split into two parts:
1. PMCS HW, which includes the models, the Boot Loader Software (BSW) and the hardware dependant software (HDSW))
2. PMCS Application Software (ASW)
The tenderer can decide to submit an offer for any of the two parts (HW or ASW) as well as for both (HW + ASW).

The Invitation To Tender will be addressed to all ESA Member States, since the geographical return of the mission is subject to change at ESA CMin25.

tenderTitle: Rehabilitation of the office area at S3F
tenderDescription:
The increased frequency of Ariane and Vega launches will swiftly highlight the necessity for greater customer availability and office reception capacity for teams engaged in campaign activities. In line with the current expansion, we have identified the necessity to upgrade the S3 area, which would enable the execution of additional satellite campaigns at the EPCU S3B.

In order to meet these needs, it is necessary to replace the existing customer office area at S3F with a new office building. This will modernise the current bungalows, which are no longer suitable for hosting satellite customers. The objective is to be able to host several satellite customer teams simultaneously.

The reception of satellite customers and the management of activities in the S3 zone also require the rehabilitation of the site manager's coordination office in order to supervise the enlarged S3 zone with the ZSE/ZSP.

All of these activities also induce the creation of the PPE store, with the aim of providing local support for operations throughout the S3 and ZSE/ZSP zones.

We are therefore expecting an office area to be set up for satellite customers, EPCU agents, and anyone else who needs to work in the S3 zone, with efficient logistics flows in line with the growth of activity in this zone.

tenderTitle: ARGONAUT LDE – Life Cycle Analysis [LCA]
tenderDescription:
Argonaut LDE (previously named EL3, European Large Logistics Lander), is one of the keystones of the “Terrae Novae” exploration capabilities presented at Council Meeting 2022. Argonaut LDE aims at enabling a substantial and sustained European presence on the surface of the Moon ensuring Europe remains a key player in space exploration. Argonaut LDE aims at providing an autonomous European capability for regular large robotic surface missions for an extended duration. This provides the possibility to conduct independent missions if required as well as being a significant and visible contribution to the international sustainable exploration of the lunar surface.

The mission is designed to support both human and robotic exploration by providing a multipurpose lander known as the Lunar Descent Element (LDE):

•	Lunar Descent Element (LDE): 
o	A recurring lander, common to all ARGONAUT LDE missions. 
o	Designed to be compatible with different delivery missions without undergoing modifications; 
o	The LDE provides the functions of Payload transport to the Moon’s surface as well as the main mission functions common to all the different missions. 

The LDE is equipped to deliver various payloads through a mission-specific interface, typically referred to as the Cargo Platform Element (CPE). For the purpose of clarity the CPE and the related Payload are subject to a separate procurement under ESA’s responsibility. 
Thales Alenia Space Italy, have been Contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the Argonaut Lunar Descent Element (LDE) which will be used for the first mission in 2031. 

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the Argonaut LDE - Life Cycle Analysis (LCA)

The procurement of the LCA studies will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

The start of the present ITT is scheduled no earlier than beginning of September 2025.

tenderTitle: PHOTONIC COMPONENTS' RELIABILITY MODELS FOROPTICAL AND QUANTUM COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.052) EXPRO+ ON REQUEST
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop reliability models for photonic and optical components used in optical andquantum communications. The models will be developed based on reliability growth test and failure results analysis.Targeted Improvements:Creating a common reliability database/model of photonic component failure mechanisms for all ESA Member States' users. Enabling modelling of photonic components failure mechanisms. Increasing the knowledge of failure mechanisms for the selected photonicscomponent families and enabling trade-offs/redundancy schemes for the better sizing of future constellations.Description:To increase the reliability of photonics technologies, it is first necessary to create a database of the component families foreseen to be used for optical and quantum communication. Once the status of each of these families is assessed, in terms of currently availabledata and the effort needed to build reliability models, it will be possible to prioritise the need for testing. This will identify the components' family with the least amount of information, high risk of failure and potential impact of failure for ongoing and future designs. The test protocols and sample sizes will be defined based on pre-test analyses, with sample sizes of at least ten components for each family being anticipated. The duration of the tests will be selected to achieve failure of all components, to develop a comprehensive understanding of the failure mechanisms involved. The failures will be investigated, and reliability models will be derived. The outcome will consist of a database including model characteristics information and tentative failure rates for different use contexts.

tenderTitle: S3 zone air network segregation
tenderDescription:
A 7 bar air production station now meets the compressed air needs of several geographical areas, bringing together the establishments of Regulus, Europropulsion, ArianeGroup, Avio-G, Air Liquide Spatial Guyane, Arianespace, BEAP, ZSE, ZSP and S3 Zone.
As part of the arrival of new launch operators and the transfer of ownership of certain areas to CNES, it has become necessary to rethink the 7 bar air production/distribution network in order to guarantee a clear and equitable distribution in terms of operation, investment, consumption and maintenance, for all subscribers.
The main objective of the project is to create independent air production and distribution for the areas operated by CNES CSG, namely the ZSE, the ZSP and the S3 zone. The new installations should allow CNES to control outages for its own maintenance needs and thus limit the operational impact. CNES's responsibility for network maintenance will also be limited to the areas operated by CNES.
To achieve this, a mastery of the current network is necessary, and a map of the air network will be established in order to identify, in particular, the dead branches to be isolated or put into hibernation. The solutions chosen to meet the need will have to take into account a general upgrade of the network in the identified areas.

tenderTitle: ARGONAUT LDE – Quick passivation system design
tenderDescription:
Argonaut LDE (previously named EL3, European Large Logistics Lander), is one of the keystones of the “Terrae Novae” exploration capabilities presented at Council Meeting 2022. Argonaut LDE aims at enabling a substantial and sustained European presence on the surface of the Moon ensuring Europe remains a key player in space exploration. Argonaut LDE aims at providing an autonomous European capability for regular large robotic surface missions for an extended duration. This provides the possibility to conduct independent missions if required as well as being a significant and visible contribution to the international sustainable exploration of the lunar surface.

The mission is designed to support both human and robotic exploration by providing a multipurpose lander known as the Lunar Descent Element (LDE):

•	Lunar Descent Element (LDE): 
o	A recurring lander, common to all ARGONAUT LDE missions. 
o	Designed to be compatible with different delivery missions without undergoing modifications; 
o	The LDE provides the functions of Payload transport to the Moon’s surface as well as the main mission functions common to all the different missions. 

The LDE is equipped to deliver various payloads through a mission-specific interface, typically referred to as the Cargo Platform Element (CPE). For the purpose of clarity the CPE and the related Payload are subject to a separate procurement under ESA’s responsibility. 
Thales Alenia Space Italy, have been Contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the Argonaut Lunar Descent Element (LDE) which will be used for the first mission in 2031. 
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the Argonaut LDE Quick passivation system design.

For safety reasons, the LDE shall provide quick passivation function of propellant tanks to avoid hypergolic explosion in case of accidental events. 
The passivation system shall work in all the mission phases, starting from launch through the spacecraft mission (once separated from the LV), until Lunar orbit insertion.

The main critical aspect is related to the timeframe and the reaction time needed, which is in the order of ms for the first mission phases, and seconds during third stage LV phase and space mission. 
The Contractor main tasks are :
• Perform trade-offs and analysis to evaluate and recommend the design solutions/architecture to ensure timely passivation of the Tanks.
• Highlight any aspect related to operational safety constraints.
• Prepare the documentation necessary to justify the test conditions, if any, established for development/qualification tests on Earth and correlation of the results with the corresponding environmental conditions seen by LDE in the realistic worst-case scenario.

The procurement of the Primary and Secondary Structures will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

tenderTitle: NAVISP ELEMENT 2  OPEN CALL FOR PROPOSALS
tenderDescription: This Shopping Cart has the following purpose under the NAVISP Programme: Under NAVISP Element 2, the Agency issues this permanentlyopen Call for Proposals for the development of innovative competitive products in the Satellite Navigation and wider Position, Navigation and Timing domain. The objective is to boost Member States' industrial competitiveness in the fast- evolving navigation sector. Proposals are welcome from space and non-space companies, from large and small enterprises and start-ups. Products can address satellite space segment, ground infrastructure and user segment including applications and services. Industry and research institutions of interested participating States are therefore invited to submit Outline Proposals for the development of pre-operational products matching their strategies and plans. Upon positive assessment of their Outline Proposal, they will be invited to submit the Full Proposal which will be evaluated once a Support Letter from the relevant national Delegation is received. The Tendering process details and the guidelines for preparing the Outline and Full Proposals are described in the AO.

tenderTitle: LITHIUM FREE BATTERIES FOR LOW EARTH ORBIT SATCOM CONSTELLATIONS( ON REQUEST) (ARTES AT 4F.177) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop, manufacture and test batteries from sustainable and ESA Member States sourced materials with high cycle life at high Depth of Discharge (DoD) and a good rate capability for small communication satellites in LEO.Targeted Improvements:Enabling a European or Canadian source of lithium free space battery for LEO satcom constellations.Description: Currently the state-of-the-art technology for energy storage in satellites are Li-ion batteries, however this technology relies on materials which are not readily available in ESA Member States and have limited lifetime and power density. Consequently, Li-ion batteries Deep of Discharge (DoD) in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) applications is severely limited (typically 20%), further reducing the effective energy densities. Over the past years, manufacturers have reached high power density and promising life cycles with technologiessuch as Na-ion batteries (up to 5 kW/kg and over 5000 cycles, with an energy density of up to 160 Wh/kg) which could revolutionise energy storage in telecommunication satellites.An inherent advantage of lithium free batteries is also, that they areconsiderably more sustainable and use ESA Member States available raw materials, such as hard carbon on the anode side and Prussianblue analogues on the cathode side for Na-ion batteries.This activity will improve the effective energy density of batteries for small satellites and secure ESA Member States' independence by using environmentally friendly materials, that are easily accessible. A lithium free battery breadboard made of non-critical materials will be designed, developed, manufactured, and tested to demonstrate both compliance with space requirements and high cycle life at depth of discharge and power relevant to telecommunication satellitesin Low Earth Orbit.

tenderTitle: ESPRIT WIT Launch Vehicle Adapter (LVA)
tenderDescription:
The Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The Gateway – European System Providing Refueling Infrastructure and Telecommunication (ESPRIT) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with refueling, logistic and telecommunication functions (this latter function will be provided with a different element that will reach Gateway at a different time). The ESPRIT includes contributions from USA, and Canada. 
The ESPRIT WIT is the Windowed Infrastructure Tunnel devoted to the logistic and circular viewport functions, in addition to the Primary Structural function of the complete system.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the development and qualification of the window panes coatings in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).

The Launch Vehicle Adapter (LVA) is a structural element, physically part of the ERM WIT Primary Structure, which shall ensure the fulfillment of the following main functions:

•	Provide the interface between the ERM WIT and the SLS adapter, adjusting the WIT diameter to the one of the Launcher adapter.
•	Provide the interface between the ERM WIT and the ERM UMAXT.

The LVA is a roll-forged truncated cone made of Titanium (Ti6Al4V), that shall be designed in order to guarantee both mechanical and thermal performances to meet the above functions.
Moreover its structure presents several holes in order to provide the piping and harness routing from the active IBDM to other services.

Further information concerning the ESPRIT campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon. 
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

tenderTitle: Q-BAND TRANSMIT ACTIVE ANTENNA FOR COMBINED USER AND FEEDER LINK ON LEO SATELLITES (ARTES AT 5B.249) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
tenderDescription: The objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a Q-band transmit, scalable active antenna for the combined user and feeder links for Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) broadband applications.Targeted Improvements:- Enabling broadband services in Q-band for LEOsatellites.- Eliminating the need for separate user and feeder link antenna.Description: Satellite telecommunication systems haveexperienced an increased traffic in Ku and Ka frequency bands and higher frequency bands are targeted to satisfy the increasing required capacity. Currently, Q/V bands are mostly used for feeder links on (Very)-High-Throughput-Satellites (V)HTS Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellites, and passive antenna solutions already available and active ones under initial development. While feeder link beams are fixed on GEO systems, in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites the feederbeams benefit from repointing of an array antennasolution as it provides more flexibility and reliability and the ability to dynamically assign multiple beams to multiple gateways and users.This activity will design a highly integrated Q-band direct array antenna for LEO satellites allowing multi-beam operations for both user and feeder links. This shall include a mechanical and thermal management concept. An engineering model of an antennatile (at least 10 cm x 10 cm size) will be developed and tested. The engineering model tile shall contain the most representative passive and active components. Commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) active components can be considered. The thermal management systemshall be designed, and representative components shall be included in the antenna tile engineering model.

tenderTitle: ATTITUDE AND ORBIT CONTROL SYSTEM FOR HIGH ASPECT RATIO SATCOM SATELLITES ( ON REQUEST) (ARTES AT 4C.072) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test an Attitude and Orbit Control System (AOCS) architecture for high aspect ratio satellites in Low Earth Orbits (LEO) and Very Low Earth Orbits (VLEO), capable as well to perform controller and propulsion-less de-orbiting operations.Targeted Improvements:- Enabling AOCS for high aspect ratio satellites- Enabling high aspect ratio satellite to perform a controlled re-entry manoeuvre.Description: High aspect ratio (HAR) satellites are of increasing interest for satcom users, due to several advantages at system level over a more traditional design (e.g. easier accommodationin the launcher, possibility to have larger surfaces for a given volume to accommodate solar arrays, antennas, radiators, etc.). However, the AOCS for such satellites takes onadditional degrees of complexity both on the hardware architecture and the modelling andcontrol algorithms side, such as limited volume for actuators accommodation such as wheels, or the compensation of increased atmospheric drag in specific attitudes when flying at lower altitudes in VLEO. The controlled re-entry for such satellite class poses additional AOCS technical challenges which require specific attention.This activity will design, manufacture and test an AOCS engineering model for a single High Aspect Ratio (HAR) spacecraft in at least two scenarios; nominal VLEO or LEO operations and a controlledpropulsion-less re-entry case from VLEO. Possible AOCS architectures, flight dynamics modelling, on-board algorithms and associatedoperational concepts will be studied. Currently available sensors (e.g. star trackers, gyros, etc) and actuators (e.g. wheels, magnetorquers, control moment gyros, etc) will be assessed andrequired adaptation will be identified for the HAR configuration. Breadboarding of AOCS hardware will be carried out and AOCS algorithms developed. An AOCS subsystem scaled engineering model will be developedand implemented into a AOCS testbed. The testbed will be used to evaluate the performance for a nominal mission scenario in VLEOor LEO and a controlled re-entry scenario without the need of propulsion system. The re-entry scenario shall be tested representative environment (e.g. wind tunnel).

tenderTitle: Replacement of CSG telemetry antennas 2026 to 2031
tenderDescription:
The downrange stations are an essential element during the launcher mission as they ensure the launcher-to-ground communication links capability. Ever since the beginning, the CSG Range has been implementing a network of downrange telemetry stations to support Ariane and then Vega launches.
This project consists in the replacement of aged large antennas in a gradual approach, beginning with the SNA Stella 35 and then continuing with others (eg. Galliot’s or Bermuda’s ones). This replacement is now essential to maintain CSG Range availability. To optimize costs, the approach consists in proposing a set of identical and smaller antennas (diameter about 4m), allowing a predictive maintenance policy to come.

tenderTitle: Bermuda station evolution toward permanent configuration - power supply equipment
tenderDescription:
Since 2011, CSG range has been operating the transportable station in Bermuda for launches featuring northward trajectory which steadily increased since. The evolution of the Bermuda station towards a permanent configuration is an essential element to ensure its availability and reliability for launches as well as an optimized maintenance.
Beside the use of an area dedicated to ESA/CNES in the Bermudian building, the installation in the latter of the telemetry system racks and the approaching of the antenna, this development will require the renewal of the entire energy configuration (power supply generator, inverter units, transformer etc..)
This activity does not include the replacement of the antenna which is covered by another Tender Action.

tenderTitle: APA SOLAR REGULATOR MODULE FOR BATTERY BUSES - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: The Advanced Power Architecture (APA) is a standard concept for the Power Conditioning and Distribution Unit (PCDU). APA follows the interoperable and interchangeable modularity approach applied for the project ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) that started in 2020. APA is aimed to be fully compatible with ADHA so that together they will form the kern of a satellite platform.As ADHA, APA is composed of two elements: a standardized Unit rack (element 1) that providesstandard services to a set of Power Modules (element 2) that populates the rack to make an APA PCDU. The power unit can be built upon modules from different manufacturers, based on performances, cost, programmatic constraints. This approach allows strong reduction of development time and recurrent costs, faster development and adoption of more performing technologies in great part enabled by the envisaged interoperable and interchangeable modules that compose the system.The definition the Advanced Power Architecture and related Standardization of the development ofthe APA element 1 (rack product) is being addressed in a dedicated activity funded by the Preparation Element of the DPTD and by the Future EO Program (ESA/IPC(2022)1,add.42). The modules that compose the element 2 of the APA are subject to several TDE activities. Element 1 outputs (APA Unit requirements and standard requirements for APA Modules) will be used as inputs to Element 2 activities. Element 2 outputs (APA Modules) will then be used as input to Element 1 (for the validation of standard power modules requirements and overall APA architecture).GaN advantages (e.g. high switching frequency, thermal performance, inherently radiation tolerant),allowing a more compact power cell, will be fully exploited in combination with resonant power conversion techniques. Digital control techniques provides flexible and reliable control of the power cell and a first level failure detection isolation and recovery (FDIR)in the module.This activity aims to develop the Solar Regulator module (SAR) for battery buses with Maximum Power Point Tracking capabilities.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidation of APA Requirements (generic and specific modules)- Trade off and evaluation of the most promising Conversion Power Cell topologies- Preliminary and detailed design definition- Manufacturing and testing the module- Contribution to the APA Unit integration and test, including APA standardised documentationand interoperability/interchangeability test.

tenderTitle: ULTRACOMPACT 778 NM RUBIDIUM SECONDARY OPTICAL FREQUENCY STANDARD - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: The objective of this activity is to develop an ultracompact, secondary, optical frequency reference based on a two-photon transition in Rb vapour at 778nm.Description:Ultra-stable miniature atomic clocks are being considered for space applications. The Rubidium two-photon transition secondary frequency standard has demonstrated interesting performance metrics with a further potential for ultra-low size, weight and power (SWaP) integration.Currently, such an approach is hindered by the lack of miniaturized laser sources with suitable power levels and spectral properties as well as a compact physics package design taking advantage of the full capabilities of the integrated photonics and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gas cell technology platforms.This activity aims at exploiting these enabling technologies and developing a further concept of a compact high-performance atomic physics package for an ultra-compact secondary optical frequency standard. The goal of this activity is to provide a fractional frequency stability < 10 - 12 at 1 second integration time implemented using integrated photonic techniques.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Evaluate sources of integrated photonic laser systems delivering the wavelengths and the required spectral properties for the defined system approach. Develop Rb cell techniques and technologies targeting an ultracompact 778 nm rubidium secondary optical frequency standard using chip-scale photonic integration. Demonstrate the fractional stability performance achievable using the chosen chip-scale photonic approach. Evaluate chip-scale optical frequency combs with SiN Kerr comb techniques to provide an initial stabilized direct optical-RF link. Provide a packaging solution to maintain the preliminary performance achieved.NOTE: This activityis currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The finallist of participating states will be known at tender issue.

tenderTitle: NAVIGATION INNOVATION SUPPORT PROGRAMME ELEMENT 3  STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS
tenderDescription: Under NAVISP Element 3, the Agency issues this Call for Proposals for the development of initiatives in the Position, Navigation and Timing domain. Element 3 is focused on participating States' priorities and aims at supporting their national navigation activities along the whole value chain. Element 3 configures as an ad-hoc support element, which is envisaged per country and possibly per domain, for the development and promotion of products, applications and services based on GNSS and more widely on PNT systems. Following participating states request, ESA may provide technical assistance in various areas. Element 3 configures as an opportunity forthe participating States delegations to animate and coordinate discussions with national entities and to set up the processes to identify and federate institutional demands. This will foster cooperation as well as possible national partnerships with a wide diversity of actors, enlarging the national space community (agency, industries, universities and research centres) and strengthening its relationships with authorities, organisations, institutions, industries and research actors from non-space sectors. Institutions andcompanies are therefore invited to submit Outline Proposals for the development of activities of national relevance and matching institutional interests. Upon positive assessment of their Outline Proposal, they will be invited to submit the Full Proposal which will be evaluated once a Support Letter from the relevant national Delegation is received. The Tendering process details and the guidelines for preparing the Outline and Full Proposals are described in the AO.

tenderTitle: Renewal of the work request orders
tenderDescription:
CNES-CSG intends to renew the system called FASO whose purpose is to edit work request orders for people who have to work on the CSG Space base.
Those work orders are generated from the scheduling and planning tool.

Currently, the system is physically disconnected from the planning tool. This enforce manual exports to specific physical ‘stations’ located at some specific places where each person who is supposed to work on the Space base will retrieve its work order.
When the job is finished, the reporting has to be manually done within the planning tool.

The purpose of the project is to :
•	Automate both import of the work orders and export when the job is completed
•	Allow all industrial partners or temporary workers to access those workorders despite the fact that they are not known on the CNES active directory
•	Allow access to those work orders from mobile devices to facilitate the on site interventions

Delivery will consist in the new FASO system

tenderTitle: TGO-MEX RADIO OCCULTATION - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: RO occurs when the transmitter of a radio signal appears to set behind a planet, as viewed from a receiving station. The radio signal is refracted by the atmosphere and ionosphere causing a frequency shift; analysing this frequency shift allows reconstruction of a high-resolution vertical profile of density (and thus pressure and temperature) in the neutral atmosphere and ionospheric electronabundances in the ionosphere. Spacecraft-to-Earth RO has been carried out for many decades by planetary missions, but the opportunities for this are limited by the orbital geometry and ground station availability.

tenderTitle: ACTIVE LOCAL STRUCTURAL CONTROL OF VERY LARGE SPACE STRUCTURES - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: The objective of this activity is to develop a breadboard of a local active control system, which demonstrates the capability of locally regulating the stiffness of very large structures in space.Description: Large space structures are expected to exhibit structural modes at low frequency likely to couple with the AOCS control system. For very large structures it is expected that the attitude control will be achieved by distributed sensors and actuators, which may potentially result in relative high loads and displacements. Past activities have shown the potential of local structural control by using strain sensors co-located with active elements for local structural stiffening (e.g. based on piezo technology).This activity is expected to provide an assessment on the critical aspects of very large structures, including: Interaction between structure and AOCS (criticality of structure stiffness vs. mass). Feasibility to reduce structural resonance through passive and/or active structuraldamping. Criticality of pointing and stability requirements, e.g. for solar power generation maintaining sun-point for solar generator surface and Earth pointing for power transmission. ROM evaluation of internal loading on structure to ensure satisfactory capability of structural design, material selection and joining technologies. Feasibility for redundancy in the design and performance of very large structures, assuming potential failure in structure or structural joining elements as well as on AOCS sensors and actuators over the anticipated in-orbit lifetime.In consideration of the above, this activity targets the development of a local active control system breadboard together with an on-ground testbed representative of very large structures in space to demonstrate this technology.The activity will encompass thefollowing tasks: Identify candidate sensing and stiffness regulators suitable for local strain sensingand stiffening. Assess and optimise the integration of strain sensing and stiffness regulators into structural elements in view of optimising the local controllability of stiffness. Design a distributed control system that drives the local stiffening systems toachieve global stabilisation and control goals. Define a suitable verification and validation process for the designed distributedcontrol system. Define and setup a ground testbed representative of very large structures in space. Demonstrate the distributed control system on a suitable scaled breadboard,adapted for laboratory environment and deployed on the ground testbed.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.
