tenderTitle: LATENCY-SENSITIVE ROUTING IN MULTI-LAYER SATCOM NETWORKS (ARTES FP 1B.143) - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: This study will examine how latency-sensitive routing techniques could be employed within a multi-orbit satcom architecture to optimise overall service delivery. The activity will determine the global proportion of latency-sensitive traffic and its likely future evolution; identify and consolidate solutions for automatic routing based on end-user latency requirements; and evaluate the impact that employing latency-sensitive routing strategies would have on the design and performance of the entire satellite communication system. The activity output will include the identification of the technology, product, and service developments needed to realise such a system.

tenderTitle: TRUTHS PHASE B2 - OPTICS ARC (Anti reflective coating)
tenderDescription:
TRUTHS (Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial- and Helio- Studies) is an Element of the European Earth Watch Programme approved at 178th PB-EO (ESA/PB-EO(2019)31) for submission at CM19+ as a new Element, called “TRUTHS”. 
TRUTHS (Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial- and Helio- Studies – is an operational climate mission, aiming to enhance by an order-of-magnitude our ability to estimate the Earth radiation budget through direct measurements and to establish a ‘metrology laboratory in space’ to create a fiducial (International System of units - SI traceable) reference data set to cross-calibrate other sensors and improve the quality of their measurements.
The TRUTHS Mission aims at measuring the incoming & outgoing energy from the climate system, including the spectral fingerprint needed to observationally attribute climate processes, with an accuracy needed to detect climate trends in the shortest possible time.
The TRUTHS Mission has been authorised as part of the European Earth Watch Programme [ESA/PB-EO(2022)18 rev1] to start its Phase B2/Advance C implementation while authorisation to implement Phase C/D/E1 is subject to the availability of funding and authorisation at C-MiN 2025. 
Airbus Defence and Space has been selected by ESA as the Prime Contractor for Phase B2 with a mandatory option for Advance C.
In this framework, Airbus Defence and Space Ltd will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of an optical anti-reflective coating for the TRUTHS Phase B2.
The scope of work is to perform a study of multi layered ARC coating operating between 320 nm and 2400 nm and deposited on curved glass substrates to minimise reflectivity considering provided angular ranges, to reduce polarisation sensitivity and to minimise scatter losses. 
Based on the successful results of this study, it will be requested to coat and test some flat samples using the preferred ARC coating, before and after the operational space environment (i.e. thermo-mechanical and radiation), to achieve TRL 6. Should the results be unsuccessful the work will cease at the end of the study. 
The Invitation To Tender will be addressed to economic operators (including those deemed to act as Subcontractors) whose registered office is established in such Member and Associated States which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating State in the ESA TRUTHS Mission. 
To date, these are: Czech Republic, Greece, Romania, Spain, Switzerland, United Kingdom.

tenderTitle: IAP.KS.DI.000 DIVERSITY, EQUITY AND INCLUSION - OPEN CALL FOR PROPOSAL
tenderDescription: In response to social movements and considering new research, Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) considerations in society have accelerated over the last decade. The ongoing demographic inversion and the related increase of the ageing population are certainly a driving force that will enhance this trend. Consequently, at both institutional (e.g. national governments, municipality/city) and business levels (e.g. within private organisations), there has been a push towards more inclusive and diverse environments. The scope of the Kick-start Theme is to investigate the technical feasibility and the viability of space technologies and applications addressing challenges related to DEI in society.

tenderTitle: Construction of a awning adjacent to the S5C Transit Hall
tenderDescription:
For few years, there has been a lack of space for Payload containers, Payload and Launchers equipment, as well as Payload Facilities mobile equipment. 
In order to respond to the need of flexibility, we must increase the storage space available protected from bad weather. That’s why we would like to have an awning adjacent to the S5C Transit Hall.
The objective is to cover an sufficiently large space so that various equipment could be stored, protected and handled. The project would require prerequisites regarding earthworks and foundations for the addition of a metal frame superstructure with cladding cover.

tenderTitle: NAVIGATION AND COMMUNICATION S-BAND PHASED ARRAY - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: In 2022, the Mars Communication and Navigation Infrastructure (MARCONI) mission concept wasstudied in the Concurrent Design Facility (CDF). The need for dual-polarized Rx/Tx S-band antennaproviding communication and navigation services has been identified. Thismultibeam antenna willneed to provide two services simultaneously:- Tx/RX Communication Service: working in S-band (2025-2300 MHz) in Left Hand CircularPolarization, the antenna shall provide the capability to receive and transmit data from Marslander and orbital assets. High directional beams with >22dBi gain within FoV (EoC=+-21deg)are required based on preliminary link budget. A trade-off (mass, volume, power, networkcomplexity, etc.) is needed to choose between a reconfigurable or a fixed multi-beam antenna(total number of beams to be defined during the activity). A simplified antenna model (notreconfigurable) shall be designed and manufactured for the proof of concept (using as much aspossible COTS components).- Navigation Service : working in S-Band (2483.5 - 2500 MHz) in Right Hand Circular Polarization,the antenna shall broadcast a navigation signal to all the assets available in the FoV (21deghalf cone TBC) generating a pattern able to provide a constant power flux density on groundover the full FoV in the Mars surface (an isoflux like pattern should be considered during thestudy).The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidate the antenna requirements and conduct a trade-off of different antennaarchitectures- Design the selected simplified antenna architecture- Manufacture a representative breadboard- Test and validate the antenna breadboard RF performance

tenderTitle: Towards Flexible Payload Processing Facilities at the European Spaceport
tenderDescription:
in the framework of the satellites preparation activities at the Guiana Space Center (CSG), CNES must be able to adapt its payload processing facilities in order to support the preparation of a wide range of satellites (from cubesat to telecommunication satellites of several tons).

This project includes several perimeters, such as:

Power distribution
- Adapt the power supply installations in the clean halls and the checkout rooms to provide uninterrupted power supply through multiple types of sockets.

Mechanical means
- Provide the Payload Facilities with dedicated mobile cranes used inside the clean halls for small satellites.

- Partitioning of the clean halls : supply the clean halls with movable walls

- Working stations : worktables and dedicated means for smallsat projects

Telecommunication
- Connection to the CSG network from the Payload Facility

- Direct communication between the clean halls and the checkout rooms

- Provide the clean halls and the checkout rooms with screens able to display the relevant information for the teams working inside

Offices and infrastructures
- Storage area with A/C system (> 150 m²)

- Break rooms for satellite teams

Competencies :

Telecommunications and network
Power distribution
Mechanics
Infrastructure works
Miscellaneous :

- 4 to 6 different clean rooms (3 buildings) and associated facilities are targeted

- Estimated schedule : 2025 to 2027

- Contracts attribution distributed by WP

tenderTitle: MULTI-BEAM RECEIVE ANTENNA FOR SATELLITE-BASED AIR TRAFFIC SURVEILLANCE  (ARTES 4.0 AT 5B.225)
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, implement and test a scaled engineering model with critical functions of a multi-beam receive antenna for satellite-based air traffic surveillance in the frequency range 950 - 1100 MHz, taking into account narrow beamwidth, directivity and mechanical constraints. Targeted Improvements:- Two-fold increase, compared to the state of the art, in the number of beams covering the visible Earth (to at least 30).- Increased beamwidth and non-uniform/flexible beam size whilst maintaining a gain of 20 dBi and respecting mechanical constraints.Description: The importance of satellites enabling global flight tracking and air traffic surveillance services is well recognised. Over-the-air aircraft signal detection results collected fromseveral space assets indicate challenges. There is a need to enhance the satellite-based Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR) messagereception, in particular the capability of detecting aircraft in highly congested airspaces when there is a high level of interfering signals arriving at the satellite.This activity aims to design, manufacture and test an on-board multi-beam antenna for reception of SSR signals and other relevant aircraft messages transmitted in the 950 - 1100 MHz range, taking into account the stringent requirements for in-band interference mitigation, grating lobe control, antenna gain and flexible multi-beam operation. Mechanical constraints on the antenna dimensions, weight and accommodation will be taken into account in the system trade-offs, antenna architecture development and design. The antenna architecture will support narrow beamwidths at large scan angles.

tenderTitle: INVESTING IN INDUSTRIAL INNOVATION - INCUBED ELEMENTANNOUNCEMENT OF PARTNERSHIP OPPORTUNITY (APO)
tenderDescription: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims at accompanying the European economic operators in the Earth Observation market rapid evolution currently witnessed in Europe and overseas. InCubed offers a new process in ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the realization of endeavours near-to-the-market with Economic Operators. Activities to be supported include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (missions, instruments, prototype element of EO constellation), innovative mission management solution, including for future EO constellation, the development of application platforms, etc. InCubed is looking for commercial viability by the end of the activity (up to at least a minimum viable product level) and a substantial degree of innovation i.e. adding new value to the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement/involvement is mandatory. Commercial customers are encouraged to be either as part of the consortium representing the value chain or as beta testers/validators of the developed product/service. Customer engagement/involvement must be highlighted at the pitch and proposal stage. Letters of potential customer support/interest are seen as a very positive aspect. The actual scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves in relevance to the InCubed objectives. Two development cycles are possible within InCubed: TheDe-Risking Cycle (start TRL 4) and Product Development Cycle (startTRL 6) depending on the maturity of the concept being developed. Regarding this forthcoming Announcement of Partnership Opportunity, Economic operators are invited to register and submit idea pitches onto ideas.esa.int (InCubed channel). Following a positive pitch meeting, the second step is to fill in a Part 1 (Outline) proposal template, which must be supported by the Participating State(s) having jurisdiction over them. Following a positive assessment, the economic operators will be invited to submit a Part 2 (Full) proposal template, as per established procedure and evaluation criteria. The proposals to be supported by InCubed will have to be co-funded by the economic operators (partnership agreements), as a sign of their engagement and belief in their own business case.

tenderTitle: MULTIFREQUENCY TRANSMIT ACTIVE PHASED ARRAYS FOR GROUND TERMINALS CONNECTED WITH MULTI-ORBIT NON GEOSTATIONARY ORBIT SATELLITES (ARTES AT 7A.078)
tenderDescription: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test enabling technologies for multi frequency transmit active antenna. This will include antenna radiating elements, beamforming techniques and active elements designed to cover Ku and Ka transmit frequency bands for ground terminals connected to non-geostationary multi-orbit satellites.Targeted Improvements: - Mass and size reduction by 30% by sharing components between frequency bands.- Enable access to satellite networks operating different orbits at Ku and Ka-band.Description: Active antenna based satcom systems in non-geostationary orbit are under development worldwide adopting mainly either Ku- or Ka- frequency bands. There is growing interest for active antennas able to cover both bands in order to better address user needs and increase flexibility.This activity will develop an antenna architecture covering RF, mechanical and thermal aspects. A baseline antenna solution will be designed. Key building blocks will be designed, manufactured and tested. This will include multichannel and multi frequency beamformers using European semiconductor processes. Beside digital control, the beamformers will embed on-chip memory for beam-states and calibration. A limited breadboard of a transmit active antenna will be designed, manufactured,and tested. The breadboard shall be able to generate at least 2 beams in variable directions in Ku-band and 2 beams in variable directions in Ka-band (4 simultaneous beams). The polarisation shall be switchable.

tenderTitle: KU AND KA DUAL-BAND TRANSMIT ACTIVE PHASED ARRAY (ARTES AT 5B.236)
tenderDescription: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test enabling technologies for multi-frequency transmit active antennas. This will include antenna radiating elements, beamforming techniques (analogue vs hybrid), active elements customised in order to cover both the Ku and Ka transmit frequency bands, integrated into a breadboard. Targeted Improvements: Enabling dual Ku and Ka-band transmit active phased arrays. Description: Active antenna based satcom systems in Geostationary (GEO) and Non-Geostationary Orbits (NGSO) are under development worldwide, mainly adopting either the Ku or Ka frequency bands. However, there is a growing interest for active antennas to be able to cover both bands in order to better address user needs and increase flexibility. This activity will develop and test enabling technologies for Multifrequency transmit active phased array antenna and beamforming networks, seamlessly covering both the Ku and Ka frequency bands. A trade-off between analogue and hybrid beamforming solutions will be considered as a minimum. Implementation and assembly concepts of the radiating elements, beamforming networks and active components including, interleaved or overlapped architectures, together with an integration concept of both antenna elements will be developed. A detailed design covering RF, mechanical and thermal aspects will be carried out. A breadboard demonstrator capable of producing at least 2 beams in Ku and 2 beams in the Ka band (4 simultaneous beams) will be developed. Architectures of beamforming MMICs required for such multifrequency active phased arrays will be defined and developed per a European semiconductor process.

tenderTitle: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT OF A VLEO SATELLITE TO ENABLE PRECISE ORBITAL MODELLING AND SYSTEM SIZING (ARTES AT 3E.026) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
tenderDescription: The objective of the activity is to develop high fidelity models to allow the mission design of satcom constellations in VLEO. An in-orbit experiment will be designed and manufactured to measure key geographically and time dependent atmospheric parameters (density, radiation, ionospheric, chemical composition etc..) as well as satellite flight parameters (including drag, solar cells efficiency, etc..). These measurements will enable the precise modelling of VLEO systems (incl. orbital mechanics, budgets, system sizing, etc.). Targeted Improvements: Enable precise VLEO orbital mechanics modelling and system sizing.Description: Due to the variability of the atmospheric conditions, the knowledge of environmental and atmospheric data (density, radiation level, chemical composition) is challenging to get, however in-situ measurements are critical to properly design attitude control processing chain. Previous in-orbit experiments have been attempted in the past but have met with limited mission success. Future VLEO satcom constellations are needed to operate for extended periods of time and will need to be resilient to highly variable environments yet providing viable system architecture. The precise orbital mechanics modelling is then crucial for the sizing of the telecommunication systems in VLEO. This in-orbit experiment will gather the relevant data of the orbital space environment in order to generate the flight dynamics modelling required for the AOCS control loop. This will benefit satellites in orbits ranging from 200km-400km, covering VLEO applications. To provide the needed measurements for the atmospheric models, a payload will be designed, including all the necessary sensing instruments. The spacecraft will be launched to a relevant orbit and in situ measurements will be gathered and communicated to ground over the operational lifetime. The key parameters to acquire and process will be: neutral atmosphere density, radiation, chemical composition and ionospheric parameters. In addition to these primary goals, secondary goals suggested by the bidders are invited (e.g. materials resistance to VLEO environment, solar cell ageing, etc.). In designing the experiment, the activity will consider important trade-offs such as:- Single vs multi spacecraft mission profiles- Life extension via on board propulsion- Co- or multi-orbit ISL to improve data latency and data recovery for very low orbits.The activity will allow design, develop or adapt existing payloads,select a host platform, integrate, launch and operate the payloads for the required time, analyse the acquired data, improve the current models and report on the next steps. In addition to the experimental campaign, the activity will include the review and improvement of current available atmospheric models, allowing for modelling improvements through correlation from the gathered in-orbit data. The minimum duration of the flight experiment will be 1 year in order to characterise and measure the atmospheric conditions in VLEO including seasonal atmospheric variability. Footnote: On Delegation Request activities will only be initiated on the explicit request of at least one National Delegation.

tenderTitle: S3B cloakrooms upgrades
tenderDescription:
The S3B location accomodates payloads in ISO 8 cleanroom. In order to preserve this environment, cleanliness specifications require that accesses [cloakrooms + material airlock] S3B HR and HN cleanrooms are upgraded to best meet the ISO 8 access standard.

The objective of this work is to upgrade the access areas (cloakrooms and material airlock) of the S3B to allow passage of equipment and all persons authorized to access it in accordance with the ISO 8 standard. The goal is to meet the ASPEC recommendations with the best possible compromise, given the existing architecture and difficult to modify.

tenderTitle: Modification of the EPCU S1A airlock
tenderDescription:
The EPCU S1A is a High Bay that can accommodate payloads in compliance with the ISO 8 cleanliness standard.
In order to access the High Bay without compromising the ISO 8 cleanliness standard, it is composed of two airlocks, one allowing transfers of payloads/equipment and the other dedicated exclusively to materials. 
Given the diversity of payload sizes, we need to adapt our facilities and optimise operational processes to accommodate different types of payload.
The aim of this work is to modify the airlock dedicated to materials into an airlock that meets the defined requirements to enable the arrival and transfer of payloads and equipment.

tenderTitle: Refurbishment and improvement of the S5E location
tenderDescription:
The S5E is a location dedicated to the maintenance of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as textile clothing, Personal Breathing Apparatus, scape operator, hoses or air bottles. All of this equipment is available to satellite customers and all users of the launch base. Today, the building no longer meets the ergonomic requirements and is not adapted to the cleanliness requirements that must be met by the revalidation flows of equipment used in clean rooms.
The objective of the proposed work is to refurbish the entire S5E location to improve the ergonomics and working conditions of operators, optimize revalidation times and create a flow of traffic where 'clean and revalidated' PPE do not use the same circuit as 'used-dirty' PPE.

tenderTitle: ExoMars - Rosalind Franklin Mission (EXM-RFM): Invitation to Tender for Isolation Valves
tenderDescription: The Rosalind Franklin Mission represents the continuation of ESA’s ExoMars programme following the breakup of the inter-Agency agreement with Roscosmos. As such, it replaces the previous Rover & Surface Platform Mission. The main objectives of the Rosalind Franklin Mission are to safely land on the Mars surface, collect and analyse in situ a range of Martian surface and subsurface soil samples, and to demonstrate technologies for planetary exploration. The key elements of the ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover are its advanced drilling system, coupled with a sophisticated on-board science laboratory, and its capability to move autonomously on a variety of terrains on Mars’ surface for at least 218 sols (8 months). Sampling down to a depth of 2 metres significantly increases the probability to detect preserved signs of past or even present life. The analysis of soil geo-chemistry will provide a detailed characterisation of the environment and geological history, and possibly provide evidence for the presence of organic compounds. The ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover will be placed on the surface of Mars by an Entry, Descent and Landing Module (EDLM). This module is the main new developmental element of the ExoMars-Rosalind Franklin mission and will require key contributions from European suppliers. The so-called “braking engines” will be provided by NASA as Customer Furnished Items (CFIs). The Rover System comprises the ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover Module and the Rover Operations Control Centre (ROCC), the latter developed by and located at ALTEC in Torino (Italy), where the ground operations of the Rover surface mission will be performed. The Rover and its payload will require maintenance and some upgrades to manage obsolescence and ensure compliance with the new mission requirements associated with the 2028 launch scenario. The ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover will benefit from the provision by NASA of Radio-Isotope Heating Units (RHUs). These RHUs are required to support the thermal control system of the Rover, replacing similar units previously provided by Roscosmos. The new flight system also requires the maintenance of the existing Carrier Module and of the Descent Module equipment and subsystems already developed by ESA. The launch services (launcher and launch site facilities) will also be provided by NASA. Airbus Defence and Space Ltd is the Lead Contractor for the Landing Platform Mechanical Thermal and Propulsion System (“MTPS”). As part of their scope of work, Airbus will release an Invitation to Tender (ITT) looking for a supplier of the Propulsion Isolation Valves. The Landing Platform will require at least 6 Propulsion Isolation Valves which will be used on the propulsion system.

tenderTitle: GSTP ELEMENT 1: DEVELOP - STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSAL: PREPARATION OF ENABLING SPACE TECHNOLOGIES AND BUILDING BLOCKS
tenderDescription: The European Space Agency ("the Agency" or "ESA") invites you to submit a Proposal under the General Support Technology Programme, Element 1: "Preparation of enabling space technologies and building blocks''The aim is to prepare and to develop enabling capabilities and the associated building blocks for space related systems and the associated sub-systems. An additional aim is to allow the targeted and coordinated development of the capabilities and building blocks (i.e. among academia and industry) in a given ESA Member State or across different Member States (in a collaborative manner). The intended output is to provide industry with a stronger foundation (i.e. building on this acquired know-how) in order to contribute to new space related system opportunities at national or international levels (institutional, commercial...).The objective is to enable Member States to support the further development of t capabilities and the associated building blocks in their industry. The technology development activities may be prepared in a targeted and coordinated manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed for a targeted type and class of space systems (in terms of performance, cost, size...) and with guiding specifications. The developments are to be performed in a coordinated manner to ensure that industry is able to work on complementary capabilities. The developments may be performed within one Member State or across several Member States in a collaborative manner.The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed to a level such that the industrial entities may then be able to perform developments and eventually produce for concrete/more specific space related developments. The developments may go from a proof-of-concept (via simulation or experiment) up to an engineering qualification model (EQM). They address any technical area (structures, avionics/GNC, power control and distribution...). The specications are to be linked to the guiding system or sub-system specifications. The maximum amount per activity is 500 KEuro.The maximum duration is 24 months.

tenderTitle: Emergency and Victim Assistance Vehicle
tenderDescription:
In the framework of its activities at the Guiana Space Center (CSG), CNES must renew five (5) Emergency and Victim Assistance Vehicles.

The vehicles, which is the subject of this pre-publication, must have the following equipments and features to perform its main functions:

•	Be compatible with the climatic conditions of French Guiana.
•	Be driven with Category B driving license
•	Be capable of taking a stretcher with a recumbent patient.
•	Be fitted with passive and active visual warnings.
•	Be fitted with audible warnings
•	Be fitted with a separate air conditioning system to serve the working area from that which serves the cab.

tenderTitle: Automatic Number-Plate Recognition (E9)
tenderDescription:
Context:
The visual verification of vehicle badges at CSG does not provide a sufficiently high level of security for access control. An automated license plate check should be set up at access points.
Description:
When approaching the barrier, the system must automatically recognize a vehicle's license plate and check whether it is authorized to enter the site. Controls must be automatic and instantaneous, with no need for the security guard to intervene, thus ensuring greater fluidity and efficiency.
In conjunction with the digital access control system, which efficiently verifies the identity of those on board, access can be authorized and the access barrier lifted.

tenderTitle: Digitalisation Plateau PMO
tenderDescription:
In the context of CSG’s Digitalization process whose goal is to :
•	Reduce re configuration delay in between two launches
•	Operation reduction costs
•	Maintenance reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification
•	Ensure Space base industrial partners workflow transversality
•	Rejuvenate and modernize the CSG’s image

The CSG will capitalize on the basis that were set by the ‘Socle Numérique Transverse (SNT)’ project in order to bring a brand new Information System.

The digitalization will use this pedestal so that a major part of the projects that will contribute to reach this target could be in line with what had been fulfilled by the CSG-NG. All those projects will be designed, thought, manufactured and deployed in order to reach those objectives

tenderTitle: CSG’s Digitalization - Radar and Launcher Simulation topic
tenderDescription:
In the context of CSG’s Digitalization process whose goal is to :
•	Reduce re configuration delay in between two launches
•	Maintenance and Operation reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification
The CSG will capitalize on the basis that was set by the ‘Socle Numérique Transverse (SNT)’ project in order to bring a brand new Information System.
The global scope that the digitalization services must address are:
•	Satellites’ and launch campaigns operations
•	Maintenance and sustainability (in line with the SNT project)
•	CSG’s space base Infrastructures (physical, software or virtual) (mainly for networks and informatics)
•	Security, Safety and protection 
•	Daily life improvement and simplification
•	Communication
•	Datacenters
•	Projects valorization and marketability
•	Process improvements and optimization
•	Radars and Simulations
In order to match those needs, the project teams will be organized according to the following topics:
•	IT Networks
•	Planification and Task/Operation management
•	Maintenance management
•	Technical fact management
•	Data management
•	IT Hardware
•	Right profile and access management
•	Safety and Security
•	Information Broadcast
•	Radar and Launcher Simulation
Two transversal teams will be in charge of the global consistency of the projects for planning and architectural/urbanization purposes
 This publication concerns the Radar and Launcher Simulation topic
The expected services provision for each of those items are:
•	Architecture and urbanization of the systems, taken into account Maintenance and optimizations 
•	Project Management officer. Projects will have to be managed through a project’s portfolio. Team guidance for steps definition and planning formalization, accurate indicators follow up.
•	Requirements analysis and formalization of the projects that will be designed to meet those requirements.
•	Project owner support for specification redaction for each identified project, document redaction and accurate technical descriptions 
•	Market surveys and state of art
•	Analysis reports of studied solutions
•	Proof of concept based on the solution identified and validation
•	Project management for design, development, implementation and deployment of the identified projects
•	Providing the solutions and implements them (could be external solutions of specialized editors and vendors)
•	Support and coaching for information security analysis 
•	On-site installation (when necessary) and global system technical validation. The holder of the contract will be responsible of the supplies that will be plugged with CNES CSG’s equipment.
•	Training of the staff that will be in charge of the exploitation of the systems to ensure its autonomy
•	Users and administrators training.
•	Ensure the maintainability and the sustainability of the systems and projects 
•	Ensure knowledge transfer and reversibility to the CNES teams in order to ensure the ability to keep going with Project management, urbanization and mastering the new deployed tools 
These services therefore provide the entire life cycle of the projects that will arise from each of the topic.
All items will have to be compliant with CNES CSG's context and constraints
Although this publication is specific to a given topic, the tenderer must ensure the mutual consistency of the projects. He will have to coordinate with the teams in charge of planning and the overall architecture of the systems.

tenderTitle: FIXED CALL FOR PROPOSALS FOR CO-SPONSORED RESEARCH ACTIVITIES (PHD THESES) UNDER THE REQUESTING PARTY ACTIVITY (RPA) IN LITHUANIA
tenderDescription: The European Space Agency (the "Agency" or "ESA") and the Ministry of Education and Science of Lithuania hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above subject.While the Call for Proposals is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, the present Call for Proposals is addressed only to Lithuanian companies (including SMEs) or academic and research organisations. Prospective Tenderers are therefore requested to note that the Agency can only consider Proposals from legal entities registered in Lithuania. Tasks may be assigned to non-Lithuanian entities registered in other ESA Member States. Such tasks shall in any case not constitute the core activities of the proposed study or development and shall not exceed 20% of the total price.3)The Standardised Requesting Party Activity (RPA) scheme for the implementation of Member States' National Programme foresees standard Activity Types. This CfP relates exclusively to activity type G2: PhD Theses. 4)The subject of this CfP is exclusively for the following activity type and the related mandatory requirements:G2 - PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from theLithuanian Space Industry and would lead to a new product or service being able to be developed.i) Tenderers are invited to submit PhD research ideas for the following maximum price: the proposals must be submitted in a co-funded basis. tenderDescription:
The Guiana Space Center, Europe’s Spaceport - CNES, located in Kourou in French Guiana, wishes to replace the video wall of its Safety Coordination Office (BCS), of its Crisis Room and its Security PC. 
- With regards to the BCS: The objective of this replacement is to have a system similar to the current one but with screens adopting current technology and with the availability of long-term spare parts stocks. This wall, made up of one or more elements will have a size of 3mx5m.
- With regards to the crisis room: the objective of this replacement is to have a system similar in terms of equipment to that of the BCS. The wall will be smaller in size 2mx3m, will be able to receive preselected images from the BCS image wall. It will be able to display at least 6 to 8 images from different sources.
- With regards to the PC Security video wall: The objective of this replacement is to have a system similar to the current one. The wall will be smaller in size 2mx3m, will be able to receive preselected images from the BCS image wall and/or the crisis room. It will be able to display at least 6 to 8 images from different sources.

tenderDescription:
CNES-CSG intends to renew its infrared cameras that follows the rockets after launching during a few minutes.

Currently, we are using MWIR cameras that are now obsolete and don't fulfill all requirements.
Recent tests have shown that LWIR cameras are more suitable.

The camera system must include image recording.

The purpose of the project is to:
•	Supply the cameras

•	Define the right parameters to optimize images

tenderTitle: CSC Data Processors Re-engineering - Level-1 and Level-2 Sentinel-3 SRAL and MWR Processors
tenderDescription:
Best practices Intended Announcement 

Open competition 

 

 

The CSC Data Processors Re-engineering Service aims at the implementation of a new Earth Observation Processor Framework (EOPF) and the re-engineering of the data processors currently used to operationally generate the Copernicus Sentinel-1/2/3(land) Level-0, Level-1, Level-2 data with the aim to harmonise and modernise the operational processing framework, to benefit from the capabilities of cloud-based environments such as the elasticity of computing resources and to efficiently support both the systematic production operations as well as the needs of a more flexible on-demand production context. 

 

CS GROUP has been selected by ESA as Prime Contractor for the Sentinels Data Processors Re-engineering Service. As part of this Service, CS GROUP will procure the implementation of the Sentinels processors re-engineering via open competitive tenders according to the ESA Best Practices procedure. 

Three open competitive tenders have already been issued: 

The first one on the 03/02/2023, covering the re-engineering of the Level -1 and Level-2 data processors for Sentinel-2 and the re-engineering of the Level-1 and Level-2 data processors for Sentinel-3 OLCI, SLSTR and Synergy. 

A second one on the 07/04/2023, covering the re-engineering of the Sentinel-1/2/3 Level-0 data processors 

A third one on the 01/06/2023, covering the re-engineering of the Level –1 and Level –2 data processors for Sentinel 1 

 

The fourth and last open competitive tender covering the following activities is planned to be published at the beginning of August 2023: 

The re-engineering of Sentinel 3 SRAL and MWR Level-1 and Level-2 data processors. 

 

Attention is drawn to the fact that the CSC Data Processors Re-engineering Service is funded by the Copernicus Programme under the MFF 2014-2021 and will therefore be open exclusively to economic operators which have their registered office in a EU Member State or a Country participating to the EU Copernicus Programme in the frame of such MFF. 

 

The Best Practices invitations to tender (each consisting of a Cover Letter, Statement of Work, Special Conditions of Tender and Draft Contract) will be available on esa-star Publication, a dedicated module of ESA’s tendering website esa-star (https://esastar-publication-ext.sso.esa.int)

tenderTitle: I-HAB –  External Work Package for AIT Activities
tenderDescription:
The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (I-HAB) is 
ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting
the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization 
requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions 
from USA, Japan and Canada. 
The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure 
designed to support both robotic and human exploration 
of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained 
lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than 
the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. 
It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four
 astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to 
two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection 
of the contractor for AIT External Wok Package in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Work Package is intended as a service to support 
the TAS-I AIT team for the Assembly, Integration and 
Test of the I-HAB Gateway module.
Services under this ITT is: 
•	AIT External Wok Package, expressed as mechanical, 
fluid, avionic, EGSE and Quality skilled personnel 
Time period for which this External WP is required are 
subject to evolution, being I-HAB a full prototype in its 
early Design Phase. Hence, actual dates will be finalized 
in the negotiation phase with selected bidder

Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can 
be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_
and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

tenderTitle: Temperature controlled truck equipped with a column tailgate
tenderDescription:
In the framework of its activities at the Guiana Space Center (CSG), CNES must be able to :
•	Transport telecom racks, small spacecrafts, crates, parcels, packages and various loads to and from CSG site and various locations in French Guiana,
•	Transport equipments of the Spacecraft Customer teams (telecoms racks, nanosatellites, secure crates, aircraft pallets)
•	Transport secure goods,
•	Transport dangerous goods

The truck, which is the subject of this pre-publication, must have the following equipments to perform its main functions:
•	a flatbed with "accordion" type side panels (3 panels per side): transported equipments (telecom racks, small spacecrafts, parcels, packages, various loads, etc.) could be loaded from the sides using a forklift truck. Transported equipments must be kept in perfect condition, protected from weather conditions during transport.
•	A horizontally elevated DHOLLANDIA column tailgate: goods could be loaded with a pallet truck, or on the ground or on a platform,
•	An air conditioning system: equipments could be transported at a temperature between 14°C and 22°C.
Moreover, knowing that the intervention zones extend beyond the private enclosure of the Guiana Space Center (CSG), this temperature controlled truck equipped with a column tailgate must be able to travel legally on public roads.

tenderTitle: Tactical Panel – Crisis GIS (E3)
tenderDescription:
Context:
At present, there are no interactive IT means available for efficient consultation of CSG infrastructures information.
In the event of an incident, response time is an essential factor in preserving people and installations. Effective sharing of information at all levels (field - emergency center - crisis room), coupled with a more relevant cross-referencing of data, would save operational time in decision-making, especially in the crisis room.
Description:
This project deals with the implementation of a GIS (Geographic Information System) on a tactical panel-type hardware support in order to provide:
- A cartographic representation of the CSG and its surroundings in real time.
- All the information required by the firemen for their operations.
- An instant consultation from the field and simultaneous monitoring of operations to the crisis room.
Setting up a GIS that can be consulted and interacted with on appropriate hardware will be a great help in decision-making and real-time information sharing between the field, the fire station located at the Technical Center and the crisis room.
Thus, adding a geographical visualization of the situation in real-time represents a major asset for improving communication between all actors, while enhancing crisis management and decision-making.

tenderTitle: Automatic Number-Plate Recognition (E9)
tenderDescription:
Context:
The visual verification of vehicle badges at CSG does not provide a sufficiently high level of security for access control. An automated license plate check should be set up at access points.
Description:
When approaching the barrier, the system must automatically recognize a vehicle's license plate and check whether it is authorized to enter the site. Controls must be automatic and instantaneous, with no need for the security guard to intervene, thus ensuring greater fluidity and efficiency.
In conjunction with the digital access control system, which efficiently verifies the identity of those on board, access can be authorized and the access barrier lifted.

tenderTitle: Introducing Connected operator
tenderDescription:
CNES-CSG intends to develop new facilities for its customers and partners. Among those new functionalities, the connected operator shall for instance allow a remote engineer to interact with a local technician to fulfill technical interventions on the rocket or on the payloads.
New functionalities are also expected to help applying technical procedures thanks to augmented reality of virtual environments

The purpose of the project is to develop new tools and functionalities compatible with the security constraints at the CNES and profitable for all industrial partners to allow remote specialist to help conducting specific repairs or technical maintenances.
This might lead to the usage of augmented reality, virtual environments , mixed or assisted reality

The purpose of the project is to :
•	Define the technical solution compatible with the security constraints
•	Deploy the solution
•	Being creative and possibly suggest other approaches in order to fulfill the business case consisting in being locally assisted by remote specialists.

Delivery will consist in the new infrastructure that will support remote assistance

tenderTitle: IAP.KS.SM.000 SUSTAINABLE MICRO-MOBILITY KICKSTART - OPEN CALL FOR PROPOSAL
tenderDescription: The aim of this Kickstart is to help tackle sustainability challenges relating to batteries, electrical products, electronic waste, and the ICT sector. Solutions can target any part of the product lifecycle, whether it's improving sourcing of materials for the micromobility industry or helping to recover useful components from landfill sites. Winning teams will receive 80% funding of up to 200,000 to run a year-long feasibility study. This call is launched in collaboration with Dott, Voi, and Material Focus.The following topics are of relevance: - Enhancing the design, sourcing, manufacturing and supply of batteries and electrical goods - Ensuring safe usage, storage, charging and repair of batteries and electrical items- Improving circularity and end of life solutions of batteries and electrical goods- Counteracting the negative environmental impacts of data centres and blockchain-powered solutions.During the Kickstart study, an in-depth analysis of the technical feasibility and economic viability of the solution should be carried out.

tenderTitle: Renouvellement du Système de Détection de la Foudre (THOR)
tenderDescription:
Pre-publication for Lightning Detection System Renewal (THOR).

This project aims to renew the current lightning detection system of the Guiana Space Center (CSG) which is currently constitute of:
•	Three interferometric detection sensors. 
•	One processing system in charge of collecting lightning data measurements and treatments.
•	A software to localize cloud-to-ground or intra-cloud lightning flashes in real time.
•	Various real-time display terminals. 

The future system could propose another method than interferometry to detect lightning as well as considering other sensors locations among a list of sites given by CSG. 

Like the current system, the new one will have a network detection sensor, a digital processor to collect and compute the lightning data, and a software which displays detection and high-precision localization of lightning flashes. 
The project perimeter contains renewal of lightning detection sensors, lightning data processing system, and an operating and display software with associated real-time display terminals.

Pré publication Renouvellement du Système de Détection de la Foudre (THOR).

Ce projet concerne le renouvellement du système de détection de la foudre du Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG) constitué actuellement : 
•	De trois capteurs de détection de type interférométrique.
•	D’un serveur central d’acquisition, de stockage et de traitement des données.
•	D’un logiciel de traitement des données pour détecter et localiser en temps réel les décharges de foudre au sol ou les décharges intra-nuages.
•	De postes opérateurs pour la visualisation en temps réel des décharges de foudre.

Le nouveau système pourra proposer une technique de détection différente de l’interférométrie ainsi que de nouveaux emplacements des capteurs parmi un ensemble de sites prédéfinis qui sera fourni par le CSG. 

A l’image du système actuel, le nouveau système doit comprendre un réseau de capteurs de détection, une centrale de traitement des données brutes ayant la possibilité de stocker les données à la station météo du CSG et un logiciel d’exploitation permettant la détection et la localisation précise des décharges de foudre en temps réel.
Le périmètre du projet concerne le renouvellement des capteurs, de la centrale d’acquisition des données, du logiciel d’exploitation et des postes opérateurs permettant la visualisation en temps réel des décharges de foudre.

MI has supported the definition of objectives and use cases for the present call. The objectives of the Call are to: i) guarantee the right of education to each student irrespective of geography,social status, economic conditions even during extraordinary circumstances;ii)support the digital transformation of the school throughthe adoption of innovative technologies and solutions to replace traditional learning solutions, iii)offer the opportunity to economic operators to develop and demonstrate applications based on space for the benefit of students and educators and iv) promote the knowledge of space related disciplines to educators and students. Tenderers shall engage with schoolsand agree with them a pilot trial to verify and deploy in an operational environment the proposed service(s).

tenderTitle: KICK-START THEMATIC CALL: NATURAL CAPITAL
tenderDescription: The purpose of this activity is to analyse the technical and business viability of space-based services which play a key role in the development of natural capital services (defined as per the topics indicated below). The services proposed by the Contractor inthe context of the present activity can leverage on the integration of space-based data together with other datasets, such as aerial imagery, in-situ data and data from other sources (e.g. statistic, maps). Solutions may also find value in integrating further terrestrial technologies such as machine learning, distributed ledger technologies, cloud computing and beyond. The following requirements shall be taken in account when carrying out the activity: o The kick-start study shall target the definition of innovative services, the development of business models for their provision, and the roadmap for further realisation, but not pure research and technology development activities.o The envisaged services shall benefit from one or more space assets (including SatNav, SatCom, SatEO, Human Spaceflight). The space assets shall represent a clear added value for the considered services and do not need to be limited to ESA's or European space assets. - Due to the customer/user-driven nature of the study and with the aim to consolidating the case for a potential follow-on demonstration project, the Contractor shall engage with the relevant customer/user community(ies) fromthe outset of the study and, whenever relevant for the successful achievement of the activity's objectives, other relevant stakeholders. Such involvement shall be reinforced by the Contractor during the whole study, to:- Understand the current solutions adopted by the users;- Define the user needs, constraints and expectations; - Validate the user requirements; - Identify potentially paying customers/users; - Validate the adequacy of the proposed system and associated services; - Coordinate and agree on the implementation roadmap of the services and possible participation in a demonstration project.

tenderTitle: Radôme station télémesure des Bermudes
tenderDescription:
The French Guyana Space Center telemetry station located on the Bermuda archipelago is often operated during the CSG launch campaigns. Installed in the Bermuda in 2011 this station is exposed to a hostile environment; high temperatures, tropical storms, high level of air salinity. These elements strongly affect the antenna mechanics and fluids. They lead to a premature drying and corrosion that can damage the system. The installation of a dome is necessary as a countermeasure to protect the whole antenna from its external environment. 
La station de télémesure du Centre Spatial Guyanais localisée aux Bermudes est régulièrement utilisée pour le suivi des campagnes de lancements depuis le site du Centre Spatial Guyanais. Installée aux Bermudes en 2011, l’antenne est soumise à l’environnement de l’archipel qui présente une climatologie éprouvante pour les éléments mécaniques et fluides par des températures élevées, des tempêtes tropicales, une salinité de l’air importante. Ces conditions impactent fortement les différents éléments de l’antenne et provoquent un assèchement et une corrosion prématurés de ces derniers. Afin de protéger l’ensemble de l’antenne de son environnement extérieur, la mise en place d’un radôme s’avère nécessaire.

tenderTitle: Study for BIM-GEM set up at CSG ( C17 )
tenderDescription:
Context

CNES-CSG wants to digitalize its activities in order to:
•	Reduce reconfiguration delay in between two launches
•	Maintenance and Operation reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification

Description

In this frame CNES-CSG intends to undergo BIM-GEM approach for its real estate assets to optimize operating costs and facilitate the management.

Activity will consists in:
-	project management assistance
-	feasibility study
-	roadmap updating
-	PoC follow up

Inputs will be:
-	preliminary roadmap
-	results of a PoC (if available)
-	results of an audit
-	graphics standards

Expected deliveries are in particular
-	updated roadmap
-	a development program

tenderTitle: Nitrogen and helium fluid networks modernization in Payload Facilities (EPCU)
tenderDescription:
Within Payload Facilities (EPCU S1, S3B, S5), the fluid networks (nitrogen and helium) are used by payload customers for campaign activities and also by EPCU operators for maintenance and operational activities. 

From one facility to another and/or within the same building, the nitrogen and helium fluid networks are different. These differences are due to initial design of the network but also to changes made on some networks and not on others. 
The objective is to : 
•	Remove disparities between networks
•	Modernize the design of the fluid networks in order to improve control, maintenance and operability
•	Create an architecture allowing the monitoring of systems in real time
•	Improve the reliability of an aging network subject to numerous leaks (introduce new materials, new technologies…)

tenderTitle: Shared data platform – SESAME ( J1 )
tenderDescription:
Context

CNES-CSG wants to digitalize its activities in order to :
•	Reduce reconfiguration delay in between two launches
•	Maintenance and Operation reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification

Description
In this context, the CNES CSG aims to deliver a new data-sharing platform that could be used by all industrial partners over the Space Centre.
Currently the data sharing in between industrial is complicated. We need a platform that could ensure the security and the sharing of data set that will allow to cover specific use cases such as Supply chain, energy consumptions.
 
The follow up and getting the big picture on those functional needs required to get a unified vision of same data that are held either by on or the other industrial partner on the base.
Setting up a data-sharing platform will enable to easily send/get those data and re-use them either on the platform itself or by importing those data in each industrial partner Information system.
This platform will also have to deliver data mining and data intelligence services so that each partner could use those tools to follow up the actions and dashboards to allow decisions

The expected delivery will consist in deploying the new data sharing platform, train and explain how it works to all industrial partners on the CSG Space port.

tenderTitle: RSVSP Project
tenderDescription:
Renewal of the Guiana Space Center’s (CSG) CCTV equipment "RSVSP Project"
This project concerns the renewal of the Guiana Space Center’s (CSG) CCTV equipment : RSVSP project.
The scope of the case includes:
•	Renewal of obsolete CCTV equipment (analog technology) by digital equipment, compatible with the fleet already deployed and operational on the Ariane 6 Ground Segment : cameras, processing and acquisition units, storage and archiving units, etc.
•	Interconnection of this new generation equipment to the CSG’s shared Safety and Protection network via active network equipment.
•	Provision, installation and connection of new cameras to the existing CCTV supervision system (SVSP).
•	Provision, installation and connection to the existing CCTV supervision system (SVSP) of new operator stations.
•	Taking into account the impacts of the various changes identified above on the existing CCTV supervision system (SVSP).
•	Taking into account functional ergonomic changes to the existing CCTV supervision system (SVSP).

Ce projet concerne le renouvellement des équipements de Vidéosurveillance Sûreté Protection (SVSP) du Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG) : projet RSVSP.
Le périmètre de l’affaire inclut : 
•	Le renouvellement des équipements de vidéosurveillance obsolètes (technologie analogique) par des équipements numériques, compatibles du parc déjà déployé et opérationnel sur l’Ensemble de Lancement N°4 Ariane 6 : caméras, unités de traitement et d’acquisition, unités de stockage et d’archivage, etc…
•	L’interconnexion de ces équipements nouvelle génération au réseau mutualisé Sûreté Protection existant du CSG via des équipements réseau actifs.
•	La fourniture, l’installation et le raccordement au système de supervision de vidéosurveillance existant (SVSP) de nouvelles caméras.
•	La fourniture, l’installation et le raccordement au système de supervision de vidéosurveillance existant (SVSP) de nouveaux postes opérateurs.
•	La prise en compte des impacts liés aux diverses modifications identifiées ci-dessus sur le système de supervision existant (SVSP).
•	La prise en compte de modifications ergonomiques fonctionnelles du système de supervision existant (SVSP).

•	Le renouvellement des équipements de vidéosurveillance obsolètes (technologie analogique) par des équipements numériques, compatibles du parc déjà déployé et opérationnel sur l’Ensemble de Lancement N°4 Ariane 6 : caméras, unités de traitement et d’acquisition, unités de stockage et d’archivage, etc…

tenderTitle: CALL FOR PROPOSALS - EO-PNRR-IRIDE-PROJECT  IRIDE - APPLICATION/TOOLBOX AND MARKETPLACE
tenderDescription: According to the "Arrangement for ESA's Assistance to the Italian National Project concerning Earth Observation and Space Transportation", ESA/LEG/525 Paris, 22 December 2021, ESA will provide technical assistance to the Presidency of Council of Ministries of theItalian Republic for the swift implementation of the Italian "Piano Nazionale di Ripresa e Resilienza" (hereinafter also IT PNRR), in the domain of Earth Observation and Space Transportation.In providing the technical assistance, ESA will manage the technical and contractual aspects of the project and will be responsible for the procurements related to the Arrangement. This contractual activity is relevant to the Component of the PNRR devoted to Space Activities for Earth Observation (hereinafter called EO PNRR IRIDE Project), which covers the realization of an End-to-End System composed by the Upstream Segment, the Downstream Segment and the Services Segment to provide the geospatial-based services at National and European level, according to the needs expressed by the Italian National Authorities with the objective to provide services to the Public Administration and to private Customers.The Upstream will be based on a Satellite Constellation(s). The payloads will be a combination of SARs and optical, panchromatic, hyperspectral an infrared ImagersThe Downstream is composed by the Flight Operation Segment, the Payload Data Ground Segment, the "marketplace" and the Cyber Italy (which is a Digital Twin of Italy)The Services will be a combination of services to public administrations and commercial services. The following 8 services for public administrations have been currently identified: Coastal service and maritime-coastal monitoring, Air Quality Service, Ground Motion Service, Monitor service coverage and land use (Land Cover/Use), Hydrometeorological Service, Water Resources Service, Emergency service, Security service.The procurement subject of the present Call for Proposals is relevant to the IRIDE Application/Toolbox and Marketplace.This is an open and scalable digital ecosystem where demand andsupply will be met using innovative developments in geospatial processing, cloud computing, artificial intelligence and fusion of different sources of data.The IRIDE Application/Toolbox and Marketplace will provide the users with access to data, applications andservices and will implement the following functionalities:Hosting of data generated in the frame of the IRIDE project and all complementary data required for the services implementationFederation with external data sources (e.g., Copernicus Dias, National missions, etc.) allowing data interoperabilityUsers' management, addressing user authentication, authorization and interactionsBilling management: managing all the required commercial transactionsData discovery, visualisation and access: allowing user to search and discover products of interest, to visualize the products and their characteristics and to download the dataData manipulation and Analysis Ready Data generation, allowing merging, sub-setting of products and more sophisticated elaborations to extract feature of interest from productsHosting and providing access to applications: allowing usage of applications available on the systems and allowing download of applicationsHosting and providing access to services: allowing users to access and exploit the offered servicesHosting and providing access to Digital Twin of Italy: allowing users to access and exploit the Digital Twin capabilitiesThe Application/Toolbox and Marketplace procurement will be implemented via a Call for Proposals, with a two-stage mechanism.In the first stage, Tenderers will be invited to submit an outline proposal. The Agency will select up to two outline proposals and enter into a dialogue with the selected Tenderer(s).The second stage of the procurement is the submission of a full proposal, eitherin restricted competition (if more than one Tenderer selected) or direct negotiation (if only one Tenderer selected), for the implementation of the marketplace, with an option for the operations and maintenance up to mid-2026. Only one contract will be placed forthe marketplace.

tenderTitle: ITT1 - PROJECT ARRANGEMENT FOR A FRAMEWORK PROJECT IMPLEMENTING ESAS SUPPORT OF SPACE-RELATED ACTIVITIES IN THE CZECH REPUBLIC
tenderDescription: The European Space Agency (the Agency) hereby invites you to submit a proposal, in the frame of the Permanently Open Call for Proposals under the Czech Third Party Framework Project. The present ITT is addressed only to Czech companies (including SMEs) and academic and research organizations. This ITT is part of the Czech Third Party Framework Project aimed at supporting the development of the Czech industry, university and research centres as well as the alignment of space-related activities carried out in the Czech Republic with the European programmes carried out by ESA. The subject of this ITT is exclusively for the following activity types: a. Development activities leading to hardware or software products, services or generic technologies with potential for re-use including technology demonstrations, industrial processes as well as related industrial capability building in areas of documentation, qualityassurance, product lifecycle management. The start TRL shall be at least 2 and the target TRL should be TRL 7 or below; b. Activities (collectively referred to as Studies) preparing for the future (e.g. feasibility studies, technology assessments, user requirements or market surveys) and/or services to support national competitiveness in space programmes. Note: Education and awareness activities shall not be considered in the present call.

tenderTitle: SPACE BASED SERVICES / APPLICATIONS ADDRESSING COVID-19 OUTBREAK
tenderDescription: The unprecedented situation caused by the characteristics of the COVID-19 pandemic has created enormous challenges to society. Beside the specific issues related to the COVID-19 outbreak, all remaining parts of the "traditional" healthcare ecosystems have been also heavily affected. As a consequence, many European countries have taken extremely challenging measures to limit the propagation of the virus, to treat affected people while maintaining, to the possible extent, the normal operations of their healthcare systems. A number of preventive measures have also been implemented (e.g. schools closure and remote schooling, social distancing, remote working) to slow down the virus propagation. Such measures have however a massive impact on Europe's economy and the daily life of European citizens. In some cases, they can even generate dramatic social fractures and inequalities, such as education dropout and domestic violence. ESA is therefore calling for actions in order to facilitate the quick integration and deployment of concrete and sustainable solutions, which shall make use of the different advantages provided by space-based products and services. These solutions shall contribute to alleviate the negative impacts caused by the COVID-19 and associated measures of containment but also help improving preparedness for future outbreaks. Proposed solutions shall be consider the evolution of the crisis situation and therefore address relevant user needs. Companies responding to the Open Call for Proposals are invited to propose Demonstration Projects dedicated to the deployment and demonstration of pre-operational services, addressing Healthcare or Education.

tenderTitle: BASS AO: SPACE IN RESPONSE TO COVID-19 OUTBREAK
tenderDescription: This Announcement of Opportunity (AO), originated from the collaboration agreement between the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Italian Minister for Technological Innovation and Digitization (MID), has the scope of supporting citizens and communities which are facing the extraordinary consequences of the COVID-19 outbreak. ESA and MID initiated a dialogue with several user communities and stakeholders which are facing the current challenges, this has led to the identification of the most important application areas which belong to the health and education sector. The high-level objectives of the AO are: Help the Italian citizens and professionals of the health and educational sector to deal with the challenges of the coronavirus outbreak; Support the development and the adoption of services in health and in education for sustain the Italian community in reacting to the coronavirus outbreak; Demonstrate the benefit provided by the utilization of space-assets integrated with other novel technologies in this extraordinary circumstances Offer the opportunity to economic operators to deploy and demonstrate applications solutions based on space for the benefit of citizens, local authorities and enterprises.The AO wants to provide a quick and effective aid to the Italian citizens which is the most COVID-19 affected community, outside China. The proposed services can also benefit user and stakeholder communities of other geographical areas which inevitably are dealing with similar struggles. The Tenderer, intending to respond to this AO, shall select one of the following topics: Health and Education and identify an application area(s) which is relevant exclusively to the specific context and related challenges. The Tenderers are requested to submit an Outline and a Full Proposal of a Demonstration Project within the deadlines defined in the Cover Letter. The proposal shall describe a pilot trial, that shall take place in Italy, to test and deploy in an operational environment the proposed service(s) with the support of the relevant user communities.

tenderTitle: CREO Project
tenderDescription:
Projet CREO "Renouvellement des moyens de calcul des retombées éléments lanceurs en opérations du CSG"

Dans le cadre de la Loi sur les Opérations Spatiale, l’opérateur de lancement doit démontrer la maitrise des zones de retombée des fragments de lanceurs (Art 23 de [RT]). Le CNES doit, au titre de son activité de contrôle, s’assurer que ces zones, nominales ou accidentelles, sont conformes à la réglementation. Des moyens existent en interne CNES, opérés par les équipes de la Sauvegarde Vol du Centre Spatial Guyanais et de la DTN, mais aucun moyen unique ne répond à tous les besoins identifiés. 

Le projet CREO (Calcul des Retombées d’Eléments lanceur Opérationnel) est un projet informatique qui consiste à utiliser l’outil développé en interne CNES, nommé OREO, comme coeur de calcul pour estimer les zones de retombées d’éléments lanceur en soumission et en temps réel (cas nominal ou dégradé). CREO devra héberger une IHM permettant une utilisation opérationnelle. Cela revient globalement à intégrer en IHM et à interfacer avec le temps réel l’outil OREO, ainsi qu’à réaliser quelques traitements simples dont de la visualisation cartographique. 
L’objectif global est de disposer d’un outil flexible et configurable facilement en fonction de l’architecture du lanceur et des moyens.
La première version sera qualifiée et testée pour le lanceur Ariane 6, puis le logiciel sera étendu aux autres lanceurs au CSG.
Le contenu des interfaces devra globalement être cohérent des autres outils actuels utilisés par le CSG (principalement le SCTV (Système de Coordination, Traitement et Visualisation)) 

CREO Project "Renewal of the means of calculating the impact of launchers in operation at CSG"

From the French Spatial Act, launch operator has to prove falling launch area conformity following Art. 23 of Technical Reglementation. The CNES has, from his control activity, to ensure that these areas, nominal or hazardous, are conform with the french reglementation. Some ground-base segment does exist already, operated by the Guyanese Space Centre (CSG) Flight Safety teams, but need improvement and unicity. 
The CREO project is an IT project which consists in integrating into the GUI and interacting it with real time tools a multi-launcher flight safety diagnostic tool currently used by the CSG Flight Safety teams called ‘OREO’, and in executing some simple treatments, including cartographic visualization. 
This tool is based on a CNES mode OREO.
The overall objective is to have a flexible and configurable tool that is easily configurable according to the launcher’s architecture and dimensioning scenarios.
The first version will be qualified and tested for the Ariane 6 launcher, and will be extended then to the others launchers.
The content of the interfaces must be consistent overall with the other current tools used by the CSG (mainly the SCTV (Coordination, Processing and Visualization System)).

La première version sera qualifiée et testée pour le lanceur Ariane 6, puis le logiciel sera étendu aux autres lanceurs au CSG.
Le contenu des interfaces devra globalement être cohérent des autres outils actuels utilisés par le CSG (principalement le SCTV (Système de Coordination, Traitement et Visualisation)) 

CREO Project "Renewal of the means of calculating the impact of launchers in operation at CSG"

From the French Spatial Act, launch operator has to prove falling launch area conformity following Art. 23 of Technical Reglementation. The CNES has, from his control activity, to ensure that these areas, nominal or hazardous, are conform with the french reglementation. Some ground-base segment does exist already, operated by the Guyanese Space Centre (CSG) Flight Safety teams, but need improvement and unicity. 
The CREO project is an IT project which consists in integrating into the GUI and interacting it with real time tools a multi-launcher flight safety diagnostic tool currently used by the CSG Flight Safety teams called ‘OREO’, and in executing some simple treatments, including cartographic visualization. 
This tool is based on a CNES mode OREO.
The overall objective is to have a flexible and configurable tool that is easily configurable according to the launcher’s architecture and dimensioning scenarios.
The first version will be qualified and tested for the Ariane 6 launcher, and will be extended then to the others launchers.
The content of the interfaces must be consistent overall with the other current tools used by the CSG (mainly the SCTV (Coordination, Processing and Visualization System)).

tenderTitle: VERY-LOW MASS-FLOW RATE FLOW CONTROLLER FOR FINE CONTROL FOR GRAVIMETRY MISSIONS - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: This ITT will allow the Agency to identify the most promising technology for fine mass-flow control of Electric Propulsion systems in order to enhance the efficiency, resolution and minimum thrust step required for Earth Observation gravimetry missions. This activity will assess and benchmark the currently available technologies at concept level and boost the Technology Readiness Level (TRL) to a level of = 3 (analytical and experimental critical function and/or characteristic proof-of-concept), with the ultimate objective to minimise development risks before entering detailed design, qualification, production and commercialisation phases.The targetof this activity is to design, manufacture, assemble and test a Breadboard Model (BBM) of a flow-rate controller that complies withthe defined requirements. To achieve this goal, several tasks are defined as intermediary objectives which shall be sequentially achieved:-To assess the system/AOCS needs for representative missions, and to extract the relevant propulsion requirements (functional, performance and robustness) -To flow-down the propulsion requirements to mass flow control specification -To survey of available flow control technologies for space and non-space applications-To perform a preliminary benchmark of suitable technologies and selection of most promising technology-To perform numerical simulations and analysis to support design and testing-To design, manufacture and test a prototype-To perform a coupling test with representative thruster (TBC of test facility and thruster to be provided as agency undertaking) for performance verification-To assess the performance improvement with the new development-To define the development roadmap

tenderTitle: S5 Door seal remplacement
tenderDescription:
The door seals of the EPCU S5 are over 20 years old.
Damage of an interior door seal has a direct impact on the ambient conditions inside the clean room (loss of overpressure). In addition, with a spacecraft inside a clean room, the loss of an exterior door seal, would no longer allow us to ensure the security of the room or dock the CCU3 for a transfer.
We have to change 4 exterior door seals first, and then the 6 interior door of the EPCU S5.

tenderTitle: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : Electronics, Electrotechnology, RF 2
tenderDescription:
Dear Sir/Madam,
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:

The "Electronic, Electrotechnology, RF, Sensors" activity is part of the operational and/or permanent functional tasks of the CNES/CSG.

The chosen Contractor will provide the CNES/CSG with maintenance (preventive, corrective and ongoing) and operational services within the scope of the following resources:

•	5 tracking RADARS installed in Kourou and St Jean du Maroni,
•	2 weather radars as well as meteorological parameter measurement facilities (weather stations, field mills, radiosonde stations) installed in Kourou,
•	2 remote launcher neutralisation stations including antennas - TSAR station (a directional antenna and omnidirectional antennas), one installed at the CSG and the other transportable and installed in St Jean du Maroni,
•	4 launcher tracking stations including one in French Guiana at the CSG (with 2 antennas/tracking systems/TeleMetryMT receiving systems); one in St Jean du Maroni or St Georges de l'Oyapock in French Guiana (with 1 antenna/tracking system/TeleMetryMT receiving system - transportable); one in Libreville, Gabon (with 1 antenna/tracking system/TeleMetryMT receiving system); and one in Bermuda (with one antenna/tracking system/MT receiving system),
•	different mobile telemetry equipment (1 transportable and naval station stored in metropolitan France, 1 transportable antenna with its tracking system stored in Kourou, telemetry receiving kits, transportable and installed in foreign stations upon request)
•	satellite tracking stations installed in French Guiana and in Libreville,
The chosen contractor will provide technical office support to the CNES/CSG covering the entire scope of the contract, including in addition to the resources already mentioned, the Ascension (Atlantic), Natal (Brazil), Malindi (Kenya), St Hubert or Gatineau (Canada), New Norcia (Australia) and Santa Maria (Azores) tracking stations.
Within this framework, the contractor will be responsible for calibrating measuring devices at the sites at which their teams will be located.
The chosen contractor will provide level 1 technical support to the CNES/CSG on EGNOS navigation aid equipment installed in Kourou.
The chosen Contractor will provide the CNES/CSG with maintenance (preventive, corrective and ongoing) services for detection equipments and altitude and surface measurement systems. The chosen Contractor will provide obsolescence management to the CNES/CSG but also ensure a technology watch for these systems.
The chosen Contractor will also provide the CNES/CSG with technical and operational services (daily functional checks, weather forecasts, climatology, data extraction and analysis) using the measurement systems mentioned previously as well as data processing, archiving and diffusion systems. The chosen Contractor will be responsible for operating the radiosounding system.

PS: The current Launch Range industrial landscape managed by the CNES/CSG can be found at: https://centrespatialguyanais.cnes.fr/fr/centre-spatial-guyanais/acteurs/partenaires
