tenderTitle: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : Industrial site maintenance
tenderDescription:
Dear Sir/Madam,
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:
"Energy, Air Conditioning and Domain Maintenance" activities are part of a global support mission associated with the operational needs of the CSG and the operational activities of the launch base.

The main geographical areas concerned are the Technical Centre, the EPCUs, the external sites (Montagne des Pères, Montabo, Météo, Îles du Salut, Saint-Georges, Saint-Laurent, Diane, Site Galiléo, etc.), and the major networks (energy, water, roads, etc.).

The chosen Contractor will provide the CNES/CSG with maintenance (preventive, corrective and ongoing) and operational and engineering services within the scope of the following resources:

•	Energy: HV/LV (CAT1) facilities and grids, 70 backup power generators (CAT2), 60 backup UPS (CAT3), lights, lifts, lightning protection, etc.
•	Air conditioning: 17 cold/hot production plants, hydraulic and air distribution networks, 1600 items of interior equipment (air processing units, ventilators-convectors, etc.), 500 electrical/control cabinets, splits/windows, etc.
•	Domain maintenance: 150 buildings (structures, facades, roofs, etc.), 300 km of road (roads, runways, car parks, signage, etc.), the entire city water system (80 km) and wastewater treatment facilities, etc.
•	Administration and use of remote management data, as well as management of remote management interface architectures with technical production facilities.

tenderTitle: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : Safety " Environment, Ground safety, Workplace safety"
tenderDescription:
Dear Sir/Madam,
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:

1) Activity Environment and Ground Safety
The "Security systems, Environment, Ground safety, Workplace safety" activity forms part of the operational and/or permanent functional tasks of the CNES/CSG.
The Contractor's mission is carried out mainly in the CNES facilities at the CSG.
The mission consists of providing services intended to ensure the protection of people, property and the environment, in the frame of the overall mission of protection of people, property and the environment of CNES / CSG relating to ground activities.
The main technical skills required are the following ones :
•	Risk analysis of complex systems : pyrotechnic systems, solid and liquid propellant systems, mechanic / electric systems…
•	Risk analysis of hazardous activities : propellant tank filling and pressurization, handling payloads/launcher stages, dangerous goods / payload / launcher transportation…
•	Labor and environmental regulations, CSG rules and regulations

2) Activity workplace safety : 
The incumbent entity will be able to carry out on site health and safety of work activities on site. The regulatory security controls will be carried out by an incumbent entity that has been approved by the Minister of labour or equivalent commissioned entity of the French Authority. It will have an expert knowledge of French regulations.
They will advise the customer in particular on the use of means and facilities.
The Contract holder will be able to carry out certain health and safety of work activities on site, upon expert reports related to Health Safety Working Conditions.
The Contract holder will lead Safety awareness sessions (in French/English) particularly for hoisting devices and for mini gas supply networks.

The successful Contractor(s) will provide these services for CNES/CSG in the following technical scope: 
 
Logistics and transport systems maintenance (including specific equipment for transporting payloads, corresponding handling equipment, and administrative and regulatory aspects); 
Centralized management of the General Warehouse and Reception, packaging, packing, internal CSG and inter-site delivery, handling, dispatch of conventional and secured freight (chargeur connu); 
Transports and logistics activities for running the launch base and satellite campaigns (specific tools, shared equipment and propellants, payloads and associated tools transports from airport or harbour to CSG). 
Management of "Base" furniture (as opposed to "Non-Base" furniture) and Procurement, removal, installation, coordination, management of handling operations; 
Reception, distribution of mail letter and small handling operations on the CSG; 
Preparation, realization and management of customs transit files on site in relation with the CNES forwarding companies (excluding the operational activities of the Transport and RETT assistants); 
Handling of all types of materials and equipment... 
Coordination of the public transport companies contracted by the CNES for the Launch Base Employee. 
Coordination/management of shuttles to and from Félix-Eboué airport for guests, schoolchildren and VIPs during one-off CNES/CSG visits (interfaces with coach transporters, etc.) and daily visits for the general public; 
Coordination/management of CNES VIP direct transport and the provision and cleaning of cars. 
Coordination of daily management of the Diesel supply for the Launch Base with the Petroleum Company contracted by the CNES. 
 
The NATIONAL and INTERNATIONAL TRANSIT services cover operations related to the general functioning of CNES/CSG and to launches and are carried out within the framework of the missions of the Launch Base. CNES/CSG entrusts the contractor (s) with the mission of organising and executing, or having executed, customs and multimodal transport operations in import and export between the various storage locations on the CNES/CSG site and the rest of the world (controlled and reactive transit network) via the maritime (Dégrad des Cannes, Pariacabo harbors in Kourou) and airport (Cayenne - Félix Éboué Airport) entry points in French Guiana. The contractor (s) shall carry out all import and export customs formalities at the place of departure or destination as indirect Representative of CNES/CSG for customs clearance operations by receiving its instructions from the CNES/CSG TRANSIT office and shall ensure the advance of funds linked to the fees and taxes on goods. In French Guiana, the contractor shall draw up monthly global declarations (DCG) integrating the calculation of duties, taxes and fees to be paid to the customs. It takes all steps with the competent authorities (port and airport authorities, DGTM, Prefecture, Gendarmerie, customs, etc.) to obtain the necessary authorisations for operations on public or private roads. As the CNES/CSG has the "Chargeur Connu" approval, the Contractor must hold the status of Authorised Agent in French Guiana, Toulouse and the Paris airports" and must be authorised by the DGAC as an Authorised Agent for "Cargo Security". All types of miscellaneous or general cargo must be able to be transported individually or in groups; dangerous goods of different classes imported or exported in residual proportions or not by qualified, trained and authorised personnel.

tenderTitle: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : " Operations Planning and Coordination"
tenderDescription:
Dear Sir/Madam,

The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:

The Operations Planning and Coordination activity is a permanent task which plays a central role in the functioning of the CNES/CSG.
This task, through the Operations Coordination Office (also referred to as BCO), manages the joint activities carried out on the Launch Site. It enables planning of all the activities on the Site and in particular harmonisation of the maintenance activities (MCO: Maintenance in Operational Condition of the technical systems) with the operational activities relating to launch campaigns.

The activities to be planned and coordinated concern all the sites under the responsibility of the CNES, the EPCUs (acronym referring to the Payload Preparation Facilities), the technical centre and the remote operational resources. The planning process also sets the pace for the maintenance or upgrading of "major networks" (eg. NRJ, CLIM, Water).
The planning of activities for which CNES/CSG is responsible must be harmonised and optimised, taking into account the activities of other industrial operators on the Base.
In order to carry out its tasks, the Contractor is required to use the PLANISWARE planning software provided by CNES.
The planning system is interfaced with the office resources via communication networks, allowing users to make planning requests for their activities. 
The technical management and system administration of the PLANISWARE software are not the responsibility of the contractor responsible for the Operations Planning and Coordination activity. They are provided on behalf of the CNES/CSG by the provider responsible for the corporate IT activity.

PS: The current Launch Range industrial landscape managed by the CNES/CSG can be found at: 
https://centrespatialguyanais.cnes.fr/fr/centre-spatial-guyanais/acteurs/partenaires

tenderTitle: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : "Engineering Services (also referred to as BET)"
tenderDescription:
Dear Sir/Madam,

The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:
:
The on-site Engineering Services activity (“Bureau d’Etudes” in French also referred to as BET) is one of the permanent operational activities of CNES at the Guiana Space Centre. 
It is responsible for global engineering support of the technical and operational activities of the launch base, linked to the operational needs of the CSG.

1.	Engineering Services task consisting in preparing the technical files necessary for upgrades to the technical installations entrusted to it;
2.	project management for the performance and coordination of the work necessary for the implementation and qualification of upgrades;
3.	topographical surveying and dimensional metrology;
4.	management, updating (internal and external) and dissemination on request of the plans of the installations configuration-managed by the CNES/CSG;
5.	archiving and making available on request the industrial files of projects whose operation is outsourced by the CNES
Note 1: the work carried out within the framework of the above-mentioned services concerns the following technical specialities: energy (high and low voltage and lightning), mechanical engineering, fluids, infrastructure, air-conditioning (including the controllers and/or PLCs of the corresponding systems).
Note 2: Engineering Services is the entry (delivery) point for descriptive technical documentation coming into the CSG (industrial plans and files).
The Contractor must have the necessary skills to integrate new projects in the form of a digital model (BIM/SIG design) and to move towards using this database as a digital repository for configuration management.

tenderDescription:

tenderTitle: VERIFICATION OF SMALL SATELLITE FITNESS FOR PURPOSE IN NEW APPLICATION DOMAINS - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Private investment has stimulated the development of several new small satellite systems within Europe over the last five years. These exploit the reduced technical risk associated with technologies coming from previous ESA and Member State funded developments and benefiting from parallel technology improvements (eg miniaturization, materials etc) so that standard commercial practices can be followed.However, in many cases the privately financed and operated satellites include technical characteristics that create the potential for exploitation in other user domains where there is less acceptance of EO or where technical effort would be required to develop and verify the required information products and services. This may be due to the fact that the sensors are in some way unique or that the the overall system offers unique performance capabilities. Addressing this asymmetric risk structure is routinely practiced within ESA programmes however and given the connections ESA has with a wide range of stakeholders and the experience in supporting diverse EO applications development, ESA is well placed to fund the required developments up to the point where fitness for purpose is demonstrated for a well defined and clearly engaged stakeholder community which can then be the basis for private sector funded follow-on developments and customer engagement. This Invitation to Tender addresses this gap in order to generate an acceptable risk pattern for private sector investors (and the satellite operators) to support the necessary operationalization and commercialization activities. The overall objectives to be achieved are:(i) Accelerate the update of data, information and services from European small satellite operators among customer segments that cannot be effectively addressed by such private sector entities alone(ii) Verify, together with key organizations within the target customer segments, that data, information and services from the small satellite operators address an agreed set of priority issues/gaps and the demonstrated operational performance and processes are consistent with customer segment working practices and are therefore considered to be fit for purposeThis will require the contractor to engage a clear set of customers with requirements that cannot be presently addressed but which could be addressed by modifications to or with a small satellite system currently in operationIdentify a clear set of developments associated with the small satellite system in order to address the requirements of the stakeholders being targeted on a timeframe that is of immediate interest to the target stakeholdersElaborate verification exercises that enable a sufficiently convincing demonstration and verificationthat the developments executed have resulted in the enhanced small satellite system being capable to provide the required information under actual operational conditions to a performance level that is considered acceptable and within working practices that are compliant with the stakeholders operational environment. This should include a clear definition as to what are these threshold performance levels as well as a credible prospect of follow-on commercial uptake if these agreed performance levels are sufficiently well achievedIdentify follow-on mechanisms that can credibly support a transition to full commercial uptake

tenderTitle: KICK-START THEMATIC CALL: WATER AS FOOD RESOURCE
tenderDescription: The objective of this Kick Start is to analyse the technical and economic feasibility of new services and solutions for production of food from oceans and inland water bodies. Water as Food Resource studies aim to address the need to increase global food volumes taking into account sustainability and safety concerns. The call addresses four key focus areas. The fishing in remote locations focus area investigates solutions for remote fish farms or shrimp vessels. Precision fishing includes solutions to monitor the environment and manage the infrastructure of fish and shellfish farms. The third area is focused on the production of algae for consumption with positive externalities, such as carbon capture. The last area aims to mitigate illegal practices and increase transparency of current and new fishing activities. The services/solutions put forward should use space assets, such as one or more of Earth observation, Satellite Communication, Satellite Navigation, and Satellite AIS.

tenderTitle: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : “Support for preparing payloads”
tenderDescription:
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months: Customer Service is part of a global assignment to support the technical and operational activities of the launch base in order to guarantee their successful conclusion. This support mainly includes:

the technical and operational activities of the Payload Preparation Complex (EPCU) to be carried out in order to manage and coordinate operations and to configure resources that will be used to support teams that are preparing and conducting satellite campaigns.

 

The management systems and resources are:

 

Mechanical systems (for lifting, handling, access to buildings, etc.)

Operational and technical premises (clean rooms, air-conditioned storage areas, offices and control room for the customer teams, utility rooms, etc.) •

power supply management and distribution systems in the EPCUs.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) management systems and specific equipment for certain rooms and operational activities (fuelling personnel PPE, clean room clothing, filtered-air hoses, etc.)

Monitoring and supervision systems for critical EPCU systems

Fluid systems: production and implementation (air, mini network, etc.) (air production, mini network, etc.)

Liquid and gaseous effluent management systems (flushing columns, effluent treatment and associated monitoring facilities)

Physical expert appraisal systems and devices (particle counting, thermometry, hygrometry, accelerometry, etc.) • chemical analysis systems and devices (gas detection)

 

The management of preventive and corrective maintenance as well as the monitoring and management of technical and operational launch base upgrades for the following facilities and activities:

 

All the systems and activities involved in operating and managing the EPCUs.

The resources for managing PPE and specific protective equipment related to operational activities for all base activities.

Specific transport and logistics activities organization for running the satellite campaigns with the support of CNES transports subcontractor.

The fleet of first-aid, fire-fighting and pollution control vehicles.

The activities of the chemical analysis laboratory (cleanness of operational rooms and analysis equipment).

The activities of the physical expert appraisal laboratory (electromagnetism, radiofrequency, accelerometry, test benches and test equipment, etc.).

These activities are carried out in a demanding operational context in terms of both security/safety and working hours.

tenderTitle: KICK-START THEMATIC CALL SPACE AND EDGE INTELLIGENCE
tenderDescription: The objective of this Kick Start is to analyse the technical and economic feasibility of new services and solutions leveraging the inherent advantages of Edge Intelligence. Edge Intelligence refers to a paradigm shift in computing in which certain data analysis processes are moved from centralised cloud or in-house data centers to the "edge" of the network. In such solutions, certain aspects of the analysis of the data and derivation and communication of insights, takes place at the site where the data is generated. The benefits of this are many and can be exploited in several settings and thematic domains, fitting into a broader distributed computingmodel that enables higher performing systems. The services/solutions put forward should use space assets, such as one or more of Earth observation, Satellite Communication, Satellite Navigation, and Human Spaceflight technologies.

tenderTitle: SAPRESS Project
tenderDescription:
The role of the Guyanese Space Centre (CSG) Flight Safety teams is to ensure the protection of people, property, the environment and public health during a space operation (Launch Operation)

The Sapress project is an IT project which consists in integrating into the GUI a multi-launcher flight safety diagnostic tool currently used by the CSG Flight Safety teams called ‘Sedia Calisa generic’, and in executing some simple treatments. 
This tool is based on a CNES model, built on Sedia Calisa Ariane 5 code.
The overall objective is to have a flexible and configurable tool that is easily configurable according to the launcher’s architecture and dimensioning scenarios.
The first version will be qualified and tested for the new Ariane 6 launcher.
The content of the interfaces must be consistent overall with the other current tools used by the CSG (mainly the SCTV (Coordination, Processing and Visualization System)).

Les équipes Sauvegarde Vol du Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG) ont pour rôle de s’assurer de la Protection des personnes, des biens, de l’environnement et de la santé publique lors d’une opération spatiale (Opération de lancement)

Le projet Sapress (Structure d'Accueil pour la Préparation des Soumissions Sauvegarde) est un projet informatique qui consiste globalement à intégrer en IHM un outil de réalisation de diagnostic sauvegarde vol multi-lanceurs utilisé actuellement par les équipes Sauvegarde Vol du CSG Sedia Calisa Générique et à réaliser quelques traitements simples. 
Cet outil est basé sur une maquette CNES, construite sur du code Sedia Calisa Ariane 5.
L’objectif global est de disposer d’un outil flexible et configurable facilement en fonction de l’architecture du lanceur et des scénarii dimensionnants.
La première version sera qualifiée et testée pour le nouveau lanceur Ariane 6.
Le contenu des interfaces devra globalement être cohérent des autres outils actuels utilisés par le CSG (principalement le SCTV (Système de Coordination, Traitement et Visualisation)

tenderTitle: I-HAB Quick disconnects (for  IATCS EATCS and ECLSS)
tenderDescription:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025.
 The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada.
 The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration.
 The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly.
 It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Quick Disconnects for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Quick Disconnects are part of the Active Thermal Control System (ATCS) and of the Environmental and Life Support System (ECLSS) belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
 Quick Disconnects will be part of both internal and external ATCS loops and are also foreseen in circuits belonging to some ECLSS functions.
The Quick Disconnects shall provide a quick and easy way of connecting and disconnecting fluid system components to perform scheduled and nonscheduled maintenance, and to facilitate fluid system reconfiguration, avoiding loss of fluid.
 Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

tenderTitle: SPACE FOR RESILIENT UTILITIES (ARTES 4.0 4S SPL)
tenderDescription: The utilities sector, including water, sewage, and energy networks amongst other, is considered a critical infrastructure, meaning that the loss, or interruption of them would result in a significant impact of the functioning of the state and/or significant economic and social impacts. These networks, as well as their associated equipment and personnel are increasingly monitored and controlled by communication technologies. While this digitalisation is highly effective in optimising systems performance and management, it also increases the threat and vulnerability surface to deliberate and intentional (cyber) attacks and unintentional and external hazards and its dependability on the availability of terrestrial networks. Satellite communications are in a unique position to not only offer safe and secure communication links to increase the network resilience (either as a primary link or as redundant system) but also extend the digitalisation of networks to remote areas. The objective of this call is to foster the development and showcase of innovative applications which embed satellite communications into the management of utilities networks, infrastructure, or personnel to enhance their safety and security. Tenderers are invited to propose Demonstration Projects in collaboration with users and stakeholders from the utilities sector.

tenderTitle: OPEN COMPETITION covering the procurement of the CRISTAL Instrument RF SS EGSE
tenderDescription:
The Copernicus programme is an evolution of the previous Global Monitoring for Environment and Security (GMES) Programme, an Earth monitoring initiative led by the European Union (EU) and carried out in partnership with the EU Member States and the European Space Agency (ESA) established to fulfil the growing need amongst European policy-makers to access accurate and timely information services to manage the environment, understand and mitigate the effects of climate change and ensure civil security.
ESA has awarded six contracts covering the implementation of the Phase B2,C/D,E1 for each of the six new Copernicus missions, encompassing the procurement of both the prototype (instrument(s) and spacecraft), funded by the ESA Member States under the CSC-4 Programme, and the recurrent satellites, funded by the EU under the future MFF 2021-2027, where the recurrent satellites are offered at the same time as the prototype and are implemented as contractual options in a single contract. 
One of these missions is the Copernicus Polar Ice and Snow Topography Altimeter Mission , hereinafter referred to as well as CRISTAL. The objective of the CRISTAL Mission, is to provide enhanced retrieval of sea ice thickness and freeboard, land ice sheet/glacier elevation and ocean surface elevation, wave-height and wind speed by measurements implementing improvement in spatial resolution and performance. The primary high-level objectives are to monitor critical climate signals including: variability of Arctic and Southern Ocean sea-ice and its snow loading, as well as ice sheet, ice cap melting and sea level. Other objectives are to support applications related to coastal and inland waters and contribute to the observation of ocean topography.
In that frame, TAS-F was awarded an Airbus Defense and Space contract for the Interferometric Radar altimeter for Ice & Snow (IRIS). TAS-F is responsible for procuring the CRISTAL RF Sub-system EGSE, using the ESA Best Practices (BP) procedures (ESA/IPC(2012)65,rev.2).
TAS will release an Invitation To Tender (ITT) for the procurement of the Ku band and Ka band front-end of the COPERNICUS Polar Ice and Snow Topography Altimeter instrument of the CRISTAL mission. The Ku band and Ka band front-end will be integrated in the CRISTAL EGSE. The Ku band and Ka band front-end are parts of the RF s/s module which interface between the Altimeter and the digital s/s
This procurement will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65,rev.2) as modified for the purpose of the Copernicus programme.

This procurement will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65,rev.2) as modified for the purpose of the Copernicus programme.

tenderTitle: SPACE-BASED SERVICES FOR WATER SCARCITY - KS
tenderDescription: Water is one of the most important substances on Earth and covers 70% of the planet. However, every year competition for a clean, copious supply of water intensifies. Fresh water is threatened by a myriad of forces including overdevelopment, polluted runoff and global warming. Space applications can help to alleviate water scarcity problems in numerous ways. The "Water Scarcity" Kick Start offers 75% funding of up to 60,000 EUR for teams to explore the technical and commercial feasibility of a new service tackling issues related to water scarcity. Proposed services can address one of the following topics: planning and monitoring desalination plants, addressing groundwater depletion, digitising the water and wastewater industry, reducing water loss during distribution, improving water harvesting, optimising purification applications, and supporting new farming techniques that use less water. The services put forward must use at least one type of space asset, such as Earth observation, Satellite Communication, or Satellite Navigation technology.

tenderTitle: LSTM Instrument OGSE for AOB EM-PFM / POB PFM test (AOB-POB-OGSE)
tenderDescription:
The Copernicus programme is an evolution of the previous Global Monitoring for Environment and Security (GMES) Programme, an Earth monitoring initiative led by the European Union (EU) and carried out in partnership with the EU Member States and the European Space Agency (ESA) established to fulfil the growing need amongst European policy-makers to access accurate and timely information services to better manage the environment, understand and mitigate the effects of climate change and ensure civil security. 
While the deployment of the first generation of Sentinels is approaching its completion, the intense use and increased awareness for the potential of Copernicus have generated great expectations for an evolved Copernicus system (“CSC Expansion”). Emerging and urgent needs for new types of observations have been consolidated in a distinct set of requirements which are addressed by six new Copernicus Sentinel missions, formerly known as “High Priority Candidate Missions” (HPCM), one of which being the Copernicus High Spatio-Temporal Resolution Land Surface Temperature Monitoring Mission, hereinafter referred to as well as LSTM Mission.
ESA has awarded six contracts covering the implementation of the Phase B2, C/D,E1 for each of the six Copernicus missions, encompassing the procurement of both the prototype (instrument(s) and spacecraft), funded by the ESA Member States under the CSC-4 Programme, and the recurrent satellites, funded by the EU under the future MFF 2021-2027, where the recurrent satellites are offered at the same time as the prototype and are implemented as contractual options in a single contract.
LSTM Mission contract was awarded to Airbus Defence and Space SAU (ES), as prime contractor, for the procurement of the LSTM satellites including LSTM instrument procured by Airbus Defence and Space SAS (FR).
The main objective of the LSTM Mission is complement the existing family of Copernicus satellites observation capabilities with high spatio-temporal resolution Thermal Infrared observations over land and coastal regions in support of agriculture management services, and a range of additional services. The LSTM primary objective is to provide timely and accurate monitoring of land and coastal areas in the spectral range of TIR, SWIR and VNIR. These measurements will allow determination of evapotranspiration at spatial scales enabling the range of innovative agricultural applications capturing the field scale variability required for irrigation, crop growth modelling and reporting on crop water productivity.
In this framework, Airbus Defence and Space SAS, instrument prime contractor, will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the instrument Optical Ground Support Equipment’s (OGSE) for AOB/POB FPA testing called AOB-POB OGSE.
This OGSE will be used to verify and test the LSTM sub-assemblies during the AIT phases of the project. In particular the AOB/POB (VNIR and SWIR focal planes assemblies) emulates the LTSM flight telescope, from the optical point of view, for the on-ground test of LSTM focal plane units (AOB&POB). It operates in the 400nm to 1700nm spectral range. It shall be noted that the telescope presents strong optical aberrations: one specific goal of the OGSE is to mimic these aberrations with the requested accuracy to be able to perform MTF measurements, coregistration, spectral measurements and straylight measurements on AOB-POB FPAs.
The procurement of the LSTM OGSE’s will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65,rev.2).

tenderTitle: CHIME Instrument WiRAL Fiber Mixing (Spectrometer Illumination) (OGSE)
tenderDescription: The Copernicus programme is an evolution of the previous Global Monitoring for Environment and Security (GMES) Programme, an Earth monitoring initiative led by the European Union (EU) and carried out in partnership with the EU Member States and the European Space Agency (ESA) established to fulfil the growing need amongst European policy-makers to access accurate and timely information services to manage the environment, understand and mitigate the effects of climate change and ensure civil security. ESA has awarded six contracts covering the implementation of the Phase B2,C/D,E1 for each of the six new Copernicus missions, encompassing the procurement of both the prototype (instrument(s) and spacecraft), funded by the ESA Member States under the CSC-4 Programme, and the recurrent satellites, funded by the EU under the future MFF 2021-2027, where the recurrent satellites are offered at the same time as the prototype and are implemented as contractual options in a single contract. One of these missions is the Copernicus Hyperspectral Imaging Mission For the Environment, hereinafter referred to as well as CHIME. CHIME Mission contract was awarded to Thales Alenia Space France (FR), as prime contractor, for the procurement of the CHIME satellites including CHIME instrument under OHB (DE). The main objective of the CHIME Mission is to complement Sentinel observations with an imaging spectroscopy observational capability for services supporting the improved management of natural resources and related policies. The mission will provide routine hyperspectral observations through the Copernicus Programme in support of EU- and related policies for the management of natural resources. This unique visible-to-shortwave infrared spectroscopy based capability will be dedicated to raw material and sustainable agricultural management with a focus on soil properties, mineral resources and agricultural services, including food security and biodiversity. To enable accurate quantitative estimates of specific vegetation bio/geo-physical/chemical variables, as well as top-soil variables and mineral compositions CHIME encompasses as payload an imaging spectrometer. This imaging spectrometer allows monitoring of land and coastal/inland water bodies with contiguous spectral channels covering the spectral range from the VIS to the SWIR. In this framework, OHB, as instrument prime contractor, will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the instrument Optical Ground Support Equipment (OGSE). The Wide Illumination Range Subsystem - WiRAL will be part of the OGSE assembly for alignment and alignment verification of the Chime instrument detectors to the respective spectrometer during the AIT phases of the project. This encompasses a bread board model as well as several flight models. The main unit will be placed in ISO8 environment and will be used as light source for another OGSE (called SpecSID). The light generated by the WiRAL will be guided by optical fibers to the further OGSE in ISO5 environment. Additionally, it will provide a software environment for command, monitoring and data logging. The software will allow commands in a local and a remote mode. The WiRAL will feature the following main building blocks: main unit (light generation, fibers and metrology), control unit and calibration system. The present ITT will be addressed to economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose registered office is established in the countries defined herewith. This procurement will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65,rev.2) as modified for the purpose of the Copernicus programme.

tenderTitle: MSR-ERO – Second Batch of Mechanical Ground Support Equipment (MGSE Batch 1)
tenderDescription:
The Mars Sample Return – Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement action is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO MGSE Batch 2 to be used for the Spacecraft integration and test activities, in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
In detail the hardware subject of this procurement selection will be:
•	The RM Avionics Module Integration Rig (ARIG) is a stand used to support a subassembly of the ERO Return Module structure (consisting of a C-shaped composition of three structural panels) and capable of rotating the test article 360o about the horizontal axis such that each of the panela can be set horizontal when needed by the activities to be performed.

tenderTitle: Système d'acquisition des Mâts Météo
tenderDescription:
This project aims to renew the current weather masts system of the Guiana Space Center (CSG). The weather masts system contains wind (direction, speed) and temperature sensors at specific levels on weather masts (typical mast height: 60 meters) all over the space center. A digital system is in charge of collecting data measurements from each weather mast to a central processing system at the weather station site. The project perimeter contains renewal of wind and temperature sensors as well as associated mechanical mast interfaces, local data concentrators on each mast site and the centralized processing system at the weather station site. 

Ce projet concerne le renouvellement du système d’acquisition des Mâts Météo du Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG). Le nouveau système comprend des capteurs d’acquisition du Vent (force et direction) et de la température à différents niveaux du sol à partir de plusieurs mâts (hauteur typique 60 mètres) répartis sur l’ensemble de la base. Un système numérique permet la collecte des acquisitions sur les différents mâts et leur centralisation pour traitement à la station Météo du CSG. Le périmètre du projet concerne le renouvellement des capteurs d’acquisition comprenant les interfaces mécaniques avec les mâts, les centrales associées en pied de mât et le système de traitement centralisé situé à la station Météo.

tenderTitle: MSR-SFR - Procurement of Central Checkout System (CCS)
tenderDescription:
The Mars Sample Return Campaign is a response to the long-running scientific objective to better understand Mars. By acquiring and returning to Earth a rigorously documented set of Mars samples, scientists will have access to the full breadth and depth of analytical science instruments available in terrestrial laboratories. The investigations will be free of the mass, volume, and power constraints that limit in-situ instruments. The resulting investigations of these returned samples will enable breakthrough advances in:
•the search for ancient and/or extant life on Mars;
•understanding the origin and evolution of Mars as a geological system;
•understanding the processes and history of climate on Mars;
•preparing for human exploration.

The MSR architecture involves a total of five campaign elements: four flight elements and one ground
element. Each campaign element consists of one or more functional elements. The four flight elements are:
•a caching rover mission, developed by NASA-JPL (Mars 2020 project), currently operating on Mars,
•a first Sample Retrieval Lander (SRL-1) mission, consisting of a NASA/JPL developed lander with a
Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV) as well as ESA provided Sample Transfer Arm (STA)
•a second Sample Retrieval Lander (SRL-2) mission, carrying a Sample Fetch Rover (SFR),
•and an ESA provided Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) mission.

The Sample Fetch Rover will be launched on-board a Sample Return Lander in 2028 and arriving on Mars surface in mid-2030. Following a successful landing, the rover will deploy and egress from the platform and traverse to the depot in which the Mars2020 rover will have stored the sample tubes containing soil and rock samples. With the capability for autonomous and fast surface mobility, the Sample Fetch Rover will traverse to the depot, collect and store on board the individual sample tubes, and safely transport them back to the Sample Return Lander. 

Airbus Defence and Space Ltd will be acting as Prime Contractor to the European Space Agency to perform the MSR-SFR Phase B2CDE1, together with its subcontractors. 

As part of this Contract (currently in Phase B2), Airbus Defence and Space Ltd will release an Invitation to Tender (ITT) looking for a Supplier of the Central Checkout System.

The scope of work of the Contractor includes the provision of the test and verification computers to the SFR Vehicle programme including the design, the development, qualification, production and verification of the systems and providing support to the programme during setup, commissioning and subsequent use of the systems. The CCS Contract includes the following computers and systems:
•	Servers hosting the Virtual Machines that will be used for the Numerical Software Validation Facilities (NSVF)
•	Guidance Navigation and Control (GNC) machines
•	Functional Validation Bench (FVB) machines 
•	Test Bench Central Check out Systems
•	Flight Rover Central Check out System
•	Central Check out System Laptops
The NSVF, GNC and FVB machines support the development and verification of the on-board software and Guidance Navigational Control system. The NSVF also supports FV and AIT test debugging and functional validation. The Central Check out System forms the central hub of the SFR Vehicle test environments, from which the majority of the on-board equipment and software testing is performed. 
The Central Check out System application will be based on the Airbus Open Center (OC) software product, hosted on several Linux servers and workstations. The OC software will be installed by Airbus Defence and Space post-delivery and acceptance of the computer hardware.

tenderTitle: IAP.KS.CE KICKSTART CIRCULAR ECONOMY
tenderDescription: Most organisations today operate in a linear way; this model functions as though there are infinite resources and generates waste. A circular economy, on the other hand, treats resources as though they are finite and is based on a 'make, use and return' model. Each resource is used in a way that maximises value to the economy and minimises damage to the environment. This Circular Economy' Kick Start offers 75% funding of up to 60,000 EUR for teams to explore the technical and commercial feasibility of a new service for the circular economy. Proposed services can address one of the following topics: circular food and drinks, circular fashion and textiles, circular urban life, or circular waste systems. The services put forward must use at least one type of space asset, such as Earth observation, Satellite Communication, or Satellite Navigation technology. The Kick Start is divided into four parts, each with its own deadline.

tenderTitle: Museum - Work Package 9 - AudioVisual and MultiMedia
tenderDescription:
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:

Context:
The CNES wishes to renovate the Space Museum in Kourou, French Guiana, to make it a space adapted to the expectations of its target public. This renovation encompasses all the interior spaces (permanent exhibition, reception area, shop), as well as the building’s cladding and the addition of exterior facilities.
Reflection on the renovation of the Space Museum is part of the strategy to promote in French Guiana the image of space and of the Guiana Space Centre (CSG), Europe’s Spaceport.
The design of the project is global and focuses on attractiveness in order to enhance the visit experience for all visitors: families, school groups, customers, institutions, employees, service providers, and others.
In addition, the project is part of a broader context, in particular associated with:
-	The modernisation of the image of the Guiana Space Centre (CSG),
-	The improvement of a global tourism offer of the CSG and the expectations regarding the welcoming of visitors,
-	A strong demand for information about the CSG and space activity in French Guiana.
Purpose of the contract:
This information concerns the contracts for works related to museum displays, scenography and graphic aspects.
The work for the CNES/CSG, at the site of the Space Museum at the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou (French Guiana), falls within a demanding operational context (project integrating an architectural and a scenographic component, CSG environment, location), which the contractor will need to take into account in their bid.
Please note that the renovation project is also the subject of a BIM-GEM (Building Information Modelling - Management-Operation-Maintenance) strategy from the design stage through to the use of the structure.
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months. These activities are part of the renovation of the Space Museum.

Work to be carried out will include:
-	AV/MM design, production: design, production, development (in French and English), integration, adjustments and on-site testing (correct operation check as well as “VBF” in French, regular operational testing as well as “VSR” in French) of audiovisual and multimedia devices;
-	Supply and installation of AV/MM equipment: technical studies, supply, preparation, programming, integration (in-workshop and on-site), transport, on-site installation, testing and adjustments (correct operation check, regular operational testing) of audiovisual and multimedia equipment

tenderTitle: Iris with IOC - AOC (Airline Operational Communication) Applications for the Electronic Flight Bag
tenderDescription:
The ESA Iris Initial Operational Capability (IOC), in addition to Air Traffic Management (ATM) services, has the ambition to be the vehicle for Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) IP applications, thus facilitating the transition of airlines to the digital age. 

These IP-enabled applications are specific to the Airline Information Services Domain (AISD). The applications are utilised by airline crew on the Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) for flight operations, airline administrative and engine and maintenance purposes.

This Statement of Work (SoW) specifies the integration, end-to-end testing and demonstration of EFB applications in an operational-like environment in the Iris Test Facility. This activity will culminate in a demonstration to ESA in the Iris Test Facility.

tenderTitle: Regional Resource On-boarding to the Network of Resources
tenderDescription:
The scope of this procurement shall support integration of regional resources (inter alia data, algorithms, models) into the Network of Resources (NoR) portfolio and manage the interaction with the regional community. As fragmentation is a major obstacle to efficiently use the “bring the user to the data” approach, regional resources shall be integrated in a partnership approach as much as possible into existing NoR Exploitation Platforms. 

Exploitation Platforms are a central element of ESA's Earth Observation (EO) Innovation Europe concept, which aims at the integration of EO data and information for a much broader use, for scientific, social and economic purposes, as well as for the generation of new commercial applications and services. 

The EO NoR initiative promotes the use of European resource and platform services to facilitate a simplified and efficient exploitation of EO data in cloud environments. The initiative incentivizes providers to contribute to a common framework harmonising the access to their services and helping the user to work with the data. ESA conducted an ITT (AO/1-9217/18/I-LG-Procurement of Earth Observation Exploitation Platform Network Resource Services) in 2018. The tender awarded a contract in December 2018 to Cloudeo AG as prime to select under the supervision of ESA, and via ESA’s Best Practices Processes, the services of eligible Resource and Platform Tier Providers. A NoR portal (https://nor-discover.cloudeo.group) lists in an online directory all the onboarded providers together with their NoR service portfolio. 

ESA can sponsor or co-fund scientists and value adding users for eligible research, development and pre-commercial projects. The portal also provides users with links to each providers helpdesk and website.

tenderTitle: I-HAB BATTERY ELECTRONIC UNIT (BEU)
tenderDescription:
The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Battery Electronic Unit (BEU)in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Battery Electronic Unit (BEU) are part of the power subsystem.
The IHAB Electrical Power Subsystem (IHAB EPS ) includes a set of batteries for energy storage and a set of power management, distribution and switch units that are responsible:
- to control and regulate the battery charging and discharging in sun or during the eclipse phase,
- to control the balancing of all the battery cells during the charging phase
- to connect each battery to the BCDR before the Launch or during the tests and disconnect it before the removal or during the test
- to connect, disconnect and distribute the primary power to other elements of the Gateway when requested.
- to convert the primary power into secondary power to supply the various internal loads and heaters by switchable and protected power lines
From functional point of view the IHAB EPS is composed by two main power chains. Each main power chain (PWR-CHA and PWR-CHB) is supplied by one isolated primary power domain:
- Primary Power Domain A1 & A2 supply the PWR-CHA
- Primary Power Domain B1 & B2 supply the PWR-CHB
All the functional blocks at this level and as part of power chain A or power chain B are indicated respectively as PPDA-A (Primary Power Distribution Assembly ChA) and PPDA-B for ChB.
All the functional blocks of IHAB EPS at Level 2 are indicated respectively as SPCD-A1 and SPCDA2 (Secondary Power Conversion & Distribution – ChA1 and ChA2) and SPCD-1B and SPCD-2B for ChB1 and ChB2. Each primary power domain A & B is constituted by two primary power isolated feeds named A1 & A2 for the domain A, and B1 & B2 for the domain B.
The Battery Electronic Unit (BEU) is designed to maintain equivalent state-of-charge of every cell of two batteries on IHAB, to the degree possible given their different capacities, over the widest possible range of the cells. The individual cells in a battery pack naturally have somewhat different capacities, and so, over the course of charge and discharge cycles, may be at a different state of charge (SOC). Balancing a multi-cell pack helps to maximize capacity and increase each cell’s. 
 
Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

First publication date: 2022-02-02T16:41:35
Description: The Mars Sample Return Programme is a response to the long-running scientific objective to better understand the past history of Mars and characterize its current environment. By acquiring and returning to Earth a rigorously documented set of Mars soil samples, scientists will have the possibility to perform extensive and accurate analyses, having access to the full breadth and depth of scientific instruments available in terrestrial laboratories. The scientific analysis of these returned samples will enable breakthrough advances in: 
• the search for ancient and/or extant life on Mars; 
• the understanding the origin and evolution of Mars as a geological system; 
• the understanding the processes and history of climate on Mars 
• preparing for future human exploration of Mars. The MSR architecture involves four campaign elements: three flight elements and one ground element (Operation Control Centre). Each campaign element consists of one or more functional elements. The three flight elements are: 
• a sample caching rover mission, developed by NASA/JPL, and currently already successfully operating on Mars;
• a Sample Retrieval Lander (SRL) mission, consisting of a NASA/JPL developed lander including a Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV) as well as the ESA provided Sample Transfer Arm (STA) and Sample Fetch Rover (SFR); 
• and the ESA provided Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) mission. SFR is scheduled to be launched on-board the NASA’s Sample Return Lander. Following a successful landing, the rover will deploy and egress from the platform and traverse to the depot in which the Mars2020 rover will have stored the sample tubes containing soil and rock samples. Leonardo S.p.A acting as Lead Contractor for the Arm and Gripper Subsystem (AGS), under contract with the MSR-SFR Prime Contractor Airbus Defense and Space Ltd to the European Space Agency. As part of this contract (Phase B2 ATP), Leonardo will release an Invitation to Tender (ITT) looking for a supplier of the EGSE for Arm and Gripper Subsystem.
The EGSE will include motor drivers, heater drivers and sensor acquisition drivers, in order to control all the AGS units, i.e. all 6 joints, Gripper, HDRMs, RRB, at the same time.
It also includes all cables from EGSE to the AGS electrical interfaces. The SW will be developed by Leonardo.

tenderTitle: I-HAB PORTABLE EQUIPMENT PANELS (PEPs)
tenderDescription: The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Portable Equipment Panels (PEPs) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.The PEPs are part of the power subsystem that includes a set of batteries for energy storage and a set of power management, distribution and switch units that are responsible to control and regulate the battery charging and discharging in sun or during the eclipse phase; to control the balancing of all the battery cells during the charging phase; to connect each battery to the BCDR before the Launch or during the tests and disconnect it before the removal or during the test; to connect, disconnect and distribute the primary power to other elements of the Gateway when requested; to convert the primary power into secondary power to supply the various internal loads and heaters by switchable and protected power lines.From functional point of view the IHAB EPS is composed by two main power chains. Each main power chain (PWR-CHA and PWR-CHB) is supplied by one isolated primary power domain: Primary Power Domain A1 & A2 supply the PWR-CHA; Primary Power Domain B1 & B2 supply the PWR-CHB.All the functional blocks at this level and as part of power chain A or power chain B are indicated respectively as PPDA-A (Primary Power Distribution Assembly ChA) and PPDA-B for ChB.All the functional blocks of IHAB EPS at Level 2 are indicated respectively as SPCD-A1 and SPCDA2 (Secondary Power Conversion & Distribution – ChA1 and ChA2) and SPCD-1B and SPCD-2B for ChB1 and ChB2. Each primary power domain A & B is constituted by two primary power isolated feeds named A1 & A2 for the domain A, and B1 & B2 for the domain B.The PEPs are designed to ensure common standard Gateway power and data interface for portable equipment at various locations for science and crew systems support. The PEPs will have physical, electrical and data interfaces to be accommodate in a single panel and accessible by crew. For this reason each PEP will provide one variable 3-28Vdc voltage output rated at 8 A and one fixed 120Vdc outputs voltage rated at 10 A to portable equipment via two standard power utility outlets accommodated into two identical standard circular connectors named “J1” and “J2” and one auxiliary at 120Vdc output voltage rated at 10 A to power crew support equipment (i.e. USB hubs, USB charger) accommodated into one blind-mate connector named “J3”. The PEP will also provide one data outlet for access to the Gateway Ethernet network (J4) and a set of switches, digital displays, trim resistors and LEDs. This is to provide a visual indication of the status of the power outlets and also to allow a control the power status as well as reset a faulted condition on each power outlets by crew. Each PEP communicate with the C&DH via 133 Mil bus interfaces. This is: to receive commands to control the power outlets (i.e. power ON/OFF and fault condition reset) and for setting the voltage levels of variable power outputs; to distribute periodically the internal HK data and for reporting of anomaly events and protection conditions.Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

The PEP will also provide one data outlet for access to the Gateway Ethernet network (J4) and a set of switches, digital displays, trim resistors and LEDs. This is to provide a visual indication of the status of the power outlets and also to allow a control the power status as well as reset a faulted condition on each power outlets by crew. Each PEP communicate with the C&DH via 133 Mil bus interfaces. This is: to receive commands to control the power outlets (i.e. power ON/OFF and fault condition reset) and for setting the voltage levels of variable power outputs; to distribute periodically the internal HK data and for reporting of anomaly events and protection conditions.Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

tenderTitle: KICK-START THEMATIC CALL ENVIRONMENTAL CRIMES RE-ISSUE TO ALLOW FOLLOW ON SUB-THEMES (PREVIOUSLY OPEN UNDER 1000026743)
tenderDescription: Biodiversity, a combination of the words biological and diversity, is the variety of life found on Earth or in a specific place on Earth. It includes every living thing - from plants and animals, to fungi and microorganisms. Biodiversity is arguably the most complex and vital feature of Earth. It is fundamental to life on Earth because it provides oxygen, food, clean water, fertile soil, medicines, shelter, protection from storms and floods, fibres for clothing, a stable climate, and recreation. Without photosynthesis from plants and phytoplankton in the oceans, there would be no oxygen. Without bees to pollinate there would be no fruits or nuts. Coral reefs and mangrove swamps provide invaluable protection from cyclones and tsunamis. Coastal ecosystems play a major role in scrubbing water of pollutants and producing clean water for drinking and washing . Trees absorb air pollution, improving air quality. Manynew medicines are harvested from nature, like the cancer-fighting fungi growing on the fur of sloths. Wild varieties of domesticated animals and crops are also crucial, coping with drought or salty soils. Biodiversity increases ecosystem stability, making habitats more resilient to environmental perturbations. Overall, it is estimated that the services provided by ecosystems are worth trillions of dollars (double the world's GDP!) Biodiversity loss in Europe alone costs the continent about 3% of its GDP, or 450m a year. The current state of biodiversity is ominous. Human civilisation is driving species to extinction at around 1000 times the naturalrate . The worst mass coral-bleaching event is taking place and affects 38% of the world's reefs , while industrial fishing takes place in more than half of the ocean . Some scientists believe that the sixth mass extinction in geological history has already begun, calling the massive loss of wildlife a "biological annihilation" . Individual species are being obliterated by habitat loss anddegradation, invasive species, the spread of pollution and disease, climate change and the over exploitation of resources. Moreover, while there were less than 1 billion humans on Earth 200 years ago , there will be a predicted 8.6 billion by the year 2030 . Overpopulation and overconsumption will drive the biodiversity crisis as people increasingly expend resources.

tenderTitle: IAP.KS.PT.000 PROPTECH - KICKSTART
tenderDescription: Property Technology, or "PropTech", is a term that encompasses the application of information technology and platform economics to real estate markets. PropTech has proliferated over the last 35 years initially due to the development of mainframe and personal computers, tools such as Lotus and Excel, more comprehensive software solutions for architecting, engineering and construction, and finally the Internet era and online marketplaces. Recent breakthroughs in technologies spanning cloud computing, machine learning, smartphones, and improved connectivity capabilities are spurring further activity in the PropTech space. Aims of PropTech can include reducing overhead, improving transactions, and optimising property management activities. Such technologies relate to digital dashboards, smart home technology, tech-enabled brokerages, residential and commercial lending, virtual viewing for online portals, and analysing and extracting data from documentation and/or imagery.

tenderTitle: ESPRIT HLCS RF Suitcase
tenderDescription:
The European Systems Providing Refuelling, Infrastructure and Tele-communication) (ESPRIT) is one of the ESAs contribution to the Cislunar Gateway. It includes: (1) the HALO Lunar Communication System (HLCS) (2) A stand-alone Refuelling Module (RM) and (3) Fluid transfer connectors (FTC) for HALO and PPE to be integrated and launched with their docking mechanisms that are used for propellant transfer.
The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration.. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the ESPRIT-HLCS RF Suitcase in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The supplier will be in charge of design, manufacturing and test for this EGSE.

Further information concerning the ESPRIT campaign can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

tenderTitle: EO Network of Resources - Best Practices ITT to procure services from resource and platform tier providers
tenderDescription:
Exploitation Platforms are a central element of ESA's Earth Observation (EO) Innovation Europe concept, which aims at the integration of EO data and information for a much broader use, for scientific, social and economic purposes, as well as for the generation of new commercial applications and services. 

The EO Network of Resources (NoR) initiative promotes the use of European resource and platform services to facilitate a simplified and efficient exploitation of EO data in cloud environments. The initiative incentivizes providers to contribute to a common framework harmonising the access to their services and helping the user to work with the data.

ESA conducted an ITT (AO/1-9217/18/I-LG-Procurement of Earth Observation Exploitation Platform Network Resource Services) in 2018. The tender awarded a contract in December 2018 to Cloudeo AG as prime to select under the supervision of ESA, and via ESA’s Best Practices Processes, the services of eligible Resource and Platform Tier Providers.

A NoR portal (https://nor-discover.cloudeo.group) lists in an online directory all the onboarded providers together with their NoR service portfolio. ESA can sponsor or co-fund scientists and value adding users for eligible research, development and pre-commercial projects. The portal also provides users with links to each providers helpdesk and website.

This intended tender is for the selection of Resource Tier and Platform Tier providers using cloud services with collocated Sentinel and non-Sentinel data.

Resource Tier and Platform Tier providers wishing to contribute to the NoR service directory are invited to provide a proposal. The tender process is made as simple as possible for interested service providers to respond to.

tenderDescription: Objectives of the Activity:The objectives of this activity are the following:1)To define at high level two strawman NewSpace-type missions/instruments that could require the use of ground coolers in space:a.One mission based on miniaturized Rotary Stirling Cooler (with or without IDDCA).b.One mission based on linear cooler (Pulse Tube or Stirling Cooler)2)To derive the two corresponding sets of technical requirements applicable to the Cryocooling Systems (including the electronics). 3)To propose, in collaboration with the cooler providers, a cost-effective documentation, PA/QA testing and verification approach that will ensure that theproduct will comply with the set of technical requirements identified before.4)To apply the recommended screening/testing sequences to at least one rotary and one linear ground based coolers coming from different suppliers.5)To collect the lessons learnt in terms of screening/testing and potential design adaptations while maintaining the price point of such cooler.The activity shall be performed in collaboration between a main contractor (otherwise called prime) which shall be knowledgeable in NewSpace type of instruments and two different Cooler Manufacturers: one for the Rotary types coolers, and one for the Linear Type of Coolers.

tenderTitle: MSR-ERO –  First Batch of Mechanical Ground Support Equipment (MGSE Batch 1)
tenderDescription:
The Mars Sample Return – Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement action is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO MGSE Batch 1 to be used for the Spacecraft integration and test activities, in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
In detail the hardware subject of this procurement selection will be:
•	Vertical Integration Stand (VIS) – used to support S/C Modules and S/C Composite during most of the integration and test phases. 
•	S/C Lifting Device – used for S/C Modules and S/C Composite hoisting operations, with CoG adjustment capabilities to cover different S/C configurations
•	Orbit Insertion Module (OIM) Handling Adapter – interfacing the OIM and the S/C Composite and the integration stands and trolleys (e.g. VIS) used during the assembly and test phases and during transport
•	OIM Clamp Band (Ø1666mm) - used to secure the OIM and the S/C Composite to the OIM Adapter during all AIT phases, and to a vibration adapter during Mechanical Dynamic Tests 
•	Return Module (RM) Handling Adapter – used to interface the RM of the Spacecraft to supporting MGSE (e.g. VIS) 
•	RM Clamp Band (Ø1194mm) – used to secure the RM to the Handling Adapter during Module Level activities
•	S/C Mass Dummy (requested as an option) – used to proof load MGSE and to validate test setups where the S/C Composite is suspended

tenderTitle: KICK-START THEMATIC CALL CONNECTED RURAL COMMUNITIES
tenderDescription: Although more than half of the world population lives today in urban areas and all countries of the world are becoming increasingly urbanized, the World Bank estimates that 47.0% of the world's population still lives in rural areas. Poverty is there a serious issue. The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) recently reported that at least 70% of the world's very poor people live in rural areas, with South Asia having the largest number of rural poor people and sub-Saharan Africa having the highest incidence of rural poverty.The nature of the term 'rural' varies from place to place, ranging from the rural urban fringe, to the extreme remote rural areas. The first case refers to areas in a country which are less densely populated, outside the cities and towns with different problems depending on how accessible they are from urban areas. The extreme case refers to remote rural areas which are often farm lands, woodland forests, plains, deserts, and prairies with few buildings and habitants living far apart from each another. Although there are commonalities among rural areas, they also differ greatly from each other and face different issues. The dominant economic activity in the rural areas is typically farming since these areas are located in the countryside. Rural communities in developing economies are almost exclusively relying on agriculture for their livelihood, and many live in extreme poverty. Farming does still happen in the rural-urban fringe in developed countries, but farmers in those areas are more under pressure to sell their land for development. In fact, the urban fringe is often associated with the building of motorways, big shopping centres, hypermarkets and industrial plants. Farming in rural communities of developed countries, such as Europe or North America, may be characterized by the usage of more advanced techniques and access to large markets. However, the number of workers in the sector is decreasing since the mechanisation and exchange of goods and products across the countries is reducing the potential for employment and therefore new business opportunities are sought. An interesting aspect is the movement of people of the communities from and to the rural areas. In some cases, it is the decline in the employment the reason why people move to urban areas to find work. Natural disasters, such as drought or flooding may also encourage migration out of the rural areas. In the More Economically Developed Countries (MEDC), some people move out of urban areas to rural communities to benefit from cheaper housing and more green space. Improvements in transport are allowing this to happen. This is putting pressure on rural areas that have good links with nearby urban areas. In the Less Economically Developed Countries (LEDC), forest clearance, mining and cash crops put pressure on rural areas. There are many resulting effects of this, one is soil erosion from the areas that used to be forests, or from the areas used for farming. There are also pressures to use rural land to build on. Roads are built in rural areas to help the movement of people to and from urban areas or to gain access to mining sites and logging sites. Moreover, rural areas may change over time. These changes are caused by economic factors, as tourism income, farming profitability; environmental factors, as land use, pollution, conservation; social factors, as population change and migration, leisure time, retirement population and others. The provision of the demographic information can be a challenge in the rural communities since the remoteness and isolation of the population makes the counting very difficult. Space technology, in particular satellite images can contribute to facilitate this task by providing indication of the presence of settlements and activities. The services to be developed within this call may apply to all types of rural communities, ranging from rural urban to the extreme remote ones, including developing economies. It is required that a business case underpins the service proposition, with potential customers identified. Rural communities present several challenges in different sectors as tourism, mobility, education, farming, energy, security and healthcare. The issues faced by residents of rural communities are very different than those in urban areas with lack of access to specialized medical care as main critical issue. Because of these many challenges, rural communities are receiving more attention from the regions and countries mainly to support their development. To this aim, various reports and policy papers have been prepared highlighting the specific characteristics of the rural regions and how their innovation capacity might be strengthened through policy improvements, new support mechanisms, new technologies and targeted actions. Limited connectivity is the one characteristic that all rural areas share in common. Rural communities have still a limited broadband access, for example in 2015 only around 25 % of rural households in EU were connected with these technologies. This rural-urban digital divide' is a factor across the EU . The main cause of this divide is that the demand is often too low in the rural areas to be profitable for the companies supplying broadband, and deployment costs are in some respects higher than in urban areas, particularly when buildings are spread over large areas. The "Digital Agenda for Europe" had clear objectives to provide by 2020 a broadband coverage for all Europeans with connectivity speeds of at least 30 Mbps. Bringing more connectivity to the rural areas is a vital factor to encourage development of the rural communities and related industries. Therefore, governments and network operators are increasingly focusing on the improvement of broadband availability. However, ensuring access to high-speed broadband services in rural areas remains one of their main challenges. Many different projects are under development in the European countries making use of innovative technologies and deploying new business and investment models. Activities in the rural communities are surprisingly large contributors to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions (9% of EU emissions and 30% globally) from different sources including nitrogen fertilisers, digestion processes of livestock, manure management, rice cultivation and field burning of agricultural residues. To increase the crop productivity for providing food to increased community, the rural farmers sometimes use pesticides and fertilizers not in the proper amount. The excess of pesticides and agrochemicals accumulate in water bodies and soil causing potential health hazards to humans and other aquatic and terrestrial living organisms. On the other side, rural activities are also affected by climate change. Changes in rainfall, temperature and soil conditions have a number of important consequences, including heat stress on livestock and crops, variations in the patterns of pests and diseases, and lower water availability.
