Description: Although more than half of the world population lives today in urban areas and all countries of the world are becoming increasingly urbanized, the World Bank estimates that 47.0% of the world's population still lives in rural areas. Poverty is there a serious issue. The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) recently reported that at least 70% of the world's very poor people live in rural areas, with South Asia having the largest number of rural poor people and sub-Saharan Africa having the highest incidence of rural poverty.The nature of the term 'rural' varies from place to place, ranging from the rural urban fringe, to the extreme remote rural areas. The first case refers to areas in a country which are less densely populated, outside the cities and towns with different problems depending on how accessible they are from urban areas. The extreme case refers to remote rural areas which are often farm lands, woodland forests, plains, deserts, and prairies with few buildings and habitants living far apart from each another. Although there are commonalities among rural areas, they also differ greatly from each other and face different issues. The dominant economic activity in the rural areas is typically farming since these areas are located in the countryside. Rural communities in developing economies are almost exclusively relying on agriculture for their livelihood, and many live in extreme poverty. Farming does still happen in the rural-urban fringe in developed countries, but farmers in those areas are more under pressure to sell their land for development. In fact, the urban fringe is often associated with the building of motorways, big shopping centres, hypermarkets and industrial plants. Farming in rural communities of developed countries, such as Europe or North America, may be characterized by the usage of more advanced techniques and access to large markets. However, the number of workers in the sector is decreasing since the mechanisation and exchange of goods and products across the countries is reducing the potential for employment and therefore new business opportunities are sought. An interesting aspect is the movement of people of the communities from and to the rural areas. In some cases, it is the decline in the employment the reason why people move to urban areas to find work. Natural disasters, such as drought or flooding may also encourage migration out of the rural areas. In the More Economically Developed Countries (MEDC), some people move out of urban areas to rural communities to benefit from cheaper housing and more green space. Improvements in transport are allowing this to happen. This is putting pressure on rural areas that have good links with nearby urban areas. In the Less Economically Developed Countries (LEDC), forest clearance, mining and cash crops put pressure on rural areas. There are many resulting effects of this, one is soil erosion from the areas that used to be forests, or from the areas used for farming. There are also pressures to use rural land to build on. Roads are built in rural areas to help the movement of people to and from urban areas or to gain access to mining sites and logging sites. Moreover, rural areas may change over time. These changes are caused by economic factors, as tourism income, farming profitability; environmental factors, as land use, pollution, conservation; social factors, as population change and migration, leisure time, retirement population and others. Space technology, in particular satellite images can contribute to facilitate this task by providing indication of the presence of settlements and activities. It is required that a business case underpins the service proposition, with potential customers identified. This rural-urban digital divide' is a factor across the EU . The main cause of this divide is that the demand is often too low in the rural areas to be profitable for the companies supplying broadband, and deployment costs are in some respects higher than in urban areas, particularly when buildings are spread over large areas. tenderTitle: I-HAB  Mechanical Ground Support Equipment batch 1 (MGSE1)
tenderDescription:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Mechanical Ground Support Equipment batch 1 (MGSE1) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Mechanical Ground Support Equipment batch 1 (MGSE1) are part of the support equipment needed for the integration of the I-HAB Gateway module.
The Mechanical Ground Support Equipment batch 1 (MGSE1)and relevant aim under this ITT are: 
Handling adapter Ring (needed to interface with the module through the LVA I/F for the handling sustaining and lifting purposes interfacing with: the lifting devices, the Integration Rotating Stand and to the Transport Container )
Lifting brackets (needed to interface with the module through the front cone flange (the one with 180 bolts) I/F for the handling sustaining and lifting purposes interfacing with: the lifting devices, and to the Transport Container )
Handling/test clamp band (needed to constraint the Handling Ring to the the LVA I/F)
Integration & Rotating Stand (needed to set the module in horizontal position with the required angle position to facilitate the integration and test activities)
Axial & Radial Hatches opening kits (needed to set the hatch doors in open position in safe way)
Modular Working platform (needed to allow accessibility for the preparation. Integration and test of all components to be integrated in I-HAB)
Horizontal Lifting Device (needed to displace the module in various configuration from the IRS to the TSC, to the tilting trolley and vieversa with the module in horizontal configuration)
Vertical Lifting Device (needed to displace the module in various configuration from the Tilting trolley to the facility test RIG and to the launch transport trolley and viceversa with the module in vertical configuration)
The Mechanical Ground Support Equipment batch 1 (MGSE1) are expected to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight.
Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

tenderTitle: ECLS Valves - I-HAB Positive Pressure Relief Assembly (PPRA)
tenderDescription:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025.
 The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada.
 The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration.
 The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly.
 It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the Contractors for the ECLS Positive Pressure Relief Assembly for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Positive Pressure Relief Assy (PPRA) protects the module structure from catastrophic failure due to over-pressurization.
 The valve assembly consists of a mechanical relief valve (Positive Pressure Relief Valve or PPRV) and a motor driven valve (Shut Off Valve or SOV) mounted in series used to provide a second barrier toward vacuum when the valve is not operating.
 The relief valve opens automatically when the pressure difference reaches the cracking pressure and closes automatically when it falls below the reseat pressure.
 The pneumatic section (PPRA/PPRV) will be equipped with a non-propulsive vent mounted on the external side of the primary structure.
 Manual override and position indication are required.
 The ITT is primarily applicable for the complete PPRA but offers for PPRV or SOV will also be considered.
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

tenderTitle: X-BAND RADIO FREQUENCY SCOE
tenderDescription:
The Mars Sample Return – Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the X-Band Radio Frequency SCOE (XRFS), to be used for the Spacecraft integration and test activities, in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The X-band Radio Frequency SCOE (also referred to as XRFS, RF SCOE or TT&C SCOE) is the EGSE element in charge for supporting measurements of the RF performance of the on-board Communication Subsystem and for implementing the RF TM/TC communication between the Ground Testing equipment (namely, the TMTC Front End) and the Spacecraft. 
The RF SCOE directly interfaces, on the Spacecraft side, with the on-board Communication Subsystem, either via Antenna test caps or with a direct RF connection to the waveguides of the RFDU through dedicated EGSE waveguide assembly. In addition to the RF interfaces, the RF SCOE directly interfaces via digital lines the on-board Communication Subsystem (TC inputs and TM outputs) for BER evaluation.

tenderTitle: CLRR - Operational Software evolution (CDO-BLA project)
tenderDescription: In the frame of the Core Launch Range Renewal development aiming at enhanced capabilities, the measure system of the Launch Range encompasses systems that compute the Telemetry data delivered by antennas, the localisation data provided by the radars, the Telecommand system. The Localisation software, after calculating the launcher position and its speed, communicates in real time the information to several operational sytem users. The Telemetry system processes the CVI extraction data coming from the downrange stations and provides with the onboard launcher information to several operational systems, in particular to the localisation. The mission analysis system performs, at least twice during a launch campaign preparation, the customisation of the specific configuration of the sensors implemented during the launch. The purpose of this activity is to carry out the evolution / adaptation of all these above measure system operational software as well as the mission analysis software and the in-flight safety submission software. It foresees also the implementation of upgraded features fostering the operational flexibility with the possibility to set the configuration depending on the perfomed activity (maintenance, launch day, training..) or the operational system implemented.

tenderTitle: I-HAB  Independent Software Verification & Validation (ISVV)
tenderDescription:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025.
 The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada.
 The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space andact as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration.
 The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly.
 It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for I-HAB Independent Software Verification & Validation (ISVV) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The I-HAB Independent Software Verification & Validation (ISVV) is part of the support equipment to integrate and test the I-HAB Gateway module.
The I-HAB Independent Software Verification & Validation (ISVV) function is a technicalactivity performed by a team independent of the developer, aimed to increase the reliability of the Software product and to improve the quality of the development process.
Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

tenderTitle: UHF-Band Low Gain Antennas (LGA) and Radio Frequency Distribution Unit (UHF LGA & RFDU)
tenderDescription:
The Mars Sample Return – Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.

Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO UHF- band Low Gain Antennas (UHF LGAs) and Radio Frequency Distribution Unit (UHF RFDU) it in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The UHF LGAs and RFDU (UHF band Low Gain Antennas and Radio Frequency Distribution Unit) shall comprise:
-	Two UHF Low Gain antennas (named “UHF ANT” or “UHF LGA”), one located on –X side (UHF ANT1) and one on +Y side (UHF ANT2) of the ERO S/C. 
-	A Radio Frequency distribution units (UHF RFDU) comprising two RF switches and a set of 8 coaxial cables 
-	Ancillaries (Dust caps, RF loads)
Note: UHF transceiver is not part of the LGA/RFDU procurement

The main function of the UHF LGAs:
•	Signal radiation, i.e. conversion from guided transmission (coaxial I/F) to radiated waveform in UHF band forward link frequency band (only for ANT1)
•	Signal reception, i.e. conversion from radiated waveform to guided transmission (coaxial I/F) in UHF band return link frequency band (for both antennas)

The main function of the UHF Radio Frequency Distribution is to ensure: 
•	the transmit routing of the high power RF signal from the UHF-band Transceivers to the UHF-band antennas 
•	the receive routing of the RF signal from the UHF-band antennas to the UHF-band Transceivers

The UHF LGAs and RFDU shall operate in the following bands:
• UHF-Band Forward Link (Orbiter to Mars Asset) : 428 MHz – 450 MHz
• UHF-Band Return Link (Mars Asset to Orbiter) : 387 MHz – 410 MHz

tenderTitle: SSA P3-SST-XX - EISCAT-3D RADAR PROCESSING PRELIMINARY DESIGN
tenderDescription: This activity will, based on the simulation results of P3-SST-290, prepare the processing software to cope with the radar data following the data policy in place. On the radar side, it will further mature the design, interface data formats and the necessary stepsto fulfil data policy criteria for space object observations. Further, the Data Processing Chain based on the given version of the SST Core Software, will be scaled to the expected data volume. The activity will specify required software components for the scheduling of multi-beam tracking and exploit ways for optimisation. Finally, the activity will study the feasibility of first staring mode observations with given transmitter elements, if available at that time.

tenderTitle: POWER PROCESSING UNIT SWITCH-ON STRATEGY AFTER SPACECRAFT SEPARATION (ARTES AT REF. 4F.099) EXPRO+
tenderDescription: Objective: The objective of the activity is to allow Power Processing Unit (PPU) switch on as quickly as possible after spacecraft separation.Targeted Improvements: To avoid long drifts during mission phases (days).Description: High power units like PPUs havethe risk of Corona at first start-up if the pressure is too high. Traditionally, such units are therefore only switched on after several days of depressurization and outgassing. With full electric orbit raising, there is a need to start PPUs within a few hours after separation, in order to start the electric orbit raising as early as possible. The days of depressurisation and outgassing lead to a decay of the spacecraft's orbit while waiting for the operational requirements to be met for switching on the plasmic propulsion.After choosing a EOR missions profile and a PPU existing design, it is proposed to define the conditions (temperature, pressure,etc.) required to switch-on the PPU as early as possible after separation, without Corona.The proposed work logic is:? Selectionof a reference PPU design reference EOR mission profile;? Define the pressure profile using materials outgassing rate and any other parameters driving pressure decay (manufacturing, temperature, etc.)? Definition of max pressure allowed to ensure no risk of Corona - analytically, or by test;? Issue of some recommended methods for a safe start-up after separation without design change - possibly by measuring temperature, pressure, time, etc.? Validation of this method by test;? recommend design changes if necessary.

tenderTitle: OPEN STANDARD FOR INTER SATELLITE LINK - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: A number of missions are being investigated, under development or even already flying that use the concept of multiple spacecraft interconnected with an intersatellite Link (ISL); they are mainly nano/smallsats (Proba-3 and Gomex-4a/b as current generation examples and AIM/HERA as future non-LEO case) but with clear interest also for regular mission. The only standardised protocol for such radio links is Proximity-1 that is however tailored for different applications (mainly data relay among landers and orbiters in a reduced complexity network topology with only limited accuracy for the line-of-sight ranging estimation). Advanced solutions have been however investigated and (partially) developed on the basis of proprietary solutions in the frame of various RD contracts (ESA or not) and to provide specific products for private/national missions. The adoption of such proprietary solutions (often kept confidential to public) is seen as a limitation for the full exploitation of such constellation/formation concept, for example for heterogeneous/progressively deployed systems developed by different industries. It also prevents the development of reusable products.This activity is meant to define requirements (functional, performance and I/F) and give recommendations for an open ISL protocol (RF, not optical, up to Layer 4) that allows implementations from different developers to be able to be part of the same network thanks to a common standard and to allows system integrators to gain from a more competitive ISL market. While the intended "market" is the European one, any coherent solution will be proposed to CCSDS. A small proof of concept (software simulator) will be produced. The ISL system shall be able to support bidirectional data exchange, 1D/3D localisation, relative attitude determination and time correlation/synchronisation in a tailorable fashion to best match specific mission needs.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- gathering of contextual data, state of the art, existing solution, and requirements for the future ISL to be fully interoperable.- protocol development- software simulator proof of concept development

tenderTitle: HIGH ACCURACY TESTING OF INTERFEROMETRIC ANTENNA WITH LARGE BASELINE - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: Future high frequency interferometric antennas (e.g. at Ka band) using large baselines require verification and testing with a veryhigh accuracy, in particular in phase. While such interferometric testing and ground calibration techniques have been successfully performed in the past (i.e. Cryosat), the consideration for baselines above 10 or 20 meters brings challenges in the ground validation in several domains: the antenna alignment, the boom effect on the antenna pattern and the synchronous co-alignment between all beams being generated are areas that require development toachieve satisfactory results, in line with the requirements. In addition, for baselines in the 15-20 meter range, the currently existing test facilities and techniques do not allow testing the complete baseline in deployed configuration. One of the solutions is to scale down the antenna sub-system, which would imply a measurement at frequencies in the order of a few hundred gigahertz - a challenge that once overcome, would allow a proper on ground characterisation ofthe complete system.A demonstrator of the scaled antenna sub-system shall be made available and tested to validate the testing conceptThe workflow of the activity is as follows:1) Identification of accuracy requirements and problem areas in large Ka band SAR interferometers2) Trade-off on verifications and testing methodologies3) Design and manufacture of scaled breadboard4) Testing ofbreadboard to validate concept

tenderTitle: AUTHENTICATION OF GNSS SIGNALS BY RADIO SIGNAL FINGERPRINTING - EXPRO+
tenderDescription: The authentication of GNSS signals poses a challenging problem. Before exploiting a signal (e.g. its pseudo-noise sequence) it would be desirable for the receiver to have assurance quickly (ideally in less than 10-s) and reliably that the signal is actually coming from a navigation satellite and not from a spoofer (e.g. unknown pseudolite, delayed version of the same signal). Classical data-level authentication solutions work after signal demodulation (PN sequence de-spreading), require data-level cryptography (shared secrets) and key management. Furthermore, they cannot combat against delayed versions of the original signal, which is a problem for navigation receivers. Physical-layer authentication techniques like radio signal fingerprinting rely instead on what signals are (no shared secrets). Minimal differences in the physical structure of RF signal transmitters such as in the oscillator, amplifier and delay circuits produce differences in the amplitude, phase and frequency. Such differences can be exploited by adapted receivers to identify and classify the signal source. These techniques could offer an alternative to such data-level techniques with less system impact. These techniques allow to compare a received signal 'signature' against a local database of signatures with certain algorithms and decision criteria/metrics (e.g. fingerprint matcher using Mahalanobis distance). They do not need to process data-level information. They rely on the normal presence of pilots or equivalent repeated symbol patterns in all data frames of wireless systems producing repetitive radio signals. They are a subject of very intense research for what concerns certain security threats (e.g. impersonation, spoofing, intrusion detection) considering context (e.g. SNR conditions, classification objective, parametric and non-parametric statistical features) and implementation complexity for all sort of wireless technologies and standards from RFID tags to ZigBee,Z-wave, Wireless LAN, LTE. GNSS signals by definition are produced by very high quality radio sources. Thus, the feasibility of exploiting small differences between those sources to define well-identifiable signatures, corresponding metrics and apply signal classification techniques needs to be confirmed first. Another line of research could be to exploit the analogue distortions typically used by fingerprinting matching techniques to create an artificial signature in the signal that could be later exploited for authentication, in contrast with the typically proposed solutions based on specific PRN injection. Signal classification techniques basicallyrely on the processing of RF signal samples, extraction of relevant features and statistical processing with machine learning techniques (e.g. decision-tree, random forests). A survey of those techniques and a selection of a subset for further analysis, simulation and even implementation (e.g. with vector signal receiver platform) has to be performed. As part of the activity, the provision ofrepresentative and distinct GNSS signal sources with similar level of quality is crucial. The I/Q samples of recorded GNSS Navigation signals with good SNR as with an In-Orbit Test Station is needed both to generate the local database of 'clean' signatures storedby the classifier and as a signal source to be used on the stimulus side. SNR and multipath conditions need to be considered and realistic scenarios reproduced through simulation and possibly testing/evaluation and channel emulation with a radio platform.The activity consists of the following tasks :1) to assess the feasibility of employing RF signal fingerprinting as an authentication technique for GNSS signals;2) to study, simulate and evaluate performance of selected radio signal classification techniques for both high-end and low-end navigation receivers;3) to propose a reliable GNSS signal authentication concept based on radio-level signal classificationProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). For additional information please go to EMITS news "Industrial Policy measures for non-primes, SMEs and RD entities in ESA programmes".

tenderTitle: I-HAB Meteorite Protection Structures (MPS)
tenderDescription:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an 
infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and 
utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA,
Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed
to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp
for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will
require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew
of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise
operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Meteorite 
Protection Structures for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Meteorite Protection Structures are part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
The Meteorite Protection Structures are housed outside the pressurized volume 
of the module via dedicated brackets that will be sized by the MPS developer. 
It acts has protective shield against the on orbit micro-meteoroids. The main
component are thin metallic panels in Aluminum Alloy, spaced from the pressure shell
and external critical equipment, provide shielding from the MMOD environment during IHAB mission. 
MMOD performance will be guaranteed from the concept that is addressed by the MPS
specification. Whereas the developer will be responsible for the other technical
aspects such as the mechanical performance specified by the contract specification.
If necessary to meet MMOD requirements, ballistic fabric layers (eg. Kevlar) integrated 
in MLI can be implemented on top of the shell / equipment. These protection if needed 
will be under TASI perimeter. Thus they will be not part of the contract.
Docking ports are protected by MLI reinforced with Nextel and / or Kevlar, if acceptable
from outgassing and temperature exposure point of view. This solution is derived
from that of the Halo Hatch and is not part of the contract.

The Meteorite Protection Structures The internal secondary structure is expected
to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight 
and Gateway Program Standards and Environment.
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for
visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical
return requirements/targets to be considered.
Further information concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:

Description: The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an 
infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and 
utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA,
Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed
to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp
for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will
require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew
of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise
operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Meteorite 
Protection Structures for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Meteorite Protection Structures are part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
The Meteorite Protection Structures are housed outside the pressurized volume 
of the module via dedicated brackets that will be sized by the MPS developer. 
It acts has protective shield against the on orbit micro-meteoroids. The main
component are thin metallic panels in Aluminum Alloy, spaced from the pressure shell
and external critical equipment, provide shielding from the MMOD environment during IHAB mission. 
MMOD performance will be guaranteed from the concept that is addressed by the MPS
specification. Whereas the developer will be responsible for the other technical
aspects such as the mechanical performance specified by the contract specification.
If necessary to meet MMOD requirements, ballistic fabric layers (eg. Kevlar) integrated 
in MLI can be implemented on top of the shell / equipment. These protection if needed 
will be under TASI perimeter. Thus they will be not part of the contract.
Docking ports are protected by MLI reinforced with Nextel and / or Kevlar, if acceptable
from outgassing and temperature exposure point of view. This solution is derived
from that of the Halo Hatch and is not part of the contract.

The Meteorite Protection Structures The internal secondary structure is expected
to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight 
and Gateway Program Standards and Environment.

visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical
return requirements/targets to be considered.

tenderTitle: MSR-ERO X-Band Radio Frequency Distribution Assembly (X-RFDA)
tenderDescription:
The Mars Sample Return Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO X- band Radio Frequency Distribution Assembly unit it in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The X-RFDA (X band Radio Frequency Distribution Assembly) shall ensure: 

	the transmit routing of the low power RF signal from the Transponder X-band transmitters output to the X-band TWTAs (amplifiers) input 
	the transmit routing of the high power RF signal from each X-band TWTAs output to any of the X-band antennas (LGA1, LGA2, MGA, HGA) 
	the receive routing of the RF signal from any of the X-band antennas (LGA1, LGA2, MGA, HGA) to the Transponder X-band receivers input 

The RFDA shall operate in the following bands:
	Uplink band: 7145 - 7190 MHz 
	Downlink band: 8400 - 8450 MHz

tenderTitle: PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS EGS-CC BASED APPLICATIONS- EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: The EGS-CC (European Ground System Common Core) project aims at developing the common core functions of the next generation European Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) and Mission Control Systems (MCS). The facilities build from the EGS-CC will support the functional verification (FV) of satellites at early development stages, the satellite level assembly integration and verification (AIV) process and the Mission Control pre- and post-launch. The EGS-CC project is currently in phase C/D.Performance of a system isits responsiveness/scalability and stability/reliability under particular workload. Ensuring optimal performance from a complex system like the EGS-CC is a difficult task as critical functions like telemetry archiving, telecommanding and telemetry processing are carried out in parallel through collaboration of multiple components and it is difficult to apportion performance to individual components. For EGS-CC to be a successful product, its performance must meet existing requirements and allow improvement of that performance in future evolution.This activity aims at ensuring that the expected performance of the integrated EGSCC product, e.g. the EGS-CC components themselves or applications built on top of it, is achieved in an optimal manner and even exceeded.In the frame of this activity the following tasks are foreseen: - Implement the necessary tools and facilties to measure performance and the system and component levels - Measure performance and associated quality attributes of the EGS-CC based on existing Reference Test Facility and defined test scenarios - Analyse and evaluate EGS-CC performance requirements based on measurements - Write evaluation report with possible recommendations

tenderTitle: EXPRO + NAVISP ELEMENT 1 (NAVISP-EL1-015): FEASIBILITY STUDY OF A SPACE-BASED RELATIVISTIC PNT SYSTEM
tenderDescription: This EXPRO+ procurement is part of the NAVISP Programme, under Elelment 1, Work Plan 2018.All GNSS in operation at present are based on Newtonian physics and rely on global reference frames fixed to Earth. Relativistic effects are treated as deviations that need to be corrected for. Precision and stability in time of the reference frames is provided via ground stations and they are limitedby the Earths dynamics and atmosphere. Several theoretical concepts have been proposed for the use of Relativistic Positioning Systems (RPS) and the required relativistic reference frames. These have been studied with different approaches during the last years and the consistency with the General Relativity has been demonstrated. However, none of the proposed approaches were intended to be practical. The proposed activity will address the maturity of RPS for timing and positioning applications, the definition of a consolidated concept and architecture for a RPS constellation suitable for navigation both in the Earth surface and the near-Earth Space,and the High Level Requirements for a proof-of-concept based on current and near-future available state of the art technology.

tenderTitle: ACOUSTIC PROPELLANT MANAGEMENT FOR FUEL TANKS OF SPACECRAFT AND LAUNCHER UPPER STAGES
tenderDescription: The purpose of the activity is two-fold: to use an acoustic beam for sounding the fluid location in a tank. to show the abilityof induce fluid movements and control of the free surface for liquid/gas mixtures, including those of cryogenic flows.Management of fluids on fuel tanks of spacecraft and launcher upper stages under microgravity conditions has always presented a challenge, because it does not naturally accumulate in a neat shape near the exit port. Gauging requires measurement or knowledge of the shape of the fluid free surface in microgravity. Knowledge of the residual quantity and location of propellant is essential for management andcontrol of both satellites and launcher upper stages, for the latter in particular if multiple firings are anticipated. Manipulation of fluids in partially filled tanks serves the purpose to ensure it is connected to the exit port.In a previous TRP activity, ultrasonic transducers have been used to impose motion in fluids (water, kerosene and LN2), as result of asymmetric flow patterns in the close vicinity of the transducer. This offers the possibility that fluids could be managed with an array of ultrasonic transducerswhere phase and amplitude control to each unit are used to generate focused acoustic beams, which can manipulate the fluids. Base on those results, it is here proposed to implement an array of transducers, and through phased driving of these, to generate a directed acoustic beam. With help of this beam one can sound the fluid location in the tank. Using a range of experimental setups (e.g. tipping the tank to collect the fluid at one end; containing the fluid in balloons, and so on), the effects of varying gas/fluid boundary locations and shapes will be investigated to extend the demonstration done in the first study, using liquid only, to liquid/gas mixtures, showing the ability to induce fluid movement and control of the free surface also under these circumstances.A specific set of trials will include an assessment of the viability of mounting the transducer array outside the tank and sounding through the wall using a typical tank wall construction (including Ti and CFRP). Some of the transducers will be immersed in fluid attached to the container walls by surface tension, and some will be in the gas-filled part of the vessel. Further, the test equipment and set-up will be adapted for a future accommodation and operation on board a parabolic flight to demonstrate the technique under micro-gravity conditions. In addition, to show the compatibility of transducers in operation at cryogenic temperature and, if a safe configuration can be designed, first trials with acoustic liquid manipulation and sensing with LH2 will be performed on ground. Finally, the experimental results will be used also to validate numerical tools for simulation of the coupling between acoustics and fluid behavior.

tenderTitle: POLAR MONITORING MISSION, ASSESSMENT AND CONSOLIDATION OF REQUIREMENTS AND ANALYSIS OF CAMPAIGN DATA (EXPRO+)
tenderDescription: Copernicus is the most ambitious space Earth Observation programme to date. It has achieved a success well beyond the initial requirements and expectations. While approaching the completion of the deployment of the first generation and while the users' feedback allows performing a mature assessment, the European Commission has initiated the collection of users' requirement in preparation for the evolution of the system. The process of prioritisation of users' needs has allowed identifying the following priorities:- A mission to measure the anthropogenic contribution to the CO2 cycle;- Observations in the thermal infrared spectral region and in the hyperspectral observation domain, supported by active microwave imaging at L-band, to expand the current Sentinel measurement capabilities (priorities for agriculture, forestry, land management);- New measurements focused on critical parameters affecting the polar regions, namely sea ice/floating ice concentration and surface elevation respectively by passive microwave imaging as highest priority and polar topography techniques.Such priorities translate into a set of preparatory activities for High Priority Candidate Missions that belong to the second leg, called "Copernicus Expansion". One of these High Priority Candidate Missions is the CopernicusPolar Ice and Snow Topography Mission. Building on CryoSat-2 experience, this mission shall provide enhanced land ice elevation andsea ice thickness measurements implementing higher spatial resolution for improved lead detection and additional capability to determine snow loading on sea ice. Improved on-board tracking systems for operation over sloppy mountain glaciers and addition of radiometer for all-round oceanographic use and coastal altimetry may also be considered.As part of these preparatory activities, activities of assessment and consolidation of requirements and analysis of campaign data are required. The objective of the present study "Polar Monitoring Mission, Assessment and Consolidation of Requirements and Analysis of Campaign Data" is to analyse collected user requirements, in particular those obtained from the Commission User Requirements Study and support the translation and detailed justification into mission requirements for a future polar ice and ocean topography mission with enhanced capabilities for ice and snow monitoring. This activity will be funded by the fifth slice (EOEP-5) of the Earth Observation Envelope Programme, which is an optional programme of the Agency. Therefore the procurement will be open to all economic operators belonging to the ESA Member and Associated States and Canada,participating in said EOEP-5 Programme; to date: Austria, Belgium, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia,Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Luxemburg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden,Switzerland and United Kingdom and Canada.

tenderTitle: AUTONOMOUS TARGETS OF OPPORTUNITY FOR ASTRONOMY MISSIONS - T209-001EC
tenderDescription: The ATHENA spacecraft baseline carries two independent instruments; a spectrometer (X-IFU) and an imager (WFI) which will share a single focal point provided by a single x-ray telescope. The mission therefore requires a means of placing one of the instruments at a time at the telescope focus via an Instrument Selection Mechanism (ISM). Two possibilities are foreseen in order to meet this requirement (a) the Movable Mirror Assembly (MMA) approach where the telescope mirror assembly shall be rotated/translated whilst the focal plane instruments remain fixed with respect to the spacecraft structure and (b) the Movable Instrument Platform (MIP) approach where the instruments are translated and the telescope mirror assembly remains fixed with respect to the spacecraft structure.This activity is foreseen to be conducted in two phases. Phase 1 shall address the preliminary design of an ISM meeting the requirements of both the MMA and MIP approaches. Phase 2 shall address the detailed design and breadboarding of one of the two approaches which will be selected by the Agency).

tenderTitle: USE OF SECURE OPTICAL COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGIES TO PROTECT EUROPEAN CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE - SCYLIGHT WORKPLAN (SL.010) - EXPRO PLUS
tenderDescription: ScyLight Workplan has been established based on an ESA internal "ARTES ScyLight Call for Ideas".This activity have been selected in line with with the programme objectives for Line 4 (Quantum Cryptography Technologies). Line 4 covers the related development as well as in-orbit and service demonstration, including Quantum Key Generation and Distribution systems, and the demonstration of related end-to-end systems.This activity targets the protection of European critical infrastructure through the exploitation of secureoptical communication technologies. "European critical infrastructure" means critical infrastructure located in European Union states, the disruption or destruction of which would have a significant impact on at least two states (e.g. related to energy, health, transport, telecommunications, finance, security and space assets).The activity shall identify the potential deficiencies of existing secure solutions for critical infrastructure protection, including crypto key management and distribution. It shall identify the required technology developments, concepts of operation and possible scenarios for deployment in space in a 2020 - 2025 timeframe. The technical and operational requirements for space-based systems (e.g. low earth orbit satellites, geostationary satellites, ground segment) shall be established and a business case developed for the protection of critical infrastructures using optical communication technologies, such asquantum key distribution.

tenderTitle: IAP.KS.PT.000 PROPTECH - KICKSTART
tenderDescription: Property Technology, or "PropTech", is a term that encompasses the application of information technology and platform economics to real estate markets. PropTech has proliferated over the last 35 years initially due to the development of mainframe and personal computers, tools such as Lotus and Excel, more comprehensive software solutions for architecting, engineering and construction, and finally the Internet era and online marketplaces. Recent breakthroughs in technologies spanning cloud computing, machine learning, smartphones, and improved connectivity capabilities are spurring further activity in the PropTech space. Aims of PropTech can include reducing overhead, improving transactions, and optimising property management activities. Such technologies relate to digital dashboards, smart home technology, tech-enabled brokerages, residential and commercial lending, virtual viewing for online portals, and analysing and extracting data from documentation and/or imagery.

tenderTitle: I-HAB  External AIT activities (EXA)
tenderDescription:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for I-HAB External AIT activities (EXA) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The I-HAB External AIT activities (EXA) is part of the support equipment to integrate and test the I-HAB Gateway module.
The I-HAB External AIT activities (EXA) aim is to cover for the C/D slice 2 program phases with relevant AIT figures consistent of (at max support phase):
-	AIT Mechanical operator
-	AIT Fluidic/Alignment operator
-	AIT EGSE expert operator
-	AIT Functional Operator
-	AIT QA operator 

The foreseen activities to be developed are related to the operational execution of the following tasks:
-	Integration and test activities documentation examination
-	Documentation preparation and configuration control of hardware and tooling
-	Operative AIT tasks execution
-	Test conduction and participation
-	Test set-up preparation
-	Handling of the flight hardware and GSE 
-	Work could be performed in shift and in holidays time
-	While the standard place of tasks execution will be in Italy, Turin, some test activities shall be performed in external country (The Netherlands, Germany, or in France, as needed) 
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.
Further information concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

tenderTitle: I-HAB Harness (HRNS)
tenderDescription:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. 
 The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. 
It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Harness (HRNS) for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Harness (HRNS) are part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
The harness (HRNS) function is to provide distribution and separation of power, analogue and digital signal, commands and lines to the different unit and/or interface.

tenderTitle: MSR-ERO ¡V Central Check-Out System (CCS)
tenderDescription:
The Mars Sample Return ¡V Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agency¡¦s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO Central Check-Out System (CCS), to be used for the Spacecraft integration and test activities, in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The CCS will be used both on the AVM and PFM spacecraft AIT campaigns and Launch Campaign, being in charge of providing supervisor control, test execution and simulation environments together at the same time. The CCS shall be the unique manager and supervisor of the overall EGSE activities during S/C testing, therefore it shall be able to provide reliable monitor and control facilities in order to assess the correct functioning of the on board unit during all test flow. The CCS will be in charge to control and monitor the operations of the other EGSE elements as well. 
In particular, the CCS is used for:
X	Generating, editing and debugging of automated test scripts and their execution and control in the frame of the S/C testing
X	Sending Telecommands to on-board units (via other EGSE elements with direct interfaces to the Spacecraft) 
X	Reception, de-commutation and monitoring of real-time S/C Telemetry
X	Recording and archiving the S/C Telemetry and other Test data from-to Spacecraft with proper time tagging 
X	Data presentation - including alpha-numeric and graphical synoptic displays - of both Telemetry and Telecommand packets/parameters in raw and engineering formats
X	SCOE communication and remote control
X	Archiving of raw Telemetry Frames 
It is a specific program requirement that CCS uses Terma¡¦s CCS5 software as Master Test Processor.

The Mars Sample Return Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.

tenderTitle: Antenna Reflector Assembly Sub-System for ESPRIT HALO
tenderDescription:
The HALO Lunar Communication Subsystem (HLCS) will serve as a data link on the LOP-G Cislunar mission, which is an international framework and stepped approach for lunar and further Deep Space exploration purposes. The communication system located on this module provide the link for the Lunar system. The currently planned launch date is in last Quarter 2023.
Within the HLCS there are two S&Ka-Band High Gain Reflectors where the ARA (Antenna Reflector Assembly) is located and it comprises a sub-system formed by the Main reflector, the sub reflector and the struts.
The ARASS baseline configuration as required by the HLCS Prime is the manufacturing of 2 Flight Model assemblies, together with 1 Structural Model, as well as the necessary GSEs such as Unit Check Out Equipment.
Thales Alenia Space France (TAS-F) has been selected by ESA to be the ESPRIT HALO Prime Contractor. In turn TAS-F has selected SENER Aeroespacial S.A. as responsible for HLCS design, development and verification activities during phases B, C/D and E1, amongst them, the ARA. The selection of subcontractors is conducted in line with the Code of Best Practices, as tailored to the specific programmatic frame of ESPRIT HALO HLCS. 
In this framework, SENER Aeroespacial S.A. will release an ITT for the procurement of the ARASS. Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

M3 (medium-class) astronomical science mission for the search of exo-planets. This is per-formed by detecting and characterizing transit signature of exo-planets in front of the parent

star, as well as measuring seismic oscillations of central stars of exo-planetary systems and
other selected stars. For this purpose, PLATO will be placed in an orbit around the L2 La-grange point of the Sun-Earth system. The mission schedule considers a launch in 2026. The operational lifetime is 6.5 years.

The objective of this procurement is the manufacturing and test of the Service Valves for the Chemical Propulsion Subsystem (CPPS) for the PLATO program.

The FLEX (Fluorescence Explorer) mission objective is

induced vegetation fluorescence in order to monitor 
vegetation photosynthetic activity.

Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer (
SLSTR) that will provide additional information 
about vegetation status (TOA reflectance 
and temperature) and accurate atmospheric correction, 
which are essential for quantitative interpretation 
of fluorescence signal.

tenderTitle: Iris IOC - ATN-IPS Standards Support
tenderDescription:
The objective of this SoW is to provide Technical Support to the Iris Programme and in support of ATN/IPS standardisation in WP 3.3.2 of the ATN/IPS Project.

Work will be conducted under standards Development and Coordination (WP3.3) which aims to provide a structured approach for ATN/IPS standardisation efforts in order to align and coordinate all standardisation activities aspects of the FOC Work Stream, as well as for the IOC wide programme. The aim is to cover project wide activities transversal to Iris IOC and Iris FOC and requiring continuity of action such as SESAR coordination, and International Standardisation.

The main objective are to produce ATN/IPS technical notes and update the existing technical working papers to serve as input into additional standards activities. Prepare recommendations and inputs into ATN/IPS standards working groups, including AEEC, EUROCAE/RTCA/ICAO and others as appropriate and ensure that the current standards are sufficient for implementation of ATN/IPS functionality within the Iris context

tenderDescription:

tenderTitle: MSR-ERO High & Medium Gain Antenna Pointing Assembly (HGA & MGA APA)
tenderDescription:
The Mars Sample Return Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO High & Medium Gain Antenna Pointing Assembly (HGA & MGA APA) unit it in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

APA shall provide the capability to move and point two antenna types: a ca. 2m parabolic reflector for HGA and a 90° offset steerable 20 cm reflector for MGA. The APA is intended as the moving mechanisms plus the relevant electronics.
APA requirements:
-	Dual Axis APM in azimuth and elevation axis arrangement
-	Pointing capability of Azimuth: -180° + 180°, Elevation: 0° -90°
-	Max slew rate: ≥0,5°/s
-	Max Acceleration ≥ 0,01°/s2
-	Pointing accuracy: better than 0.05° for HGA and 0.1° for MGA
-	Position sensing in each axis (resolution 0.008°)

tenderTitle: I-HAB TCS Filters
tenderDescription:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an
 infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and
 utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from 
USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed
 to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp
 for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will
 require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of
 up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise 
operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for TCS Filter 
for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The TCS Filter function is to protect the pump unit from incoming particles that might
 damage it and to maintain the fluid quality in terms of particulate matter and
 impurity at a desirable level. The action of the filter is carried out both 
in removing ( by capturing in the mesh) free bubbles dispersed in the coolant matrix due
 to marginal ATCS circuit filling procedure and in breaking and/or fragmenting of
 potential concentrated trains or plugs of entrained bubbles.
The filter is composed of a metal mesh contained in a case and it is constantly fluxed
 by the coolant main stream. The filter hydraulic interfaces and internal fluid path 
are selected to ensure the minimum hydraulic pressure drop localized in the device.
The metallic mesh is characterized by two fundamental parameters:
-	Filtration rating
-	Dirt holding capability
The TCS Filter is expected to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight.
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for
 visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of 
geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.
Further information
 concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

tenderTitle: Space Rider: OBC/OBDH, MMU, GNSS
tenderDescription:
The Space Rider Mission definition activities, are progressing and targeting a reusable space transportation system integrated with VEGA-C 
able to operate in-orbit, de-orbit, re-enter, land on ground and be re-launched after limited refurbishment for n.5 subsequent missions.

The Program is very challenging in terms of technology and schedule and will require a dedicated effort from Industry in matching the Agency objectives 
to conduct the Space Rider Program in such a way as to achieve the scientific and technological objectives set for the missions whilst minimizing the costs.

and the two GNSS receivers. 

The contracts will be managed by Industrial Co-Primes (TAS and AVIO) being ESA the final customer of Space Rider Vehicle.

tenderTitle: Ariane 6 - ITT : Sequencer LLL
tenderDescription:
Ariane Group intend to issue an ITT for a payload sequencer on December 20th, 2019.
The ITT will be restricted to the companies from Czech republic.
The perimeter of the ITT is to provide a validated preliminary design of a sequencer for the Ariane 6 launcher. 
The sequencer shall allow multiplying the number of separation orders to separate a higher number of payloads than currently possible. The sequencer shall address any type of separation systems.
In this preliminary phase, a preliminary design of the sequencer based on a technical requirement specification (TRS) document is required, confirmed by the functional validation of a breadboard. First a preliminary definition file shall be proposed along with the design of the breadboard. Then the readiness of the breadboard hardware, test bench and test plan will allow starting of the functional tests. Deliverables will include in addition to the test report, a justified matrix of compliance to the TRS and the statement of work, the updated sequencer preliminary file after test, the preliminary sequencer specification, the development plan, the recurrent cost of the sequencer and sizing requirement for design to cost. 
The foreseen duration of the activity is six months.

tenderTitle: EO Network of Resources - Best Practices ITT to procure services from platform tier providers
tenderDescription:
Exploitation Platforms are a central element of ESA's Earth Observation (EO) Innovation Europe concept, which aims at the integration of EO data and information for a much broader use, for scientific, social and economic purposes, as well as for the generation of new commercial applications and services. 

The EO Network of Resources (NoR) initiative promotes the use of European resource and platform services to facilitate a simplified and efficient exploitation of EO data in cloud environments. The initiative incentivizes providers to contribute to a common framework harmonising the access to their services and helping the user to work with the data.

ESA conducted an ITT (AO/1-9217/18/I-LG-Procurement of Earth Observation Exploitation Platform Network Resource Services) in 2018. The tender awarded a contract in December 2018 to Cloudeo AG, with RHEA and BHO Legal as subcontractors, to select under the supervision of ESA, and via ESA?s Best Practices Processes, the services of eligible Resource and Platform Tier Providers.

A NoR portal will list in its online directory all the selected providers together with their NoR service portfolio which can be procured via a shopping cart. ESA can sponsor scientists and value adding users for eligible research, development and pre-commercial projects to procure such services. A NoR helpdesk staffed with remote sensing and IT experts, working closely with the providers, will support users in the selection of the services, as well as in the application process for sponsoring.

This intended tender is for the selection of Platform Tier providers using cloud services with collocated Sentinel and non-Sentinel data.

Platform Tier providers wishing to contribute to the NoR service directory are invited to provide a proposal. The tender process is made as simple as possible for interested service providers to respond.

tenderTitle: BIOMASS Instrument Bench
tenderDescription:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of the Instrument Bench by Airbus Defence and Space GmbH as a Core team 
member of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The Contractor (i.e. the equipment Contractor) shall be responsible for the 
provisions of all materials, manpower, facilities, supplies, tools, unit, 
documentation and support services as may be required to design, 
manufacture, assemble, test and deliver to Airbus Defence and Space the 
Biomass Instrument Bench, which consists of the Instrument Trolley and the 
Instrument EQM Structure.

The instrument trolley shall be used to manipulate the Biomass Instrument 
during its assembling, integration and test (AIT) procedure.
The Instrument EQM structure shall be used as mechanical support of the 
Biomass Instrument EQM Subsystems during the Biomass Instrument EQM AIT 
campaign.

The concepts of both assemblies are provided as engineering solution in the 
specification as a guideline.

In this framework, the present Invitation to Tender is addressed to 
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose 
registered office is established in such Member and Participating States 
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating 
State in the ESA Earth Observation Envelope Programme 4.

Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal,

tenderDescription:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 in Graz, Austria. The overall objective of the mission is to 
reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide spatial distribution and dynamics 
of forest biomass in order to improve current assessments and future 
projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,

growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of Biomass ISVV by Airbus Defence and Space Ltd as Prime
contractor of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development, production,
testing and delivery of the ISVV.

The ISVV is the independent software verification and validation of the 
Biomass mission software running on the on board computer and other flight 
hardware. ISVV is an engineering practice intended to improve quality and 
reduce costs of a software product. It is also intended to reduce 
development risks by having an organization independent of the software 
developer to perform verification and validation of the specifications and 
code of a software product.
Software verification and validation activities check the software
against its specifications. Every project must verify and validate the 
software it produces. This is done by:
· checking that each software item meets specified requirements
· checking each software item before it is used as an input to another
activity;
· ensuring that checks on each software item are done, as far as
possible, by someone other than the author
· ensuring that the amount of verification and validation effort is 
adequate
to show each software item is suitable for operational use.

tenderDescription:
The Ariane 62 launcher will become the baseline launcher for the deployment of the Galileo satellite constellation from Galileo Batch 3 satellites.

tenderTitle: PROSPECT IMAGING SYSTEM
tenderDescription:
The subject ITT addresses part of the PROSPECT Drilling and Sample Analysis package
 development (managed by Leonardo as Prime), due for flight on board the Russian 
Luna-Resource (Luna-27) mission in 2022. As part of PROSPECT an Imaging System 
is foreseen which shall deliver images of drilling and sampling operations. 
This Imaging System is composed of 3 main elements: 
1) a Camera Unit (CU), 2) an Artificial Illumination Unit (AIU) and 
3) an Imaging Support and Interface Unit (ISIU). 

The Camera Unit has been subjected to ITT AO130114 and shall be considered 
as a CFI for the present ITT, whose subject is targeted specifically at Artificial 
Illumination Unit (AIU) and Imaging Support & Interface Unit (ISIU). 

The Camera Unit will acquire static images and video footage of drilling and sampling
operations under both artificial illumination and natural sunlight conditions. 
The AIU and ISIU shall support the Camera Unit providing with proper support, 
interface and artificial illumination.

This procurement aims to identify and / or develop hardware of high technical 
maturity which can fulfil the requirements and which is compatible with the 
cost and schedule constraints of the project. 

The Contractor is also required to support the Prime Contractor responsible by providing
 relevant data associated with the Imaging System HW, to support via HW testing the
 verification of the performance, and to supply Engineering Model HW which can be
 used in overall system tests. This work shall be carried out within the overall scope 
of the running PROSPECT Phase B+ activity.

tenderTitle: FLEXITT05FLEX PLM / TEL - RE-ISSUE
tenderDescription:
The FLuORescence Imaging Spectrometer (FLORIS) is the Instrument of the FLuorescence Explorer
 Mission (FLEX) of Earth Explorer 8 (EE8) mission, 4th ?Fast-Track? (formerly known as 
Opportunity) Mission of European Space Agency.
The FLEX (Fluorescence Explorer) mission objective is to perform quantitative measurements of the
 solar induced vegetation fluorescence in order to monitor vegetation photosynthetic activity.
The FLEX Space Segment consists of a single satellite carrying the FLuORescence Imaging
 Spectrometer (FLORIS) push-broom instrument. This high-resolution imaging spectrometer will
 acquire data in the 500? 780 nm spectral range, with a sampling of 0.1 nm in the oxygen bands 
(759?769 nm and 686?697 nm) and 0.5?2.0 nm in the red edge, chlorophyll absorption 
and Photochemical Reflectance Index bands. FLEX satellite is flying in convoy with Copernicus
 Sentinel-3. The FLEX mission will work in combination with Sentinel-3's Ocean and Land Colour
 Instrument (OLCI) and Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer (SLSTR) that will provide 
additional information about vegetation status (TOA reflectance and temperature) and accurate
 atmospheric correction, which are essential for quantitative interpretation of fluorescence signal.
Leonardo S. p. A. is the Instrument Prime of the FLORIS Instrument contract placed by ESA. 
The FLEX Satellite Prime will be selected in a second procurement step. At FLEX Prime Satellite 
contract award, the FLORIS Instrument Contract will be novated under the full responsibility of the 
FLEX Satellite Prime.

for the Telescope (TEL) as part of the FLEX Instrument (FLORIS).

tenderTitle: BIOMASS Instrument SCOE
tenderDescription:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of the Instrument Electronic System (INES) Satellite Checkout Equipment 
(SCOE) by Airbus Defence and Space GmbH as a Core team 
member of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The Instrument Electronics System (INES) comprises the following subsystems:
- Central Electronics Subsystem (CES) including a Digital Control Unit (DCU), 
 Calibration Distribution Network (CDN), 
 all supported by an Application Software (ASW)
- Power Amplifier Subsystem (PAS)
- Receive Amplifier Subsystem (RAS)

The Feed Array is part of the BIOMASS Antenna System and has the function 
of transmitting and receiving the RF signals to and from the LDR (Large 
Deployable Reflector) by the INES. The LDR is an element of the Platform 
and forms together with the Instrument the SAR Payload.

The primary function of the INES SCOE is to provide the Biomass satellite
platform interfaces to the Instrument before it is integrated onto the 
platform. Hence, the INES SCOE shall provide the same interface types, 
interface connectors and functionalities than the ones provided by the 
platform, allowing interface verification and functional testing on Biomass 
Instrument AIT level prior to delivery to Biomass Satellite system 
integration, where the INES SCOE will be fully replaced by the satellite 
platform.

tenderTitle: BIOMASS Instrument Receive Amplifier Subsystem (RAS)
tenderDescription:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of Receive Amplifier Subsystem (RAS) by Airbus DS GmbH as a Core team 
member of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development (including the
required qualification activities), manufacturing, testing and delivery of
the RAS.

The Receive Amplifier Subsystem (RAS) routes and amplifies the received 
radar echo from the PAS to the CES at low noise for one polarisation. The 
envisaged architecture 1 and architecture 2 for the RAS is shown in the 
Specific Statement of Work (SSOW). The RAS comprises protection for the 
instrument, even if the Instrument is powered off. Degradation of the RAS 
and data unavailability in case of Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) is 
minimized by bandpass filters before or after the LNA, depending on the 
supplier solution after thorough analysis of Scenario 1 and Scenario 2. 

For the two polarisations available, the Biomass Instrument contains two 
identical RAS, one for each polarisation. For the accommodation and 
mechanical envelope of the two RAS on the satellite, the SSOW provides 
the necessary details.

A thorough analysis on the RFI, especially with, but not limited to 
different levels of RFI, image rejection, noise figure, damage levels, 
linearity and dynamic range shall be performed by the Tenderer. 

The Tenderer is requested to provide a detailed proposal describing both 
architectures. The proposal shall also contain for each architecture, the 
corresponding price breakdown supported by PSS forms, a schedule and a 
development plan. The decision to implement architecture 1 or 2 will be 
taken by Airbus DS GmbH / Satellite Prime not later than 6 months after 
the KO based on the contractor phase B2 tasks as described in SSoW.

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating
State in the ESA Biomass project. 

The following States are participating in the said Programme: Austria,
Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany,
Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland,
Portugal, Romania, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.

tenderTitle: BIOMASS Instrument Central Electronic Subsystem (CES)
tenderDescription:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of Central Electronics Subsystem (CES) by Airbus DS GmbH as a Core team 
member of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development (including the
required qualification activities), manufacturing, testing and delivery of
the CES.

The Central Electronics Subsystem (CES) is the heart of the Biomass 
instrument. It is an assembly of several equipments, connected by internal 
harness up to and including a connector bracket and mounted on the MXPZ
panel wall of the Instrument/satellite.

The CES contains all units required to form a full, cold redundant radar 
core including all networks required for internal calibration, plus the 
Boot Software. 

One important EGSE of the CES procurement is the INES SCOE that shall be 
used both at CES level by the contractor and at instrument level by Airbus 
Defence and Space. 

The INES SCOE shall be used to operate, test, and checkout the CES. The 
INES SCOE will also need to offer all interfaces from the satellite 
avionics to the PAS, RAS-V and RAS-H in addition to the functions described 
for the operation of the INES SCOE on CES level. For this purpose, the INES 
SCOE shall provide the same interfaces types, interface connectors and 
functionalities as provided by the satellite avionics, allowing interface 
verification and functional testing on instrument level.

The INES SCOE is expected to be procured by the successful CES bidder under 
Best Practice Open competition and under the management of the CES bidder. 

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating
State in the ESA Biomass project. 

The following States are participating in the said Programme: Austria,
Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany,
Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland,
